title: PluginConfigCreate request body
description: Edge's PluginConfigCreate request schema (openapi.yaml components.schemas.PluginConfigCreate), generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3) with every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. Admission rules that exist only in Edge's Rust code are not in this schema; resource-schemas/README.md lists them. This is Edge's own API schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md).

A2aGatewayConfig.description: Plugin: a2a_gateway — transparent Agent-to-Agent protocol gateway for HTTP JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON/REST, and gRPC/grpcs A2A traffic. The implemented A2A protocol version is 0.3.x, whose canonical gRPC service is a2a.v1.A2AService (package a2a.v1); A2A 1.0's lf.a2a.v1.A2AService carries a renumbered AgentCard and is never decoded as 0.3. Detects standard A2A methods, optionally denies methods by gateway policy, rewrites HTTP JSON and unary gRPC Agent Card endpoint URLs to the gateway address, preserves SSE/gRPC streaming for non-card traffic, and emits a2a.* metadata for existing Ferrum logging, tracing, chargeback, WAF, and alerting plugins. It does not manage A2A task state or aggregate multiple agents in V1. Cannot be composed with request_deduplication on the same proxy while discovery.public_base_url is unset and discovery.trust_forwarded_headers is true; admission rejects that pairing with 400 because the rewritten Agent Card origin is then derived from per-request forwarded headers and the connection's transport security, neither of which a replay fingerprint binds. A configured discovery.public_base_url composes normally. Null is accepted everywhere a value is optional and means the same thing as omitting the key. Unknown keys are rejected at construction, at the root and inside every nested fixed-shape object.

path.description: Public JSON-RPC A2A endpoint path. Must be a non-empty absolute path beginning with /.

agent_card_path.description: Public Agent Card discovery path suffix. Must be a non-empty absolute path beginning with /.

protocol_versions.description: Supported A2A protocol versions as EXACT version strings. There is no family, range, or wildcard syntax - listing 0.3.0 admits 0.3.0 and not 0.3.99. The first entry is the gateway's preferred version for a2a.protocol_version metadata. gRPC Agent Card rewriting additionally requires the responding gRPC service to declare the a2a-0.3 card schema (see endpoint.grpc_services) AND the matched version to belong to the implemented A2A 0.3 wire layout, so an exactly-configured 1.0.0 is still refused.

oneOf.description: Fully-qualified gRPC service name. A published A2A service name resolves to the Agent Card wire layout the A2A specification gives it - a2a.v1.A2AService is A2A 0.3 (card_schema a2a-0.3) and lf.a2a.v1.A2AService is A2A 1.0 (card_schema a2a-1.0). Any other name is a custom service with no published layout and resolves to card_schema none.

service.description: Fully-qualified gRPC service name. Required; null is not accepted here. Duplicate service names across entries are rejected.

card_schema.description: Agent Card protobuf wire layout this service is declared to serve. a2a-0.3 is the only layout the gateway decodes and rewrites; a2a-1.0 and none are detected and policed but fail card rewriting closed. Omitted means the published layout for a published A2A service name and none for a custom one. Declaring a value that contradicts a published A2A service name is rejected - the layout is a property of the protocol, not of the deployment.

grpc_services.description: Fully-qualified gRPC service names recognized as A2A services, each with a declared Agent Card wire layout. RPCs on these services are detected, mapped to canonical a2a.method names, and gated by method policy from request metadata alone - request protobuf payloads are never decoded. The defaults recognize both the canonical A2A 0.3 service a2a.v1.A2AService (package a2a.v1 in a2aproject/A2A at tag v0.3.0) and A2A 1.0's lf.a2a.v1.A2AService so upgrades preserve method-policy enforcement for either published identity. The 0.3 service is the identity whose card layout the default endpoint.protocol_versions 0.3.0 describes. The 1.0 service uses package lf.a2a.v1 with a renumbered AgentCard; it is detected and policed by default while card rewriting on it fails closed with agent_card_grpc_schema_unsupported rather than decoding a 1.0 card as 0.3. The one decoded payload is the unary Agent Card reply (GetAgentCard / GetExtendedAgentCard) on an a2a-0.3 service when discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls is enabled - a proven-successful reply is decoded against the A2A 0.3.x Agent Card wire layout, rewritten, and re-encoded as a single uncompressed frame, and anything unsupported or malformed fails closed with a fixed diagnostic. A card RPC on a service whose declared layout is none fails closed with agent_card_grpc_schema_undeclared; set discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls false or declare card_schema a2a-0.3 for such a deployment. All other gRPC responses, including streaming ones, pass through undecoded.

bindings.description: A2A bindings to detect. Each entry is one of three bindings, and two of them accept aliases that normalize to the canonical name - "json-rpc" is "jsonrpc", and "http_json" and "http+json" are "rest". The list must be non-empty; repeating a binding under two spellings is accepted and deduplicates.

version_header.description: Header used to record/accept A2A protocol version hints. Must be a valid non-empty HTTP field name.

max_request_body_size.description: Maximum JSON-RPC request body bytes parsed for A2A detection; 0 means no plugin-level detection limit. Oversized JSON-RPC candidates fail closed (HTTP 413, JSON-RPC -32013) when default_action is deny, any per-method deny or group-conditioned rule is configured, or discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls is enabled.

allow_unknown_methods_with_version_heade.description: Treat JSON-RPC requests carrying the version header as A2A even when the method is not in the built-in standard-method table. Metadata records method as unknown to bound cardinality. An unknown method without the version header is unclassified, and is refused while a deny-capable policy or discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls is enabled.

strip_accept_encoding.description: Remove Accept-Encoding on non-streaming A2A HTTP requests whose responses may be parsed or rewritten by the plugin. Enabling this plugin with the default true value marks request headers mutable for all traffic on the proxy.

rewrite_agent_card_urls.description: Rewrite Agent Card endpoint URLs for detected HTTP JSON and unary gRPC card requests. Rewrites every advertised interface on a transport the gateway fronts - JSONRPC (or no transport) and HTTP+JSON/REST URLs become the public base plus endpoint.path, GRPC URLs become the public base itself, and the top-level url follows preferredTransport the same way; interfaces on any other transport keep the backend URL. Removes stale signatures after mutation. An HTTP card response whose backend representation is content-coded (gzip, br, ...) or a 206/226 fragment is claimed by the shared buffered-response representation gate - a supported coding is decoded and the decoded card rewritten and served as identity bytes, anything else fails closed with 502 - so an encoded card is never forwarded with its internal URLs. Also re-encodes A2A 0.3.x protobuf Agent Cards on the gRPC path. The gRPC path only inspects a proven-successful reply - HTTP 200 with a terminal grpc-status of exactly 0 - so a non-OK upstream response is forwarded as written rather than mistaken for a card. It rewrites the A2A 0.3.x wire layout only and requires positive proof of it TWICE - the responding gRPC service must be declared to carry the a2a-0.3 card schema (endpoint.grpc_services; a service declared a2a-1.0 or none fails closed with agent_card_grpc_schema_unsupported / agent_card_grpc_schema_undeclared before a byte is decoded) AND the card must carry an explicit protocol_version that exactly matches a configured endpoint.protocol_versions entry AND belongs to the 0.3 family. A card with an absent or empty protocol_version fails closed with a trailers-only gRPC INTERNAL under HTTP 200 and an unsupported_agent_card_protobuf_version diagnostic, and is not assumed to be 0.3.x even when endpoint.protocol_versions lists only 0.3.x. A2A renumbered AgentCard for 1.0, so guessing would corrupt the card and re-serve it under a stale signature. All seventeen known 0.3 top-level fields are schema-validated before any rewrite - each must carry the wire type the 0.3 schema declares (a canonical 0/1 varint for supports_authenticated_extended_card), each singular field may appear at most once, and every known string that is re-emitted must be valid UTF-8. url and every AgentInterface url must parse as a bounded absolute http/https URL with a real host and no embedded credentials, and an AgentInterface without a url is refused rather than counted as a usable endpoint. Faults fail closed with agent_card_protobuf_field_wire_mismatch, agent_card_protobuf_field_duplicated, agent_card_protobuf_string_invalid, agent_card_protobuf_bool_invalid, agent_card_protobuf_interface_url_missing, or agent_card_protobuf_url_layout_mismatch. The submessages the rewriter preserves rather than parses - provider, capabilities, security_schemes, security, skills, and signatures - are checked for wire type and multiplicity only; their contents are never decoded and are not claimed to be well formed. Unknown fields with any valid wire type are preserved untouched. Diagnostics are fixed strings; response bytes are never reflected into grpc-message or metadata. Set this to false when fronting a non-0.3 A2A backend; leaving it true refuses such cards rather than serving un-rewritten internal URLs. While enabled on an instance serving the jsonrpc binding, every POST to endpoint.path must be classified as JSON-RPC by that instance, at arrival and on the final request body, whichever instance claimed the request (an Agent Card call claimed by a sibling as a non-card operation, or by a sibling that does not rewrite cards, is refused with -32001 / a2a.error operation_class_changed), because an unclaimed card call would be answered with the backend's internal URLs - an oversized, duplicate-member (including a case-variant spelling of jsonrpc, method, params, or id), malformed, envelope-less, unknown-method (without the version header), mixed-batch, or non-JSON-media-type POST there fails closed with JSON-RPC -32001 (a2a.error request_body_uninspectable) or, when oversized, HTTP 413 / -32013, even under the default allow policy. A leading UTF-8 BOM is skipped for classification wherever classification is required. The JSON-RPC endpoint.path must therefore not equal a native gRPC method path; such an overlap fails closed. Set false (with no deny-capable policy) to keep transparent passthrough of unrecognized JSON-RPC.

public_base_url.description: Explicit public gateway base URL, for example https://agents.example.com. Rewriting defaults to enabled and requires this value or trust_forwarded_headers=true with nonempty allowed_public_origins. Empty plugin configurations fail admission. Explicit rewrite_agent_card_urls=false selects unchanged backend cards. When deriving an origin, X-Forwarded-* and Host must select an allowed normalized origin; missing, malformed, comma-separated or unlisted origins fail closed before backend dispatch with agent_card_public_origin_unavailable (HTTP 502 or gRPC INTERNAL). Configuring this value is also what makes the Agent Card rewrite a pure function of configuration, which is required to compose this plugin with request_deduplication on the same proxy.

trust_forwarded_headers.description: Derive the public gateway origin from X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host, and Host when discovery.public_base_url is omitted. Requires nonempty allowed_public_origins when rewriting is enabled; the trusted front door must replace forwarded headers. Schemes and ports must match an allowed normalized origin. Without X-Forwarded-Proto the scheme is https exactly when the client connection is secure (TLS, or HTTP/3), never inferred from TLS SNI. In that request-derived mode the origin also depends on that transport security, which no replay fingerprint binds, so admission rejects the pair with request_deduplication on the same proxy with 400 (fatal in file mode, rejected update in DP) and the runtime retains and replays nothing. Setting discovery.public_base_url resolves it; a configured public base composes normally.

allowed_public_origins.description: Allowed absolute HTTP(S) origins for request-derived card URLs, without paths, credentials, queries or fragments. Required with trust_forwarded_headers when rewriting is enabled and public_base_url is absent. Compared after URL origin normalization, including scheme and non-default port. A configured public_base_url takes precedence.

emit_metadata.description: Emit a2a.* request and response metadata for downstream logging, tracing, authz, and chargeback plugins. When true (default), detected non-streaming A2A HTTP responses are buffered so response metadata (a2a.task_id, a2a.context_id, a2a.task_state, a2a.error) can be extracted; SSE and non-card gRPC responses are never buffered for metadata. Detected unary gRPC Agent Card responses are buffered when discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls is true so protobuf cards can be rewritten. Detected 2xx SSE streams are observed without buffering and write a2a.stream_events plus any observed a2a.task_id, a2a.context_id, and a2a.task_state into transaction metadata at stream termination, where key-based metadata redaction applies. The buffer is bounded by the global FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES limit, not max_payload_size. Set false together with discovery.rewrite_agent_card_urls=false to keep responses fully streaming; request detection and method policy still apply.

log_payloads.description: Copies bounded A2A response payloads into metadata. Payloads can contain secrets or PII and are copied verbatim into a2a.payload.response rather than field-redacted; enable only for protected logging paths. Request payloads are not logged. Requires emit_metadata=true, because payload capture writes the a2a.payload.response metadata key; with emit_metadata=false this option has no effect.

max_payload_size.description: Payload logging byte limit. Task and context identifiers, textual errors and protocol-version metadata are capped at min(max_payload_size, 1024) UTF-8 bytes including a trailing ~ marker, with a companion .truncated flag. Task states are normalized to the protocol state set; unrecognized states become unknown with .unrecognized=true, and normalized states too large for this limit are omitted with .truncated=true. Applies to request hints, JSON replies and SSE completion metadata; does not cap response buffering or alter response bytes.

default_action.description: With deny, any per-method deny rule, or any group-conditioned allow rule (policy.methods.*.allowed_groups / denied_groups), unrecognized requests inside the configured endpoint, discovery or gRPC-service scope fail closed, including unsupported payloads, methods, paths and disabled bindings. Known batch members are individually policed. Unrelated sibling paths and services are outside scope.

methods.description: Per-method policy overrides. Keys must be a canonical A2A method name — message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/list, tasks/cancel, tasks/resubscribe, tasks/pushNotificationConfig/set, tasks/pushNotificationConfig/get, tasks/pushNotificationConfig/list, tasks/pushNotificationConfig/delete, agent/getCard, agent/getExtendedAgentCard, agent/getAuthenticatedExtendedCard — or the literal "unknown". PascalCase gRPC/REST aliases such as SendMessage or GetTask are accepted and normalized to these canonical names. Unrecognized keys are rejected at config validation. Two keys that canonicalize to the same method — for example "tasks/get" and "GetTask", or "SubscribeToTask" and "TaskSubscription" — are a duplicate and are rejected; that cross-key restriction is not expressible in this schema.

action.description: Required; null is not accepted here.

allowed_groups.description: Requires action allow. Grants the method only to a request whose gateway-mapped Consumer holds at least one of these acl_groups; a request with no mapped Consumer is never granted a group-conditioned method, and an ungranted method is refused exactly like a deny rule (JSON-RPC -32001, REST 403, gRPC PERMISSION_DENIED), re-decided over the final backend-visible JSON-RPC body. Omitting it (or null) drops only the allowed-group requirement; a mapped Consumer is still required whenever denied_groups is present. An empty list is rejected. Entries are matched byte-for-byte, must not contain control characters other than tab, LF, and CR, and are at most 255 bytes (the schema bounds code points; the byte bound is enforced at plugin load, as for Consumer acl_groups). A group-conditioned entry counts as a deny-capable rule for in-scope fail-closed classification.

denied_groups.description: Requires action allow. A Consumer holding any of these acl_groups is refused the method even when it also holds an allowed group; with no allowed_groups it grants every mapped Consumer except these, and never a request without a mapped Consumer. An empty list is rejected, and one entry may not name the same group in both lists (enforced at plugin load). Entries follow the allowed_groups entry rules.

AccessControlConfig.description: Plugin: access_control — consumer-based, group-based, and exact external-principal allow/deny for HTTP-family and TCP/UDP stream proxies. Evaluation order: deny (consumer username → group) then allow (consumer username → group); unmapped external identities are judged by `disallowed_consumers`, `disallowed_external_identities`, then `allowed_external_identities` or the `allow_authenticated_identity` bypass. Deny always overrides allow. Once any allow-list is configured, a principal matching none of them is denied — a mapped Consumer on a policy whose only allow-list is `allowed_external_identities` included. At least one of `allowed_consumers`, `disallowed_consumers`, `allowed_groups`, `disallowed_groups`, `allowed_external_identities`, `disallowed_external_identities`, or `allow_authenticated_identity=true` must be configured, and an allow-list (`allowed_consumers`/`allowed_groups`/`allowed_external_identities`) that is present must be non-empty: omit it for no allow restriction. Unknown config keys are rejected. `allow_authenticated_identity=true` cannot be combined with an allow-list (`allowed_consumers`/`allowed_groups`/`allowed_external_identities`): the consumer allow-lists are not applied to unmapped external identities, and the bypass would admit every external identity an external allow-list omits. Use ip_restriction for IP/CIDR rules. Rule entries match principal values byte-for-byte (no trimming) and must contain at least one non-whitespace character. Whitespace admission follows Rust `str::trim` Unicode `White_Space` semantics.

allowed_consumers.description: Consumer usernames that are explicitly allowed. Omit the key for no username allow check (other allow rules still apply). An explicitly empty array is rejected rather than read as allow-all or deny-all. Each entry is at most 255 Unicode characters.

disallowed_consumers.description: Consumer usernames or, when allow_authenticated_identity is true, exact external principals that are explicitly denied. Takes precedence over every allow rule. The 4096-character bound is independent of the 255-character gateway Consumer username ceiling so JWT, OIDC, and SPIFFE-style principals can be revoked; longer external identities fail closed at runtime.

allowed_groups.description: ACL group names that are explicitly allowed. The check matches if any of the consumer's `acl_groups` appears in this list. Omit the key for no group allow check; an explicitly empty array is rejected. Each entry is at most 255 Unicode characters.

disallowed_groups.description: ACL group names that are explicitly denied. If any of the consumer's `acl_groups` appears in this list the request is rejected, even when the username is in `allowed_consumers`. Each entry is at most 255 Unicode characters.

allow_authenticated_identity.description: Allow requests whose `ctx.authenticated_identity` is set by an external auth plugin (e.g. jwks_auth) even when no gateway Consumer was mapped. Empty or whitespace-only identities are unauthenticated. Cannot be combined with an allow-list (`allowed_consumers`/`allowed_groups`/`allowed_external_identities`); the deny-lists `disallowed_consumers` and `disallowed_external_identities` are still applied to the external identity.

identity.description: The external identity string, matched byte-for-byte (no trimming). Must contain a non-whitespace character; at most 4096 characters.

mechanism.description: Restrict the rule to identities committed by this built-in authentication mechanism. Omit to match the identity from every mechanism.

authority.description: Restrict the rule to identities committed with this verifying authority: the opaque 64-character hex realm authority digest the authentication boundary commits with the identity (the value `opa` exposes as `input.consumer.realm.authority`, and the plugin-trigger `external_identity_authority` predicate accepts; compared case-insensitively). Two providers of one mechanism (two `jwks_auth` issuers, two `oauth2_introspection` endpoints) have different digests, so this is what tells them apart, as far as the mechanism's realm derivation does. For `oauth2_introspection`, client credentials do not distinguish authorities, and a provider without an `issuer` pin commits one digest per returned `iss` (plus a base digest when `iss` is absent), so two such providers on the same endpoint and identity claim share a digest whenever the returned issuer is equal. Pinning `issuer` gives one digest per provider and requires the response `iss` to match; distinct endpoints separate providers, but an unpinned provider still commits one digest per returned `iss`, so cover each with its own entry. `jwks_auth`, `oauth2_introspection`, `ldap_auth`, and `oidc_relying_party` commit a digest for every identity; `soap_ws_security` commits none. Allow entries never match an identity with no committed digest. Combined with `mechanism`, both must hold.

allowed_external_identities.description: Exact unmapped external principals (for example a `jwks_auth` `sub`) that are allowed when no gateway Consumer was mapped — the narrow alternative to `allow_authenticated_identity`. An entry with `mechanism` matches only an identity committed by that authentication mechanism, and an entry with `authority` only an identity committed with that verifying authority; an identity with no verified realm (stream proxies, or an identity a custom plugin set directly) never matches a realm-scoped allow entry. On a route with more than one provider of one mechanism (multi-provider `jwks_auth` or `oauth2_introspection`), bind `authority`: `mechanism` alone cannot tell the providers apart, so an equal subject from any of them would match. Omit the key for no external allow list; an explicitly empty array is rejected. Mapped Consumers are not judged by this list, but configuring it makes the policy an allow-list, so a mapped Consumer must then match `allowed_consumers`/`allowed_groups` to pass.

identity.description: The external identity string, matched byte-for-byte (no trimming). Must contain a non-whitespace character; at most 4096 characters.

mechanism.description: Restrict the rule to identities committed by this built-in authentication mechanism. Omit to match the identity from every mechanism.

authority.description: Restrict the rule to identities committed with this verifying authority: the opaque 64-character hex realm authority digest the authentication boundary commits with the identity (the value `opa` exposes as `input.consumer.realm.authority`, and the plugin-trigger `external_identity_authority` predicate accepts; compared case-insensitively). A deny entry fails closed: it also matches an identity with no verified realm or no committed digest, unless the entry also names a `mechanism` and the identity was committed by a different one. Combined with `mechanism`, both must hold.

disallowed_external_identities.description: Exact unmapped external principals that are denied, optionally scoped to the authentication mechanism and/or verifying authority that verified them, so one principal can be revoked without revoking an equal subject string from a different mechanism or provider. A realm-scoped entry also matches an identity with no verified realm, and an `authority`-scoped entry also matches an identity with no committed digest (it fails closed) unless its `mechanism` is a known mismatch. Takes precedence over every allow rule. `disallowed_consumers` remains a realm-blind deny for external identities.

AccessLogFilterExpression.description: Bounded boolean predicate tree for stdout logging. Runtime validation rejects trees larger than 32 nodes, and any `and` conjunction whose own status atoms can never all hold (a `status_code_min` above a `status_code_max`), wherever it appears in the tree. This form is mutually exclusive with the flat stdout filter predicates. Status-code nodes evaluate false for stream summaries, which do not carry an HTTP status; duration and error nodes continue to evaluate against stream fields.

AdaptiveConcurrencyConfig.description: Plugin: adaptive_concurrency — Target-aware backend admission for upstream survival. Runs after load balancing for HTTP, gRPC, native HTTP/3 backend dispatch, HTTP/3 fallback bridge dispatch, and WebSocket upgrade admission with the permit held for the full session lifetime.

key_by.description: Limit key scope. `proxy_target` keys by proxy plus selected backend. `upstream_target` keys by upstream plus selected backend when the proxy uses an upstream, and falls back to proxy-target scoping for direct backends. `backend_target` shares one limit per backend endpoint across every proxy using this plugin instance.

max_tracked_keys.description: Maximum number of distinct target keys this stable plugin policy will track, bounding limiter memory for high-cardinality wildcard upstreams. State is retained across compatible config reloads. Lowering this value or changing the policy's effective subset-filtered backend targets, route-override destinations, or route execution order publishes an independent tracking space; retired permits finish against detached state, while retired cache and load-balancer views cannot admit, repopulate, or train the replacement. Service-discovery changes outside the policy's selected subset remain compatible. When the cap is reached, new target keys fail open — they are admitted without adaptive limiting (never rejected with a 503) until the policy is removed/recreated, its route key space changes, or the process restarts. Existing keys continue to be admitted subject to their adaptive limit.

min_limit.description: Lower bound for the adaptive in-flight request limit.

initial_limit.description: Starting in-flight request limit for a new target key. Must be between `min_limit` and `max_limit`.

max_limit.description: Upper bound for the adaptive in-flight request limit. Must be greater than or equal to `min_limit`.

min_samples.description: Successful backend samples required before latency-based limit changes are applied.

baseline_window_samples.description: Healthy backend samples per latency-baseline window, counted per target key. The learned baseline is the minimum latency of the current and the previous window, so an unusually fast outlier stops tightening the latency target once two windows have closed after it (at most `2 × baseline_window_samples` healthy samples), and saturated healthy traffic can then regain capacity. A sustained latency increase is measured against the older, faster window and keeps shrinking the limit until that window rolls out; explicit backend failures always shrink it. Changing this value is a compatible reload that keeps learned state.

target_latency_multiplier.description: Target latency threshold as a multiple of the learned windowed-minimum backend latency (see `baseline_window_samples`).

decrease_ratio.description: Multiplicative decrease applied after backend 5xx responses, connection errors, or high latency.

increase_step.description: Additive increase applied when the target is saturated and latency remains within the target.

shadow_mode.description: Learn and expose state without rejecting requests when the current in-flight count is at or above the limit; each such admission is counted as `would_reject` on `ferrum_adaptive_concurrency_decisions_total`. Retired cache/load-balancer views and requests crossing a structural generation handoff still fail closed so they cannot repopulate the replacement tracking space.

expose_headers.description: Include `x-adaptive-concurrency-limit` and `x-adaptive-concurrency-inflight` on genuine per-target limit rejections. Generation-handoff rejections omit them because no truthful per-target limit or in-flight value exists.

AiFederationConfig.description: Plugin: ai_federation — HTTP-family OpenAI Chat Completions gateway. Dispatches from the finalized-request-egress phase after request-body transforms and the complete final request-policy hook pass, so priority_override cannot move provider I/O ahead of WAF/OpenAPI/body/size policy. Translates final request bodies to provider-native JSON with a 64 MiB serialization cap and normalizes bounded, non-streaming responses back to OpenAI format. Native gRPC is not supported or advertised. Provider and OAuth redirects are never followed. Configuration is strict: unknown root, provider, and circuit fields are rejected. Streaming Chat Completions (`stream: true`) are served by a separate non-buffering path that is OFF by default: with the root `streaming` block enabled, before_proxy commits exactly ONE provider before any downstream-visible byte and rewrites the routing decision through route_override_* so the ordinary dispatch path relays provider SSE incrementally. Provider fallback for a stream happens only during that pre-commit selection (open circuit, ineligible provider, unusable endpoint); after the commit no second provider is ever spliced into the same logical stream, and a post-commit failure truncates with one gateway-authored terminal SSE `error` event. Streaming eligibility is narrow: only providers whose native streaming wire format already is the OpenAI Chat Completions SSE contract (openai, mistral, xai, deepseek, meta_llama, hugging_face, azure_openai) with a static header credential. anthropic, google_gemini, google_vertex, aws_bedrock, and cohere, and any provider using AWS SigV4 or Google OAuth2, fail closed with a field-specific 501 — use ai_stream_router for Anthropic/Gemini streaming translation. With `streaming.enabled` the plugin declares a backend-boundary header policy plus request header/destination mutation, so it can no longer be composed with request_deduplication or response_caching on the same proxy. A claimed stream consumes one `max_concurrent_requests` permit and one real provider-circuit admission for the whole life of the response, and both are released exactly once on completion, client disconnect, downstream policy cut, backend error, or cancellation; a 2xx stream is scored a circuit success only after a valid terminal `data: [DONE]`. The selected provider's `multimodal_mode` is applied to a streamed request exactly as to a buffered one: a reject-mode provider declines the request during pre-commit selection and the next matching provider is considered, a text_only_with_warning provider has the non-text content parts removed from the provider-visible body, and the finalized body is re-checked before egress so a later transform cannot reintroduce content the committed provider forbids. The provider-visible top-level `model` is rewritten to the value `model_mapping` / `default_model` resolved, and the committed provider's `connect_timeout_seconds` / `read_timeout_seconds` become the streaming route's dispatch budgets instead of the matched proxy's. Provider response headers on a claimed stream are reduced to the same bounded safe allowlist the buffered path publishes plus a gateway-authored `Content-Type: text/event-stream` — provider cookies, redirects, auth challenges, validators/digests, and unknown metadata never reach the client. Streaming is disabled by default and `stream: true` then returns 501 as before. Priority fallback is allowed for configured statuses and proven pre-wire transport failures; a completed 2xx that cannot be normalized is TERMINAL and returns 502 (response_normalization_failed) without calling another provider, because that generation has already been performed. Ambiguous POST outcomes are not replayed by default. Fails closed by default when a JSON POST cannot be inspected, lacks a string `model`, or has no matching provider. Outbound calls use the shared PluginHttpClient and global TLS settings (FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH, FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY); per-proxy backend TLS overrides do not apply. On the buffered path a provider non-2xx response body is never relayed: the client receives a fixed OpenAI-shaped envelope (`error.type`/`error.code` `upstream_error`, message naming only the status) plus the bounded safe provider headers, so provider error codes such as context_length_exceeded do not reach the client (a claimed stream relays the provider's own error envelope instead). Translating providers (anthropic, google_gemini, google_vertex, aws_bedrock) map messages, max_tokens/max_completion_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, tools, and tool_choice; google_gemini/google_vertex additionally map response_format json_object/json_schema (responseMimeType application/json plus responseJsonSchema; a json_schema needs a schema object, and a strict one may only use the Gemini-enforced keyword subset listed in docs/plugins.md), n > 1 (candidateCount), seed, and non-zero presence/frequency penalties, and anthropic maps parallel_tool_calls false. Any other semantic control that a translating provider cannot represent (response_format JSON modes, n > 1, seed, or non-zero penalties on anthropic/aws_bedrock; parallel_tool_calls false on google_*/aws_bedrock; logprobs true, top_logprobs, a non-empty logit_bias, tools[].function.strict true, reasoning_effort, reasoning, verbosity, audio, prediction, web_search_options, legacy functions/function_call, or non-text modalities on all three) is refused before provider I/O; the next matching provider is tried and otherwise the request fails 400 provider_translation_failed. Gemini/Vertex function-call thought signatures are exported on the tool call as `extra_content.google.thought_signature` (Google's OpenAI-compatibility convention, at most 64 KiB) and restored on the native functionCall part when the client sends that assistant message back.

providers.description: One or more provider definitions. Tried in priority order (lower number = first).

name.description: Unique provider name used in logs and metadata (e.g. ai_federation_provider field).

priority.description: Lower = tried first. Defaults to provider's index + 1. Providers with equal priority keep configuration order unless one of them sets `weight`.

weight.description: Optional weighted-selection share. When any provider in the leading equal-`priority` group of a request's matching providers sets `weight`, the FIRST attempt is chosen at random in proportion to the weights (an unset weight counts as 1; a provider whose circuit cannot currently admit, whose multimodal_mode refuses the request's content parts, or on the streaming path a streaming-ineligible provider, gets no share); the remaining attempts keep the deterministic priority/configuration order. A random value is drawn only when at least two providers of the group can take the first attempt. Applies to buffered and streaming selection alike. When no provider sets `weight`, selection is fully deterministic.

api_key.description: API key for the provider. Required for all providers except aws_bedrock (uses SigV4) and google_vertex (uses service account JWT). An empty value is treated as absent and fails configuration admission; the resolved value must also be a valid HTTP header value (no newlines or control characters). A whole-value `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference (uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) is resolved from the gateway process environment at construction, so the secret need not be stored in plugin configuration (the namespace is materializable from Vault/AWS/Azure/GCP/file at startup); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or to an unset/empty one, is refused at admission without echoing it.

model_patterns.description: Glob patterns to match the request's `model` field (e.g. ['claude-*', 'gpt-4*']). Empty = catch-all.

model_mapping.description: Map client-facing model names to provider-native names (e.g. {claude-4-sonnet: 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'}).

default_model.description: Model to send to the provider when no mapping matches.

multimodal_mode.description: How this provider handles OpenAI Chat Completions content parts that are not text. Translated providers default to reject; OpenAI-compatible providers and Cohere default to translate. text_only_with_warning intentionally drops non-text parts and records ai_federation_multimodal_* metadata.

connect_timeout_seconds.description: Per-provider TCP + TLS handshake timeout for outbound provider calls.

read_timeout_seconds.description: Overall per-request deadline for outbound provider calls.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Maximum provider response bytes collected and maximum normalized JSON bytes emitted. Collection/serialization aborts as soon as this bound is exceeded.

base_url.description: Override the provider endpoint. Userinfo, query strings, and fragments are rejected. HTTPS is required unless allow_plaintext is explicitly true; literal and resolved IPs remain subject to FERRUM_BACKEND_ALLOW_IPS.

allow_plaintext.description: Permit an explicit http:// base_url. This weakens credential transport security and never permits provider-generated redirects.

azure_resource.description: Azure OpenAI resource name (the {resource} in {resource}.openai.azure.com). Required for azure_openai.

azure_deployment.description: Azure OpenAI deployment name. Required for azure_openai. Interpolated into the provider endpoint path, so the traversal sequence `..` is rejected.

azure_api_version.description: Azure OpenAI api-version query parameter. Interpolated into the provider endpoint, so the traversal sequence `..` is rejected.

google_project_id.description: Google Cloud project ID. Required for google_vertex. Interpolated into the provider endpoint path, so the traversal sequence `..` is rejected.

google_region.description: Google Vertex AI region (e.g. us-central1). Required for google_vertex.

google_service_account_json.description: Google service account JSON contents (the file body, not the path). Required for google_vertex; used to mint OAuth2 access tokens via JWT bearer flow. An empty value is treated as absent and fails configuration admission. A whole-value `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference (uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) is resolved from the gateway process environment at construction, so the secret need not be stored in plugin configuration (the namespace is materializable from Vault/AWS/Azure/GCP/file at startup); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or to an unset/empty one, is refused at admission without echoing it.

aws_region.description: AWS region for Bedrock (e.g. us-east-1). Required for aws_bedrock unless AWS_DEFAULT_REGION/AWS_REGION env var is set. The default endpoint is partition-aware: cn-* regions derive bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com.cn and every other region derives bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com. When the key id or secret resolves from the process environment, the region must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials).

aws_access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID for Bedrock SigV4 signing. Falls back to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID env var. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official Bedrock Runtime endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). A whole-value `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference (uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) is resolved from the gateway process environment at construction, so the secret need not be stored in plugin configuration (the namespace is materializable from Vault/AWS/Azure/GCP/file at startup); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or to an unset/empty one, is refused at admission without echoing it. A referenced value counts as provider-config credentials, not ambient ones.

aws_secret_access_key.description: AWS secret access key for Bedrock SigV4 signing. Falls back to AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env var. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official Bedrock Runtime endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). A whole-value `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference (uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) is resolved from the gateway process environment at construction, so the secret need not be stored in plugin configuration (the namespace is materializable from Vault/AWS/Azure/GCP/file at startup); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or to an unset/empty one, is refused at admission without echoing it. A referenced value counts as provider-config credentials, not ambient ones.

aws_session_token.description: Optional AWS STS session token for temporary credentials. Falls back to AWS_SESSION_TOKEN env var only when aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key also resolve from the environment; the environment token is never paired with a config key pair. A process-environment token may only be sent to an official Bedrock Runtime endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). A whole-value `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference (uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) is resolved from the gateway process environment at construction, so the secret need not be stored in plugin configuration (the namespace is materializable from Vault/AWS/Azure/GCP/file at startup); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or to an unset/empty one, is refused at admission without echoing it.

allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_crede.description: aws_bedrock only. When aws_access_key_id or aws_secret_access_key is omitted here and resolves from the gateway process environment (AWS_SESSION_TOKEN is then used too; it never completes a config key pair), the region must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region, and the provider endpoint (base_url, or the host derived from aws_region) must be an official Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint for that region over HTTPS on the default port: bedrock-runtime[-fips].<region>.amazonaws.com, bedrock-runtime[-fips].<region>.api.aws, or an interface VPC endpoint vpce-<id>[-<az>].bedrock-runtime[-fips].<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com, where <region> is a commercial or GovCloud region; a cn-* region uses amazonaws.com.cn and the dual-stack api.amazonwebservices.com.cn instead. Anything else is refused at configuration admission, and every provider call re-checks the rendered endpoint fail closed. Credentials written into the provider config are not scoped. Set true only to deliberately sign requests for a private endpoint (for example LocalStack), an air-gapped ISO partition, or the AWS European Sovereign Cloud with the process credentials; anyone who can write this plugin config can then direct those credentials to that endpoint.

circuit_breaker.description: Optional passive circuit. State belongs to this resolved provider instance and is discarded on configuration reload. Transitions are exported both in the aggregate ferrum_ai_federation_circuits_* series and per configured provider name in ferrum_ai_federation_provider_circuits_open / _opened_total / _closed_total (label `provider`). On a claimed stream, a provider transport fault (a dispatch timeout/reset/refusal answered by a gateway-authored 502/504 before any provider header, or a body that dies on a read timeout/reset after headers) scores a circuit failure regardless of fallback_on_status_codes (body-phase classes match proxy core's post-wire backend-failure set); client disconnects, authorization-lifetime terminations, and gateway-local refusals stay neutral, and route deadlines are settled exactly as proxy core settles them (a body cut by the route deadline is neutral; a pre-header expiry is charged only when the provider held the attempt).

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive configured transport, status, or protocol failures before opening.

cooldown_seconds.description: Time to skip an open provider before permitting one half-open probe.

success_threshold.description: Successful half-open probes required to close the circuit.

fallback_enabled.description: Try the next provider when one fails (network error or matching status code).

fallback_on_status_codes.description: Non-2xx HTTP status codes from a provider that trigger fallback to the next provider. Success codes are rejected because the generation has already committed.

fallback_on_network_errors.description: Trigger fallback only for transport failures proven to occur before the non-idempotent provider POST reached the wire.

fallback_on_protocol_errors.description: Try the next provider when a redirect is returned. A completed 2xx that cannot be normalized returns 502 without replay, even when ambiguous-outcome fallback is enabled.

fallback_on_ambiguous_errors.description: Permit replay on the next provider after a POST may have reached the prior provider. Enabling this can duplicate model calls and charges; leave false unless the provider contract supplies replay safety.

fail_on_missing_model.description: Reject JSON POST requests whose body cannot be inspected as JSON or lacks a top-level string `model` field. Set to false only to explicitly pass such requests through to the normal backend.

fail_on_no_matching_provider.description: Reject requests whose `model` does not match any configured provider. Set to false only to explicitly pass unsupported models through to the normal backend.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Maximum simultaneous federation provider chains, including fallback and OAuth work, and including claimed streaming chains — a stream holds its permit for the whole life of the response and returns it on completion, client disconnect, downstream policy cut, backend error, or cancellation. Excess requests fail with 503 without queueing.

streaming.description: Incremental provider response streaming for OpenAI Chat Completions requests with `stream: true`. Disabled by default; when absent, streaming requests keep returning 501 and non-streaming federation behavior is unchanged.

enabled.description: Claim streaming requests in before_proxy and commit one eligible provider before any downstream-visible byte. Enabling this makes the plugin declare a backend-boundary header policy and request header/destination mutation, so it can no longer be composed with request_deduplication or response_caching on the same proxy.

max_event_bytes.description: Ceiling on one retained server-sent event. This is the whole retained state of a claimed stream — at most one event is held at a time (the partial event being assembled, or the terminal `data: [DONE]` event once the provider frames its completion) and there is no queue — so retention grows with neither stream length nor transport chunk size: the ceiling is enforced on every complete AND partial event before any of its bytes are retained or released. An event that exceeds it fails closed with a fixed-cardinality terminal SSE error event that never echoes provider bytes. The terminal event is held until the provider's body ends, because a client may stop reading at `[DONE]`; any provider byte after it fails the stream closed and the marker is dropped rather than released.

read_timeout_seconds.description: Streaming-only override for the provider whole-exchange budget. When omitted, a claimed stream uses the SELECTED provider's own `read_timeout_seconds`. On the reqwest dispatch path this budget covers connect through the last response body byte — it is a whole-exchange bound, not a per-chunk inactivity bound — so a generation that legitimately runs longer than the provider's per-call budget needs this override. `0` removes the gateway-imposed whole-exchange bound entirely. The provider's `connect_timeout_seconds` is always applied to the committed streaming destination and is not overridable here.

AiPromptCompressorConfig.description: Plugin: ai_prompt_compressor — Shortens LLM prompt text to reduce token usage, cost, and latency using a bounded model-free statistical (extractive) filter. Rewrites messages[].content (per role) and the legacy top-level prompt for admitted OpenAI Chat Completions or Text Completions representations, and — as fixed-family opt-ins — OpenAI Responses instructions/input message text and Anthropic Messages system/messages[].content text blocks. Code blocks, inline code, URLs, Unicode numbers, and common identifiers are preserved verbatim; negations, restrictive connectives (unless, except, only) and the word after them, plus conditions, obligations, quantifiers, and spelled-out numbers, are always kept. Configured preserve markers use a bounded representation-preserving fallback whenever statistical compression is skipped, and the final hook refuses (400) an admitted final representation — including the decoded view of a content-coded body — that still carries a marker in a string value. Successful compression rewrites reserialize the complete JSON body. No model files, network calls, or external services are used.

compress_roles.description: Message roles whose content is compressed (case-insensitive; at most 32 entries of at most 64 characters). Defaults to user only so system instructions are preserved; add 'system'/'assistant'/'tool' to compress those too. When 'user' is included, the legacy top-level `prompt` field (and a string Responses `input`) is also compressed. 'system' covers the Anthropic top-level system prompt; 'system' or 'developer' covers Responses `instructions`.

target_ratio.description: Fraction of word-tokens to keep. 0.5 targets ~50% reduction; 0.3 is more aggressive. Must be between 0 and 1 (exclusive).

min_content_tokens.description: Estimated-token floor per content string. Content below this is passed through unchanged so short prompts are not mangled. Token counts are estimated (~4 characters per token); no model tokenizer is embedded. A mathematically integral value is accepted however it is spelled (200 and 200.0 alike).

max_scan_bytes.description: A mathematically integral value is accepted however it is spelled. Skip statistical compression when the request body exceeds this size. Configured preserve-marker sanitation remains active up to the immutable 1048576-byte hard body/output maximum and fails closed above it. Eligible prompt text is additionally capped at 524288 bytes, 32768 combined whitespace/tokenizer/marker work units, 256 rewritable fields, and 1024 preserve markers per body. A transformed body is staged beside request metadata for wire-path reuse only when it is at most 65536 bytes.

preserve_tag.description: Optional marker name. Text wrapped in <TAG>...</TAG> in JSON string values is copied through verbatim (the markers themselves are stripped), letting operators protect must-keep spans. Preserve-marker sanitation applies only to string values: object member-name bytes are preserved and names are never sanitized, including marker-shaped or escaped content. Nested spans are flattened while preserving their text; unmatched and JSON-escaped markers in values are stripped deterministically from every admitted request family even when statistical compression is skipped. Name may contain at most 64 ASCII letters, digits, '-', and '_'.

request_family.description: Request-family gate. 'auto' requires a body shape matching the standard endpoint path suffix (/chat/completions or /completions). A fixed family is an explicit opt-in for compatible custom endpoint paths; malformed, provider-native, or ambiguous body shapes pass through unchanged. 'responses' admits OpenAI Responses bodies (string or array `input`; message items' input_text/output_text parts; `instructions`) and 'anthropic_messages' admits Anthropic Messages bodies (`messages` plus optional top-level `system`; text blocks only); neither is ever admitted by 'auto'. Fixed 'text_completions' requires 'user' in compress_roles (after trimming and case normalization).

target_max_tokens.description: Optional aggregate estimated-token budget for all eligible prompt text in one request. Requests within it are not statistically compressed; larger requests keep a per-request word ratio of target_max_tokens / eligible_tokens, never more aggressive than target_ratio. Best effort: protected spans, the target_ratio floor, and the word-versus-token approximation can leave a request above the budget, which is then forwarded rather than refused. A mathematically integral value is accepted however it is spelled.

mode.description: 'enforce' forwards compressed prompts. 'observe' runs the same bounded pipeline, records would-be savings under ai_prompt_compressor.observed_* metadata, and forwards the original prompt text; configured preserve markers are still removed and still fail closed.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of requests eligible for statistical compression (or observation), decided deterministically per request and instance. Unsampled requests are forwarded uncompressed with ai_prompt_compressor.instances.<id>.skipped=not_sampled; preserve-marker sanitation applies to every request.

AiPromptShieldConfig.description: Plugin: ai_prompt_shield — HTTP-only PII detection and redaction in bare JSON AI prompts. Native gRPC is unsupported (not registered for the Grpc protocol view). Framed gRPC-Web bodies (recognized by the proxy's delimiter-aware gRPC-Web classifier, so application/grpc-webhook+json is ordinary JSON) remain outside the JSON inspection scope and are skipped without decoding. In content/all mode every other POST, PUT, and PATCH is in scope whatever its Content-Type: a JSON media type is declared JSON, and a non-UTF-8 body, a body the strict JSON parser refuses, an oversized body, or a non-UTF-8 charset declaration is refused by reject/redact (400 ai_shield_rejected=non_utf8_body / malformed_json / unsupported_charset, 413 above max_scan_bytes) and recorded by warn; any other or missing Content-Type is sniffed and held to the same rules whenever the body may be a JSON document (strict JSON, a BOM, UTF-16/UTF-32, a leading comment, or a JSON root scalar), while text and binary uploads are left alone. Enforcing actions claim encoded sniffed bodies so the representation gate decodes them first. Inspection is scoped to POST/PUT/PATCH (mcp_arguments: POST) on every hook, including the request-body transform, so a co-located body plugin that forces buffering cannot extend redaction to another method. Every in-scope request — scope decided again from the final headers, so a header rewrite cannot carry a request past it — is re-decided in on_final_request_body over the exact backend-visible body after all request-body transforms; reject and warn re-decide there and redact fails closed, because that hook cannot rewrite wire bytes.

patterns.description: Built-in patterns: ssn, credit_card, email, phone_us, api_key, aws_key, ip_address, iban. Each name at most once.

custom_patterns.description: Custom {name, regex} patterns. Each entry accepts exactly these two members; an unknown member is fatal at construction, like an unknown top-level field. `regex` must not match the empty string — a zero-width rule would insert the redaction placeholder at every position — and `name` is bounded (maxLength, in characters) because it is substituted into redaction_placeholder. At most 256 entries. Match enumeration is work-bounded: each walk over a custom pattern's matches is charged, per match, up to the match start plus the pattern's longest possible match (the rest of the string when unbounded), against 256 times the scanned string's length (4 MiB floor); exhaustion fails closed (redaction returns 413 redaction_budget_exceeded, detection counts the pattern as matched).

scan_fields.description: Which parts of the request to scan. 'mcp_arguments' scans only params.arguments of MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests (a singleton or every tools/call member of a batch), accepts the media types mcp_gateway admits (application/json, application/json-rpc, +json, or no Content-Type), and refuses a body with duplicate member names under reject/redact (400, ai_shield_rejected=ambiguous_json). 'content' scans LLM prompt fields only: chat messages[].content plus top-level prompt, input, instructions, system, inputText, message, preamble, and inputs (completions/responses/embeddings/Anthropic-system/Bedrock-Titan/Cohere-v1/HuggingFace-TGI shapes), Google Gemini contents[].parts[].text and systemInstruction/system_instruction parts, Cohere chat_history[].message, Google Vertex legacy predict instances[].prompt, Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolResult content and guardContent text, Anthropic tool_result block content, tool-call arguments replayed in the history (OpenAI messages[].tool_calls[].function.arguments and function_call.arguments, Responses input[] function_call arguments, Anthropic tool_use/server_tool_use/mcp_tool_use input, Bedrock Converse toolUse.input, Gemini parts[].functionCall.args), and Azure On Your Data role_information — including content blocks that carry no type discriminator (Bedrock Converse) and matches split across adjacent text parts. Detection and redaction cover the same field set. 'all' scans the entire request body recursively while exempting only top-level structural scalar values such as model/id/role and numeric tuning parameters; nested occurrences remain scannable. Use 'all' for request shapes that carry prompt text in non-standard fields.

exclude_roles.description: Message roles to skip scanning. Applies to scan_fields: content ONLY — scan_fields: all deliberately scans every value in the body regardless of role, so a role exemption does not preserve a message there. In content mode it filters messages[].role, Gemini contents[].role, and Cohere chat_history[].role (matched case-insensitively, since Cohere spells roles USER/CHATBOT/SYSTEM/TOOL); the value 'system' additionally suppresses the top-level system field, the Cohere preamble, and the Gemini system instruction. Provider inputs that carry no role, such as an OpenAI Responses function_call_output item, are never suppressed.

redaction_placeholder.description: Template for redacted text. `{type}` is substituted with the matched pattern name; the RENDERED result must be at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, since every match re-emits it. Redaction output is additionally charged against a per-request growth allowance of four times the request body size (minimum 65536, maximum 67108864 bytes), measured on the JSON-escaped form, with live intermediate buffers bounded by the same allowance; an expanding policy that exhausts it fails the request closed with 413 rather than forwarding a partially redacted body.

max_scan_bytes.description: Maximum body size to scan; enforcing actions reject larger bodies instead of bypassing inspection. Hard ceiling 67108864 (64 MiB). A mathematically integral value is accepted however it is spelled (1024 and 1024.0 alike); a fractional, negative, zero, or out-of-range value is rejected at construction rather than truncated.

AiRateLimiterConfig.description: Plugin: ai_rate_limiter — HTTP-only token-aware rate limiting for LLM APIs. Native gRPC is unsupported (not registered for the Grpc protocol view): protobuf message frames have no supported usage schema, so an attachment there would never charge the budget. Framed gRPC-Web bodies are likewise never classified as JSON AI traffic and are never charged as zero usage. Pre-dispatch prompt estimates walk the request JSON once, counting billable string values, visited object member names (including tool/function schema property names), and JSON scalar literals at serialized width so a present recognized field cannot suppress unknown billed text; exclusions are path/context aware (unsigned numeric output caps only at the exact paths also read for completion-budget reservation — negative/fractional values count fail-closed; multimodal URL/base64/file leaves only inside matching provider content-part family and part type — member names and unrelated textual siblings still count; wrong-family/malformed parts and ordinary strings including data: URLs in instructions/schemas always count). The estimate weights each character by its UTF-8 width (ASCII at chars/4 as before; two-byte scalars such as Cyrillic or Greek at two per token; CJK, kana, Hangul, Indic, and emoji at one token each) and adds media_token_estimate per recognized image/audio/file part; it is a reservation heuristic, not provider tokenizer parity. Only identified AI calls (or POST bodies it cannot inspect) consult the budget: GETs, framed gRPC-Web, and parsed non-LLM JSON are never refused or counted. Every uncompressed POST is classified from its bytes whatever its Content-Type label, and a body a request transform turns into an AI call is re-classified and admitted at the final request-body stage. Budget refusals (429) carry Retry-After. Supports centralized Redis-backed mode for cross-instance token budget coordination. Counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. When Redis is unavailable at terminal reconciliation, actual usage is charged locally within the existing identity cap and the reservation lifecycle is finalized, including zero-token reservations and committed streams. Successful fallback sets instance-scoped ai_ratelimit_locally_accounted=true. Local usage is not replayed to Redis. Process counters ferrum_ai_rate_limit_local_accounting_tokens_total and ferrum_ai_rate_limit_unaccounted_tokens_total expose fallback charges and capacity-limited accounting gaps. Admission remains fail closed; buffered/federated successful responses still receive 503 and committed streams retain their response.

token_limit.description: Required maximum tokens allowed per window. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer. Omission is rejected at construction; there is no default.

window_seconds.description: Sliding window duration in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.

expose_headers.description: Inject x-ai-ratelimit-* headers. For successful buffered metered responses, usage and remaining reflect the bucket after provider-usage reconciliation (not the admission estimate). Limit and window stay coherent with the configured budget. Unmetered charge_estimate keeps the reservation; warn releases and refreshes; reject substitutes a 502 that still carries all four headers, describing the retained reservation, because the rejection-path after_proxy publishes this instance's telemetry onto the final response. Only the centralized enforcement-unavailable 503 carries no rate-limit headers, because no authoritative counter could be consulted. Non-2xx and gateway-rejection releases refresh to the post-release bucket. Federation reconciles before header copy on the rejection-path after_proxy.

provider.description: LLM provider format for token extraction. Accepted values: auto, openai, anthropic, google, cohere, mistral, bedrock, tgi. The constructor trims surrounding Unicode whitespace and lower-cases the value, so `" OpenAI "` is accepted and normalizes to `openai`; the pattern above admits exactly those spellings and no others. Gemini/Vertex payloads use `google`; Hugging Face TGI native `/generate` and `/generate_stream` shapes use `tgi`, whose authoritative counter is `details.generated_tokens` (TGI's OpenAI-compatible surface stays `openai`).

on_unmetered_response.description: Action for successful responses without usage metadata. charge_estimate keeps the pre-request reservation, reject returns a 502 and keeps the reservation (the 502 carries the x-ai-ratelimit-* headers when expose_headers is on), warn logs and releases the reservation. On a STREAMED response the headers are already committed, so reject cannot substitute a 502; it degrades to its fail-closed accounting half (the reservation stays charged) and logs the violation.

consumer_limits.description: Per-consumer token ceilings, keyed by mapped Consumer username (requires limit_by consumer). An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username. A listed consumer keeps its own window; only the ceiling differs. Unlisted consumers, external identities, and IP-keyed fallbacks use token_limit.

model_limits.description: Per-model token budgets, keyed by the request body's exact top-level `model`. A request for a listed model is charged against that model's own window per identity, with this ceiling, and never against the default window; a model budget takes precedence over consumer_limits. Unlisted models use the default budget. While model_limits is set, an AI candidate whose model cannot be read before dispatch is refused (415 with Accept-Encoding identity for a still-compressed body, 400 for an unparseable one). A request transform that changes model re-attributes the reservation to the final model's budget.

media_token_estimate.description: Tokens pre-reserved for each recognized image, audio, or file content part (the parts whose binary payload the prompt estimate excludes). 0 reserves nothing for media; reconciliation still charges the provider-reported usage.

sync_mode.description: Token budget storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized), parsed case-insensitively (`LOCAL`, `Redis`). `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

AiRequestGuardConfig.description: Plugin: ai_request_guard — Validates and constrains AI/LLM API requests. All five numeric limits (`max_tokens_limit`, `default_max_tokens`, `max_choices`, `max_messages`, `max_prompt_characters`) are unsigned 64-bit integers: negative, fractional, and above-`uint64` values are rejected at plugin construction, and `0` is a valid, maximally strict setting rather than "unset" (omit the field to leave the policy unconfigured). Two relationships between sibling values are also enforced at construction and are **not** expressible in JSON Schema 2020-12, so a schema-valid configuration can still be refused by `ferrum-edge validate` and at startup; operator tooling must apply them as supplemental validation: `default_max_tokens` must be `<=` `max_tokens_limit` when both are set, and `temperature_range[0]` must be `<=` `temperature_range[1]`.

max_tokens_limit.description: Maximum allowed output-token request value across OpenAI and provider-native token fields (including both Gemini ProtoJSON spellings, `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens` and `generation_config.max_output_tokens`). Request caps spelled as integral floats, exponents, or quoted integers are evaluated (and clamped) by value; a present cap that is not a non-negative integer (negative, fractional, boolean, unparseable string, ...) is rejected with HTTP 400 in both reject and clamp modes. Unsigned 64-bit integer; `0` is accepted and refuses any request that asks for a positive number of tokens. When `default_max_tokens` is also set it must not exceed this value — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description).

enforce_max_tokens.description: Reject (400 error) or clamp (silently cap) max_tokens

default_max_tokens.description: Unsigned 64-bit integer (`0` accepted), and must be <= max_tokens_limit when that limit is also configured — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description). Inject a default output-token limit if no supported token field is present (a JSON null cap counts as absent and is replaced); top-level-shaped bodies keep a family-correct top-level fallback (max_output_tokens for Responses, else max_tokens) so a spoofed provider marker or stray cross-provider alias cannot uncap them, while unambiguously provider-native bodies receive only their native cap (including TGI parameters.max_new_tokens). With supported_schema bedrock_converse every body receives inferenceConfig.maxTokens (created when absent) and no top-level cap

max_choices.description: Maximum completions one request may ask for, across OpenAI `n` and `best_of`, Cohere `num_generations`, Gemini `generationConfig.candidateCount` (both ProtoJSON spellings), and TGI `parameters.best_of`. `max_tokens_limit` bounds tokens per completion, so the worst case per request is `max_choices` × `max_tokens_limit`. A larger or non-integer value is rejected with HTTP 400. A request that omits the count (or sends `0`) is counted as the provider default of one completion, so `0` refuses every request. Unsigned 64-bit integer.

supported_schema.description: Request schema family accepted when strict_schema is true. bedrock_converse also binds default_max_tokens injection to Amazon Bedrock Converse (inferenceConfig.maxTokens, created when the optional inferenceConfig is absent)

strict_schema.description: Reject JSON request bodies that do not match supported_schema coverage

allowed_models.description: Whitelist of allowed model names (empty = allow all). Matched against the body model and against any model the request path selects (Gemini/Vertex models/{model}:{method}, Bedrock model/{modelId}/converse|invoke, Azure openai/deployments/{deployment}); every model found must be allowed

blocked_models.description: Blacklist of model names (takes precedence over allowed). Matched against the body model and any request-path model (see allowed_models)

require_model_for_model_policy.description: Require a non-empty string model field when allowed_models or blocked_models is configured, unless the request path selects a model (see allowed_models). Setting false only relaxes a genuinely-absent model; a present-but-invalid model (non-string or empty/whitespace) is still rejected with HTTP 400

require_user_field.description: Require a non-empty string user field in the request body (null and blank values are rejected)

max_messages.description: Maximum message entries across messages, Responses input, Gemini contents, and Cohere chat_history arrays. Unsigned 64-bit integer; `0` is accepted and refuses any request that carries a counted message entry.

max_prompt_characters.description: Maximum total prompt characters (Unicode scalar values; `0` is accepted and refuses any request carrying counted text) across prompt/input/system fields, message text, text multimodal parts, Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolResult content and guardContent text, tools (including Bedrock Converse toolConfig.tools[]), tool arguments (including Bedrock Converse messages[].content[].toolUse.input) and Gemini contents[].parts[].functionResponse.response tool results, document/RAG fields (including Anthropic text document source.data and every eligible member value of a Cohere documents[] map, minus its id and _excludes-named members), Google Vertex legacy predict instances[].prompt, and Azure "On Your Data" data_sources[]/dataSources[].parameters.role_information/roleInformation

temperature_range.description: Allowed [min, max] range for top-level temperature plus Gemini generationConfig.temperature / generation_config.temperature and Bedrock inferenceConfig.temperature; conflicting aliases are rejected. Both bounds must be finite and temperature_range[0] must be <= temperature_range[1] — a construction-time relationship JSON Schema cannot express (see the component description)

block_system_prompts.description: Reject system/developer prompt fields and roles, including Responses instructions, provider-native top-level system fields, and Azure "On Your Data" data_sources[]/dataSources[].parameters.role_information/roleInformation (a de-facto system instruction the backend applies)

system_prompt_aliases.description: Additional message roles or top-level fields treated as system prompts when block_system_prompts is true

required_metadata_fields.description: Required top-level fields in the request body; each must be present, not null, and not a blank string

fail_on_uninspectable_body.description: Reject in-scope POST requests whose body cannot be inspected because the buffered body is missing, empty, non-UTF-8, malformed JSON, ambiguous JSON (duplicate object member names, including escaped spellings, or a document over the duplicate-scan budgets), or still compressed after request transforms (no compression/decompress_request decoded it). Set false only for compatibility when the backend must handle such uninspectable bodies itself.

AiResponseGuardConfig.description: Plugin: ai_response_guard — validation and filtering for AI/LLM API responses. Enforcing actions fail closed when a governed buffered response is oversized or uninspectable. Native gRPC protobuf responses are inspected only for methods enrolled in the descriptor-based grpc block; unenrolled methods are never decoded and never buffered. With grpc, JSON-only rules must be inactive: require_json must be omitted or false, and required_fields must be omitted or empty.

action.description: Action when a violation is detected in the response body. Content rules govern successful (2xx) responses; max_scan_bytes applies to every buffered status, and a redact transform may still rewrite a buffered non-2xx body it can parse. warn records ai_response_guard_* metadata and never adds a response header. Buffered SSE is parsed and redacted by complete event; content spanning events that cannot be safely rewritten is rejected. Live SSE requests are never re-buffered by this plugin. A governed JSON body, SSE data payload, or serialized tool-arguments document with duplicate object members is uninspectable (reject/redact answer 502; warn records ambiguous_json_document) whenever a detection, required_fields, or max_completion_length rule is active.

pii_patterns.description: Built-in PII pattern names to scan for (e.g., ssn, credit_card, email, phone_us, api_key, aws_key, ip_address, iban). Each name at most once. credit_card covers Visa, Mastercard (including the 2221-2720 2-series), Discover, UnionPay, JCB, American Express (contiguous, 4-6-5, or 4-4-4-3), and Diners Club numbers and is confirmed with a Luhn checksum; api_key covers multi-segment sk-proj-/sk-ant-api03- style keys plus GitHub, Google, and Slack token formats; ip_address covers IPv4 (octets 0-255) and IPv6 (full, or ::-compressed, inner or trailing, with at least three groups); iban accepts compact or space-grouped IBANs with a registry country code.

name.description: Pattern identifier used in redaction placeholders and violation reports (at most 128 characters)

regex.description: Regular expression pattern to match. Must not match the empty string; a zero-width rule is rejected at construction.

custom_pii_patterns.description: Custom PII {name, regex} patterns for domain-specific detection. At most 256 entries. A regex that matches the empty string is rejected at construction, and a zero-width match produced at runtime (for example by a bare word-boundary assertion) makes redaction fail closed.

blocked_phrases.description: Exact phrases to block in response content (case-insensitive). Literal values are never exposed in placeholders, metadata, logs, or reject bodies; bounded positional rule IDs are used instead. At most 1024 entries.

name.description: Pattern identifier for violation reports (at most 128 characters)

regex.description: Regular expression pattern to match. Must not match the empty string; a zero-width rule is rejected at construction.

blocked_patterns.description: Custom {name, regex} patterns for blocking arbitrary content in responses. At most 256 entries; the empty-match rule is the same as custom_pii_patterns.

scan_fields.description: Which response fields to scan: 'content' scans supported completion and tool/function-call fields (OpenAI chat/Responses, Anthropic content[], Gemini candidates[].content.parts[], Bedrock Converse output.message.content[], Cohere v1 text and chat_history[].message, and Hugging Face TGI's top-level array of generated_text objects), 'all' scans the entire response body

redaction_placeholder.description: Template for redacted text. {type} is replaced with the pattern name; the RENDERED result must be at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, since every match re-emits it. Structured (JSON, SSE, gRPC) redaction output is additionally charged against a per-response growth allowance of four times the response body size (minimum 65536, maximum 67108864 bytes), never more than the room the response's retained-body ceiling leaves above the body.
