Growth is measured on the JSON-escaped form, and live intermediate buffers are bounded by the same allowance, so a rewrite can be refused even when its final net growth would fit; an expanding policy that exhausts it fails closed rather than delivering a partially redacted body.

max_scan_bytes.description: Maximum governed buffered response size, including the aggregate decoded/decompressed native-gRPC payload across frames. Hard ceiling 67108864 (64 MiB). Reject/redact and structural rules fail closed above this limit; warn-only content rules record a bounded warning and pass through.

require_json.description: Reject responses that are not valid JSON

required_fields.description: JSON field names that must be present in the response body

max_completion_length.description: Maximum allowed length of completion content, measured in characters (Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes). 0 = no limit

allowlist.description: Exceptions for PII findings (pii_patterns and custom_pii_patterns only; blocked_phrases and blocked_patterns are never excused). Compared against the complete matched text, identically for detection, redaction (an allowed match is left verbatim), and residual re-scans.

items.description: Exact matched text that is not a finding. The runtime bound is 1024 UTF-8 bytes, so a multi-byte value within 1024 characters can still be refused.

values.description: Exact values never reported as PII, e.g. a public support address. At most 1024 entries.

items.description: Regular expression anchored by the runtime as ^(?:pattern)$, so it must match the entire matched text. Must compile on its own.

patterns.description: Whole-match regexes for values never reported as PII, e.g. an order-number family. At most 256 entries.

grpc.description: Native-gRPC response inspection contract. Present means the plugin also applies to native gRPC, but only for the enrolled methods: every other gRPC method is left undecoded, uninspected, and unbuffered. Enrolled methods fail closed for reject/redact actions when the descriptor is unavailable, the payload does not decode as the configured type, the message carries fields outside the descriptor, the framing is malformed or truncated, the message encoding is not gzip/identity, or a bound is exceeded. Requires at least one detection pattern, blocked phrase, or positive max_completion_length. require_json must be omitted or false, and required_fields must be omitted or empty. Unchanged responses preserve trailers; a redaction rewrite retains reserved gRPC terminal metadata and retires application trailers and their merged-header copies under the shared body-rewrite policy.

descriptor_path.description: Node-local path to a compiled protobuf FileDescriptorSet. Validated shape-only at Admin/CP admission and against the real descriptor by mode-aware file-dependency validation. A readable but invalid descriptor rejects the candidate configuration; an absent or unreadable descriptor retains enrollment and fails closed for enforcing actions at request time.

methods.description: Map of "/package.Service/Method" to that method's response inspection contract. Only these methods are inspected. Leading/trailing whitespace and one optional leading slash are normalized by the runtime; every dotted service segment and the method identifier must be a protobuf/gRPC identifier. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime.

text_fields.description: Dotted field paths restricting what is scanned and rewritten. Each path has 1 to 32 segments, each non-empty after trimming whitespace. Exact duplicates are rejected by the schema; duplicates after segment trimming are rejected at runtime. Descriptor resolution also runs at runtime: paths must end at a string field, may traverse repeated messages, and may not traverse map fields. Omit to cover every string field and known extension value recursively.

max_message_bytes.description: Per-message ceiling, applied to the declared frame length and enforced while inflating a gzip-compressed frame; inflation stops at the tighter of this ceiling and the remaining max_scan_bytes budget. Aggregate decoded payload across frames is additionally capped by max_scan_bytes. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 67108864 (64 MiB), equal to the max_scan_bytes ceiling — a larger per-message value could never produce an inspection.

max_messages.description: Maximum number of length-prefixed frames one buffered gRPC response may carry. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 1024 frames: the decoded-byte scan budget bounds decoded payload, not frame count, so legal zero-length frames would otherwise let an operator-configured value drive an effectively unbounded frame vector.

AiSemanticCacheConfig.description: Plugin: ai_semantic_cache — Caches LLM responses keyed by family-correct prompts across Ferrum's recognized request families (OpenAI Chat messages, Anthropic messages/system, OpenAI Responses input/instructions, Gemini/Vertex contents/systemInstruction, Cohere chat_history/message, legacy prompt, TGI inputs, and Titan inputText). Unknown or ambiguous JSON shapes bypass caching. Exact keys preserve LLM-significant prompt case and whitespace while applying structurally safe canonicalization; optional semantic similarity uses a configured embedding provider and a local HNSW vector index. Both exact and semantic scope keys bind the shared canonical effective-destination partition (proxy namespace and ID, listen path, upstream or direct host/port/scheme, route authority, rewritten path), a mandatory caller-authorization partition, and a length-framed backend-visible request-context digest (original client authority and Host, method, path, the effective outbound query, and every non-credential request header; credential header values are digested, never embedded). Only transport/hop-by-hop framing fields Ferrum provably regenerates for the backend hop are excluded from that binding (Host/authority is bound separately); tracing and correlation headers such as traceparent, tracestate, b3, X-B3-*, X-Request-Id and X-Correlation-Id ARE bound, because a client-supplied value can be preserved and reaches the origin. The one exception is a correlation_id header whose live value private request provenance records as generated by the gateway on this request (the rule response_caching applies), plus the x-ratelimit-* values the owning rate_limiting instance staged; both change on every request. A conservative miss is preferred over an unbound dimension. Lookup runs at priority 4057 in the final-request-body hook, not before_proxy, so the partition and the prompt digest describe the fully transformed request the provider would receive; it runs after ai_prompt_compressor (4055) enforces its staged marker-sanitization rejection and before ai_federation (4060) performs provider I/O, while every before_proxy admission guardrail still precedes any hit. Supports local DashMap and Redis exact-response storage. Redis mode requires redis_integrity_key and treats Redis as an untrusted, authenticated trust boundary. Quarantine DEL failures are counted with rate-limited warnings (no keys/payloads/credentials) and suppressed by a bounded per-instance local fingerprint+TTL marker (fingerprints only after admission failure; constant-work capacity eviction) so the same poisoned remote value cannot amplify download/parse/delete on every request; suppression never converts a miss into a hit. Multiple instances on one proxy namespace request staging metadata under ai_semantic_cache.<instance_id>.* and keep embedding/scope vectors in per-instance RequestContext maps so differing key policies and semantic/non-semantic combinations remain independent across priority order and reload generations. Unknown root, semantic-policy, and Redis sync keys are rejected at admission with path-qualified diagnostics (registration policy KeepLastKnownGood). There are no intentionally open maps. All numeric retention/time bounds must be positive. The constructor additionally enforces max_entry_size_bytes <= max_total_size_bytes (including omitted defaults), the 32 UTF-8 byte redis_integrity_key minimum, platform-sized integer limits, URL parsing, and the deployment backend egress policy. These residual checks are not fully expressible in this schema. Provider-managed Responses conversations, Gemini retained contexts, and Cohere conversation_id requests bypass replay; other unmodeled root context is canonically bound to exact and semantic identities. Request bodies with duplicate JSON members, a request Cache-Control no-store/no-cache, or an unprovable response-presentation policy also bypass. Instruction state (system, developer, instructions, systemInstruction, preamble, Cohere SYSTEM history) is bound byte-exactly in semantic scopes. Exact keys and semantic scopes bind the request's response-policy provenance (RTDS gate content and static presentation-policy digest). Responses with Cache-Control no-store/private or Set-Cookie are not stored; provider-backed ai_federation answers are. Cache hits preserve finalized application bodies while current response enforcement, live header rules, and negotiated compression still run.

ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live for cached entries in seconds

max_entries.description: Maximum number of cached entries (local mode). In semantic mode, HNSW snapshot memory scales with this count and is charged against max_total_size_bytes.

max_entry_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of a single cached response body in bytes (1 MiB). Hard maximum 16 MiB; larger values are rejected at admission so Redis transfer caps cannot saturate platform integers.

max_total_size_bytes.description: Maximum retained local cache memory in bytes (100 MiB, local mode; hard maximum 1 GiB). Includes response bodies, cached headers, semantic scope keys, retained embedding vectors, published HNSW snapshot generations, and in-flight rebuild workspace reservations. Concurrent stores and rebuilds use lock-free byte leases so overlapping old/candidate generations are charged at peak and failed/superseded rebuilds release promptly. A store or rebuild that cannot reserve is skipped.

include_model_in_key.description: Include the model name in the cache key (different models get separate cache entries)

include_params_in_key.description: Include request parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens) in the cache key. Default `true` — different sampling params produce different responses and must not collide. Set `false` only when cross-parameter cache reuse is intentional.

scope_by_consumer.description: Additionally include the authenticated consumer's display identity in the cache key. Caller isolation no longer depends on this flag — every exact and semantic key binds a mandatory caller-authorization partition (authentication mechanism, resolved identity/consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, and SHA-256 digests of every credential header presented), so two credentials resolving to one display subject with different scopes can never share a retained completion. Setting `false` no longer lets distinct callers share entries.

anonymous_caller_scope.description: How anonymous callers (no gateway identity, no credential header, no peer SPIFFE identity) are partitioned. caller_address (default) binds the gateway-resolved canonical peer address, which the origin observes through Ferrum's regenerated X-Forwarded-For; a request whose canonical address cannot be parsed is refused rather than keyed incompletely. shared is an explicit operator attestation that the origin does not vary its result by caller address on this route — only set it when that is known-safe, because it re-opens cross-caller replay for address-sensitive origins. It applies to anonymous callers only: an authenticated caller always binds its canonical peer address, because the backend receives Ferrum's regenerated forwarding identity for that caller too and may vary policy or content by it.

cache_multimodal.description: Multimodal request caching mode for non-text content parts. `reject` bypasses cache lookup/store, `exact_only` uses hashed fingerprints for exact matches and disables semantic hits, and `include_fingerprints` also includes those fingerprints in semantic scope keys. The parser and schema accept surrounding whitespace, ASCII case variants, and the listed underscore/hyphen aliases.

semantic_similarity_enabled.description: Enable embedding-based semantic lookup after exact Redis/local misses. Exact matching remains active when this is disabled or enabled.

semantic_embedding_provider.description: Embedding provider request/response format. Values are trimmed and ASCII case-insensitive. Aliases include openai_compatible/openai-compatible, azure/azure-openai, voyageai/voyage_ai/anthropic/claude, google/gemini/google-gemini, vertex/vertex_ai/vertex-ai/google-vertex, amazon_titan/amazon-titan/bedrock-titan, and cohere_bedrock/cohere-bedrock/bedrock-cohere; anthropic and claude are aliases for Voyage-compatible embeddings because Claude does not expose a native embedding model.

semantic_embedding_endpoint.description: Nonblank embedding endpoint. Required and validated as an HTTP(S) URL when semantic_similarity_enabled is true; disabled semantic mode only checks that the supplied string is nonblank. A cleartext http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] (other spellings and the name localhost do not qualify) unless semantic_embedding_allow_plaintext is true. Must not include URL userinfo; use semantic_embedding_api_key for credentials. Query parameters and path tokens required by signed or credential-bearing endpoints are preserved on the outbound request but stripped from logs and error diagnostics (canonical redacted form uses scheme/host/port plus /...). OpenAI-compatible endpoints use input/model JSON; other providers send native embedding JSON.

semantic_embedding_model.description: Model name sent in the embedding request body. Omit for local endpoints that do not require a model field.

semantic_embedding_input_type.description: Provider-specific input or task type, such as query/document for Voyage, search_query/search_document for Cohere, SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY for Gemini, or Vertex task_type.

semantic_embedding_output_dimension.description: Provider-specific reduced embedding dimension from 1 to 16384 when supported. Mistral uses output_dimension; OpenAI and Azure OpenAI use dimensions.

semantic_embedding_api_key.description: Nonblank API key; the final header value is validated at admission and retained as sensitive. Invalid header characters in the key or scheme are rejected without echoing values. Sent in semantic_embedding_auth_header with semantic_embedding_auth_scheme when configured.

semantic_embedding_auth_header.description: HTTP header used for semantic_embedding_api_key. Defaults to Authorization, except Azure OpenAI uses api-key and Google Gemini uses x-goog-api-key. Must not be the gateway-owned X-Ferrum-Hops proxy hop count (any case, `_` or `-`), which the embedding call carries itself.

semantic_embedding_allow_plaintext.description: Admit a cleartext http:// semantic_embedding_endpoint whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The embedding API key then crosses the network in clear.

semantic_embedding_auth_scheme.description: Prefix for the API key header value. Defaults to Bearer, except Azure OpenAI and Google Gemini send the raw key. Set to an empty string to send the raw key.

semantic_similarity_threshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic cache hit.

semantic_vector_max_candidates.description: Number of nearest HNSW candidates to inspect during semantic lookup (`ef_search` / `ef_construction`). Hard maximum 1024; larger values are rejected at admission so semantic search cannot be configured into an unbounded graph walk.

semantic_embedding_timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout for embedding calls in milliseconds. Embedding failures fall back to a normal exact-cache miss.

sync_mode.description: Storage backend: local or redis, ASCII case-insensitive without whitespace trimming. Redis requires redis_url and redis_integrity_key.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (required when sync_mode is redis). Must not carry a URL fragment. The database path selects an integer from 0 to 2147483647, without a sign, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. URL port validity and server database availability remain constructor/server checks. TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. URL-embedded userinfo is accepted but never disclosed: connection/health-check logs and non-admin/audit projections keep only the scheme, host, port, and database, replace the userinfo, and replace query/fragment data with `[REDACTED_QUERY]` and `[REDACTED_FRAGMENT]` markers. Full admin reads stay raw.

redis_key_prefix.description: Redis key namespace prefix. When omitted, the runtime derives `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:ai_cache` (for example `ferrum:ai_cache` when the namespace is `ferrum`). No static OpenAPI default is advertised because the value depends on the gateway namespace.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Interval for background health check pings when Redis is unavailable

redis_integrity_key.description: Narrowly scoped HMAC-SHA256 secret that authenticates Redis cache envelopes. Required when sync_mode is redis (fail closed if omitted). Minimum 32 UTF-8 bytes, checked by the constructor (JSON Schema string length counts characters). Bound to the full status/header/body envelope and the Redis namespace/key context. Compared in constant time; never logged, and replaced by [REDACTED] in admin audit diffs and in viewer/operator plugin-config reads (full admin reads stay raw so rotation by read-modify-write works). Rolling the key quarantines prior entries — there is no legacy unauthenticated read path during build-out.

AiSemanticFirewallActivePolicy.description: At least one ai_semantic_firewall rule source is active: any built-in pack (omitting builtins enables all seven), an allow topic, a deny topic, or a custom rule. An enabled instance with no active rule source is rejected by the constructor.

AiSemanticFirewallActiveRequestPolicy.description: At least one REQUEST-direction ai_semantic_firewall rule is active: any built-in pack except the response-only response_leakage (omitting builtins enables all of them), an allow topic (request-side only), a deny topic (bidirectional), or a custom rule whose direction is not response.

AiSemanticFirewallActiveResponsePolicy.description: At least one RESPONSE-direction ai_semantic_firewall rule is active: the bidirectional built-ins system_prompt_exfiltration / tool_abuse, the response-direction built-in response_leakage (omitting builtins enables all three), a deny topic (bidirectional), or a custom rule whose direction is not request. Allow topics are request-side only and never satisfy this.

oneOf.description: Boolean shorthand. true enables the pack with Ferrum defaults; false disables it.

enabled.description: Enable or disable this built-in pack.

examples_mode.description: Append customer examples to Ferrum defaults or replace the semantic example set for this pack. replace requires examples.

examples.description: Customer semantic examples for this built-in pack (at most 64, each at most 2048 characters). Each entry must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Required when examples_mode is replace.

oneOf.description: Object form for tuning a built-in AI semantic firewall pack. The pack keeps its built-in rule id, pack metadata, and compiled-in matching behavior either way.

AiSemanticFirewallBuiltinPackConfig.description: Built-in pack toggle or tuning object.

AiSemanticFirewallConfig.description: Plugin: ai_semantic_firewall — Semantic LLM guardrails for prompt injection, jailbreaks, system/developer prompt exfiltration, data exfiltration intent, indirect prompt injection, tool abuse, business-topic allow/deny policy, response leakage, dry-run rollout, and audit metadata. An enabled instance must carry a provider, at least one active rule source, and rules that apply to the enabled inspection directions; a disabled instance (enabled: false) is exempt from those cross-field requirements but every block it DOES carry is still validated, matching the constructor. Three relationships standard JSON Schema cannot express and ferrum-edge validate still rejects with a field-specific error: streaming.overlap_bytes must be strictly less than streaming.max_window_bytes; streaming.overlap_tokens must be strictly less than streaming.max_window_tokens; and every allow_topics/deny_topics/custom_rules id must be unique across those three lists AND against the ids of the ACTIVE built-in packs (prompt_injection, jailbreak, system_prompt_exfiltration, data_exfiltration, indirect_prompt_injection, tool_abuse, response_leakage). A rule id is an operator-facing label only — naming a custom or deny-topic rule after a disabled built-in pack does not give it that built-in's matching behavior. A fourth constructor-only bound: the ACTIVE rule material (built-in packs, allow_topics, deny_topics, custom_rules) may carry at most 512 examples in total, because every example is embedded when the rule index is built.

mode.description: Dry-run mode never rejects or cuts traffic and emits would_action metadata. This covers every disposition on both the buffered and the windowed streaming paths: a matched rule, an uninspectable body/window, an unmapped governed provider stream, an exhausted streaming.max_inspections budget, a provider error under on_error=reject, and an expired streaming.max_hold_ms hold (including on_hold_timeout=cut) are all recorded and released.

on_error.description: Behavior when embedding/evaluation fails. The default is conditional and is NOT advertised as a static schema default on purpose: when omitted, enforce mode defaults to reject (required semantic evaluation fails closed) while dry_run defaults to warn (provider outages are audited as would_warn, not would_reject). Tooling that materializes OpenAPI defaults must therefore leave this field unset to inherit the mode-appropriate default; sending an explicit reject for a dry_run config would skew rollout/audit telemetry.

default_action.description: Default action for built-in semantic rules.

fail_on_uninspectable_body.description: When true, missing, empty, malformed, encoded, oversized (above the 10 MiB inspection ceiling), governed LLM JSON with no extractable content, or a body yielding more than 1024 segments is handled through on_error (rejecting by default in enforce mode). In enforce mode with on_error=reject this also caps buffered governed request bodies at 10 MiB, refused at collection. Set false only as an explicit compatibility opt-out on a generic shared JSON proxy that intentionally forwards such bodies uninspected.

streaming_response.description: Behavior for stream:true requests when response-side inspection is active. The default is conditional and is NOT advertised as a static schema default on purpose: when omitted, enforce mode with response-side rules active defaults to reject (clients cannot bypass response inspection by streaming) while dry_run or request-only configurations default to skip. Tooling that materializes OpenAPI defaults must leave this field unset to inherit the correct default — sending an explicit reject for a dry_run/request-only config would flip request-body buffering on (requires_request_body_before_before_proxy) and buffer every JSON POST just to read the stream flag, unlike the omitted-field behavior. skip is an explicit fail-open opt-out that allows the streamed response uninspected and records ai_semantic_firewall.response_inspection_skipped when the request body is available; reject fails closed and rejects the request so a client cannot disable response inspection by streaming — clients retry with stream:false to receive an inspectable buffered response; buffer forces the streamed response onto the buffered path, reassembles its SSE deltas into coherent text, and runs the full response engine before anything reaches the client (most accurate, highest time-to-first-byte; an oversized stream fails closed via FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES); inspect inspects the stream progressively in windows (reassemble to a sentence/paragraph or byte-cap boundary, inspect, release if clean) and cuts the stream mid-flight on a violation with a terminal SSE error event — preserves streaming UX (low time-to-first-byte) at the cost of windowed granularity plus a per-window inspection. inspect records ai_semantic_firewall.response_inspection=streaming_windowed. Production enforcement should use reject, buffer, or inspect with on_error=reject. A stream is DECLARED by a body stream:true or by a streaming request target (Gemini/Vertex :streamGenerateContent, Bedrock converse-stream / invoke-with-response-stream). A governed AI request that did not declare one but receives a text/event-stream response anyway (a backend that streams by default) is still governed: buffer and reject keep it buffered and inspect it whole, inspect windows it; an NDJSON stream (Ollama application/x-ndjson) is buffered and reassembled under every non-skip policy, and a Bedrock application/vnd.amazon.eventstream body fails closed through on_error.

streaming.description: Windowed-inspection tuning. Only valid when streaming_response is inspect. window=tokens requires an explicit tokenizer, and tokenizer / max_window_tokens / overlap_tokens are rejected for every other window kind. on_hold_timeout requires max_hold_ms, and its cut value is rejected with enforcement=detect. Two ordering relationships are not expressible here and are enforced by the constructor: overlap_bytes < max_window_bytes and overlap_tokens < max_window_tokens.

window.description: Window boundary detector. `tokens` requires an explicit `streaming.tokenizer` (`chars4`, `whitespace`, or `unicode_words`) plus optional `max_window_tokens` / `overlap_tokens`; these are bounded deterministic estimators, not provider BPE models. Soft token budgets still honor `max_window_bytes` as the hard memory/CPU cap.

tokenizer.description: Required when window=tokens. Explicit bounded tokenizer selection — `chars4` (~4 Unicode scalars per token, matching ai_rate_limiter / ai_prompt_compressor), `whitespace` (Unicode whitespace-delimited runs), or `unicode_words` (alphanumeric runs; each non-whitespace non-alphanumeric scalar is its own token, and CJK ideographs, kana, and Hangul syllables are one token per character rather than a joined run). Rejected when window is not tokens.

max_window_bytes.description: Hard aggregate cap for the current window's input and retained raw/frame/reassembled state. Coalesced chunks are expanded event-by-event: only one complete event's bytes are taken at a time and a ready window is inspected and released before more events are absorbed, so transport batching never changes a clean completion's disposition. Only an event that cannot fit with nothing else retained is uninspectable (fails closed under on_error=reject, forwarded under warn/allow). The start of an event kept after a fail-open hold timeout forwarded it (see on_hold_timeout) counts toward the cap together with the rest of that event; when the two do not fit together, the rest of that event is uninspectable.

overlap_bytes.description: Bytes of already-cleared text re-inspected with the next window so a violation phrase split across a boundary is still caught. Prose and tool-call tails split this aggregate budget with a reserved tool-state share. Must be less than max_window_bytes and is included within that aggregate retained-state cap. For window=tokens this remains the hard memory ceiling on retained overlap while overlap_tokens selects the prose token budget.

max_window_tokens.description: Only valid when window=tokens; NO static default is advertised because materializing one on any other window kind turns a valid configuration into one the gateway rejects. Soft window size in complete tokens under the selected tokenizer. Omit to inherit 256. Values above 65536 or 0 are rejected. The hard max_window_bytes cap still forces a window (preferring a complete-token cut) when retained state fills first.

overlap_tokens.description: Only valid when window=tokens; NO static default is advertised because the effective default is CONDITIONAL — min(32, max_window_tokens-1) — so materializing a fixed 32 invalidates every small token window. Complete tokens of already-cleared prose re-inspected with the next window; retained overlap tokens count against the next window's max_window_tokens, so a window closes once retained + new tokens reach the budget (at least one new token is always required). Must be strictly less than max_window_tokens. Still subject to the overlap_bytes memory ceiling.

max_inspections.description: Safety cap on provider inspections per response (at most 10000). Once reached, further inspectable windows honor on_error (reject cuts/fail-closed; warn/allow forward best-effort).

on_violation.description: Whether a cut emits an OpenAI-compatible terminal SSE error event or ends the stream silently. Applies to enforcement=block only (detect never cuts).

max_hold_ms.description: Absolute deadline, in milliseconds, on how long response content may be held awaiting a semantic verdict. Independent of max_window_bytes, provider.request_timeout_ms, and any transport timeout: the budget covers the time the bytes have already been held plus the semantic round-trip (including queueing for a detect-mode admission permit). The clock is anchored when un-released content first enters the hold and is never refreshed by further chunks or by a partial release that leaves older bytes held, so a drip-feeding backend cannot extend it. It clears only when the current hold is fully released, so the next hold receives a fresh budget. On expiry the in-flight evaluation is cancelled and streaming.on_hold_timeout decides. Omit the field to leave the hold unbounded (the historic behavior); 0 and values above 300000 are rejected.

on_hold_timeout.description: The effective default is on_error, but NO static schema default is advertised: the field is rejected outright unless streaming.max_hold_ms is also set, so tooling that materializes defaults must leave it unset. Policy when streaming.max_hold_ms expires before a verdict. on_error inherits the plugin's on_error policy (reject fails closed by cutting, warn/allow fail open by forwarding every byte that caused the hold uninspected — complete events and any un-terminated partial SSE event — then, when that partial event already carries data, passing its remainder through until the next event boundary, while a partial event with no data yet is kept to inspect the rest of that event with), matching how a provider error or an exhausted inspection budget is handled. cut always fails closed (discards all held/partial bytes) in mode=enforce and degrades to forward in mode=dry_run, which never cuts; forward always fails open. Requires streaming.max_hold_ms to be set. cut is rejected with enforcement=detect, whose bytes were already forwarded before the evaluation began — an expired detect hold can only abandon the evaluation and release its admission permit. A cut is client-indistinguishable from a policy cut (same terminal error event), and every expiry folds into the fixed-cardinality ai_semantic_firewall.stream_hold_timeouts count (saturating-summed across active instances) and ai_semantic_firewall.stream_hold_timeout_action (most restrictive of cut > forward > detect_abandoned) transaction metadata; a zero-expiry instance neither synthesizes nor erases those keys.

enforcement.description: block holds each window until it passes inspection, then releases it (or cuts the stream on a violation) — no un-inspected bytes reach the client, at the cost of windowing latency. detect is release-then-detect — bytes stream through immediately and a violation is only logged (to the structured log, never the client or metrics), never cut; use it to observe what would be blocked without affecting traffic.

type.description: OpenAI-compatible embeddings provider. Exact spelling only — no aliases and no surrounding whitespace.

endpoint.description: Embeddings endpoint URL, with no whitespace or control characters anywhere. Literal IP hosts are checked against FERRUM_BACKEND_ALLOW_IPS; hostname resolution is checked by the shared plugin HTTP client at request time. A cleartext http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] (other spellings and the name localhost do not qualify) unless provider.allow_plaintext is true.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit a cleartext http:// endpoint whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The provider API key then crosses the network in clear. Omit or null means false.

model.description: Embedding model sent in the request body.

api_key_env.description: Name of the `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable holding the provider API key (`<NAME>` uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`; surrounding whitespace is trimmed and an empty value means unset). Any other process environment variable, including every other `FERRUM_*` setting, is refused at admission with a 400. The variable must exist after Ferrum startup secret resolution (`FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>_FILE` / `_VAULT` / `_AWS` / `_AZURE` / `_GCP` work) and is sent in provider.auth_header (default Authorization) prefixed by provider.auth_scheme (default Bearer); an unset or empty value fails the first embedding call.

auth_header.description: Header the provider credential is sent in. Omit for Authorization. Azure OpenAI deployments use api-key (with auth_scheme set to the empty string). An HTTP token of at most 64 characters, taken verbatim; Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, and X-Ferrum-Hops (any casing) are refused. Requires api_key_env.

auth_scheme.description: Scheme prefixed to the credential with one space. Omit for Bearer; the empty string sends the raw key (Azure OpenAI api-key). An HTTP token of at most 32 characters. Requires api_key_env.

request_timeout_ms.description: Per-request embedding provider timeout in milliseconds (at most 60000). Also bounds how long a request waits for a provider.max_concurrent_requests admission permit before following on_error.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Outbound embedding calls this plugin instance may have in flight at once. A governed request that cannot obtain a slot within provider.request_timeout_ms follows on_error instead of queueing, so a stalled provider cannot pin an unbounded number of buffered requests.

provider.description: Required when the plugin has active rules.

builtins.description: Built-in rule packs. When omitted, all built-ins are enabled; when provided, omitted packs are disabled. Object form can append or replace semantic examples per pack while keeping the built-in rule ID and pack metadata.

request_json_paths.description: Supported simple request extraction paths. When configured, this list replaces the defaults.

response_json_paths.description: Supported simple response extraction paths. When configured, this list replaces the defaults.

id.description: Rule identifier. Must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Ids must be unique across allow_topics, deny_topics, custom_rules, and the ACTIVE built-in pack names.
Rule identifier. Must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Ids must be unique across allow_topics, deny_topics, custom_rules, and the ACTIVE built-in pack names.

action.description: Omit to INHERIT the plugin's default_action (reject unless default_action is warn); no static default is advertised because materializing reject would turn an inherited warn into a rejection. allow is not accepted here — use allow_topics for allowlist semantics.

deny_topics.description: Customer-defined request/response semantic deny topics. Deny topics are bidirectional and apply to both inspection directions.

id.description: Rule identifier. Must contain a non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Ids must be unique across allow_topics, deny_topics, custom_rules, and the ACTIVE built-in pack names.

action.description: Custom rules can warn or reject; use allow_topics for allowlist semantics. Omit to INHERIT the plugin's default_action (reject unless default_action is warn); no static default is advertised because materializing reject would turn an inherited warn into a rejection.

snippet_hash_salt.description: Optional salt mixed into snippet_hash digests so short/low-entropy matched segments written to logs cannot be reversed by brute force/rainbow tables. Keep consistent across a fleet for correlation and out of the same logs. Unsalted (default) is reversible for short segments.

privacy.description: Raw prompt/response text is not written by default; hashes are for correlation only.

expose_rule_id_to_client.description: Include matched rule IDs in reject responses.

AiSemanticFirewallEnabledBuiltinPack.description: Matches a builtins.<pack> value that leaves the pack ACTIVE: the boolean shorthand true, or the object form without enabled: false. Used only by the ai_semantic_firewall active-policy conditionals.

AiStreamRouterConfig.description: Plugin: ai_stream_router — streaming counterpart to ai_federation. Claims ONLY OpenAI Chat Completions requests with `stream: true` and preserves true end-to-end SSE streaming. Runs at priority 2984 (before ai_semantic_cache at 4057, before ai_federation at 4060). Instead of an internal terminate-and-respond HTTP call, it rewrites the routing decision via RequestContext.route_override_* so the normal proxy dispatch streams the provider response straight back to the client. Strips every canonical client credential header (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, X-API-Key, API-Key, APIKey, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-Access-Token, X-Auth-Token, X-Amz-Security-Token, X-Forwarded-Authorization — case-insensitive and with `_` treated as `-`), the route's own configured authentication header locations, and provider-protocol headers, then injects the provider's credential; gateway-asserted x-consumer-* identity headers are also suppressed toward the provider. openai/openai_compatible providers pass through unchanged except optional stream_options.include_usage injection; anthropic requests are translated to the Anthropic Messages API streaming request and Anthropic SSE events are normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE. google_gemini requests are translated to the Gemini/streamGenerateContent body shape and provider SSE/JSON streams are normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE (authentication is the x-goog-api-key header only; Vertex AI OAuth2 is not supported). OpenAI request parameters are mapped exactly or refused with an OpenAI-shaped 400, never silently dropped: response_format (Gemini responseMimeType/responseJsonSchema; refused for Anthropic), n (Gemini candidateCount; n > 1 refused for Anthropic), presence_penalty/frequency_penalty/seed (Gemini; non-zero/any refused for Anthropic), parallel_tool_calls false (Anthropic disable_parallel_tool_use; refused for Gemini with callable tools), and logit_bias/logprobs/top_logprobs (refused for both). Anthropic extended thinking (thinking.type enabled or adaptive) with callable tools or a tool-result continuation is refused because signed thinking blocks cannot round-trip through the OpenAI representation. A strict Gemini json_schema must use only keywords Gemini enforces or it is refused. Gemini thought signatures round-trip through tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature. Base64 data-URL image_url parts (image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp) in user messages translate to native image parts; remote image URLs are refused. A claimed normalizing 2xx response whose Content-Type is not a supported stream media type fails closed for both translated providers. When it claims a request it sets ctx.metadata ai_stream_router_claimed=true so ai_federation defers. Fails closed by default when a streaming request lacks a top-level string `model` or matches no provider. Non-streaming requests Continue to ai_federation. Provider fallback is NOT implemented and a `fallback` config block is REJECTED at admission (issue #3328): the plugin commits one provider route, credential set, backend TLS resolution, and translated request body before dispatch and never switches providers, pre- or post-first-byte, so a stored fallback policy could only be silently inert. No ai_stream_router.fallback_attempts metadata is emitted. Configuration is strict: unknown root and provider fields are rejected with path-qualified diagnostics (and spelling suggestions when useful), so typos such as `enabeld` cannot silently leave the router enabled. The same constructor contract admits file validate/startup, Admin/database writes, and CP/DP snapshot or reload publication; invalid enabled configs reject publication and retain the last-known-good instance under the plugin's FailClosed policy. NOTE: this plugin is HTTP-only and routes over the normal dispatch path, but the claim commits its own egress policy rather than inheriting the proxy's: an https provider endpoint is verified against the built-in public trust roots only — never the global FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH, never disabled by FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY, and never presenting the global backend client certificate — unless that provider sets inherit_backend_tls: true, and any dns_override inherited from the matched proxy is explicitly revoked so the provider host resolves through provider DNS.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false the plugin never claims requests.

fail_on_missing_model.description: Reject a streaming request that lacks a top-level string `model`. Set to false to pass such requests through (to ai_federation / normal backend).

fail_on_no_matching_provider.description: Reject a streaming request whose `model` matches no configured provider. Set to false to pass such requests through.

inject_usage_options.description: For openai/openai_compatible/azure_openai providers, inject stream_options.include_usage=true so the provider emits a final usage event.

normalize_response_stream.description: Normalize provider-native SSE (e.g. Anthropic Messages API events) to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE. Disabling forwards provider-native SSE verbatim.

max_stream_bytes.description: Cumulative provider plaintext bytes one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer accepts before it fails closed with an upstream_error frame. A residual provider Content-Encoding is still decoded under the fixed 8 MiB per-layer residual-decode limit. An explicit null means omission.

max_stream_events.description: Complete provider stream events one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer accepts before it fails closed. An explicit null means omission.

max_normalized_stream_bytes.description: Cumulative OpenAI-shaped output bytes one Anthropic/Gemini response normalizer may emit before it fails closed. A buffered normalization is additionally bounded by the response's retained ceiling. An explicit null means omission.

providers.description: One or more streaming provider definitions. The first provider (in priority order) whose model_patterns match the request `model` wins.

name.description: Unique provider name (surfaced in ai_stream_router.provider metadata). Must be non-empty, and unique across the instance's providers; that uniqueness check is a runtime admission rule this schema cannot express.

provider_type.description: Provider wire format. openai/openai_compatible/azure_openai pass through (azure_openai authenticates with the api-key header); anthropic and google_gemini are translated + normalized to OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE.

endpoint.description: Full https (or http with allow_plaintext) provider streaming endpoint URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions, https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, or https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent. May contain a literal {model} path placeholder. A google_gemini endpoint without {model} is admitted only when model_patterns is the single exact model name the endpoint path names (.../models/<model>:...), because Gemini routes the model only through the URL. An endpoint query string (e.g. an Azure-style ?api-version=...) is preserved and merged with the client's own query using '&'. Embedded userinfo (user:password@) and a #fragment are rejected. IPv6 literal hosts are bracketed in the forwarded authority.

api_key.description: Provider API key. The resolved value must be a valid HTTP header value (no CR, LF, NUL, or other control byte) or construction fails. Supports a whole-value ${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>} reference resolved from the process environment at construction; a ${...} reference to any other variable, including every other FERRUM_* setting, is refused at admission with a 400. Injected as Authorization: Bearer for openai(-compatible), api-key for azure_openai, x-api-key for anthropic, x-goog-api-key for google_gemini.

model_patterns.description: 1–128 glob patterns matched against the request `model`; each is 1–256 ASCII bytes using letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, slash, plus, hyphen, or star, with no `..` sequence. `*` is the only wildcard, matches any run of characters except URL-structural separators (`/ ? # & \`) and whitespace, and the pattern is anchored at both ends — so `*mini` matches `model-mini` and `mini-mini` alike, and never matches `mini-pro`. Example: ['gpt-*', 'o*'] or ['claude-*'].

priority.description: Lower = matched first. Defaults to provider index + 1. Stored as a u32, so a larger value is rejected; an explicit null means omission.

allow_plaintext.description: Permit an http:// endpoint. Plaintext provider egress is rejected by default, so this is the required opt-in for an internal HTTP-compatible provider. It has no effect on an https endpoint and does not relax runtime TLS/FIPS policy. An explicit null means omission.

anthropic_version.description: anthropic providers only (a non-null value on any other provider_type is rejected, by this schema and at admission): anthropic-version header value sent to Anthropic providers. Must be a non-empty valid HTTP header value; an explicit null means omission and keeps the default.

default_max_tokens.description: anthropic providers only (a non-null value on any other provider_type is rejected, by this schema and at admission; when omitted on an anthropic provider the router forwards 4096): Anthropic max_tokens forwarded when the OpenAI request sets neither max_tokens nor max_completion_tokens. A present non-null client max_tokens / max_completion_tokens must be a positive integer or the request is rejected with 400. An explicit null means omission.

inherit_backend_tls.description: By default an https provider endpoint is verified against the built-in public trust roots only, isolated from every gateway-global backend TLS fallback: the global FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH is not used, FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY cannot disable verification, and the global backend client certificate (FERRUM_BACKEND_TLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH / _KEY_PATH) is never presented. Set true to keep the proxy's own resolved backend TLS instead — custom CA bundle, SNI/SAN policy, and backend mTLS client certificate, including the gateway-global fallbacks that resolution normally inherits — for internal openai_compatible endpoints behind private PKI. No effect on http endpoints. An explicit null means omission.

AiTokenMetricsConfig.description: Plugin: ai_token_metrics — Extracts token usage from HTTP JSON LLM response bodies and from streamed SSE / AWS event-stream responses. Native gRPC protobuf messages are unsupported and the plugin is not registered for the Grpc protocol view. Unknown keys are rejected. Streamed responses are metered incrementally without buffering; buffer_streaming_responses instead collects SSE before inspection and disables live delivery. A collected body above 4 MiB (before decoding) is not inspected. Cohere counts come from usage.tokens, delta.usage.tokens, or meta.tokens, not billed_units; configured cost rates estimate cost from those token counts, not provider billing units.

provider.description: Exact lowercase LLM provider format; surrounding whitespace and alternate casing are rejected. `tgi` selects Hugging Face TGI native `/generate` shapes (`details.generated_tokens`).

buffer_streaming_responses.description: Buffer text/event-stream responses and meter them after the full response is collected; disables streaming delivery for those responses. Not required for SSE token accounting, which observes streams incrementally by default.

cost_per_prompt_token.description: Calculate estimated cost per request from prompt tokens; range 0 through 18446744073709.55. Omitted or null disables this rate.

cost_per_completion_token.description: Calculate estimated cost per request from completion tokens; range 0 through 18446744073709.55. Omitted or null disables this rate.

model_pricing.description: Ordered per-model rate overrides. The first entry whose `model` glob matches the response's reported model supplies the rates (an omitted entry rate leaves that side unpriced); when none matches, or no publishable model is reported, the flat rates apply. Federation usage is priced at the flat rates.

model.description: Anchored glob matched against the response's model; `*` is the only wildcard and never matches URL-structural separators (`/ ? # & \`) or whitespace.

cost_per_prompt_token.description: Prompt-token rate for matching models; null or omitted leaves the prompt side unpriced.

cost_per_completion_token.description: Completion-token rate for matching models; null or omitted leaves the completion side unpriced.

AiToolGovernorCallerScopeList.description: Per-tool caller-identity scope (ai_tool_governor allowed_consumers / denied_consumers by Consumer username, allowed_groups / denied_groups by Consumer acl_groups). Evaluated after a per-tool deny or dry_run and before argument checks and approval. A denied_* match denies; with any allowed_* list configured the caller must match an allowed consumer or group; with any scope configured, a request without a mapped Consumer is denied. A tool definition outside the caller's scope is refused like a denied tool. Runtime admission enforces a stricter 512 UTF-8 byte entry cap (OpenAPI maxLength counts Unicode characters).

AiToolGovernorConfig.description: Plugin: ai_tool_governor — Deterministic allow/deny/approval policy for AI tool/function calls. Inspects request tool definitions across every provider shape (OpenAI tools[].function.name / functions[].name, Anthropic tools[].name, Google tools[].functionDeclarations[].name, Bedrock toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec.name), buffered response tool calls (OpenAI choices[].message.tool_calls[] and legacy function_call, OpenAI Responses output[] function_call items, Anthropic content[] tool_use blocks, Google candidates[].content.parts[].functionCall, Cohere v2 message.tool_calls[], Bedrock Converse output.message.content[].toolUse), streaming SSE tool-call deltas in the OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (response.output_item.added / response.function_call_arguments.delta, with every .done / response.completed restatement required to match the accumulated call exactly), Anthropic (content_block_start / input_json_delta), Cohere v2 (tool-call-start / tool-call-delta), and Google shapes (held until complete and cleared by policy/approval, then released — or the stream is cut with an SSE error event, never leaking the held call), and optionally MCP tools/call and A2A JSON-RPC methods. A payload carrying a tool-call marker this plugin cannot read is ungovernable and fails closed in enforce mode by default (see unknown_shape_action). Complements ai_semantic_firewall (which catches intent): every decision here is a deterministic function of names, arguments, JSON Schema, regexes, identity, and an optional approval webhook. In enforce mode, governed bodies the plugin cannot inspect fail closed: Content-Encoding'd, oversized (>4 MiB), non-UTF-8, or unparseable JSON request bodies are rejected when request inspection is enabled, oversized JSON responses are rejected, a JSON response that is well-formed but beyond the inspection parser's nesting/numeric limits is rejected (malformed JSON is still forwarded), an SSE event that is not valid UTF-8 or carries such JSON cuts the stream, and streaming holds past the 4 MiB cap cut the stream. Configuration is strict: unknown root, inspect, tool-policy, blocked-pattern, approval, response, and observability properties are rejected (with path-qualified diagnostics). The free-form `tools` name map and arbitrary per-tool `json_schema` document remain open. Does not execute tools or replace mcp_gateway/A2A routing. HTTP-family only.

enabled.description: When false the plugin is inert (no buffering, no inspection), and policy field *values* are ignored — but unknown property names are still rejected at every fixed-shape layer.
When false the plugin is inert (no buffering, no inspection).

mode.description: enforce rejects/cuts blocked tool calls; dry_run evaluates and emits metadata but never rejects and never calls the approval webhook (safe rollout).

default_action.description: Action for a tool with no explicit policy entry. tools may be empty only when default_action governs (deny/require_approval).

unknown_shape_action.description: Posture for a governed payload that carries a live tool-call marker (tool_calls / toolCalls / tool_use / toolUse / function_call / functionCall member names, or a block tagged type: tool_use / function_call / tool-call) from which no call could be extracted — a provider tool-call shape this plugin cannot read — or, when calls WERE extracted, a marker outside every location the extractors read (a second call a normalizing client may honor; markers inside an extracted call's own arguments never count). deny (default) treats it as ungovernable: enforce rejects the body or cuts the stream, dry_run forwards. allow forwards it as if no tool call were present. BOTH settings record the fixed ai_tool_governor.uninspectable_reason=unrecognized_tool_call_shape observation without claiming a decision, so an unreadable shape is never silently permitted. Payloads with no tool-call marker at all (ordinary REST JSON on a shared proxy, embeddings/moderations responses, content-only completions) are out of scope under both settings.

inspect.description: Independently toggled inspection surfaces. At least one must be enabled. Unknown surface switches are rejected.

request_tool_definitions.description: Reject/dry-run requests that expose disallowed tool definitions to the model.

response_tool_calls.description: Govern tool calls in buffered (non-streaming) responses. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch (unconditional; applies to allow/deny/redact_args/require_approval/dry_run).

streaming_response_tool_calls.description: Govern OpenAI SSE tool-call deltas. Held tool-call frames are released only after policy/approval clears the call; a block cuts the stream with a terminal SSE error event. Duplicate choice/tool indexes, empty-string or non-string IDs, conflicting IDs, or an ID introduced after an untagged fragment are ungovernable and fail closed in enforce mode. JSON null for tool_calls[].id is treated as omitted (same as a missing field). At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per SSE batch. In streaming, a redact_args match fails closed (denies) since mid-stream surgical redaction of split-JSON arguments is out of scope.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Inspect MCP JSON-RPC tools/call request bodies directly (params.name + params.arguments), including calls inside JSON-RPC batch arrays. When params.arguments is omitted, the governor normalizes it to {} before required-arg / regex / hash / approval / JSON Schema evaluation (MCP zero-argument calls). Provider response shapes that omit function.arguments are not normalized. With mcp_gateway aggregate_router on the same proxy, policy identity stays the public namespaced tool name across the gateway's trusted upstream-name rewrite; final arguments are still rechecked and unrelated name changes fail closed.

a2a_methods.description: Govern A2A JSON-RPC method names against the tools policy map (params carried as arguments).

tools.description: Per-tool policy, keyed by a non-empty tool name (may be namespaced, e.g. github.create_pr, or an MCP/A2A method name) or by a glob containing `*` (e.g. github.*, *delete*). `*` matches any run of characters including none (it crosses `.`, `/`, and `_`), anchored at both ends. Precedence: an exact key always wins; among matching globs the one with the most literal (non-`*`) bytes wins, then fewer wildcards, then byte order of the key. At most 256 glob keys, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; globs are never A2A aliases. policy_ids metadata records the governing key. When composed with mcp_gateway aggregate_router, keys remain the public namespaced names: a trusted public-to-upstream rewrite is remapped for the final-body recheck only when the final wire name exactly matches that staged upstream alias; final arguments are still re-evaluated and unrelated name changes fail closed. The tool-name map is intentionally free-form; each policy object is closed.

action.description: allow forwards; deny blocks; redact_args replaces blocked_arg_patterns matches with redaction_placeholder (buffered path); require_approval calls the approval webhook; dry_run forwards and records ai_tool_governor.decision=dry_run distinctly from a real allow. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch regardless of action.

risk.description: Risk band surfaced as ai_tool_governor.risk (max across a batch) and in approval requests.

max_arg_bytes.description: Deny when the raw arguments string exceeds this many bytes.

required_args.description: Deny when any listed key is absent from the parsed arguments object.

name.description: Pattern identifier; substituted into redaction_placeholder {name}. OpenAPI maxLength: 256 counts Unicode characters; runtime admission enforces a stricter 256 UTF-8 byte cap.

regex.description: Regex matched against the raw arguments string and, when the raw text contains a JSON escape, also against its JSON-decoded views (the canonical re-serialization and every decoded string, member names included), so an escaped spelling such as a unicode-escaped underscore cannot hide a match. Under a non-redact action a match in any view denies; under redact_args a raw match is redacted, and a match visible only in a decoded view (which raw-text redaction cannot remove) denies instead. Patterns that match empty input are rejected at config load; contextual zero-length matches fail closed at runtime.

blocked_arg_patterns.description: Named regexes screening tool arguments. At least one entry is required when action=redact_args. At most 32 patterns per tool; every append is checked before allocation and redacted output is capped at the 4 MiB inspectable body limit.

json_schema.description: JSON Schema (validated with the jsonschema crate) the parsed arguments must satisfy, else deny. Intentionally open — arbitrary JSON Schema keywords are allowed; do not set additionalProperties: false here.

approval.description: Approval webhook, required when any policy can reach require_approval.

endpoint_url.description: http/https URL POSTed with request_id, consumer, principal (the authority-qualified caller: {kind: consumer, namespace, id} for a mapped Consumer, or {kind: external, subject, mechanism, authority} where authority is the opaque hex digest of the verifying authority), proxy, model, provider, tool_name, arguments_hash, risk (and raw arguments only when include_arguments=true). An http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal host written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] (URL userinfo does not count as part of the host) unless allow_plaintext is true, because a cleartext channel lets a man-in-the-middle forge allow verdicts. The URI scheme is case-insensitive (runtime parsing normalizes it before the http/https check), so HTTPS://host/path is admitted exactly like https://host/path. Response: {"decision":"allow|deny"} or {"allow":true|false}, optional approval_id. Response bodies are capped at 64 KiB.

timeout_ms.description: Per-request approval webhook timeout (max 30000). A batch resolves its approvals with at most 8 webhook calls in flight and the whole batch is capped at 30s of approval wait; after an enforce-mode block, no further webhook call in that batch is started (calls already in flight complete). Calls identical in name and arguments within one batch share one resolution when cache_ttl_seconds > 0. At most 64 concrete tool calls are governed per request/response/SSE batch. Dropping the governing future (client cancel) cancels any in-flight approval HTTP call.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: TTL for caching an approval decision keyed by consumer+principal+proxy+model+provider+tool+arguments, so equal subject strings verified by different authorities never share a decision. 0 disables caching. The cache is bounded (4096 entries); at capacity expired entries are purged and new decisions are not cached rather than growing memory.

fail_on_error.description: Behavior when the approval endpoint cannot be evaluated: reject fails closed, warn/allow fail open.

include_arguments.description: Include the raw tool arguments in the approval request body. Off by default so secrets are not sent.

headers.description: Extra request headers for the approval call (for example an Authorization credential). A value is a literal, or a whole-value ${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>} reference resolved from the process environment at the first approval call (an unset or invalid secret is an approval endpoint error handled by fail_on_error; config validation does not need the live secret). Names must be valid HTTP header names, unique case-insensitively, and may not be content-type, content-length, host, transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, proxy-connection, te, trailer, upgrade, or X-Ferrum-Hops; values must be valid header values. Runtime admission additionally enforces the reference namespace and a stricter 8192 UTF-8 byte value cap (OpenAPI maxLength counts Unicode characters). Values are never logged or echoed in diagnostics.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// endpoint_url whose host is not a loopback IP literal. Verdicts, any headers credential, and (with include_arguments) raw arguments then cross the network in clear.

deny_status_code.description: HTTP error status (400-599) returned for a deterministic tool policy denial in enforce mode. Uninspectable governed bodies fail closed with 502.

redaction_placeholder.description: Template for redacted argument matches; {name} is replaced with the matched pattern name. OpenAPI maxLength: 256 counts Unicode characters; runtime admission enforces a stricter 256 UTF-8 byte cap. Redacted argument output is capped at the 4 MiB inspectable body limit.

streaming_deny_event.description: Emit a terminal SSE error event when cutting a streamed tool call.

emit_metadata.description: Emit ai_tool_governor.* transaction metadata (enabled, mode, decision, tool_names, risk, policy_ids, approval_id, arguments_hashes, redacted_tools).

hash_arguments.description: Emit SHA-256 hashes of tool arguments as ai_tool_governor.arguments_hashes. Raw arguments are never placed in metadata.

max_argument_log_bytes.description: When > 0, log up to this many bytes of a blocked call's raw arguments at debug for audit. 0 keeps raw arguments out of logs entirely.

AiTranscriptAuditConfig.description: Plugin: ai_transcript_audit — Controlled AI payload capture for compliance/audit. Priority 2740 runs after authentication/authorization and before request_deduplication (3010); local/Redis replays emit one record with cache.request_deduplication.replayed=true, and priority overrides that reverse the order are rejected. Captures AI request/response bodies (after redaction), keyed HMAC-SHA256 body hashes (keyed with redaction.hash_secret when set, else a per-process random key), model/provider, token metadata, guardrail decisions (including bounded ai_tool_governor.* fields), tool names, and allow-listed cache telemetry (namespaced `ai_semantic_cache.<id>.{cache_status,cache_match,cache_similarity}` and `request_deduplication.replayed`; never `cache_key`), then exports them asynchronously to an HTTPS collector in batches. Capture excerpt limits each have a deployment-safe hard maximum of 1048576 bytes and a cross-field aggregate maximum of 2097152; request-derived model/tool metadata is independently bounded (256/64/128/4096) before staging. Retention is bounded by BOTH record count (sink.buffer_capacity) and an aggregate retained-byte budget (limits.buffer_max_bytes / limits.max_entry_bytes) covering staged candidates, fail-closed pre-commit reservations, active fail-open stream capture, exact pre-serialized queue payloads, JSON-array assembly, and every sequential retry. A fail-open stream reserves the maximum retained-record charge before copying response bytes and transfers that lease at terminal enqueue; a fail-closed stream reuses its pre-commit lease. Retry clones share immutable Bytes rather than deep-cloning records; reqwest receives the already-escaped exact-capacity JSON body rather than reserializing it. In redacted_body, limits.max_redaction_scan_bytes is checked before JSON classification/model/tool extraction/redaction; oversized JSON POSTs are conservatively audited as possible streaming AI requests with explicit omission evidence rather than bypassing audit. Streamed keyed hashing is bounded by capture.stream_hash, and active-stream reservations by limits.max_stream_reservation_secs. Authenticated /health exposes effective admitted ceilings plus live retained_bytes/retained_byte_drops/stream_reservations_expired/sink_healthy gauges without transcript content. Never blocks or rejects the proxy hot path unless an operator opts into a fail-closed policy (sink.on_buffer_full=reject or sink.on_sink_error=reject); those policies also apply to request-only and conservatively classified oversized capture. In-flight staging is hard-bounded at 4096 entries per plugin instance while candidate/record_id/sample markers remain shared across co-located instances: a saturated instance neither erases a peer's live candidate nor borrows it for response buffering, response hooks, stream reservations, sampling/admission, or record emission. The local staging entry is consumed by atomic removal at buffered or ordinary stream-terminal commit. Expiry first revokes capture/hash work and releases all staging/queue/byte owners; its single-fire request-owned terminal slot carries only the local sampling roll needed for a body-free best-effort fallback and cannot be created from shared peer markers. Orphan/reservation sweeps are time-gated. Not a security boundary on its own — pair with ai_prompt_shield, ai_semantic_firewall, ai_response_guard, and ai_tool_governor for enforcement. HTTP by default; native gRPC capture requires an explicit descriptor-based grpc enrollment block (enrolled methods only). Unknown keys are rejected at the root and every fixed nested object (capture, sampling, redaction, custom_patterns items, limits, privacy, sink); sink.custom_headers remains the only intentional free-form string map. Outbound sink header values are literal text plus optional ${secret:NAME} references scoped to the FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_* env namespace (no generic process-environment interpolation), fully materialized and validated when the background worker activates so a missing/empty/invalid secret fails activation instead of sending unauthenticated. privacy.path_mode governs request-path export; a privacy mode never exports the literal path by default. Nested objects may be omitted or null to keep defaults. Redacted captures replace malformed function.arguments JSON with [UNPARSEABLE] and set arguments_redaction_failed=true on the captured function object; valid arguments retain member-name redaction. Explicit full_body raw capture is unchanged. Every fixed scalar whose runtime default is used when the key is omitted also accepts an explicit null; the batching keys (sink.batch_size, sink.flush_interval_ms, sink.buffer_capacity, sink.max_retries, sink.retry_delay_ms), sink.endpoint_url, sink.custom_headers, redaction.custom_patterns, grpc, grpc.descriptor_path, and grpc.methods do NOT — null is a type error for those, exactly as the schema states. RUNTIME-ONLY CHECKS this component deliberately cannot express, all of which still reject the configuration at construction: (1) arithmetic relationships between limits — limits.max_entry_bytes must be >= the worst-case serialized-JSON contract implied by the configured capture limits, limits.buffer_max_bytes must be >= both 65536 and the retained charge of limits.max_entry_bytes, and max_request_bytes + max_response_bytes + max_stream_capture_bytes must be <= 2097152; (2) Rust `regex` crate compilation of every redaction.builtins entry and every redaction.custom_patterns[].regex, and rejection of an unknown redaction.builtins name beyond the enum; (3) sink.endpoint_url authority, userinfo, and backend-egress SSRF screening, plus the rule that cleartext http:// is admitted only with sink.allow_insecure_loopback: true AND a loopback IP-literal host (not the name localhost); (4) sink.custom_headers name/value validity and the ${secret:NAME} template grammar (a resolvable FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_<NAME> is checked later still, when the background worker activates); (5) node-local existence and decodability of grpc.descriptor_path, and resolution of each method's request_type / response_type / text_fields against that descriptor — Admin/CP admission validates shape only; (6) grpc.methods key normalization (trim plus one optional leading slash) and the rejection of two keys that normalize to the same method path; (7) grpc.methods[].text_fields segment trimming, the per-path segment-depth ceiling, and duplicate detection after normalization, which catches pairs that uniqueItems cannot ("a.b" versus "a . b"); and (8) the plugin-cache composition rule that refuses a priority override placing this instance at or after a co-located request_deduplication instance.

mode.description: Null keeps the default, as for every other fixed scalar here. metadata_only: keyed body hashes + model/provider/token/guardrail metadata, no body. redacted_body: capped, PII-redacted request/response excerpts. Values beneath normalized sensitive JSON keys (password/auth/cookie/session/credential/private-key/client-secret/API-key/token variants) are replaced regardless of value shape; everything under an Azure 'On Your Data' parameters object inside a data_sources / dataSources / data-sources container is additionally replaced wholesale, and recognizing that container name never short-circuits the ordinary visitor — a value under it that is not the provider's conventional array (object, string, number, boolean, null) is still traversed with the same member-name and pattern rules; JSON objects/arrays encoded inside strings (including tool arguments) are recursively decoded/redacted to a depth cap of 64. Uniform OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE is reassembled before redaction with exact shape {sse_reassembled:true,object:'chat.completion.chunk',completion_text:{'<choice>':'…'},tool_calls:{'<choice>':[{index,id,type,function:{name,arguments}}]},finish_reason:{'<choice>':'…'}}; absent categories are omitted, and text/tool fragments are concatenated by choice/tool index under max_stream_capture_bytes. Only a provider-declared unsigned index correlates fragments across deltas; array position is intra-delta identity only (exported as 'position:<n>' choice keys and a tool-call 'position' field, never as a fabricated index). Malformed optional fields do not abort reassembly (that would drop back to per-frame redaction, which cannot see a secret split across fragments): ignorable ones (finish_reason, delta, delta.content, tool_calls, id, type, function, function.name, function.arguments) are skipped, while a malformed identity-bearing index (choices[].index, tool_calls[].index) takes a collision-free per-occurrence bucket ('unattributed:<n>' choice key, index_unattributed:true plus occurrence:<n> on a tool call) rather than collapsing onto index 0, sharing one unattributed bucket, or being dropped. Where identity is a guess, payload is withheld instead of joined or split: ambiguous completion text becomes '[REDACTED:ambiguous_choice]' with choice_identity_ambiguous:true and completion_text_withheld:true, and ambiguous tool arguments become '[REDACTED:ambiguous_tool_call]' with arguments_withheld:true. Skipped or re-routed fields are listed in a sorted malformed_fields array of compiled-in field paths (never provider values); the key is omitted for well-formed streams. Other or non-parseable SSE stays per-event: each event's data lines are joined with a newline as a client reads them and redacted as one document, and a JSON-shaped event payload the parser refuses is replaced, continuation lines included, by one data: [UNPARSEABLE] line. A leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped before any structural parse; a request candidate or JSON-typed response that no structural parse can read (UTF-16/UTF-32, NaN, comments, a batch past the nesting limit) is never pattern-redacted, because sensitive member names need the parse: its excerpt is withheld with request_body_omitted_reason / response_body_omitted_reason unparseable_document. full_body: capped unredacted excerpts (requires allow_full_body). hash_only: keyed body hashes + envelope only. Body hashes are keyed HMAC-SHA256 in every mode, never plain SHA-256.

allow_full_body.description: Required guardrail for mode=full_body, which captures unredacted payloads. Construction fails if full_body is set without this opt-in.

capture.description: What to capture. Omit or null to keep defaults. At least one of request, response, or streaming_response must stay enabled.

streaming_response.description: Capture SSE response excerpts. false | true | 'sampled', or the string spellings 'true' / 'false', or null for the default. true forces every AI-candidate request's response onto the stream-inspection path. 'sampled' tees only requests that win the sampling.rate roll (or whose request-side guardrail fired when always_capture_on_guardrail is set — the tee decision is evaluated at dispatch time, after the request-phase guardrail plugins ran); error responses and response-side guardrail hits on un-sampled streaming requests still emit records via the log fallback, but without a response body/hash — teeing every stream to cover those late triggers would defeat sampled capture.

headers.description: Capture response headers (redacted by key). Also gated by privacy.include_raw_headers.

tool_calls.description: Extract tool/function names from the request body.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Treat MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests (a singleton, or a batch with a tools/call member) as audit candidates for JSON-ish content types. Content-Type-less POSTs are buffered and captured when they carry a tools/call (a byte pre-scan skips parsing and staging for anything else); set capture.mcp_endpoint_path to limit this to one exact path; add an mcp section to records with the public tool name, keyed arguments_hash, optional excerpt, outcome, and bounded gateway metadata. At most 32 calls per record; later ones are counted in calls_omitted.

mcp_endpoint_path.description: Optional exact path that narrows Content-Type-less MCP capture. When unset, Content-Type-less POSTs on every path are buffered and checked for a tools/call; when set, only this path is. Set it to the mcp_gateway endpoint.path to avoid buffering other Content-Type-less uploads.

mcp_arguments.description: Add each MCP call's arguments excerpt, shaped like a body excerpt (redacted in redacted_body, raw in full_body) and sharing limits.max_request_bytes with the request excerpt. Requires mcp_tool_calls and mode redacted_body or full_body.

stream_hash.description: How much of a streamed (SSE) response the exported keyed HMAC-SHA256 response_hash covers. capped (default) stops hashing at limits.max_stream_capture_bytes, so limits.max_stream_capture_bytes bounds audit CPU as well as retained bytes and an indefinitely long high-bandwidth stream cannot keep a keyed hash running for the life of the connection; the digest is then marked response_hash_scope=partial, carries the exact response_hash_bytes it covered, and is domain-separated so it can never collide with or be presented as a full-stream digest. full is the explicit opt-in for deployments whose evidence chain genuinely re-derives the provider's complete response, and accepts unbounded per-byte keyed-hashing cost. The response_hash is a tamper-evidence/correlation token over the captured transcript, not an integrity attestation of the client's byte stream — abnormally terminated and downstream-cut streams already omit it entirely. Buffered (non-streamed) responses are complete by construction and always hash full.

sampling.description: Sampling controls. Omit or null to keep defaults.

rate.description: Fraction of eligible AI transactions emitted as full records. Guardrail/error captures override the roll.

always_capture_on_guardrail.description: Override a losing sampling roll for a fired guardrail. A non-empty ai_tool_governor.decision other than allow (deny, dry_run, require_approval, or redact_args) fires this override on request, buffered-response, and terminal-stream paths; ordinary allow does not. Exported guardrails include bounded ai_tool_governor.enabled, mode, decision, tool_names, risk, policy_ids, approval_id, and redacted_tools fields. The governor's ai_tool_governor.arguments_hashes (an unkeyed SHA-256 of each call's arguments, an offline guessing oracle) is never exported; mcp.calls[].arguments_hash is the keyed equivalent.

always_capture_on_error.description: Override a losing sampling roll for a failed transaction. Fires on an HTTP status >= 400, on a streamed body that did not complete, and on the final client-visible gRPC application status: a native gRPC call normally fails under HTTP 200 with a non-zero grpc-status, and that status (from the terminal trailers, a Trailers-Only header block, or the UNKNOWN a gRPC transaction with no terminal status carries) is treated as an error at buffered commit, stream termination, and the transaction-log fallback alike. grpc-status 0 remains a success and stays subject to ordinary sampling.

max_records_per_minute.description: Records-per-minute cap (0 = unlimited). Over the cap, records are dropped and traffic is NEVER rejected: a record the window has already refused takes no queue permit or retained-byte reservation and cannot select a fail-closed 503, so sink.on_buffer_full/on_sink_error: reject cannot deny traffic for an audit record that could not have been written.
