Suppression is bounded by the window — the first record admitted after it rolls over flushes normally, which is the same background-send recovery probe that restores sink health elsewhere. The admitted maximum is the unsigned 64-bit ceiling (a larger literal is a type error, not a clamp); the effective in-window ceiling is clamped to 4294967294.

redaction.description: PII redaction policy for captured excerpts. Omit or null to keep defaults. In mode=redacted_body and mode=metadata_only the pattern set must not be empty: builtins=[] with no custom_patterns is rejected at construction (a pass-through redactor would export unredacted data — body excerpts in redacted_body, the request-derived model/tool_names in both — without the full_body opt-in; hash_only exports no request-derived strings and is exempt). redacted_body also replaces values beneath normalized sensitive parent keys and recursively redacts JSON-encoded object/array strings before applying regex patterns.

builtins.description: Built-in PII patterns, shared with ai_prompt_shield/ai_response_guard. Omit or null for the default set; an explicit empty array with no custom_patterns is refused in redacted_body/metadata_only, and under privacy.path_mode: redact in every mode.

placeholder.description: Non-hashing replacement template; {type} is substituted with the pattern name.

hash_redacted_values.description: Replace matches with [REDACTED:<type>:<hmac-prefix>] so identical values stay correlatable without storing the raw value. The digest is a keyed HMAC-SHA256 (see hash_secret), never a plain hash — most PII value spaces are small enough to brute-force offline from an unsalted digest.

hash_secret.description: Optional key for the redacted-value HMAC and the exported request/response body hashes. The minimum length is counted in CHARACTERS (Unicode code points), matching this minLength — not in UTF-8 bytes, so a 16-character multi-byte secret is refused even though it carries 32 bytes. When set (min 32 characters), hashed placeholders and body hashes are stable across gateway instances and restarts, so values correlate fleet-wide. When omitted or null, each process generates a random key at startup: digests still correlate within one process lifetime but never across restarts/instances, and can never be dictionary-attacked from exported records. Treat like any other secret — do not log or export it.

limits.description: Capture size caps for request/response/stream excerpts. Each field has a deployment-safe hard maximum (1048576). The sum of all three must be <= 2097152 so a valid combination cannot retain an unsafe aggregate body budget. Request-derived model/tool metadata is bounded independently of these excerpt settings (model <= 256 bytes, <= 64 tool names, each name <= 128 bytes, aggregate tool-name bytes <= 4096). Omit or null to keep defaults.

max_request_bytes.description: Maximum retained request-body excerpt bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate with max_response_bytes and max_stream_capture_bytes.

max_response_bytes.description: Maximum retained buffered response-body excerpt bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate.

max_stream_capture_bytes.description: Maximum retained SSE stream-capture bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate. Also bounds the streamed keyed digest unless capture.stream_hash is full.

max_redaction_scan_bytes.description: Independent hard processing bound for redacted-mode request classification, model/tool extraction, and body shaping. In mode=redacted_body the raw length is checked before serde_json: payloads above this bound are never JSON-parsed, model/tool scanned, redaction-scanned, or copied into an excerpt. An oversized POST application/json is conservatively audited as a possible AI request and treated as potentially streaming (so capture does not buffer a possibly unbounded SSE response); parse-derived model/tool fields are omitted and fail-closed queue/byte admission still applies. The record carries request_body_omitted_reason / response_body_omitted_reason = redaction_scan_limit with the body_truncated flag set. Hashes, envelope, status, and bounded guardrail metadata still export. Streaming redacted capture enforces this bound while chunks arrive: if it is smaller than max_stream_capture_bytes, no more than max_redaction_scan_bytes is copied and crossing the bound records response_body_omitted_reason = redaction_scan_limit rather than exporting a raw boundary fragment. The keyed digest still follows capture.stream_hash until reservation expiry revokes all audit work. mode=full_body caps on a UTF-8 boundary first and never scans past the cap, so it is unaffected.

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized JSON bytes for one admitted record. Queue admission first performs an allocation-free bounded counting serialization, then serializes into one exact-capacity immutable Bytes payload. The default/minimum is derived from the configured capture limits and worst-case JSON escaping: 6 * (max_request_bytes + max(max_response_bytes, max_stream_capture_bytes) + 256 + 4096 + 8192). The hard maximum is 16777216. A complete record whose bounded envelope still exceeds this ceiling is dropped/rejected, never partially serialized.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained-byte budget for one plugin instance, covering staged request candidates, fail-closed pre-commit reservations, active fail-open stream capture, immutable pre-serialized queue payloads, one exact-capacity JSON-array request body, and every sequential retry. sink.buffer_capacity bounds the RECORD COUNT only; without this budget a slow collector can retain capacity x attacker-shaped record bytes. Retry clones share Bytes and do not deep-clone transcript fields; reqwest does not reserialize the batch. The exact per-record lease is 2 * (serialized_record_bytes + 1) + 128. Admission is (count AND bytes) and is enforced atomically before publication; leases release on every completion, discard, TTL-sweep, reservation-expiry, and failed-batch path. Saturation follows sink.on_buffer_full (drop or reject). Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1) + 128. Live retained_bytes and retained_byte_drops are exposed on authenticated /health.

max_stream_reservation_secs.description: Maximum lifetime of one active stream's staging entry and its reserved commit permit. An active stream is exempt from the one-hour orphan TTL, so without this bound a never-ending stream, or one whose terminal hook is lost, would hold a staging slot, a queue permit, and its retained bytes forever until all reservations were exhausted. The staging entry owns one cancellable single-fire deadline from first active response selection until staging is actually consumed or dropped. It revokes even an idle selection with no concrete inspector at its deadline without waiting for another request or chunk, and remains armed after normal inspector terminal claim while staging is retained for the immediate transaction-log fallback. Normal staging consumption wakes and cancels the task promptly; the amortized sweep remains a repair net. Both paths dynamically resolve and first revoke any current per-stream response accumulator and keyed HMAC through narrowly scoped shared state, then release the queue permit, staging slot, staging lease, and worst-case queued-record lease exactly once. An atomic fired/cancelled token makes deadline, sweep, terminal, inspector-drop, and log-fallback races single-fire. Later bytes forward unchanged without capture or hash work. No global tombstone remains for the live connection: inspector drop publishes a body-free request-owned handoff only when the stream actually terminates. Normal or abnormal late termination emits at most one best-effort fallback without request/response excerpts or hashes and without resurrecting the released commit permit. The process-global live-slot map is capped at 4096 and expiry releases that capacity; the remaining stream-owned handle has no capture/hash/accounting state. Reclamations are logged and counted in stream_reservations_expired on authenticated /health.

sink.description: Async batched HTTPS sink. The endpoint is SSRF-screened against the backend egress policy at construction (literal IPs) and at send time (resolved hostnames). Cleartext HTTP requires allow_insecure_loopback=true and is then limited to a loopback IP literal (not the name localhost). Unknown sink keys are rejected; custom_headers remains an open string map.

endpoint_url.description: Collector URL. Only the http and https schemes are admitted (the pattern is spelled case-insensitively because URL schemes are). HTTPS is required by default. HTTP is accepted only for a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1], not the name localhost) when allow_insecure_loopback is explicitly true. Userinfo credentials (https://user:pass@host) are rejected — authenticate with custom_headers. A collector that requires a credential in the URL path or query is supported, and this value is never rendered in operational output: egress-denial, DNS/TLS, retry, slow-call, and batch-failure diagnostics show only a structurally redacted scheme://host:port/redacted form. The admin audit and non-admin read projections apply the schema-aware sensitivity contract instead, keeping only scheme://host[:port] with `[REDACTED_PATH]` / `[REDACTED_QUERY]` / `[REDACTED_FRAGMENT]` markers.

allow_insecure_loopback.description: Allow an http:// collector only when endpoint_url uses a loopback IP literal. The name localhost does not qualify: DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects. This never permits remote cleartext delivery.

custom_headers.description: Extra headers sent on every batch. Arbitrary header names are accepted (the only intentional free-form map in the plugin config). Values are literal text plus optional ${secret:NAME} references, which resolve ONLY the FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_<NAME> environment namespace (e.g. Authorization: 'Bearer ${secret:AUDIT_TOKEN}' reads FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_AUDIT_TOKEN, composing with the _VAULT/_AWS/_AZURE/_GCP/_FILE external-secret suffixes). There is no generic ${ENV_VAR} process-environment interpolation, so unrelated Ferrum/database/cloud/system secrets cannot be exfiltrated into an outbound header; any other ${...} form, or a NAME outside [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*, is rejected at config admission. Names/templates are validated at admission; secrets are materialized once when the background worker activates. A missing, empty, or invalid secret/header value fails activation (the generation is never published) rather than being silently omitted, so on_sink_error=reject is honored on the first request. Materialized secret values are marked sensitive and never logged.

retry_delay_ms.description: Fixed delay between batch send retries for transient collector failures.

on_buffer_full.description: drop: silently drop when the queue or per-instance 4096-entry staging bound is full (never block). reject: fail selected request-only, buffered, streaming, synthetic, or final-body-fallback audit records with 503 before dispatch/response commit when staging or a queue slot cannot be reserved. Either reject policy also claims the finalized request representation of candidate-shaped POSTs, so a Content-Encoding is decoded by the shared request representation gate before classification (an undecodable one is refused with 400), and any candidate body no parser can read (comments, UTF-16/UTF-32, NaN, trailing commas — independent of capture.mcp_tool_calls) is conservatively audited rather than forwarded unaudited. Shared candidate markers from co-located peers do not bypass this bound. Streaming admission honors sampling plus configured error/guardrail overrides.

on_sink_error.description: warn: log and drop on permanent sink failure. reject: fail selected request-only, buffered, streaming, synthetic, or final-body-fallback audit records with 503 before dispatch/response commit while the sink is unhealthy. Like on_buffer_full: reject, it claims the finalized representation of candidate-shaped POSTs (content codings decoded before classification, unreadable candidate bodies conservatively audited). Streaming admission honors sampling plus configured error/guardrail overrides. Sink health is published from the COMPLETE delivery outcome, never from response headers alone: the acknowledgement body is drained and validated under sink.ack_max_bytes / sink.ack_timeout_ms first, and a 2xx whose acknowledgement stalls, overruns its bound, fails transport, or fails ack_policy validation is an ambiguous delivery that marks the sink unhealthy AND returns the batch for retry. Any non-2xx collector response also marks the sink unhealthy — including non-retryable 4xx (401/403/413, e.g. an expired token) whose batch is discarded rather than retried — so records silently lost at the collector stop audited traffic instead of letting it flow unaudited. Hysteresis: health drops on the first failed or ambiguous delivery with no damping, and is restored only by a 2xx whose acknowledgement fully drained and validated; each retry attempt re-publishes, so recovery happens on the attempt that actually succeeded. Rejected transactions still build and enqueue their audit record — the background flush of those records is the recovery probe.

ack_policy.description: How a collector acknowledgement is validated before sink health is published. drain: read the acknowledgement to EOF under sink.ack_max_bytes and sink.ack_timeout_ms, discarding the bytes (content is not inspected). json: additionally require a JSON object that does not report rejected records — a non-object/unparseable body, a non-zero/non-empty errors|failed|rejected|error_count field, or a status string outside the unequivocal affirmative set ok|success|accepted|created fails the batch. Ambiguous partial-delivery values such as partial_ok are unhealthy even without an explicit failure count. Acknowledgement bytes are never retained beyond the bound and never logged; only compiled-in failure classes appear in diagnostics, so a hostile collector cannot echo captured transcript content back into gateway logs.

ack_max_bytes.description: Hard bound on the acknowledgement body read from the collector. An advertised Content-Length above this, or a stream that exceeds it, fails the batch instead of buffering unbounded collector output into the flush worker.

ack_timeout_ms.description: Maximum time spent draining/validating one acknowledgement after headers arrive. Separate from the plugin HTTP client request timeout so a stalled acknowledgement cannot pin a flush worker for the full request budget.

privacy.description: Identity/header/path export controls. Omit or null to keep defaults.

path_mode.description: How the request path is exported. Applications often embed emails/account-ids/document-names/tokens in path segments, so a privacy mode never exports the literal path by default. omit: no path. template: export the matched route identifier (proxy listen_path, else proxy name; omitted when unavailable) instead of the user-controlled path. redact: literal path with the configured PII redactor applied (requires at least one redaction.builtins/custom_patterns pattern). hash: keyed HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the literal path (shares redaction.hash_secret; not brute-forceable offline). raw: literal path verbatim. Default is template for metadata_only/redacted_body/hash_only and raw for full_body (the deliberate raw-capture opt-in).

grpc.description: Native-gRPC capture contract. Present means the plugin also applies to native gRPC, but only enrolled methods are decoded and captured. Because the backend-effective method is not authoritative until after routing, the presence of this block conservatively buffers every native-gRPC request on the proxy; unenrolled responses are not buffered by this plugin. Captured string fields honor the same mode/redaction contract as HTTP excerpts: in redacted_body a value is replaced wholesale when ANY enclosing name matches the sensitive field-name policy — the field itself, any ancestor message field, or the protobuf map key of a map entry (map keys are never exported as labels; each map value is exported under a collision-free ordinal path such as `metadata.0`, and the key still decides redaction) — every element of a repeated field inherits that field's own decision, and JSON embedded inside a protobuf string is decoded and redacted before export. Malformed, truncated, oversized, undecodable, or unknown-field payloads omit the excerpt with a compiled-in reason rather than exporting partial or unredacted bytes. Requires a node-local FileDescriptorSet; Admin/CP admission validates shape only, and mode-aware file-dependency validation resolves the descriptor on data-plane nodes. The enrolled method is the BACKEND-EFFECTIVE one, which is not known until after routing and listen-path stripping, so configuring this block fully buffers the request body of EVERY native gRPC request on the proxy — enrolled or not — and the final request-body hook makes the authoritative enrollment decision. An enrolled instance joins the backend-path boundary itself, so that decision uses the backend-effective path the proxy binds (its trailing /Service/Method) and does not require grpc_method_router; the bound path is never outranked by the plugin-writable grpc_full_method metadata. A call enrolled only by its backend-effective method is staged at that boundary, so a deferred before_proxy short circuit after it still leaves a record. A client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming method on such a proxy therefore gets fully buffered request semantics; max_messages caps how much is captured, not how much is buffered.

descriptor_path.description: Node-local path to a compiled protobuf FileDescriptorSet. Validated shape-only at Admin/CP admission and against the real descriptor by mode-aware file-dependency validation. A readable but invalid descriptor rejects the candidate configuration; an absent or unreadable descriptor retains enrollment and omits body excerpts at request time.

methods.description: Map of "/package.Service/Method" to that method's capture contract. Only these methods are captured. Leading/trailing whitespace and one optional leading slash are normalized by the runtime; every dotted service segment and the method identifier must be a protobuf/gRPC identifier. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime. Each entry must set request_type and/or response_type.

request_type.description: Fully-qualified protobuf request message type. Null (or a blank string) is treated exactly as absent, so the other direction must then be set.

response_type.description: Fully-qualified protobuf response message type. Null (or a blank string) is treated exactly as absent, so the other direction must then be set.

text_fields.description: Dotted field paths restricting which string fields are exported. Each path must end at a string field and may not traverse a map field. Repeated fields retain every selected value under indexed paths such as tags.0 or messages.2.text. Omit, or set null, to cover every string field recursively; an explicit empty array is refused. The runtime additionally trims each dotted segment before comparing, so it rejects duplicates uniqueItems cannot see ("a.b" versus "a . b"), rejects an empty segment, and rejects a path deeper than the message-nesting ceiling.

max_message_bytes.description: Per-message ceiling, applied to the declared frame length and enforced while inflating a gzip-compressed frame; inflation stops at the tighter of this ceiling and the remaining redaction-scan budget. Aggregate decoded payload across frames is additionally capped by limits.max_redaction_scan_bytes. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 8388608 (8 MiB), equal to the hard maximum of that aggregate scan ceiling — a larger per-message value could never produce a capture.

max_messages.description: Maximum number of length-prefixed frames one buffered gRPC request or response may carry; above this the excerpt is omitted rather than partially captured. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 1024 frames: the decoded-byte scan budget bounds decoded payload, not frame count, so legal zero-length frames would otherwise let an operator-configured value drive an effectively unbounded frame vector. Descriptor-tree depth and node ceilings are aggregate across the complete buffered body, rather than resetting for every frame; exhaustion omits the complete excerpt with grpc_scan_limit.

ApiChargebackConfig.description:
Plugin: api_chargeback — Per-consumer API usage charge tracking across
three independent pricing dimensions: per-call pricing by billable
status code, per-byte bandwidth pricing (both client->backend and
backend->client, applied to HTTP-family AND stream proxies), and
per-connection pricing for stream proxies (TCP/TCP+TLS/UDP/DTLS).
Ordinary HTTP uses the wire status. Native gRPC and translated
gRPC-Web use the final client-visible grpc-status mapped to the
canonical effective HTTP status; missing/malformed/unknown terminal
status, and a terminal status present on the wire but unreadable by the
gateway, fail closed to 500. Explicitly zero-priced tiers still meter calls.
Bandwidth pricing bills WebSocket sessions from the parsed relay's
payload byte counters, so a bandwidth-priced instance keeps its proxy's
WebSocket sessions off the raw tunnel relay and is refused on a
`websocket_permessage_deflate: passthrough` proxy.
Successful H1/H2/H3 WebSocket handshakes share the 101 pricing tier;
rejected handshakes retain their error status.
At least one of `pricing_tiers`, `bandwidth_pricing`, or
`stream_connection_pricing` must be configured.
Unknown top-level keys and unknown `pricing_tiers[]` keys are
rejected so a misspelled pricing dimension cannot silently bill
at zero.
Exactly-once accounting: after scope merging, each proxy may retain
at most one effective `api_chargeback` instance. Multiple proxy-scoped,
proxy-group-scoped, or mixed attachments on one proxy are rejected
because the process-global `/charges` registry has no ledger/instance
dimension. Distinct proxies may each attach one instance (including
different currencies/pricing). Shared render/cleanup/budget tunables
(`render_cache_ttl_seconds`, `stale_entry_ttl_seconds`,
`cache_invalidation_min_age_ms`, `cleanup_interval_seconds`,
`max_entries`, `max_retained_bytes`) must
agree across every enabled instance in the process.
Cardinality budget: the shared registry retains at most `max_entries`
billing rows (complete registry entry keys) and at most
`max_retained_bytes` of state. Keys include consumer, proxy, status,
protocol family, currency, namespace, and prices, so one principal can
occupy many slots. A new ordinary row beyond either ceiling uses its
prepared aggregate fallback, preserving totals while losing per-identity
attribution. Outside a prepared matrix, an aggregate that cannot reserve
bytes drops the charge and increments `dropped_charges_total`. The
aggregate `consumer` label is the internal sentinel
`__cardinality_overflow__~sha256:ferrum-edge/api-chargeback/overflow/v1`,
preserving billable totals while losing only per-identity attribution.
The aggregate overflow rows are created and their missing bytes reserved
atomically while staging, before the cache generation can serve. There
is one row per priced status, one shared status-0 bandwidth row when
bandwidth is priced, or one row per stream proxy. Global instances also
reserve unknown-proxy fallback rows in their own and all known namespaces.
Rows stay pinned while a cache generation owns them; unused preallocations
consume estimated bytes but do not appear as billing series. Ordinary
admission leaves an additional matrix of reload headroom. This cannot
guarantee that a larger matrix or repeated repricing fits beside history.
That sentinel lives in the digest-form billing-identity class, so a real
authenticated or configured identity can never share its registry key.
Billing identities are never prefix-truncated: an external identity
claim above 512 bytes is rejected at authentication, and any remaining
oversized value is represented as a prefix plus a domain-separated
SHA-256 digest of the complete value.
Runtime-only admission (not expressible here): every enabled instance
must resolve to the same shared tunables and the same projection; a
`schema_ref` must name a definition a `transaction_log_schema` plugin
registered; a status code must not appear in more than one tier across
the whole `pricing_tiers` array; `max_retained_bytes` must hold twice
the configured overflow-row matrix, and a reload whose not-yet-created
overflow rows do not fit beside the billing state the live registry
retains is refused wholesale when a node builds that generation (not by
offline validation). This includes a budget-lowering reload needing new
fallback rows; if every fallback row already exists, a lower budget is
accepted and existing state drains through eviction. Current aggregate
rows and their cumulative exported series remain retained while pinned.
`stale_entry_ttl_seconds` /
`cleanup_interval_seconds` interact with the collection contract
described in docs/plugins.md.

currency.description:
Currency label included in Prometheus metrics and JSON output.
Informational only — the plugin does not perform currency
conversion. Trimmed at admission and rejected when the trimmed
value is empty, so a whitespace-only label cannot become a currency.

status_codes.description: Billable status codes that trigger this tier's charge. Must be real HTTP status codes in 100–599 and distinct within the tier. Ordinary HTTP uses the wire status. Native gRPC and translated gRPC-Web map final terminal codes as 0→200, 1→499, 2→500, 3→400, 4→504, 5→404, 6→409, 7→403, 8→429, 9→400, 10→409, 11→400, 12→501, 13→500, 14→503, 15→500, and 16→401; missing, malformed, unknown, or present-but-unreadable terminal codes map to 500. A status code must appear in exactly one tier; cross-tier duplication is rejected at construction.

price_per_call.description:
Charge per HTTP API call (e.g. 0.00001). Must be finite,
non-negative, and at most 1e288 so `u64` counter × price stays
finite in IEEE-754 binary64. Stored counters are converted to
binary64 before multiplication, so values above 2^53 follow
normal binary64 rounding; Ferrum applies no additional decimal
rounding. Prometheus formats 10 fractional digits.

pricing_tiers.description:
HTTP-family per-call pricing. Each tier maps a set of billable
status codes to a per-call price. Ordinary HTTP uses its wire
status; native gRPC and translated gRPC-Web use the canonical
effective-HTTP mapping of the finalized terminal grpc-status.
Stream proxies (TCP/UDP/DTLS) have no HTTP status code and use
`stream_connection_pricing` instead.

bandwidth_pricing.description:
Optional bandwidth pricing applied to both HTTP-family and stream
transactions, using the gateway-perspective `bytes_sent` /
`bytes_received` counters from the transaction-summary schema.
WebSocket sessions are billed from the parsed relay's payload byte
counters; any nonzero price keeps the proxy's WebSocket sessions on
the parsed relay (no raw tunnel copy) and is refused on a
`websocket_permessage_deflate: passthrough` proxy.

price_per_byte_sent.description:
Per-byte charge for bytes flowed client->backend. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

price_per_byte_received.description:
Per-byte charge for bytes flowed backend->client. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

stream_connection_pricing.description:
Optional per-connection pricing for stream proxies (TCP, TCP+TLS,
UDP, DTLS). Charges the configured flat fee once per session at
disconnect time. Streams have no HTTP status code so they cannot
use `pricing_tiers`.

price_per_connection.description:
Per-session charge applied at stream disconnect. Finite,
non-negative, at most 1e288 (same binary64 counter×price bound
as `price_per_call`).

render_cache_ttl_seconds.description:
How long the cached /charges response is served before rebuilding.
Unsigned 64-bit; a negative or fractional value is rejected at
construction. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance
must use the same value.

stale_entry_ttl_seconds.description:
How long an idle chargeback entry may live before it becomes
eligible for eviction. Eligibility is not deletion: an idle entry is
removed only once two delivered GET /charges exports (the admin
connection took the complete document) have collected its current
counters, and only together with every row sharing its consumer,
proxy, and currency, so uncollected billing state is never discarded
on age alone and a live cumulative series never shrinks. Unsigned
64-bit. Process-global: every enabled
api_chargeback instance must use the same value.

cache_invalidation_min_age_ms.description:
Minimum age (ms) of a render cache before record() will invalidate
it. Evaluated per format against that document's own timestamp, so
a JSON-only collector gets the same protection as a Prometheus one.
Unsigned 64-bit. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback
instance must use the same value.

cleanup_interval_seconds.description:
How often (seconds) the background task evicts entries that have
been idle longer than stale_entry_ttl_seconds AND have already been
confirmed collected by two delivered exports. Set to 0 to disable. At most
31536000 (one year); larger values are rejected because the task's
sleep deadline would overflow. Process-global: every enabled
api_chargeback instance must use the same value.

max_entries.description:
Hard ceiling on retained billing rows (complete registry entry keys)
in the shared /charges registry. One principal can occupy many slots
because keys also include proxy, status, protocol family, currency,
namespace, and prices. Charges for a new row beyond this ceiling are
folded into the fixed-cardinality internal overflow aggregate row
(`__cardinality_overflow__~sha256:ferrum-edge/api-chargeback/overflow/v1`)
when its prepared fallback exists — per-identity attribution is lost
while recorded totals are preserved. A charge outside a prepared
matrix may be dropped if no aggregate can reserve bytes; inspect
dropped_charges_total. 0 is rejected — there is no unlimited mode.
Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must use the
same value.

max_retained_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on estimated retained registry bytes, covering ordinary
billing rows and aggregate overflow rows together. The overflow rows
the configured proxies and pricing tiers can create are reserved
and created during cache staging, plus equal headroom for a pricing
reload. Admission refuses a budget that cannot hold twice that matrix.
A node also refuses the whole reload if missing fallback rows cannot
fit beside retained state under the candidate budget, including a
budget decrease needing new rows. A decrease with all rows already
present is allowed and drains existing state through eviction. Charges
outside a prepared matrix can still be dropped when a new aggregate
cannot reserve bytes; inspect dropped_charges_total. 0 is rejected.
Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must use the
same value.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Projects the per-proxy billing row inside the `GET /charges` document (`proxy_id`, `namespace`, `proxy_name`, `currency`, `protocol_family`, `total_calls`, `total_charges`, `by_status`, `bandwidth`, `stream`). Billing identity, charge accounting, registry keys, and the Prometheus exposition are unaffected. `summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, `transforms`, and every derived kind except `summary_kind` are rejected for this surface. Process-global: every enabled api_chargeback instance must resolve to the same projection because one render cache serves them all. See docs/log_schema.md.

ApiChargebackRenderSchema.description: `SummaryLogSchema` narrowed to what an `api_chargeback` billing row can actually express. The `/charges` row is an aggregate assembled into a `serde_json::Map`-backed document, so it has no HTTP/stream summary type, no RFC3339 timestamp field, no metadata map, and no member order under the projection's control: `summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, and `transforms` are rejected at construction rather than silently ignored. `omit` names and `rename` sources must be native billing-row fields, and `summary_kind` is the only derived kind representable from a row that spans many transactions (it has no single status, backend, or outcome). See docs/log_schema.md.

ApiChargebackSinkConfig.description:
Plugin: api_chargeback_sink — Durable ClickHouse charge export. At most one
effective sink is admitted per proxy after scope merging; independent
event_id keys would otherwise duplicate durable billing rows. Uses the
same `pricing_tiers`, `bandwidth_pricing`, `stream_connection_pricing`,
and `currency` fields as `api_chargeback`, then exports either
per-transaction events (`mode: per_event`) or periodic accumulator
deltas (`mode: snapshot`) to ClickHouse. Ordinary HTTP uses its wire
status for pricing. Native gRPC and translated gRPC-Web use the final
normalized grpc-status mapped to the canonical effective HTTP status.
Explicitly zero-priced tiers still count matching calls. Successful H1/H2/H3
WebSocket handshakes use the 101 tier and ws protocol label; rejected
handshakes retain their error status. Admission into memory is not durable:
pending batches and spool handoffs can be lost on abrupt process termination.
Durable events preserve that billable status, the raw HTTP status, and
the normalized gRPC status separately. Snapshot mode aggregates by every
exported categorical dimension (namespace, consumer_id, consumer_name,
proxy_id, proxy_name, route_id, billable status, raw HTTP status, final
gRPC status, and protocol) so mixed route/protocol/name traffic cannot
be labeled with first-record metadata.

At least one nonempty pricing dimension must be configured with the same
semantics as runtime `PricingConfig::has_any_pricing`: a nonempty
`pricing_tiers` array, `bandwidth_pricing` with at least one strictly
positive per-byte rate, or `stream_connection_pricing` with a strictly
positive `price_per_connection`.

OpenAPI encodes material cross-field invariants that JSON Schema can
represent accurately: `clickhouse` (with runtime-mandatory `url`) is
required; snapshot mode forbids `spool.enabled=false`; nonempty
`clickhouse.password_ref` requires `https://`, forbids disabled TLS
certificate/hostname verification, and requires a non-blank
`clickhouse.username` (the password is sent as that user's HTTP Basic
password); `clickhouse.url` must be http(s) without user-info;
`clickhouse.database` is a single identifier and `clickhouse.table` is
`table` or `database.table`, each part not starting with a digit;
`insert_query_params` may not name the reserved `database` / `query`
parameters; an enabled spool's `max_bytes` is at least 1048576;
`clickhouse.tls.client_cert_file` and
`client_key_file` must be set together; `pricing_tiers[].status_codes`
entries are unique within a tier; and batch/spool/snapshot numeric,
length, and character bounds match the constructor. Settings the
constructor ignores while `spool.enabled` is false (`dir`, `max_bytes`,
`replay_interval_secs`, `delivery_queue_capacity`) are constrained only
while spooling is enabled, which is the default.

Cold constructor validation (`validate`, Admin, file mode, and CP-DP all
share it) adds the checks that need no I/O but that OpenAPI 3.1 cannot
express safely: `retry.max_delay_ms >= retry.initial_delay_ms`;
worst-case cumulative inter-attempt delay
(`retry.max_attempts` / `retry.initial_delay_ms` / `retry.max_delay_ms`)
must not exceed 600000 ms;
`snapshot.stale_entry_ttl_secs >= snapshot.interval_secs`; ClickHouse
URL egress IP screening; whitespace-only trimming for `currency` /
`pricing_version` / `password_ref`; that a nonempty `password_ref` *is
spelled* `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>`; and UTF-8 byte bounds where `maxLength` above
counts characters instead.

Activation (serving startup) adds the checks that require local files,
the process environment, or the filesystem, and therefore do NOT run
under `ferrum-edge validate`: resolving `password_ref` to a set
environment variable, reading/parsing the TLS CA and client
certificate/key files, and creating the spool tree with private
permissions (`ensure_private_dir`). A configuration accepted by
`validate` can still abort serving startup on a node missing those
files or variables.

mode.description:
Export one event per transaction or periodic snapshot deltas.
Snapshot mode requires spool.enabled=true for durable delta delivery.
Snapshot accumulator identity is every exported categorical field:
namespace, consumer_id, consumer_name (empty when absent), proxy_id,
proxy_name, route_id (empty when absent), billable status_code, raw
http_status_code, final grpc_status, and protocol. Delta emission,
last-emitted bookkeeping, and stale cleanup share that identity so
mixed routes, protocols, or display names cannot collapse into one
mislabeled aggregate.

currency.description: Currency label written to each charge event. Runtime also rejects whitespace-only values after trim, and bounds the label at 512 UTF-8 bytes: it is copied verbatim into every exported row and counts against the bounded charge-event budget, so a longer label would make every per-event export fail admission. `maxLength` counts characters, so the runtime byte bound is the stricter of the two for non-ASCII labels.

pricing_version.description: Operator-controlled pricing/version label written to each event. Runtime also rejects whitespace-only values after trim, and bounds the label at 512 UTF-8 bytes for the same reason as `currency`. `maxLength` counts characters, so the runtime byte bound is the stricter of the two for non-ASCII labels.

include_request_id.description: Include request/correlation ID metadata when present.

include_trace_id.description: Include trace ID or traceparent metadata when present.

status_codes.description: Billable status codes. Ordinary HTTP uses the wire status; gRPC/gRPC-Web uses the canonical effective mapping of final grpc-status, with missing/malformed/unknown terminal status mapped to 500.

price_per_call.description:
Finite non-negative per-call price at most 1e288 (shared
chargeback binary64 counter×price bound).

pricing_tiers.description: HTTP-family per-call pricing by billable status. A status code must appear in at most one tier. A nonempty tiers list satisfies has_any_pricing even when prices are zero.

bandwidth_pricing.description: Optional per-byte pricing for client->backend and backend->client bytes. When this is the only pricing dimension, at least one rate must be strictly greater than zero (has_any_pricing).

stream_connection_pricing.description: Optional flat per-session charge for TCP/TCP+TLS/UDP/DTLS disconnects. When this is the only pricing dimension, price_per_connection must be strictly greater than zero (has_any_pricing).

url.description: ClickHouse HTTP endpoint. Must use http:// or https://, include a host, and must not contain user-info (use username/password_ref instead).

database.description: ClickHouse database identifier sent as the INSERT `database` parameter. A single identifier of ASCII letters, digits, and underscore that does not start with a digit; dots are rejected.

table.description: ClickHouse table identifier interpolated into INSERT, as `table` or `database.table` (at most one dot). Each part uses ASCII letters, digits, and underscore and must not start with a digit, so names such as `123charges`, `.`, `ferrum.`, `a..b`, or `a.b.c` that ClickHouse cannot parse as an unquoted INSERT target are rejected at admission.

username.description: Optional ClickHouse HTTP Basic username. `null` is accepted and means unset; an empty or whitespace-only string is rejected. Required whenever `password_ref` is nonempty, because the resolved password is only ever sent as this user's HTTP Basic password.

password_ref.description:
Name of the `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable
containing the ClickHouse password (`<NAME>` uppercase
`[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`), often materialized at startup from a
`FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>_FILE`, `_VAULT`, `_AWS`, `_AZURE`,
or `_GCP` secret suffix. Any other process environment
variable, including every other `FERRUM_*` setting, is refused
at admission. Empty values are treated as unset. Because the password is sent via HTTP Basic auth,
`clickhouse.url` must use `https://` and TLS certificate/hostname
verification must stay enabled when this is nonempty after
trimming. Empty or whitespace-only values are treated as unset.
Runtime additionally requires the referenced env var to be set.

ca_file.description: PEM CA bundle for this ClickHouse endpoint.

client_cert_file.description: PEM client certificate for ClickHouse mTLS. Must be set together with `client_key_file`; the constructor rejects an incomplete pair during file/Admin/CP-DP admission rather than only when the TLS client is built.

client_key_file.description: PEM client private key for ClickHouse mTLS. Must be set together with `client_cert_file`.

verify_hostname.description: Verify the ClickHouse server hostname. Disabling this logs a warning and is for testing only, and requires `ca_file` (the server certificate is still verified against that pinned bundle) or `insecure_skip_verify: true`; without either the constructor refuses the configuration.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable certificate verification for this ClickHouse endpoint. Logs a warning and cannot be used with password_ref. Testing only.

insert_query_params.description:
Extra query parameters appended to the ClickHouse INSERT request.
Durable mode rejects `wait_for_async_insert` values that disable
persistence waits (`0`, `false`, `no`, `off`) unless
`allow_lossy_async_insert` is true. Recommended durable settings
use `async_insert=1` with `wait_for_async_insert=1`. Whenever
the wait setting is omitted, the sink pins
`wait_for_async_insert=1` on every durable request rather than
inheriting a ClickHouse user/profile default, including one
that enables `async_insert` while disabling the persistence
wait.

Credential-bearing parameter names are rejected: the exact names
`user`, `password`, `access_token`, and `session_id`, plus any
name containing `apikey`, `api_key`, `credential`, `passwd`,
`secret`, or `token`. Authenticate with `username` and
`password_ref`, which are sent as an HTTP Basic header rather
than appended to the INSERT URL. The names `database` and
`query` (case-insensitive) are reserved: the sink sets them from
`clickhouse.database` and its fixed
`INSERT INTO <table> FORMAT JSONEachRow` statement, and a second
occurrence would leave the executed statement to ClickHouse's
duplicate-parameter handling. Parameter values stay arbitrary
bounded strings, so the sink never renders the INSERT query
string in any diagnostic; failures report a structurally
redacted `scheme://host:port/redacted` endpoint. Admin audit
projections redact every value in this map.

Names are 1-128 bytes and values at most 512 bytes, and neither
may contain a Unicode control character. The `maxLength`
keywords above count characters, so for non-ASCII names or
values the runtime UTF-8 byte bound is the stricter of the two.

allow_lossy_async_insert.description:
Explicit fire-and-forget opt-in. When true, permits
`insert_query_params.wait_for_async_insert=0` (and equivalent
falsy values). ClickHouse may acknowledge buffered inserts before
persistence; spool deletion still follows a complete
exception-free HTTP acknowledgement, which is not a durability
proof in this mode. Default false keeps the durable contract.

timeout_ms.description: Per-attempt ClickHouse connect/request timeout. Bounded at ten minutes so the cross-process spool claim horizon used for stranded-claim diagnostics remains finite and strictly longer than the accepted request/retry budget. The horizon never authorizes descriptor-free claim restoration.

buffer_capacity.description: Bounded in-memory export channel capacity. With spool.enabled=false, the 80% high-water mark is telemetry only and every slot remains usable until the channel is actually full. With spool enabled, high-water overflow is diverted to durable spool delivery instead of consuming the remaining channel slots.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained-byte budget for ChargeEvent records awaiting ClickHouse export or async spool delivery.

retry.description:
Retry budget and bounded exponential backoff. OpenAPI cannot express
`max_delay_ms >= initial_delay_ms` or the worst-case cumulative
inter-attempt delay budget; the plugin constructor rejects inverted
bounds and budgets over 600000 ms during Admin/file/CP-DP admission.
`max_attempts` is the total attempt count (including the initial try);
`0` is rejected. Each delay field is capped at 60000 ms.

max_delay_ms.description:
Cap on inter-attempt delay. Runtime requires max_delay_ms >=
initial_delay_ms and that the worst-case cumulative inter-attempt
delay stays within 600000 ms.

dir.description: Spool root. Constrained only while spooling is enabled (the default): the constructor requires a nonempty, NUL-free path, and ignores `dir`, `max_bytes`, `replay_interval_secs`, and `delivery_queue_capacity` entirely when `enabled` is false.

max_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on total encoded on-disk bytes owned by this sink under
its managed namespace
(<spool.dir>/<safe_node>/<safe_plugin>/o<owner_digest>/) after
compression. While spooling is enabled it must be at least
1048576 bytes. This is a policy floor: a quota that small or
smaller refuses ordinary failed batches and snapshot chunks so
often that spooling (and snapshot finalization) cannot be relied
on, even though an individual small artifact may fit. The owner digest binds the plugin config id, Ferrum
namespace/ledger, sanitized ClickHouse endpoint, database, table, and
node id; it contains no credentials. Counts active spool files
(*.ndjson / *.ndjson.zst), atomic-write temps
(*.write-<process_tag>-<generation>.tmp), in-flight replay claims
(*.inflight), and quarantined (*.corrupt) / dead-letter payload and
metadata files. Ordinary pending writes are sized before admission;
incrementally streamed dead-letter payloads are admitted before each
bounded replay-batch append. Admission/inventory/eviction and the
corresponding mutation hold one stable ownership-bound exclusive
filesystem lock shared by every manager, plugin generation, and
cooperating Ferrum process using the namespace. The private
no-follow lock inode and spool.meta.json identity are revalidated
after acquisition; lock/identity failures refuse the mutation. The
zero-length coordination file is excluded from quota/status counts.
The oldest evictable owned file is dropped until the incoming bytes fit.
In-flight claims, temps under an active write,
and records carrying another owner's tag are never evictable, so a
write that cannot fit is rejected rather than exceeding the ceiling
or destroying another owner's or another delivery's records. Each
encoded and decoded artifact is also capped at 268435456 bytes;
zstd replay additionally applies a 200x expansion limit with a
1 MiB floor, and oversized artifacts are quarantined without first
being read or expanded without bound.

delivery_queue_capacity.description: Bounded async handoff queue for overflow and failed-batch spool writes. Request and body terminal hooks only enqueue here; compression, directory work, writes, and fsync run on the owned delivery worker. Saturation drops are counted without blocking the proxy path.

emit_zero_deltas.description: Emit unchanged keys on every snapshot tick.

cleanup_interval_secs.description: How often idle snapshot accumulator keys are evicted.

stale_entry_ttl_secs.description:
How long a snapshot accumulator key may remain idle before
entries and last-emitted state are removed. Runtime requires
`stale_entry_ttl_secs >= interval_secs`. Cleanup also refuses to
evict keys whose current totals still exceed their last durable
baseline (pending/uncommitted deltas survive TTL).

max_entries.description:
Hard ceiling on distinct snapshot accumulator identities.
New identities beyond this budget are spooled as per-event rows
through the bounded async spool delivery worker (never inline on
the terminal hook), or staged within the retained-byte budget for
the next durable emission, rather than merged into unrelated
keys. Exhaustion of both durable handoff and bounded staging
increments the explicit cardinality-rejection counter.

max_retained_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on estimated retained bytes for snapshot
accumulator identities and staged overflow events, enforced as a
single combined reservation so concurrent identity admission and
overflow staging cannot exceed it. Overflow uses the same bounded
async delivery-worker spool strategy as max_entries. Runtime
additionally requires the value to be at least one bounded
charge-event size.

schema_ref.description: Nonempty name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema` by key presence, including null values. The referenced definition must also satisfy ApiChargebackSinkLogSchema; existence and compatibility are checked at construction, since JSON Schema cannot resolve registry contents. Named definitions must first compile against the transaction-summary field inventory, so use inline schema for charge-event-only fields. Projects the exported charge-event record (the JSONEachRow row delivered to ClickHouse and the durable spool artifact that replays it), not the pricing, the accumulator identities, or the snapshot keys. Renaming a field renames the ClickHouse column the row inserts into, so the target table must agree. `summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, the `metadata` policy, `transforms`, and the `backend_host` derived kind are rejected for this surface: a charge event has no RFC3339 timestamp field, no metadata map, and no backend target. See docs/log_schema.md.

ApiChargebackSinkLogField.description: Native exported charge-event field available to omit or rename.

ApiChargebackSinkLogSchema.description: Projection of the exported charge-event record. Supports omit, rename, order, static_fields, and derived_fields. The summary_type, timestamp_format, metadata, and transforms keys are forbidden, even with null or default values. received_at remains an epoch-nanosecond integer. Derived kinds are status_class (from billable status_code), summary_kind (always charge_event), and outcome (error for status_code >= 500 or a nonzero grpc_status, otherwise ok). backend_host is unavailable. Shared constructor checks still enforce output-key uniqueness, sensitive-data restrictions, omit/rename conflicts, and order coverage against the final output keys. See docs/log_schema.md.

BasicAuthConfig.description: Plugin: basic_auth — HTTP Basic credentials verified against HMAC-SHA256 password hashes. The property set is CLOSED: `null` and an empty object both select the defaults, and no other key is accepted. (The enclosing PluginConfig `config` property is independently restricted to objects, so `null` is only reachable when this component is validated on its own.)

hide_credentials.description: Remove the `Authorization` field carrying the RFC 7617 `Basic` scheme before forwarding an authenticated request upstream, including when another mechanism wins a multi-auth chain and this credential merely rode along. Basic encodes a reusable password in reversible Base64, so it is removed by default. Only the `Basic` scheme is removed; a `Bearer` or other scheme another policy needs is left in place. Disable only when a legacy backend explicitly requires the reusable credential. A request that sends more than one `Authorization` credential (repeated field lines, or a second credential after a top-level comma) never reaches this plugin: the ingress protocol guard rejects it with 400 on every protocol.

BodyValidatorConfig.description: Plugin: body_validator — JSON Schema, XML, and gRPC protobuf validation for request/response bodies. Unknown top-level keys and unknown keys inside a protobuf_method_messages entry are rejected at construction, so a typo can never silently disable an intended rule; the plugin is fail-closed, and a rejected configuration keeps the last known-good generation. Configured JSON Schemas are compiled once at construction under an explicit draft, XML bodies are parsed by a real XML parser, and decoded protobuf messages must satisfy proto2 required-field initialization. Configuration errors use value-free field and category messages; supplied keys, paths, URIs, schema values, XML entries, and compiler diagnostics are not reproduced. Applicability follows the configured representation, never the request method: any request whose Content-Type matches content_types (or is application/grpc for protobuf configs) is buffered and validated, including GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, DELETE, PUT, PATCH, and non-standard methods. Once a configured rule applies, an empty, absent, or non-UTF-8 representation fails closed (400 request, 502 response) instead of being skipped, and native gRPC always runs frame validation. The only exemptions are protocol-defined: empty terminal gRPC error replies (a single valid non-zero grpc-status), and responses that carry no content by status/method semantics (1xx, 204, 205, 304, and responses to HEAD). Early before_proxy inspection prefers a rewritten UTF-8 request_body metadata view when present, falls back to raw buffered bytes when no text view exists, then the transport-proven-empty witness, and otherwise fails closed; the final request-body hook validates the exact backend-visible bytes. A request that declares a non-identity Content-Encoding is not judged early at all: the shared backend-visible representation gate decodes it under bounded, budget-charged limits and the final request-body hook validates the resulting plaintext before any byte reaches the backend, so a valid gzip JSON/XML upload succeeds while an undecodable coding is still refused. Representation-gap diagnostics are fixed strings and never echo body bytes. gRPC protobuf validation covers native gRPC and gRPC-Web (binary and text) framing in both directions, including a translated gRPC-Web response after the grpc_web plugin re-framed it; only methods a configured descriptor applies to are buffered, so unenrolled streaming RPCs keep streaming. Protobuf decoding is bounded before reflection (message, value, and 32-level depth budgets, for every descriptor pool) and its decompressed and reflected working set is charged to the aggregate decode budget; a budget refusal is a 503 / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED capacity terminal. Response validation applies only to response_status_codes (default 2XX) and never to 206/226 fragments; an empty synthetic success (for example an empty response_mock body) is validated like an empty backend response. Every constraint below mirrors a runtime admission rule, so a configuration this schema accepts is one BodyValidator::new accepts, except for two dependencies that are node-local and cannot be expressed statically: protobuf_descriptor_path must name a readable FileDescriptorSet, and every configured message type must resolve inside it (and reject_unsupported_media_types paired only with response-direction protobuf_method_messages entries is refused at runtime).

json_schema.description: JSON Schema for request body validation. Compiled at plugin construction under json_schema_draft; a malformed schema, an unknown or unsupported keyword shape, an invalid type name, a non-local $ref/$dynamicRef, a non-fragment $id/id, a $vocabulary declaration, a $schema naming another draft, or a schema exceeding the 32-level / 20000-node budget fails construction. Reference and identifier policy applies only at actual schema positions; property/definition names and unreferenced literal annotation/instance objects are not interpreted as keywords. A supported local URI-fragment JSON Pointer makes its object/boolean target an actual schema even under a normally literal or unknown container; pointer percent-decoding, escaping, root handling, and cycles match the validator library. Draft 7 walks definitions but not $defs unless directly referenced; Draft 2020-12 walks both. Budgets count every JSON node in the supplied value.

json_schema_draft.description: JSON Schema dialect used to compile json_schema and response_json_schema. There is no auto-detect mode; a schema whose $schema names a different draft is rejected. $dynamicRef has reference semantics only under draft2020-12 and remains an unknown, inert keyword under draft7.

required_fields.description: Simple required field names in request body. Empty entries are rejected at construction; an empty list simply configures no required-field rule.

validate_xml.description: Enable XML well-formedness validation. The body must parse as a single well-formed XML document (one root element, valid names, attribute grammar and uniqueness, valid characters, declared entity references, no text outside the root). The original text is parsed without Unicode whitespace trimming. External SYSTEM/PUBLIC identifiers on the DOCTYPE or an entity declaration are always rejected; external entities are never retrieved.

required_xml_elements.description: Required XML element names, matched against parsed element names. A bare name matches that local name in any namespace; Clark notation ("{http://example.com/ns}item") requires the expanded namespace URI and local name to match, and "{}item" requires no namespace. An entry that opens Clark notation without closing it, or whose local name is empty or is not an XML NCName (no whitespace, markup, braces, or "prefix:local" spelling), is rejected at construction: the matcher compares against parsed local names, so such an entry could never be satisfied by any well-formed document.

xml_max_entities.description: Max <!ENTITY declarations allowed in an XML DOCTYPE before the body is rejected as a possible entity-expansion (billion-laughs) attack. Applies to request and response XML when well-formedness validation runs.

xml_reject_nested_entities.description: Reject XML whose entity definitions reference other general entities (the billion-laughs expansion signature). Entity declaration names and general/parameter entity references are read with the XML Name grammar, the same production the parser uses, so a non-ASCII entity name is subject to the restriction rather than invisible to it. When this is enabled, an entity declaration the policy cannot read a replacement text out of is refused outright rather than counted as safe.

content_types.description: Request media types to validate. Matching uses the Content-Type type/subtype essence only (parameters stripped, OWS trimmed, ASCII case-insensitive). An entry of the form type/*+suffix is an RFC 6838 structured-suffix pattern matching any type/name+suffix with a non-empty name (for example application/problem+json), except the gRPC-family types application/grpc+*, application/grpc-web+*, and application/grpc-web-text+*. Distinct neighbors such as application/json-seq and parameter values that merely contain a configured string do not match. An empty list is rejected (omit the field for the defaults), as are empty or parameter-only entries; malformed actual headers do not match and are skipped (or refused with 415 under reject_unsupported_media_types).

response_json_schema.description: JSON Schema for response body validation. Compiled at plugin construction under json_schema_draft with the same fail-closed rules as json_schema. Response-side violations are reported to the client without the rejected upstream value or its instance location.

response_required_fields.description: Required field names in response. Empty entries are rejected at construction; an empty list configures no required-field rule.

response_validate_xml.description: Enable response XML well-formedness validation with the same exact- text parsing and external DOCTYPE/entity identifier rejection as validate_xml.

response_required_xml_elements.description: Required XML element names in responses, with the same parsing, Clark-notation, and XML NCName admission rules as required_xml_elements.

response_content_types.description: Response media types to validate. Same type/subtype and structured-suffix pattern matching semantics as content_types (parameters stripped; neighbors, parameter collisions, and malformed headers do not match). An empty list is rejected.

response_status_codes.description: Upstream response statuses response validation applies to: exact integer statuses and/or status classes 1XX-5XX (case-insensitive X). Defaults to 2XX, so a backend error document (404, 422, 500, ...) keeps its own status and body instead of being judged against the success schema and replaced by a 502. Partial (206) and delta (226) responses are fragments and are never validated. An empty list is rejected.

enforcement_mode.description: block rejects violations (400 request, 415 unsupported request media type, 502 response). log_only evaluates every configured rule but always continues, never claims the shared representation gates (so a content-coded body is recorded as uninspected), and records the would-be outcome. In both modes a violation is published in transaction metadata as body_validator.request_outcome / body_validator.response_outcome (rejected, would_reject, uninspected, or capacity_refused) with the matching _status and payload-free _detail keys.

reject_unsupported_media_types.description: Refuse with 415 a request that carries a body no configured request rule inspects: a missing, malformed, or comma-joined Content-Type, a media type outside content_types, an allowlisted type no rule can inspect, or a gRPC request when no protobuf request rule is configured. Bodyless requests (proven by Content-Length 0 or by the buffered transport), CONNECT requests, and frontend-classified WebSocket handshakes are unaffected; a bare Upgrade header is not. Requires at least one request validation rule.

protobuf_descriptor_path.description: Node-local path to a compiled FileDescriptorSet binary (protoc --descriptor_set_out --include_imports). CP admission is shape-only; file/DP nodes validate the local dependency, and an unavailable runtime dependency fails applicable gRPC validation closed.

protobuf_request_type.description: Default fully-qualified protobuf message type for request validation. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path.

protobuf_response_type.description: Default fully-qualified protobuf message type for response validation. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path.

request.description: Fully-qualified protobuf message type for request validation

response.description: Fully-qualified protobuf message type for response validation

protobuf_method_messages.description: Per-method message type overrides keyed by gRPC path. Requires protobuf_descriptor_path. Each key must be the gRPC method path the hooks look up — '/package.Service/Method': one leading '/', exactly two non-empty segments, and no whitespace, control character, query, or fragment. A key spelled any other way could never be selected by the exact method lookup, so it is rejected rather than admitted as an inert rule. Each entry accepts only 'request' and 'response', must set at least one of them, and any other key rejects the configuration. An entry is direction-authoritative: a direction it omits is not validated for that method, rather than falling back to protobuf_request_type / protobuf_response_type. The method is the trailing /Service/Method of the bound backend-effective path, else (request side) the synthetic :path the native gRPC ladder injects, else grpc_full_method, else the request path, so prefixes and backend base paths cannot change which entry applies and per-method rules apply on HTTP/3 and every dispatcher.

protobuf_reject_unknown_fields.description: Reject messages containing field numbers not in the descriptor, at the top level and inside every present nested, repeated, map-value, oneof, and extension message value, in both directions, under the same bounded 32-level / 50000-message walk as the initialization check. A closed (proto2) enum is judged per wire occurrence: any occurrence outside the declared set is an unknown field (refused in either order, including packed, map-value, and extension values), and a required closed-enum field with only undeclared occurrences is unset; open proto3 enums keep any number. The rejection carries a count only, never a field number or payload byte. This is independent of proto2 required-field initialization, which is always enforced: a decoded message that omits any proto2 required field, at the top level or inside a present nested/repeated/map/extension message value, is rejected regardless of this setting.

grpc_max_decompressed_size_bytes.description: Maximum decompressed gRPC protobuf payload size in bytes for both request and response validation. Positive integer matching runtime `usize` parsing. Zero is rejected so compressed input is always bounded. When omitted, inherits `FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES` when that value parses as an unsigned integer; otherwise falls back to 10 MiB (10485760). Hard ceiling 67108864 (64 MiB): a larger configured value is rejected, and an environment-inherited value above it is clamped to it. No static OpenAPI default is advertised because the effective value can be environment-derived.

BotDetectionConfig.description: Plugin: bot_detection — case-insensitive User-Agent matching. Configuration must be an object and unknown properties are rejected. `blocked_patterns` are substring matches; `allow_list` entries are word-boundary matches and are consulted before blocked patterns, so a User-Agent that contains a blocked substring can still pass if it also contains an allow-list entry as a standalone token (useful for permitting GoogleBot while blocking generic `bot` patterns). The word-boundary anchoring on the allow list prevents an allowed token from being smuggled inside an otherwise-blocked agent. A no-op config (empty `blocked_patterns` while missing User-Agent headers are allowed) is rejected; an allow-list alone is not enforcement. The User-Agent is client-controlled and spoofable, so this is a coarse filter, not strong bot verification. Pattern entry whitespace follows Rust `str::trim` Unicode `White_Space` semantics. A User-Agent whose every field line is empty or only spaces/tabs is treated as missing. A present User-Agent field line that is not valid UTF-8 cannot be matched, so the request is rejected with `custom_response_code` regardless of `allow_list` and `allow_missing_user_agent`. HTTP-family only.

blocked_patterns.description: User-Agent substrings to reject (case-insensitive). Specifying this field with an array replaces the defaults entirely. Entries are trimmed and must contain a non-whitespace character. `null` is the same as omission and installs the documented defaults. Setting the field to `[]` is valid only when `allow_missing_user_agent: false` creates a missing-header reject path; an allow-list alone is not enforcement.

allow_list.description: User-Agent tokens that always pass, evaluated before `blocked_patterns` (allow wins). Matching is case-insensitive and word-boundary anchored, so an entry only matches when it appears as a standalone token in the User-Agent. Entries are trimmed and must contain a non-whitespace character. `null` is the same as omission and installs an empty allow list.

allow_missing_user_agent.description: When true (default), requests with no User-Agent header, or only empty/whitespace-only User-Agent values, pass — this keeps health-check and load-balancer probes working. Set to false to reject them with `custom_response_code`. A non-UTF-8 User-Agent is not treated as missing and is rejected either way. `null` is the same as omission and selects `true`.

custom_response_code.description: For non-gRPC requests, the final 4xx or 5xx HTTP status returned with the JSON rejection body. Native gRPC requests instead return an empty-body HTTP 200 trailers-only error with this HTTP status mapped to `grpc-status` and `Forbidden` in `grpc-message`. Values outside 400–599, including informational and no-body status codes, and non-integer values are rejected. `null` is the same as omission and selects 403.

CompressionConfig.description: Plugin: compression — Null or an empty object uses defaults. On-the-fly HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 response compression (gzip, Brotli, and opt-in zstd) and optional request decompression. Process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_GZIP_ENABLED and FERRUM_COMPRESSION_BROTLI_ENABLED gates intersect with every instance and default to true; an instance with no remaining usable algorithm after those gates fails admission. Gzip/Brotli codec CPU is offloaded via a bounded spawn_blocking admission pool acquired only immediately before the blocking worker, while response buffering for compression is admitted by an independent bounded response-buffer semaphore reserved in before_proxy and held across the encode (with ineligible owners leaving the slot on the context for sibling handoff), so a slow backend cannot starve request decompression; authenticated /metrics exports ferrum_compression_codec_{admitted,saturated,join_failures,worker_failures}_total and ferrum_compression_response_buffer_{admitted,saturated}_total. Encode abort after a committed Content-Encoding restores identity headers on shared buffered H1/H2/H3 paths when identity remains acceptable, or replaces the response with 406 when the client excluded identity, rather than emitting mislabeled or explicitly refused plaintext. Optional request decompression parses Content-Encoding as an ordered coding list (OWS-tolerant), decodes supported chains in reverse order under hard-capped size/amplification limits, and fails closed on malformed/unsupported members. That decode runs on the shared strict, budget-charged decoder: br refuses Large Window Brotli, and the decoder's own heap plus every output growth (and, on a stacked chain, the previous pass's still-resident buffer) is reserved against FERRUM_REQUEST_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES before allocation, so an aggregate-budget refusal is a gateway 503 rather than a client 400. Normalization happens exactly once per request on every frontend: H1/H2 dispatch now receives the ownership context the native H3 path always had, so an already-normalized upload is never decoded a second time. Content negotiation follows RFC 9110 §12.5.3, treats x-gzip as the gzip compatibility token, strictly parses qvalues, and includes the identity coding: an uncoded response is acceptable by default at q=1 unless refused with `identity;q=0` or `*;q=0` without a more-specific identity entry (a nonzero wildcard does not lower identity quality), the most preferred acceptable representation wins (server preference order breaks ties toward compression), and the response is rejected with 406 when identity is unacceptable and no acceptable coded representation can be produced — including size/content-type ineligibility, identity range/delta responses (206/226, Content-Range, or the internal range marker), and `response_caching` HIT paths. That refusal is taken only after every effective instance in the chain has declined, so an earlier instance whose algorithms or content_types cannot serve this response never pre-empts a later sibling that can, and a committed coding is never turned back into a 406. Identity range/delta responses are non-transformable (forwarded unchanged when identity is acceptable); no-body statuses and already-encoded upstream responses remain protocol hard skips. Reject-path 406 replacement is scoped to cache HITs so auth/policy rejection statuses are not masked. Negotiation reads the client's own Accept-Encoding captured at request init, so a request_transformer rule that rewrites or removes the backend-facing header cannot select a coding the client refused or erase an identity;q=0. Honors request/response Cache-Control: no-transform and strong ETag validators by skipping compression (still 406 when that leaves no acceptable representation), unless weaken_strong_etag opts into compressing with a weak validator. When FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES (or the route ceiling) is unlimited or above 32 MiB, compression is length-gated: only a response whose backend declares a Content-Length within min(32 MiB, the buffered-response fallback) is buffered and encoded, other responses stream identity (406 when identity is refused), and plugin construction logs a warning. A later hook relabeling a committed Content-Encoding to a coding the instance cannot produce aborts the encode to identity (or 406). Unknown top-level keys are rejected at construction (for example `min_content_lenght` or `gzip_leveel`). Invalid generations fail file/admin/database/CP-DP admission while KeepLastKnownGood retains the prior published instance. Response buffering is only forced for responses this instance could actually encode: already-encoded origin responses and responses whose known Content-Length is below min_content_length stream instead of being collected. Multiple effective instances compose with first-wins ownership: the first instance that claims a supported request Content-Encoding owns strip+decode exactly once; the first instance that commits a gateway response Content-Encoding owns the single coding layer. Siblings must not delete the owner's request marker or compress again. An earlier identity/Vary-only decision does not block a later compress. H1/H2 and native H3 share the same sequential transform loops; reload snapshots remain atomic. WebSocket, gRPC message compression, and raw stream compression are separate protocol mechanisms.

algorithms.description: Enabled compression algorithms in server preference order (ties in client q-value go to the earlier entry). `zstd` (RFC 9659) is opt-in and never part of the default; it has no process-wide gate, and listing it also enables zstd request decompression when decompress_request is true. Each algorithm may appear once (`brotli` is an alias of `br`, so the pair is a repeat and is rejected at construction). An empty array is rejected at construction, as is an array left with no usable codec after the process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_* gates. Null selects the default.

min_content_length.description: Skip compression for bodies smaller than this (bytes). Must be an unsigned 64-bit integer that also fits usize on this host. Null selects the default.

content_types.description: Content-type whitelist (at most 64 rules). Defaults to 10 common text/application types. Every entry must be a bare ASCII type/subtype media type, or a type/* range covering every subtype of one top-level type, with no surrounding whitespace and no parameters; an empty array, an empty entry, a non-ASCII entry, a parameter-bearing or whitespace-only entry, any other `*` (*/*, */json, application/vnd.*+json), and a repeat of an earlier entry (compared case-insensitively) are all rejected at construction, because the matcher could never equal such a rule. Explicit null is rejected (unlike the other optional fields) — omit the key for the defaults. Matched as an exact media-type token (before the first semicolon, ASCII case-insensitive), or by top-level type for a type/* rule; response parameters like ; charset=utf-8 are ignored. Substring matching is not used, so application/jsonp does not match application/json.

max_decompressed_request_size.description: Zip bomb protection: max decompressed request body size in bytes (default 10 MiB). Hard-capped at 32 MiB; when request decompression is enabled, it must also be ≤ FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES if that wire limit is set. Per-layer/cumulative decode ceilings and a 1024:1 raw-to-decoded amplification bound apply, and the decode's complete working set (strict decoder heap plus output capacity) is charged to FERRUM_REQUEST_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES before allocation — a budget refusal is the gateway capacity terminal (503), not a 400. Null selects the default.

remove_accept_encoding.description: Strip Accept-Encoding from backend request so backend sends uncompressed. Only applied when the instance still has at least one usable response codec after process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_* gates. Null selects the default.

gzip_level.description: Gzip compression level (0=no compression, emits gzip framing only; 1=fastest, 9=best). Null selects the default.

brotli_quality.description: Brotli quality (0=fastest, 11=best). Null selects the default.

zstd_level.description: Zstandard compression level for the opt-in `zstd` algorithm (1=fastest, 19=best). Capped at 19 because higher levels use a window above the 8 MB RFC 9659 allows for the zstd content coding. Null selects the default.

weaken_strong_etag.description: Opt-in. When false (default), a response carrying a strong ETag is never compressed, so the validator is preserved. When true, such a response is compressed and the coded variant carries the weak form of the validator (W/"…"); an origin weak validator is kept as is, and an aborted encode restores the origin validator on the identity body. An ETag with no weak form (unquoted, list-valued, or containing invalid characters) and a strong ETag a later hook adds still keep the response uncoded. Null selects the default.

decompress_request.description: Enable decompression of gzip/brotli request Content-Encoding lists (plus zstd when `algorithms` lists it; one complete frame per layer, window capped at 8 MB, trailing bytes refused) (OWS-tolerant ordered chains; malformed/unsupported members fail closed). Each gzip/x-gzip layer must contain exactly one complete member with a valid trailer and no remaining bytes; additional members (even empty ones), padding, and trailing data fail closed with 400. The shared request representation gate applies the same rule; a claimed response representation rejects these forms with its existing 502 inspection error (gRPC INTERNAL). Unclaimed encoded responses retain their existing pass-through behavior. Null selects the default.

CorrelationIdConfig.description: Plugin: correlation_id — With the default inbound_policy preserve, keeps a non-empty inbound ID only when it is at most 256 bytes and matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]+; every missing or rejected value is replaced (never truncated) with UUID v4. With inbound_policy generate, every HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket request receives a fresh gateway-owned UUID v4 that overwrites any inbound value on that header. Multiple instances retain independent authoritative values in private typed request/session state. The first instance in priority order owns the canonical request_id, while every instance forwards and echoes only its own private value, including on successful H1/H2/H3 WebSocket handshakes. Public request_id and correlation_id.instance.* metadata are compatibility projections; later plugin writes cannot change authoritative forwarding, echo, or logged values.
