Effective instances on one proxy chain that overlap on any supported protocol must normalize to distinct header_name values and have distinct effective priorities; use priority_override to make canonical ownership deterministic. Disjoint protocol owners do not conflict. Admission and reload reject either overlapping ambiguous composition. Runtime admission also rejects the deployment-specific effective FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER value case-insensitively; that dynamic exclusion cannot be expressed by this static schema. CP/DP config sync requires every DP to advertise the same effective value as the CP before configuration is distributed. The top-level config must be an object; null fields select defaults.

header_name.description: Header name (surrounding Rust `str::trim` Unicode White_Space is trimmed and the name is lowercased internally). After trimming, the token must be a valid `http::HeaderName` of at most 65,535 ASCII bytes. Used for the inbound preserved value and this instance's outbound/echoed value. Protocol-managed request, forwarding, framing, connection, content-coding, W3C tracing context (traceparent and tracestate), gRPC status, WebSocket handshake, and internal marker names (including early-data, x-grpc-web-mode, and x-ferrum-original-content-encoding), plus security-sensitive credential/authentication names, every name in the gateway-owned x-consumer-* consumer assertion namespace (with `_` equivalent to `-`, so x_consumer_role is included), the other gateway-owned backend assertions that outbound refresh strips and regenerates (x-authenticated-identity and the GeoIP x-geo-country, either spelling), the literal x-real-ip that backend builders drop from untrusted peers, and the gateway-owned x-ferrum-hops proxy hop count (either spelling), are rejected case-insensitively. Runtime also rejects the effective deployment-specific FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER value case-insensitively; CP/DP config sync enforces one matching value across the cluster before distribution. Null selects x-request-id.

echo_downstream.description: When true, this instance's resolved ID is added to ordinary responses, rejection responses, and successful H1 Upgrade/H2-H3 Extended CONNECT WebSocket handshakes. Null selects true.

inbound_policy.description: preserve keeps a well-formed inbound ID (at most 256 bytes matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]+) and replaces only missing or rejected values. generate always mints a fresh UUID v4 and overwrites any inbound value, so the backend header, downstream echo, canonical request_id log metadata, WebSocket handshake echo, and response_caching generated-value provenance all carry the gateway-owned ID. TCP/UDP sessions always generate. Null selects preserve.

oneOf.description: Native wildcard-subdomain matcher such as `*.example.com`. The suffix is a DNS hostname, normalized to IDNA ASCII at config load; Unicode `*.bücher.example` matches `shop.xn--bcher-kva.example`. URL delimiters, percent-encoding, whitespace, control characters, IP literals, and empty labels are rejected. After IDNA conversion, labels must contain only ASCII letters, digits, or interior hyphens, at most 63 bytes each and 253 bytes total excluding an optional trailing root dot. A root dot is preserved for matching. The bare domain does not match. Runtime also enforces 512 UTF-8 bytes per matcher; JSON Schema maxLength counts characters.

CorsConfig.description:
Plugin: cors — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing. Unknown keys, null values,
non-object configs, and an omitted origin policy are rejected. Actual
requests evaluate origin/credentials/exposure behavior; method/header
allow-lists and max age govern preflight only. Denials return a JSON
object with a fixed error message, without reflecting method/header
values. Successful preflight bodies remain empty. Participating CORS
policies merge Origin into Vary even for originless and unmatched
responses, preserving existing Vary tokens and Vary: *.

oneOf.description: Istio StringMatch-shaped origin matcher: EXACTLY ONE of exact / prefix / regex (no extra or unknown keys). Empty or multi-key objects are rejected at config time.

prefix.description: Literal byte-prefix of the request Origin header (case-sensitive), e.g. "https://app.". Matching is an unbounded starts_with with no origin parse, so a prefix constrains the host ONLY when it terminates at an origin boundary — the form "scheme://host:" (trailing port separator, any port). Every other shape, including a bare "https://app.example.com" (which also matches "https://app.example.com.evil.net"), "https://app.", "https://app.example.com:8443", "https://" and "h", is effectively universal: admitted without credentials, but it cannot be combined with allow_credentials.

regex.description: RE2 pattern that must FULLY match the request Origin header. Compiled once at config construction/reload (never per request) under explicit bounds — 512 pattern bytes, a 64 KiB compiled-program limit, a 64 KiB lazy-DFA limit, and an AST nesting limit of 24. An invalid or over-budget pattern is rejected with a field-specific error. A regex that admits the opaque `null` origin or every origin of a scheme (for example `.*` or `https://.*`) cannot be combined with allow_credentials.

allowed_origins.description: Required permitted-origin policy, bounded at 64 entries. Each entry is either a string — NATIVE syntax: `"*"` for intentional allow-all, an exact `scheme://host[:port]` origin canonicalized on the cold config path, or a `*.suffix.com` wildcard-subdomain pattern — or an Istio `StringMatch`-shaped object carrying exactly one of `exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. The two families are SEPARATE matcher semantics: object `exact`, `prefix`, and `regex` all retain literal Istio semantics and are never broadened by the native form's canonicalization or wildcard interpretation, so `{"exact": "*.example.com"}` matches only that literal string while the plain string `"*.example.com"` matches every subdomain.

allowed_methods.description: Preflight-only allowed methods returned in Access-Control-Allow-Methods. Method tokens are case-sensitive. With credentials disabled, `*` allows any valid method; with credentials enabled, it is a literal token. Multiple policies intersect these permissions without widening a sibling's policy. This list is not evaluated against the actual request method. Omission uses the native direct-plugin default; with `unmatched_preflights`, omission/empty preserves Istio's empty list.

allowed_headers.description: Preflight-only allowed request headers returned in Access-Control-Allow-Headers. Header names are case-insensitive. With credentials disabled, `*` permits every header except Authorization, which must be listed explicitly by every policy. With credentials enabled, `*` is a literal token. Multiple policies intersect these permissions; a literal `*` is omitted if dropping credentials would give it wildcard meaning in the final response. The same literal-token rule applies to allowed_methods. This list is not evaluated against headers on the actual request. Omission uses the native direct-plugin default; with `unmatched_preflights`, omission/empty preserves Istio's empty list.

exposed_headers.description: Response headers exposed to browser JavaScript, returned in Access-Control-Expose-Headers. Header names are case-insensitive. With credentials disabled, `*` exposes every response header; with credentials enabled, it is a literal token. Multiple policies intersect exposure: an uncredentialed `*` intersected with an explicit list keeps that list, and a credentialed policy's literal `*` is omitted rather than widened when the aggregate disables credentials. Bounded at 128 entries of at most 256 bytes each, like allowed_methods and allowed_headers.

allow_credentials.description: Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Incompatible with wildcard origins (native `"*"` / `{exact: "*"}` logs a warning and disables credentials), opaque exact `null`, and an effectively universal prefix or regex (refused at config load rather than silently weakened). A prefix must terminate at an origin boundary — only the `scheme://host:` form pins the host, because prefix matching is an unbounded starts_with; a regex must not match `null` or every origin of a scheme (universality is probed against reserved DNS-shaped origins, so a hostname-character-class pattern such as `https://[\w.-]+` is effectively universal), and must provably pin the host: every literal suffix of the pattern must be a complete origin, contain the literal authority, or end in a fixed non-public domain after its first dot (optionally with a literal port, after a trailing :[0-9]+ or optional (?::[0-9]+)? port is set aside), or every match must start with a literal scheme://host:. Numeric (IP-literal) suffixes never count. A native `*.suffix` wildcard is refused with credentials when the suffix is a single label, a public suffix, or has a Public Suffix List rule beneath it (`*.com`, `*.co.uk`, `*.github.io`, `*.run.app`, `*.amazonaws.com`).

allow_private_network.description: Private Network Access opt-in. When true, a preflight from an allowed origin that carries `Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true` is answered with `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true` (locally or, with preflight_continue, on the forwarded response). The field is never sent on actual responses or on preflights that did not ask, and a backend's own value is always stripped. With multiple policies, every matching policy must opt in.

max_age.description: Preflight cache duration in seconds, from 0 through 18446744073709551615. Native direct-plugin omission defaults to 86400; translated Istio omission remains absent.

preflight_continue.description: Pass allowed preflights to the backend. Backend status/body are retained, but every Access-Control response field is replaced by the complete gateway-authoritative policy.

unmatched_preflights.description: Istio projection marker. `forward` preserves omitted, `UNSPECIFIED`, and `FORWARD` behavior; `ignore` returns a local 200 without CORS authorization fields. Its presence also preserves omitted/empty method and header lists and omitted max age instead of applying native direct-plugin defaults. It is mutually exclusive with `preflight_continue`.

CorsExactOrigin.description: Exact HTTP(S) origin. The runtime URL parser additionally validates the host and port and canonicalizes scheme/host case, default ports, IDNA, IPv4, and IPv6. Exact `*` is Istio's allow-all value. JSON Schema maxLength counts characters; runtime admission additionally enforces the 512-byte UTF-8 matcher budget.

CorsLiteralExactOrigin.description: Istio `StringMatch.exact` origin matcher. LITERAL semantics: compared byte-for-byte and case-sensitively against the request `Origin` header with NO canonicalization and NO wildcard interpretation, so a value such as `*.example.com` stays the exact string upstream assigns it instead of becoming the native wildcard-subdomain matcher. The single exception is `*`, which Istio itself defines as allow-all. Whitespace-only values are rejected; the value is bounded at 512 bytes.

DisconnectCause.description: Stream session termination cause. `gateway_policy` is a gateway admission or dispatch-policy decision before any backend was selected (for example opaque-TLS SNI fail-closed refusal).

ErrorClass.description:
Stable classification of a backend dispatch failure. Emitted on
`TransactionSummary.error_class` / `StreamTransactionSummary.error_class`
and used by alert rules. `graceful_remote_close` is the HTTP/3 backend's
spec-legal teardown signal (RFC 9114 §8.1) — the request still 502s but
the connection stays H3-capable. `dispatch_policy_rejected` covers
terminal gateway decisions taken before any backend dial (for example
an unsupportable backend TLS SNI override) and is intentionally not a
connection error, so retry policies do not fire.
`gateway_buffer_capacity` is the gateway's process-wide budget for
*retained* (buffered) response bodies refusing another response: the
backend answered correctly and within every configured per-response
ceiling, so the refusal is gateway-local transient capacity. It is
health-neutral (no circuit-breaker, passive-health, or
adaptive-concurrency effect) and not retried, and it surfaces as HTTP
`503` or gRPC `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` — never as a backend `502` /
`response_body_too_large`.
`backend_connection_limit` is the gateway refusing to open one more
physical backend connection because the destination is already at its
DestinationRule `connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections` ceiling. Nothing was
dialed, so it is health-neutral (no circuit-breaker, passive-health,
load-balancer-penalty, or adaptive-concurrency effect) — a saturated
operator-configured ceiling must never eject a healthy destination —
while still being pre-wire, so `retry_on_connect_failure` may rotate to
another load-balanced target with its own admission lane.
`trust_withdrawn` is a gateway-to-mesh transport refused because an
accepted gateway trust publication withdrew an authority: the connection
was dialed under the outgoing trust generation, or a checked-out
transport was retired before it could open the next stream. Nothing was
sent, so it is health-neutral for the same reason as
`backend_connection_limit` — withdrawing a root is gateway policy, not
evidence about the destination workload — while staying pre-wire, so a
retry re-dials under the freshly published trust generation.

FaultInjectionConfig.description: Plugin: fault_injection — Probabilistic aborts and latency injection for chaos testing. HTTP-family faults run in before_proxy; TCP/UDP/DTLS session admission faults run on stream connect; UDP/DTLS also apply per-datagram faults on on_udp_datagram (client→backend) in isolated session workers without blocking the shared recv loop. Each fault side is decided once per first contact: a session's first client→backend datagram (the plain-UDP opening packet, or the first DTLS application datagram after an admitted handshake) has its abort decided only by stream connect and its delay only by the datagram hook. Optional `match.headers` targets HTTP-family requests and `expires_at` ends the experiment.

status_code.description: Final HTTP status returned when the abort fault triggers. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 503.0) are accepted as integers.

percentage.description: Abort probability as a percentage. Positive values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to that first bucket.

grpc_status.description: Optional gRPC status emitted only for native application/grpc requests; plain HTTP, WebSocket, and gRPC-Web rejects omit it. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 14.0) are accepted as integers.

body.description: HTTP response body returned with the abort. Null is equivalent to omission and yields an empty body. Non-gRPC responses label a body that parses as JSON `application/json` and every other body, including empty, `text/plain`. Native gRPC still normalizes to trailers-only.

duration_ms.description: Delay duration before continuing or aborting, capped at one minute. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 80.0) are accepted as integers.

percentage.description: Delay probability as a percentage. Positive values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to that first bucket.

runtime_overlay_scope.description:
Optional RTDS scope containing at least one non-whitespace
character after Rust `str::trim` Unicode White_Space trimming;
null is equivalent to omission. The published pattern uses the same
White_Space set as Rust (including U+0085, excluding U+FEFF), not
ECMAScript `\S`. The accepted request epoch captures
`ferrum.fault_injection.<scope>.abort_percent` and `.delay_percent`
atomically with this plugin config. Missing or malformed keys fall
back independently to the static percentage.

match.description: Optional blast-radius targeting; null is equivalent to omission. An HTTP-family request is faulted only when every configured header is present on the client-sent request with a field line exactly equal to the configured value; unmatched requests are never faulted and consume no roll. Raw TCP connections and UDP/DTLS datagrams carry no request headers, so an instance with `match` never faults stream or datagram traffic.

headers.description: Header name to exact expected value. Names are valid HTTP header names, matched case-insensitively and unique ignoring case; gateway-asserted names (`x-consumer-*`, the private GeoIP header, path-param headers) are rejected. Values are valid HTTP header values compared byte-for-byte (case-sensitive) against each field line. Values are redacted in non-admin projections.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp (offset required) ending the experiment; null is equivalent to omission. From this wall-clock instant every hook of the instance is a no-op. A timestamp already in the past is accepted and leaves the instance inert, so a stored config that outlives its experiment never blocks a restart or reload.

GeoRestrictionConfig.description: Plugin: geo_restriction — country-level access control backed by a MaxMind GeoIP2 / GeoLite2 `.mmdb` file. The database is fully verified and loaded into bounded owned immutable memory at construction. Files larger than 512 MiB, aggregate verified MMDB content above 512 MiB per validation generation/cache build, and records containing unsupported country codes are rejected before publication. File dependency validation is fatal in file mode and warns for absent/unreadable files in database mode. CP performs structure-only validation without opening node-local files; DP validates and refreshes its node-local files for full snapshots and affected incremental rebuilds. On runtime nodes that construct the plugin, a missing file uses `on_lookup_failure`, while a readable corrupt, incompatible, or wrong-product database is rejected. Exactly one of `allow_countries` and `deny_countries` must be non-empty. Runs on every protocol — HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, TCP, UDP. Every evaluated request or stream session records the log-allowlisted metadata `geo.decision` (`allowed`, `country_not_allowed`, `country_denied`, `lookup_failed_allowed`, `lookup_failed_denied`, `db_not_loaded_allowed`, `db_not_loaded_denied`) and, when a country was resolved, `geo.country`.

db_path.description: Filesystem path to a MaxMind GeoIP2 or GeoLite2 `.mmdb` database no larger than 512 MiB. Across one validation generation/cache build, the verified sizes of all distinct content snapshots must also total no more than 512 MiB; equivalent path spellings with identical verified content are charged once. A changed candidate overlaps the live snapshot; when their combined size exceeds 512 MiB, hot replacement is rejected and the installed database must be loaded by restarting the gateway. Required.

allow_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (case-insensitive — normalized to uppercase) that are allowed. Mutually exclusive with `deny_countries`. Example: `["US", "CA", "GB"]`.

deny_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (case-insensitive — normalized to uppercase) that are denied. Mutually exclusive with `allow_countries`.

inject_headers.description: When true, inject the resolved country code into the proxied request as the `x-geo-country` header (uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Central header materialization strips any client-supplied value even when no geo plugin is attached. The header remains absent on fail-open lookup paths unless an earlier geo instance already emitted an authoritative value; later non-injecting instances preserve that value. HTTP-family proxies only — ignored on TCP/UDP streams.

on_lookup_failure.description: Action when the client IP cannot be resolved to a country. Applies to both genuine MaxMind misses (private IPs, unallocated ranges) and to the data plane fallback path when the `.mmdb` file is missing on disk. The default `allow` is fail-open: unresolved traffic is permitted, so a missing or stale `.mmdb` silently disables the geo gate. Set this explicitly to `deny` for fail-closed behaviour. When the default is used, a one-time warning is logged at startup, and the first request-time fail-open is logged at warn.

GeoRestrictionCountryCode.description: A currently assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or XK (the user-assigned Kosovo code emitted by MaxMind). Matching is case-insensitive and runtime storage is normalized to uppercase. Other reserved, user-assigned, deleted, and alias codes are rejected.

GraphqlConfig.description: Plugin: graphql — Query depth/complexity limiting, introspection control, and per-operation rate limiting. At least one effective protection rule is required (`max_depth`, `max_complexity`, `max_aliases`, `introspection_allowed: false`, a non-empty `type_rate_limits`, or a non-empty `operation_rate_limits`). `introspection_allowed: true` alone is not an effective rule. Unknown top-level keys are rejected. Unsupported GraphQL HTTP representations fail closed with HTTP 400 GraphQL-style JSON errors (non-POST methods including GraphQL GET/`?query=` and GraphQL-over-SSE GET, non-JSON content types including `application/graphql`, missing or unparseable bodies, JSON batch arrays, APQ envelopes without an inline query document, and multipart `operations`). The plugin attaches to HTTP and WebSocket proxies so WebSocket upgrade handshakes are refused before uninspectable GraphQL-over-WebSocket frames can be admitted; it does not inspect post-upgrade frames. gRPC, TCP, and UDP are unsupported. Rate-limit counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. When `sync_mode` is `redis`, `redis_url` is required. Explicit Redis fields are validated even in local mode so latent configuration cannot become invalid only when the mode is changed. Runtime numeric fields require integer JSON encoding (for example `2`, not `2.0`); JSON Schema treats those two encodings as the same mathematical integer. Runtime also rejects invalid Redis URL shapes that JSON Schema cannot fully cross-validate with every authoring tool.

max_depth.description: Maximum allowed query nesting depth. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

max_complexity.description: Maximum allowed field count. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

max_aliases.description: Maximum allowed alias count. Admission requires an unsigned integer that fits in 32 bits, so the inclusive range is 0-4294967295.

introspection_allowed.description: Whether introspection queries are permitted. Setting this to `false` counts as an effective protection rule; the default `true` does not.

type_rate_limits.description: Rate limits by operation type. Only `query`, `mutation`, and `subscription` keys are accepted; unknown keys are rejected.

operation_rate_limits.description: Rate limits by named operation. Keys must be valid GraphQL Names (`[_A-Za-z][_0-9A-Za-z]*`).

sync_mode.description: GraphQL rate-limit counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized). Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds (must be ≥ 1). Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable

GraphqlRateSpec.description: Closed GraphQL rate limit specification. Both fields are required and must be positive integers; unknown keys are rejected.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests allowed in the window. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key.

window_seconds.description: Time window in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.

GrpcDeadlineConfig.description: Plugin: grpc_deadline — Manages the grpc-timeout metadata header. Supports all gRPC timeout units (H, M, S, m, u, n). At least one effective rule is required. When both deadline values are configured, default_deadline_ms must be less than or equal to max_deadline_ms, and headroom_ms must be less than max_deadline_ms; runtime validation enforces these cross-field relationships. Caps compose across instances independently of their order: a default injected by one instance is still clamped by another instance's max_deadline_ms. Malformed or zero client values never pass through verbatim: an enforced fallback deadline is rewritten onto the outbound header and invalid client values set bounded transaction-log metadata grpc_timeout_invalid=true. That metadata and grpc_adjusted_deadline_ms are recorded at request receipt, so they are present even when the request is rejected before the backend hook runs.

max_deadline_ms.description: Cap incoming deadlines to this value (milliseconds)

default_deadline_ms.description: Inject grpc-timeout when client omits it

headroom_ms.description: Fixed margin (milliseconds) reserved from a client-supplied grpc-timeout after every cap. Both the gateway's own RPC deadline and the forwarded grpc-timeout end this much earlier than the client's, so the gateway's DEADLINE_EXCEEDED reaches the client before the client's own deadline cancels the call. The remaining budget is floored at 1 ms. An injected default_deadline_ms is not reduced. Multiple instances reserve the largest configured value once. Must be less than max_deadline_ms when both are set.

subtract_gateway_processing.description: Plugin-checkpoint remaining-budget control. When true, the plugin writes remaining receipt-anchored milliseconds into grpc-timeout and grpc_adjusted_deadline_ms, and rejects with gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (status 4) if that remaining time is already zero. Backend H2/H3 dispatch always rewrites grpc-timeout to the remaining absolute budget independently of this flag.

reject_no_deadline.description: Reject requests missing a positive grpc-timeout. Takes precedence over default_deadline_ms. Native H2/H3 gRPC clients receive HTTP 200 with a non-OK grpc-status in the trailers-only header block; the internal plugin rejection status is not exposed as HTTP 400.

GrpcMethodRouterConfig.description: Plugin: grpc_method_router — Per-method access control and rate limiting for gRPC services. Authorizes the backend-effective gRPC path after route rewrites, listen-path stripping, backend-path composition, and initial target selection, then populates grpc_service, grpc_method, and grpc_full_method metadata with that final method. Method rules are exact `package.Service/Method` paths or service-level `package.Service/*` rules (the method segment is exactly `*`; no other wildcard or pattern syntax). At least one access or rate rule is required. Unknown top-level keys are rejected by the runtime and by this schema. Rate-limit counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. Rejections use content-type application/grpc and map to native gRPC status from the HTTP status: 403 is PERMISSION_DENIED (denied, not allowed, or an unparseable backend-effective path), 429 is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and 503 is UNAVAILABLE (fail_closed Redis outage, with no rate-limit headers). A quota 429 carries x-grpc-ratelimit-limit (the matched rule's max_requests), x-grpc-ratelimit-remaining (0), and x-grpc-ratelimit-method (the refused method, without the leading slash) as initial metadata of the trailers-only response; the state-capacity 429 (a previously unseen caller key while the local map is full) carries none of them. No retry hint is sent.

allow_methods.description: Only these gRPC methods are permitted (allowlist). Each entry is a full method path like /package.Service/Method, or /package.Service/* to permit every method of one service. Leading/trailing whitespace and one optional leading slash are normalized by the runtime. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime; JSON Schema uniqueItems can reject only byte-identical duplicates. `null` is the same as omission. An empty array is valid block-all policy.

deny_methods.description: These gRPC methods are explicitly blocked; /package.Service/* blocks every method of one service. Deny takes precedence over allow, including an exact allow entry under a denied service. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime; JSON Schema uniqueItems can reject only byte-identical duplicates. `null` is the same as omission (no deny rules).

method_rate_limits.description: Per-method rate limits keyed by full method path (e.g., /myapp.UserService/CreateUser) or by a service-level /package.Service/* rule. An exact key wins over the service-level rule for that method, and only the most specific rule is charged. An exact key is a per-method budget; a service-level key is one budget per caller pooled across every method of the service that has no exact key. Duplicate normalized keys cannot be expressed by JSON Schema and are rejected at runtime. `null` is the same as omission (no per-method rates).

default_rate_limit.description: Rate limit for every method that no exact or service-level method_rate_limits key covers. It is one budget per caller pooled across all of those methods, so request-chosen method names never create new counters. Keyed by limit_by like every other rule. On its own it is a configured rule. `null` is the same as omission (uncovered methods are not rate limited).

limit_by.description: Rate limit key. Canonical values are `ip` and `consumer`; ASCII case is ignored (`CONSUMER` and `Ip` are admitted). `null` is the same as omission (`ip`). When consumer, uses identified_consumer then authenticated_identity then client IP as fallback.

sync_mode.description: gRPC method rate-limit counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized). ASCII case is ignored. Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds (must be ≥ 1). Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable

GrpcWebConfig.description: Plugin: grpc_web — Translates between gRPC-Web (browser-compatible) and native gRPC (HTTP/2) wire formats. Supports binary (application/grpc-web) and text (application/grpc-web-text) encoding, including message-format suffixes such as +proto, +json, +thrift, and other valid +subtype values. The request message-format suffix is preserved on the native backend Content-Type (application/grpc-web-text+json dispatches as application/grpc+json); a bare type and +proto both dispatch as the canonical bare application/grpc. Request-body decoding follows request Content-Type; response encoding and Content-Type follow Accept negotiation (absent Accept defaults to the request Content-Type mode and suffix; lists, q-values, and */* / application/* wildcards are honored; Accept can select binary versus text but cannot transcode to a different message-format suffix; malformed or fully refused Accept fails closed with HTTP 406; translated responses merge Vary: Accept so caches separate variants). A media range carrying parameters other than q still matches when its type, subtype, and suffix match (so application/grpc-web-text;charset=utf-8 is acceptable), but those parameters are ignored for precedence and quality selection and cannot veto an unparameterized representation (application/grpc-web+proto;q=1, application/grpc-web+proto;version=2;q=0 is served as application/grpc-web+proto). A range whose type or suffix does not match still yields HTTP 406. Config must be a JSON object (not null); `{}` and objects that only set `expose_headers` are accepted. Unknown keys are rejected. When a backend or intermediary response omits a valid numeric grpc-status, the response trailer frame synthesizes status from the official HTTP-to-gRPC client mapping (400→13, 401→16, 403→7, 404→12, 429/502/503/504→14, others→2); a valid supplied grpc-status remains authoritative. The client-visible HTTP status is not rewritten to 200 on this path. When such a non-200 response carries a non-gRPC entity (for example a text/plain or text/html error document), that entity is dropped rather than framed: the client receives a terminal-only gRPC-Web body carrying the mapped status, on both the streaming and buffered paths. The body trailer frame preserves backend `grpc-status` / `grpc-message`, binary `*-bin` metadata, and valid ASCII custom trailing metadata while excluding hop-by-hop, forbidden, pseudo, connection-listed, and invalid names/values; initial response headers are not copied into the frame. Multiple effective instances are supported: the first in configured order owns body translation exactly once; siblings union expose_headers only.

expose_headers.description: Additional response headers to include in Access-Control-Expose-Headers for browser CORS compatibility. grpc-status, grpc-message, and grpc-status-details-bin are always exposed. Multiple grpc_web instances union their lists in configured order. Explicit null is accepted at this field and means the empty list (unlike the plugin config object itself, where null is rejected). Each item is trimmed of surrounding spaces/tabs and must then be a non-empty HTTP field name (token characters only); empty, whitespace-only, and names containing an internal space or a colon are rejected. Accepted names are lowercased and de-duplicated in first-seen order, so entries differing only in case collapse to one.

HmacAuthConfig.description: Plugin: hmac_auth — versioned HMAC request authentication with mandatory request-body integrity protection. The Ferrum profiles (`ferrum-hmac-v2`) uses `Authorization: hmac` and a Ferrum signing base; the `rfc9421` profile verifies RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures (`Signature-Input` / `Signature`, `hmac-sha256`, key looked up by `keyid` among the Consumers' `hmac_auth` secrets). RFC 9530 defines Content-Digest. Requests must include exactly one of Digest or Content-Digest matching the original body (`rfc9421` requires Content-Digest and must cover it). Sending both headers is refused as ambiguous; unsupported algorithms and malformed members fail closed. The signing base's FIRST field is the profile version, so a signature produced under one profile can never verify under another. `ferrum-hmac-v2` (the default) signs the profile version, matched proxy namespace, credential identity, normalized authority, method, raw path, raw query, Date, literal digest value, and a mandatory client nonce, and makes each accepted request single-use by claiming that nonce against a declared replay authority before backend dispatch. A verbatim transport retry is therefore a replay and is rejected; safe retries send a fresh nonce with a recomputed signature. HBONE CONNECT and request-body-transformer compositions fail closed. The pre-authentication body path is bounded by max_body_bytes (default 10 MiB). A WebSocket handshake (HTTP/1.1 Upgrade, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Extended CONNECT) is signed over the EMPTY body: tunnel DATA is never drained as a request body, so the transport proves the handshake's empty representation from its own wire framing, and a handshake that declares a body is rejected.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Maximum allowed clock skew in seconds for the Date header freshness window. Bounded because the fixed replay retention horizon (601s) is derived from twice this ceiling, so no reload can shorten an already-admitted request's protection.

signing_profile.description: Versioned signing profile. 'ferrum-hmac-v2' requires a client nonce in the Authorization parameters, binds it into the signature, and makes each signed request single-use. 'rfc9421' verifies (never signs) exactly one RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature with alg 'hmac-sha256' (an absent alg means hmac-sha256; any other is refused). Covered components must include @method, @authority, @path, @query, content-digest, every signed_headers entry, and every required_components entry; 'created', 'keyid', and 'nonce' are required, 'expires' is enforced when sent, 'created' must be within clock_skew_seconds, and the nonce is claimed single-use like v2 (in its own replay domain). Unknown algorithms, components, component parameters, and signature parameters are refused. Supported derived components are @method (the wire method: CONNECT for an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 WebSocket Extended CONNECT), @authority, @path, @query, and @request-target (the target as sent, including HTTP/1.1 absolute form and an empty query).

replay_scope.description: Required for every profile; there is no default. Use 'shared' together with sync_mode 'redis' for any deployment running more than one gateway replica: every replica then claims each nonce through one atomic Redis SET NX EX. Use 'process' to declare a single-process deployment whose replay protection is stable across equivalent reloads but explicitly not cross-replica. There is no fallback between them — a shared-backend timeout, partition, authentication failure, or capacity failure rejects the request instead of falling back to freshness-only acceptance.

replay_max_entries.description: Capacity this process-scoped authority enforces against the shared replay lane (at most 10,000,000; use replay_scope 'shared' for more). At capacity only expired markers are reclaimed; if none can be, the request is refused (503) rather than a live marker evicted. Repeated full-live refusals are O(1) until an expiry is actually due, and a due reclamation pops only markers whose expiry has passed from an ordered expiry index, never rescanning live markers. An equivalent reload applies the new cap without forgetting live markers. Ignored for 'shared'.

signed_headers.description: Lowercase request header names every accepted signature must cover, for all profiles. Under the Ferrum profiles each is appended to the signing base, in this order, as one '\n{name}:{value}' line after the nonce, where value is the RFC 9421 section 2.1 canonical value (each field line trimmed, joined by ', '). Under rfc9421 each must appear in the covered components. A configured header missing from the request is refused (401). Signature carriers and connection-specific fields cannot be named. Omitted or empty leaves the signing base unchanged.

required_components.description: rfc9421 only (rejected with the Ferrum profiles): additional derived components every signature must cover beyond the mandatory @method, @authority, @path, @query, and content-digest. Require header fields with signed_headers.

max_body_bytes.description: Pre-authentication request-body ceiling in bytes (at most 256 MiB). Only a request whose signature already verified is buffered, and the stricter of this, the route, and the global request-body limits applies; a larger signed body is refused (413).

sync_mode.description: Replay-marker storage. 'redis' is required by (and only valid with) replay_scope 'shared'; it is what makes replay protection cross-replica. Any RESP-compatible single-endpoint server works (Redis Cluster is not supported and is screened, not assumed).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for shared replay markers. Must be non-empty when supplied. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:hmac_auth:{plugin-config-id}`, which isolates independent policies inside a namespace while keeping every replica of one policy claiming against the same keyspace. An explicit prefix is the opt-in for deliberately sharing a keyspace across policies.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

HttpLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: http_logging — Sends transaction logs to an HTTP endpoint in batches. Unknown top-level keys are rejected. `schema` and `schema_ref` are mutually exclusive. WebSocket session ends are sent as the shared session-end transaction record via on_ws_disconnect. Registration policy is KeepLastKnownGood.

endpoint_url.description: Required URL to POST transaction logs to. Must be http:// or https:// with a hostname or IP address (IPv6 authorities are allowed); empty strings and userinfo credentials (https://user:pass@host) are rejected — authenticate with custom_headers. Some collectors require a credential in the URL (Sumo Logic path token), so this value is never rendered in operational output: egress-denial, DNS/TLS, retry, slow-call, and batch-failure diagnostics show only a structurally redacted scheme://host:port/redacted form. The admin audit and non-admin read projections apply the schema-aware sensitivity contract instead, keeping only `scheme://host[:port]` with `[REDACTED_PATH]` / `[REDACTED_QUERY]` / `[REDACTED_FRAGMENT]` markers.

custom_headers.description: Key-value pairs of custom HTTP headers to include on every batch request. Names use HTTP token syntax. Values are visible ASCII plus HTAB; CR/LF and other controls are rejected. Use this for service-specific auth (e.g., DD-API-KEY for Datadog, Api-Key for New Relic) or metadata headers.

batch_size.description: Number of entries to buffer before sending a batch

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing a partial batch

max_retries.description: Retry attempts on failed batch delivery

retry_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts

buffer_capacity.description: Channel capacity — new entries are dropped when full

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes for one admitted log record. Oversized records are dropped before enqueue.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained serialized-content budget across queued, assembled, and retrying records. Admission reserves two copies plus framing before serialization and shrinks that lease to the exact retained size. Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1).

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. See docs/log_schema.md.

IpRestrictionConfig.description: Plugin: ip_restriction — IP/CIDR allow/deny enforcement. Rules are validated and compiled at config load time into sorted, merged numeric intervals; invalid IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR prefixes reject plugin creation. Request lookup is allocation-free, lock-free, and logarithmic in the number of non-overlapping intervals. The authoritative client IP is parsed/canonicalized once per request or stream session and reused by every plugin instance. IPv4 octets must use canonical unsigned decimal notation (for example, `010.1.2.3` and `+10.1.2.3` are rejected). Supports IPv4 exact and CIDR (`/0`-`/32`) and native IPv6 exact and CIDR (`/0`-`/128`). IPv4-mapped IPv6 rules normalize to IPv4, so mapped CIDRs accept only `/96`-`/128` (equivalent to IPv4 `/0`-`/32`); shorter mapped prefixes are rejected as ambiguous. CIDR prefixes must be canonical unsigned decimal (`/08`, `/+8`, and `/096` are rejected). IPv6 zone identifiers (e.g. `%eth0`) on rules or client IPs are stripped before matching; a rule's zone must be non-empty. Runs on every protocol — HTTP, gRPC, WebSocket, TCP, UDP, and DTLS. HTTP-family requests are checked per request; TCP/TLS, UDP/DTLS, and WebSocket sessions are checked once at admission, and an established session is not re-evaluated when a reload changes the policy. Responses the gateway produces before this plugin runs — route 404/405, gRPC method admission, a `cors` preflight answer, `request_termination` — still reach a denied client. Every rejection records `ip_restriction.reason` (`unparseable_client_ip`, `not_in_allow_list`, or `ip_denied`) in transaction-log metadata. Config must be an object, unknown properties and null values are rejected, and at least one of `allow` or `deny` must be non-empty.

allow.description: Allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 or IPv6). Empty list disables allow-list enforcement. Each entry must match `IpRestrictionRule`.

deny.description: Denied IP addresses or CIDR ranges (IPv4 or IPv6). Always takes precedence over an `allow` match. Each entry must match `IpRestrictionRule`.

IpRestrictionRule.description: One IP or CIDR rule admitted by `ip_restriction`. Surrounding whitespace follows Rust `str::trim` Unicode `White_Space` semantics. IPv4 octets must be canonical unsigned decimal (no leading zeros, no `+`), and CIDR prefixes must be canonical unsigned decimal too (`/8`, never `/08`, `/+8`, or `/008`). Native IPv6 follows the standard textual grammar, including `::` compression in front of an embedded dotted IPv4 tail (`2001:db8::1:192.0.2.1`). It may be bracketed and may carry a zone identifier, which must be non-empty and contain no whitespace, `/`, or `]`; CIDR prefixes sit outside the brackets. IPv4 CIDR prefixes are `/0`–`/32`; native IPv6 prefixes are `/0`–`/128`. IPv4-mapped IPv6 — any spelling whose value lies in `::ffff:0:0/96`, such as `::ffff:a.b.c.d`, `0::ffff:c000:201`, or `0:0:0:0:0:ffff::` — accepts exact addresses or CIDR `/96`–`/128` only.

JwksAuthConfig.description: Plugin: jwks_auth — Multi-provider JWKS JWT validation with claim-based authorization. JWT header kid is required and binding: a missing, empty, or unknown kid is rejected with a generic 401. There is no all-keys fallback; a known kid selects only that trusted key. A token is verified only against providers whose issuer equals its unverified iss claim, then providers that configure no issuer; providers pinning a different issuer are never tried. At most 64 providers are allowed, and for every issuer the providers sharing it plus the providers without an issuer must total at most 8 (at most 8 may omit issuer). A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose verified iss is the issuer of a provider in the same instance that requires DPoP or mTLS binding, so it cannot strip that realm's sender constraint. Verified algorithms: RS256/RS384/RS512, PS256/PS384/PS512, ES256/ES384, and EdDSA (Ed25519 OKP keys; refused while FIPS mode is enforced). ES512 is not supported. Verification is bound to the selected JWK's alg (an RSA JWK without alg is RS256).

jwks_uri.description: Direct URL to the IdP's JWKS endpoint. HTTPS is required except for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]); the name localhost does not qualify, because DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects. URL userinfo is rejected. Exactly one of jwks_uri, discovery_url, jwks, or jwks_source may be configured per provider.

discovery_url.description: OIDC discovery URL (auto-discovers jwks_uri). The discovered jwks_uri must use the same origin as the discovery URL (scheme, host, and effective port). For IdPs that serve JWKS from a different origin than discovery, configure jwks_uri directly instead. HTTPS is required except for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]); the name localhost does not qualify. URL userinfo is rejected. After the first successful resolution, discovery is re-run every jwks_refresh_interval_secs; a changed jwks_uri is adopted once its key set has usable keys, otherwise the last-known-good store is retained.

jwks.description: Inline JWKS JSON string or object

jwks_source.description: Admin-managed JWKS record: `managed://jwks/<id>#jwks` (also accepted: `managed://jwks/<id>`, `managed://<id>#jwks`, and the `#jwks-json` / `#jwks_json` fragment aliases), stored through `/admin/tls/jwks`. Exactly one of jwks_uri, discovery_url, jwks, or jwks_source may be configured per provider. Only the `managed://` scheme is accepted; a fragment or collection that selects other material, `?` options, and an invalid record id are refused at config load. The record is read from this node's managed TLS store (`FERRUM_TLS_MANAGED_STORE_PATH`): while it is present and holds a usable signing key the key set is fresh; once it is deleted, of another kind, or keyless every key is withdrawn and tokens are refused (like an expired remote set); a store that cannot be read keeps the last-read keys in grace for at most jwks_max_stale_seconds. The record is re-read every jwks_refresh_interval_secs, on an unknown kid (subject to kid_miss_refresh_cooldown_seconds), and immediately after a local `/admin/tls/jwks` write. Admin writes refuse a reference to a record that does not exist; file mode refuses to start without it; database mode warns. Namespace-bounded operator tokens may not introduce one.

issuer.description: Expected JWT iss claim — routes tokens to this provider. When set, the token MUST carry iss and it must match exactly; the issuer check alone rejects only a mismatching claim. Per RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 a present iss must be a single string: an array, object, number, boolean, or null iss is rejected even when one element matches this value. Required and must be nonblank when require_dpop is true: the DPoP replay realm is this exact issuer, so key-set or JWKS source rotation cannot reopen a proof. Issuers are compared exactly and are not URL-canonicalized. Providers in one policy that share this exact issuer share one replay realm and must agree on require_dpop; when DPoP is required they must also agree on dpop_replay_scope and, for process scope, dpop_replay_max_entries. A non-DPoP sibling for the same issuer is refused as a bearer-only bypass.

audiences.description: Accepted JWT aud claims; OR matched. No entry may be blank. When non-empty the token MUST carry aud and at least one value must match. When empty, tokens without aud are accepted and a token that carries aud is rejected because no acceptable audience is configured (RFC 7519 4.1.3).

name.description: Header name to read the token from; must be a valid HTTP header name (surrounding whitespace is trimmed)

prefix.description: Optional token prefix to strip; an empty string or null is treated as no prefix

from_params.description: Custom query parameter token locations; no entry may be blank

forward_original_token.description: Whether to forward the token-bearing header or query parameter upstream

require_exp.description: Per-provider override for requiring an exp claim. Expiry is always validated when present. A present nbf is always validated too (it is not required). exp is an RFC 7519 section 2 NumericDate (a JSON number that may carry a fractional part); a fractional exp bounds the authenticated stream exactly like an integer one, truncated toward the past so the enforced expiry is never later than the token states. nbf presence and validation are delegated to the JWT validation layer; Ferrum does not normalize a fractional nbf. JWT exp/nbf use the effective clock_skew_seconds leeway (default 0); DPoP skew is a separate proof contract.

required_scopes.description: Scopes that must all be present in the token; no entry may be blank. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must declare the same list and, when it is non-empty, the same effective scope_claim.

required_roles.description: Roles where any one must be present; no entry may be blank. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must declare the same list and, when it is non-empty, the same effective role_claim.

scope_claim.description: Per-provider override for scope claim path. A dot path with no empty segments. Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer and require scopes must resolve to the same effective path.

role_claim.description: Per-provider override for role claim path. A dot path with no empty segments. Same equivalence requirement as scope_claim.

consumer_identity_claim.description: Per-provider override for the external authenticated identity claim (falls back to global); a dot path with no empty segments. The identity is never resolved to a gateway Consumer.

consumer_header_claim.description: Per-provider override for X-Authenticated-Identity claim (falls back to global, then to this provider's effective consumer_identity_claim); a dot path with no empty segments

claim_headers.description: Per-provider claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

claim_headers_separator.description: Separator for array claim header values; must not be empty

header.description: Backend-visible request header the claim is published to; must be a valid HTTP header name. Reserved, framing, provenance, and credential-bearing destinations are additionally rejected at config load (the closed list is not expressible as a pattern).

claim.description: Dot-path claim to publish; no empty segments, and no whitespace or control characters

output_claim_headers.description: Istio RequestAuthentication jwtRules[].outputClaimToHeaders projection. An ordered list rather than a map, because one claim may be published to several headers. Destinations are gateway-owned exactly like claim_headers: each is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before validation and set only from a validated claim, so an unauthenticated or invalid request can never forge one. Duplicate destination headers, reserved/credential-bearing destinations, and invalid header names are rejected at config load; names are compared with _ treated as - (X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, X_Real_IP is reserved). Only nonblank string, integer, and boolean claims are published (Istio ClaimToHeader does not support arrays, objects, null, or floating-point numbers); anything else or a header-illegal value leaves the destination absent. A rendered claim value over 8192 bytes is omitted before fan-out.

require_mtls_binding.description: Require cnf.x5t#S256 to match the frontend client certificate. A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose iss is this provider's issuer. A provider that sets this without an issuer is admitted only when every provider in the instance also sets it; otherwise the configuration is rejected, because an unbound sibling could accept its tokens without the certificate.

require_dpop.description: Require and validate an RFC 9449 DPoP proof. Requires a nonblank exact issuer (the replay realm) and dpop_replay_scope, because an accepted proof must be made single-use against a declared replay authority. The access token is accepted under either the DPoP (RFC 9449 7.1) or Bearer authorization scheme, and the DPoP scheme is matched only against providers that set this flag. Validated proof claims are htm, htu, iat, jti and ath (RFC 9449 4.2); exp is not an RFC 9449 proof claim and is not required, but a proof that carries one is rejected once it has passed. The proof htu path is canonicalized exactly like the request path (percent-encoded pchar escapes decoded), so a proof bound to the URI the client sent matches. Proofs may be signed with ES256/ES384, RS256/RS384/RS512, PS256/PS384/PS512, or EdDSA (Ed25519; refused while FIPS mode is enforced). Equivalent providers that share one exact issuer must agree on this flag; matching order would otherwise let a sibling skip the proof. A provider without an issuer never authenticates a token whose iss is this provider's issuer.

dpop_clock_skew_secs.description: DPoP proof clock skew allowance in seconds, applied to iat (and to exp when a client sends the non-standard claim). Bounded because the fixed replay retention horizon (601s) is derived from twice this ceiling, so no reload can shorten an already-admitted proof's protection.

dpop_replay_scope.description: Required when require_dpop is true; there is no default. Use 'shared' together with sync_mode 'redis' for any deployment running more than one gateway replica: every replica then claims each proof through one atomic Redis SET NX EX. Use 'process' to declare a single-process deployment whose replay protection is stable across equivalent reloads but explicitly not cross-replica. There is no fallback between them — a shared-backend timeout, partition, authentication failure, or capacity failure rejects the protected request. Equivalent DPoP providers that share a replay domain must declare the same value; a mixed process/shared pair is refused even when Redis is configured, because matching order would otherwise claim the same proof once in the process store and once in Redis.

dpop_replay_max_entries.description: Capacity this process-scoped authority enforces against the shared replay lane. At capacity only expired markers are reclaimed; if none can be, the request is refused (503) rather than a live marker evicted. Repeated full-live refusals are O(1) until an expiry is actually due. An equivalent reload applies the new cap without forgetting live markers. Duplicate equivalent providers that share a replay domain must declare the same value. Ignored for 'shared'.

jwks_max_stale_seconds.description: Per-provider maximum monotonic age of the last validated non-empty remote JWKS. Overrides the plugin default. Zero is invalid and cannot disable bounded stale-key expiry. Applies to jwks_uri, discovery_url, and jwks_source sources (for a managed record it bounds how long the last-read keys survive an unreadable store); supplying it on an inline jwks provider is rejected. jwks_refresh_interval_secs must not exceed this value — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, enforced at config load.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Per-provider JWT exp/nbf clock leeway in seconds; overrides the plugin-level clock_skew_seconds. The authenticated-stream deadline is exp plus this leeway.

scope_claim.description: Global scope claim path; a dot path with no empty segments

role_claim.description: Global role claim path; a dot path with no empty segments

consumer_identity_claim.description: JWT claim used as the external authenticated identity; a dot path with no empty segments. The identity is scoped to the provider that verified it and is never resolved to a gateway Consumer (not by username, id, or custom_id), so Consumer-scoped policy does not apply to jwks_auth principals.

consumer_header_claim.description: JWT claim for X-Authenticated-Identity header (defaults to each provider's effective consumer_identity_claim); a dot path with no empty segments

claim_headers.description: Global claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

claim_headers_separator.description: Separator for array claim header values; must not be empty

emit_mesh_request_principal_metadata.description: Emits mesh.request_principal plus mesh JWT claim/audience metadata for direct mesh_authz request-principal and when-condition evaluation. Metadata only; it never relaxes authentication.

allow_missing_token.description: Istio RequestAuthentication semantics. When true and this is the only applicable auth plugin, a request carrying no token is forwarded UNAUTHENTICATED (an invalid token is still rejected). Mesh mode sets this on its generated RequestAuthentication instance; leave it false on a standalone gateway unless optional authentication is intended.

require_exp.description: Global default for requiring an exp claim

clock_skew_seconds.description: JWT exp/nbf clock leeway in seconds for every provider without its own clock_skew_seconds. The authenticated-stream deadline is exp plus the effective leeway, never later. DPoP proof skew is the separate dpop_clock_skew_secs.

jwks_refresh_interval_secs.description: JWKS key refresh interval in seconds. Must not exceed the effective jwks_max_stale_seconds for any remote provider. discovery_url providers also re-run OIDC discovery at this interval.

jwks_max_stale_seconds.description: Maximum monotonic age of the last validated non-empty remote JWKS. Cached keys fail closed at this deadline even if refreshes keep failing or return empty. Zero is invalid and cannot disable expiry.

kid_miss_refresh_cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum spacing between out-of-band JWKS refetches triggered by a token naming a kid the trusted key set does not contain — the observable shape of an identity-provider key rotation. At most one fetch is issued per window, so tokens carrying random identifiers cannot become a fetch storm. The triggering request is never blocked on the fetch and still fails closed; a later request verifies once the refreshed key set is published. A token with a missing or empty kid triggers nothing. Zero disables the on-demand refetch, leaving jwks_refresh_interval_secs as the only recovery path. Shared stores use the most restrictive value requested by active consumers (disabled wins, otherwise the longest cooldown).

sync_mode.description: DPoP replay-marker storage. 'redis' is required by (and only valid with) at least one provider declaring dpop_replay_scope 'shared'; it is what makes DPoP replay protection cross-replica. Any RESP-compatible single-endpoint server works (Redis Cluster is not supported and is screened, not assumed).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for shared DPoP replay markers. Must be non-empty when supplied. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:jwks_auth:{plugin-config-id}`, which isolates independent policies inside a namespace while keeping every replica of one policy claiming against the same keyspace. An explicit prefix is the opt-in for deliberately sharing a keyspace across policies.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

JwtAuthConfig.description: Plugin: jwt_auth — HMAC (HS256/HS384/HS512) JWT Bearer token authentication.

token_lookup.description: Exact credential location (header:<name> or query:<name>). Whitespace is not trimmed; header names must be valid HTTP tokens, and query names must be non-empty and contain no whitespace. A location no request could satisfy is rejected at config admission.

consumer_claim_field.description: JWT claim identifying the consumer; must not be blank

expected_issuer.description: Required iss claim, compared as an exact case-sensitive string; must not be blank. Mutually exclusive with expected_issuers — supplying both is rejected.

expected_issuers.description: Accepted iss claims; no entry may be blank. Mutually exclusive with expected_issuer. A token still claims exactly one issuer: per RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 a present iss must be a single string, and an array, object, number, boolean, or null iss is rejected even when one element matches an accepted value.

audiences.description: Accepted aud claims (OR-matched); no entry may be blank. When non-empty, the token must carry a matching aud. When empty, a token without aud is accepted and a token that carries aud is rejected.

require_exp.description: Require an exp claim; expiration is always validated when present. exp is an RFC 7519 section 2 NumericDate (a JSON number that may carry a fractional part); a fractional exp bounds the authenticated stream exactly like an integer one, truncated toward the past so the enforced expiry is never later than the token states. nbf presence and validation are delegated to the JWT validation layer; Ferrum does not normalize a fractional nbf.

require_nbf.description: Require an nbf claim; when present, nbf is always validated

leeway_secs.description: Clock leeway for time-based JWT claims

algorithm.description: HMAC algorithm every token on this instance must use. Pinned by configuration and never taken from the token header: a token whose header names any other algorithm is rejected. RSA/EC/JWKS verification belongs to `jwks_auth`.

hide_credentials.description: Remove the token-bearing header (for `header:Authorization`, only a `Bearer` value) or query parameter before forwarding an authenticated request upstream, including when another mechanism wins a multi-auth chain. Defaults to false so backends that re-verify the JWT keep receiving it.

KafkaLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: kafka_logging — Produces transaction summaries as JSON messages to an Apache Kafka topic. Uses an async channel to decouple the proxy hot path from Kafka I/O, with librdkafka handling batching, compression, and delivery retries. Local queue admission is distinct from terminal broker acknowledgement; flush_timeout_seconds bounds blocking-pool scheduling plus the owned shutdown/reload producer flush. KeepLastKnownGood admission rejects invalid startup configuration and preserves the previous accepted generation on invalid reload. librdkafka resolves bootstrap hostnames itself and dials brokers advertised by cluster metadata, and the pinned client exposes no connect/resolve callback, so those addresses cannot be screened. Admission therefore returns 400 whenever FERRUM_BACKEND_* policy can deny any address (including the default posture), unless the node operator attests the Kafka cluster with FERRUM_KAFKA_ALLOWED_BROKERS and every broker_list entry is listed there (host:port, or an IP covered by a listed CIDR); a listed literal broker IP may pass FERRUM_BACKEND_DENY_CIDRS and the FERRUM_BACKEND_ALLOW_IPS mode but never the dangerous-range baseline. That depends on the node's environment, so this schema does not model it. broker_list is parsed with librdkafka's [proto://]host[:port] grammar, so protocol-prefixed denied literals and protocol prefixes that disagree with security_protocol are rejected.

topic.description: Kafka topic to produce messages to. Held to Kafka's own topic syntax at admission: 1-249 characters drawn from ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', and '-', and never "." or "..". Whether an otherwise valid topic exists (or may be auto-created) is still a broker decision.

key_field.description: Partition key field: client_ip (groups by client), proxy_id (groups by route), consumer_username (groups by the summary's effective identity — the mapped Consumer's username, or the external authenticated identity when no Consumer is mapped; unauthenticated records carry no key), none (omits the record key and delegates partition selection to the configured librdkafka partitioner — by default consistent_random with sticky batching, NOT a Ferrum per-record rotation). Matched exactly: lowercase, no surrounding whitespace.

buffer_capacity.description: Ferrum userspace channel capacity (record count). Zero is rejected. A channel slot is reserved before serialization. Hard maximum 100000.

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum retained bytes for one pre-serialized Kafka payload plus its optional partition key. Oversized entries are dropped before enqueue. An explicit producer_config message.max.bytes must be at least max_entry_bytes + 128 bytes of record framing (a cross-field bound the constructor enforces); without one, message.max.bytes defaults to the larger of 1048576 and that floor. Hard maximum 1048576.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate Ferrum retained-content byte budget across queued records awaiting librdkafka admission and transient serializers. Admission reserves max_entry_bytes before serialization and shrinks that lease to the exact retained record size. Must be at least max_entry_bytes (a cross-field bound JSON Schema cannot express; the constructor enforces it). The charge is NOT released when librdkafka send returns: it is transferred into the record's delivery opaque and covers librdkafka's own retained copy until terminal delivery, terminal failure, purge-on-destroy, or an immediate send rejection. Hard maximum 268435456.

flush_timeout_seconds.description: Total bounded seconds for blocking-pool scheduling and librdkafka flush during graceful shutdown and reload disposal after Ferrum admission is closed. Zero is rejected. Hard maximum 300.

acks.description: Delivery acknowledgment level: 0 (fire-and-forget local completion still observed via delivery callback), 1 (leader ack), all/-1 (full ISR ack)

message_timeout_ms.description: Timeout for message delivery in milliseconds. librdkafka's own range; 0 means no local timeout.

security_protocol.description: Kafka security protocol. Unknown root keys are rejected so a misspelled control cannot silently select PLAINTEXT. Explicit TLS controls require ssl/sasl_ssl; explicit SASL controls require sasl_plaintext/sasl_ssl; username and password must be paired.

sasl_mechanism.description: SASL mechanism, matched exactly (librdkafka compares it case-sensitively). Required with sasl_plaintext/sasl_ssl. PLAIN and SCRAM-* require sasl_username and sasl_password; OAUTHBEARER and GSSAPI refuse them. GSSAPI is refused at admission except on Windows builds, because this gateway's librdkafka is built without Cyrus SASL.

ssl_ca_location.description: Path to CA certificate for broker TLS verification. Falls back to FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH. librdkafka reads this value as a local filename, so an `operator` whose token carries an `ns` claim (or any `operator` where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on) cannot introduce it: a gateway-local path is refused with `400` before it is loaded, and the references such an operator may otherwise use (inline PEM, `system://`, a `k8s://` Secret) are not filenames. A value already stored in this field is exempt; set or change it with an `admin`-role token.

ssl_no_verify.description: Skip broker TLS certificate verification. Falls back to FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY

ssl_certificate_location.description: Path to client certificate for mTLS. librdkafka reads this value as a local filename, so an `operator` whose token carries an `ns` claim (or any `operator` where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on) cannot introduce it: a gateway-local path is refused with `400` before it is loaded, and the references such an operator may otherwise use (inline PEM, `system://`, a `k8s://` Secret) are not filenames. A value already stored in this field is exempt; set or change it with an `admin`-role token.

ssl_key_location.description: Path to client private key for mTLS. librdkafka reads this value as a local filename, so an `operator` whose token carries an `ns` claim (or any `operator` where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on) cannot introduce it: a gateway-local path is refused with `400` before it is loaded, and the references such an operator may otherwise use (inline PEM, `system://`, a `k8s://` Secret) are not filenames. A value already stored in this field is exempt; set or change it with an `admin`-role token.

queue.buffering.max.kbytes.description: librdkafka producer queue size in KiB, 1-262144.

message.max.bytes.description: librdkafka maximum message size in bytes, 1-4194304, and at least max_entry_bytes + 128 (enforced by the constructor).

producer_config.description: Escape hatch: additional librdkafka producer properties as string key-value pairs. Cannot override bootstrap.servers or authoritative TLS/SASL controls, including official aliases, PEM/keystore identity alternatives, or hostname-verification disablement. Every spelling of acks, message.timeout.ms, and compression (aliases such as request.required.acks, delivery.timeout.ms, compression.type, and topic.-prefixed forms) is refused — use the top-level field — and two keys naming the same librdkafka property (for example linger.ms and queue.buffering.max.ms) are refused, because librdkafka would apply them in hash order. enable.idempotence=true requires acks all. TLS-namespace properties require ssl/sasl_ssl; SASL/HTTPS-auth properties require sasl_plaintext/sasl_ssl. Queue/message budgets cannot exceed Ferrum hard maxima. ssl.crl.location cannot conflict with gateway file-backed gateway CRL source when verification is enabled. transactional.id is refused outright: the logging lifecycle never calls init_transactions/begin_transaction/commit_transaction, so a transactional producer would reject every record. delivery.report.only.error is refused regardless of value or casing: Ferrum owns delivery reporting and always enables successful delivery reports. Retained-byte leases release at terminal delivery, terminal failure, purge-on-destroy, or immediate send rejection. Values carrying inline PEM private-key material are refused by shape, which JSON Schema does not model here. Keys that load native code, run a host command, or make librdkafka read or write a gateway file (plugin.library.paths, ssl.engine.location, ssl.engine.id, ssl.providers, sasl.kerberos.kinit.cmd, sasl.kerberos.keytab, sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.private.key.file, sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.file, sasl.oauthbearer.assertion.jwt.template.file, https.ca.location, offset.store.path) are refused case-insensitively for every token unless the node sets FERRUM_KAFKA_ALLOW_NATIVE_CONFIG=true. That depends on the node's environment, so this schema admits them.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Note: Kafka partition keys (`client_ip` / `proxy_id`) read typed summary fields and are NOT affected by `rename:`. See docs/log_schema.md.

key_location.description: Exact credential location (header:<name> or query:<name>), or an ordered array of 1 to 8 such locations. Locations are evaluated in order; credentials present in two different configured locations are refused with 401 as ambiguous, even when their values match. Repeated locations count once (header names are case-insensitive; query names are case-sensitive).
