Whitespace is not trimmed; header names must be valid HTTP tokens, and query names must be non-empty and contain no whitespace. A query name that also appears as a `;`-separated sub-parameter (`carrier=;api_key=k`, raw or percent/form-decoded) is ambiguous: the request is refused with 401 and the alias never authenticates. Every configured header name is always removed from client request trailers.

hide_credentials.description: Remove every configured API-key header and query parameter before forwarding an authenticated request upstream, including when another mechanism wins a multi-auth chain. For each query location this also removes a `;`-separated sub-parameter alias. Disable only when a legacy backend explicitly requires the reusable credential.

LdapAuthConfig.description: Plugin: ldap_auth — LDAP directory authentication with optional AD group filtering. Status codes distinguish failure classes: invalid credentials or unknown user return 401; a user authorized by bind but not in any `required_groups` returns 403; backend/configuration failures (directory unreachable, service-account bind failure, or search RPC error) return 500 rather than 401, so clients are not falsely told their credentials are wrong. When `required_groups` is set without a service account (`service_account_dn`/`service_account_password`), the group-membership search uses an ANONYMOUS bind; group enforcement then only works if the directory permits anonymous reads of group objects, so a service account is recommended. TLS connections (`ldaps://`/STARTTLS) honor the gateway CRL (`FERRUM_TLS_CRL_FILE_PATH`), rejecting revoked server certificates. Every connection/reconnection performs an uncached A+AAAA lookup, screens the complete candidate set and each imminent dial under the active backend egress policy, and retains the configured hostname for TLS/SNI verification. Non-loopback plaintext `ldap://` is rejected unless the development-only `allow_plaintext` override is explicitly enabled. Exactly one authentication mode may be configured; combining `bind_dn_template` with `search_base_dn`/ `search_filter` is rejected. Both modes require a canonical identity attribute, reject ambiguous or duplicate values, and export the authenticated entry's canonical value rather than the presented username: direct bind reads it with a base-scope search on the bound DN, and search-then-bind takes it from the uniquely selected search entry. A returned group entry satisfies `required_groups` through its `group_attribute` values alone whenever the directory returns that attribute; only an omitted `cn` falls back to the entry's own `cn` RDN. DNs and attribute names are validated at admission. `failover_ldap_urls` adds directory endpoints tried in order when one is unreachable or answers busy/unavailable; credential rejections never fail over.

ldap_url.description: LDAP server URL. Use ldaps:// or ldap:// with starttls=true; non-loopback plaintext ldap:// requires the explicit development-only allow_plaintext override. The scheme is matched case-sensitively and the value must carry no leading or trailing whitespace. A hostname is required and an explicit port must be 1-65535 (port 0 can never be dialed). Embedded URL credentials are rejected; a bare '@' with empty userinfo carries none and is accepted. Each connection freshly resolves and policy-screens all A/AAAA candidates while retaining this hostname for TLS/SNI verification. The connection-establishment budget is split across the screened candidates, so a candidate that stalls during TCP or TLS setup, or fails TLS, leaves time to try the next one.

failover_ldap_urls.description: Further directory endpoints (replicas) tried in order after ldap_url, each validated like ldap_url and using the same scheme. A flow moves to the next endpoint only when the current one cannot be reached, its connection or TLS setup fails, an operation fails at the transport level, or it answers busy (51) / unavailable (52); a credential rejection, a group non-membership, or any other directory error is final. Every attempt shares request_timeout_seconds. The replicas join the identity realm digest.

bind_dn_template.description: Direct bind DN template with {username} placeholder. A DN-shaped template (one containing '=') must, with the placeholder substituted, be an RFC 4514 distinguished name; an Active Directory userPrincipalName ({username}@corp.example.com) or down-level (CORP\{username}) template is accepted as-is.

search_base_dn.description: Base DN for search-then-bind user search. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected, and the value must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name (an unescaped '=' inside a value is refused as a likely missing comma)

search_filter.description: LDAP search filter with {username} placeholder. The value must also parse as an RFC 4515 search filter; a malformed filter is rejected at load rather than failing every request with 500

canonical_identity_attribute.description: Required in both bind modes. Exactly one value from the authenticated entry (the uniquely selected search entry, or a base-scope read of the directly bound DN) becomes the authenticated identity, Consumer mapping key, custom group-filter {username}, and default memberUid value (for example uid or sAMAccountName). Choose the authoritative attribute whose value username-based groups store; mismatches fail closed and never fall back to the presented login. Attribute-name matching is LDAP case-insensitive. The value must be an RFC 4512 attribute description (a name or numeric OID with optional ;options); 1.1 is refused.

service_account_dn.description: DN for the service account used in search-then-bind. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected. A DN-shaped value (one containing '=') must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name; an Active Directory userPrincipalName or down-level logon name is accepted as-is.

service_account_password.description: Password for the service account. Taken verbatim: it is never trimmed, so a secret with leading or trailing whitespace binds as configured. Only an empty string is rejected

group_base_dn.description: Base DN for group membership search. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; a whitespace-only value is rejected, and the value must be an RFC 4514 distinguished name

group_filter.description: Group search filter. The value must parse as an RFC 4515 search filter; a malformed filter is rejected at load. When required_groups is non-empty, a custom filter must contain {user_dn} or {username}. {username} is the authenticated canonical identity read from canonical_identity_attribute in both bind modes, never the presented login. Before authorization, every custom-filter match is rechecked against the exact returned group DN with the membership predicate (member, uniqueMember, and memberUid by default; group_member_attribute and group_membership_mode change it) so a static branch cannot fabricate membership.

required_groups.description: LDAP/AD group names the user must belong to (OR logic). Names compare like LDAP caseIgnoreMatch: case-insensitively, ignoring surrounding whitespace and collapsing interior whitespace runs. When the directory returns group_attribute for a group entry, only those values decide; a present non-matching value never falls back to the DN. Only when group_attribute is cn and the directory omits it does the entry's OWN first RDN stand in, and then only a cn-typed component with a matching RFC 4514-decoded value; any other omitted group_attribute fails closed. An entry merely nested under a required group never matches

group_attribute.description: Authoritative attribute containing the group name (for Active Directory prefer the domain-unique sAMAccountName over cn, which may repeat across OUs); returned LDAP attribute names are matched case-insensitively. Must be an RFC 4512 attribute description; 1.1 is refused.

group_member_attribute.description: DN-valued attribute on group entries that lists members, used for the default group search and for the custom-filter membership recheck instead of the built-in member/uniqueMember/memberUid predicate (for example member or a custom appMember). With group_membership_mode ad_in_chain it names the link attribute evaluated transitively (default member); with member_of it names the attribute on the user's entry listing group DNs (default memberOf). Must be an RFC 4512 attribute description.

group_membership_mode.description: member_of finds the required groups under group_base_dn by their group_attribute value and accepts one only when a base-scope equality search on the authenticated user's entry confirms that its group_member_attribute (default memberOf) lists that exact group DN, so DN matching follows the directory schema; it cannot be combined with group_filter. direct proves membership from the group entry's own membership attribute. ad_in_chain (Active Directory only) uses LDAP_MATCHING_RULE_IN_CHAIN (1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941) on group_member_attribute (default member), so a user who is a member through nested groups matches; the directory evaluates the chain under the group search's size and time limits, and custom-filter matches are rechecked with the same in-chain predicate.

starttls.description: Use STARTTLS to upgrade ldap:// connections; invalid with ldaps://

allow_plaintext.description: Development-only override allowing a non-loopback ldap:// endpoint without STARTTLS. Service-account and user passwords then have no transport confidentiality.

connect_timeout_seconds.description: Per-connection DNS resolution, candidate TCP/TLS establishment, and per-operation timeout in seconds; also applied as the server-side LDAP search time limit

request_timeout_seconds.description: Strict wall-clock deadline in seconds for the complete uncached authentication and group-check flow. The effective default is 15 seconds, raised to connect_timeout_seconds when that value is larger.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Maximum concurrent LDAP directory flows per plugin instance, shared by uncached authentications and due cached group re-checks; excess requests fail immediately

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Cache TTL for successful auth results (0 = disabled, maximum 24 hours). A cache hit skips the bind, so a password change or account disablement in the directory takes effect only when the entry expires; values above 900 seconds log that revocation lag at construction. required_groups membership is re-checked separately (group_cache_ttl_seconds).

group_cache_ttl_seconds.description: With required_groups and the cache enabled, the longest a cached authentication is admitted without re-running the group search (0 = every cache hit). A due hit re-checks membership under max_concurrent_requests and request_timeout_seconds; a user no longer in any required group gets 403 and the entry is evicted, and a directory failure returns 500 and keeps the entry. Never extends cache_ttl_seconds.

max_cache_entries.description: Strict maximum entries in the auth result cache (1-1,000,000). At capacity, one existing entry is replaced without a full-cache scan. Cache keys use the exact presented username and password. The same cap bounds the rejected-credential cache and the per-username failure tracker; the tracker never evicts live failure state, so when it is full an untracked username gets 500.

negative_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long an exact username/password pair the directory rejected (wrong password or unknown user) is answered 401 without contacting the directory (0 = disabled, maximum 300). A different password for the same username is still checked.

max_failed_attempts_per_user.description: After this many consecutive directory credential rejections for one presented username, that username is answered 401 without contacting the directory for failed_attempt_backoff_seconds, even with the correct password (0 = disabled, maximum 1000). This keeps a spray from reaching directory lockout counters; a successful bind resets the count. The count folds the username's case and whitespace, survives a compatible reload of the same plugin config, and is never evicted while live (a full tracker answers an untracked username 500).

failed_attempt_backoff_seconds.description: How long a username stays refused after max_failed_attempts_per_user consecutive failures; also the quiet period after which its failure count starts over.

service_connection_max_age_seconds.description: Reuse one connection bound as the service account, per directory endpoint, for user and group searches for at most this many seconds (0 = a fresh connection per flow). New shared connections are resolved, screened, dialed, and bound exactly like fresh ones; a shared connection that failed at the transport level is retired. End-user binds always use their own connection. Requires service_account_dn and service_account_password.

hide_credentials.description: Remove the verified Authorization: Basic credential from the backend request, including when another mechanism wins a multi-auth chain. Only the Basic scheme this plugin consumes is removed; an Authorization header carrying another scheme reaches the backend unchanged. Set to false only for a legacy backend that explicitly requires the directory password.

LoadTestingConfig.description:
Plugin: load_testing — On-demand proxy load testing triggered by
X-Loadtesting-Key header. Spawns concurrent clients through the
gateway's own proxy listener (HTTP only). Unknown top-level keys are
rejected. File, admin/database, and CP/DP admission share the same
constructor validation; serving-mode publication uses KeepLastKnownGood
so an invalid candidate keeps the prior valid generation active.
Omitted optional fields select defaults; runtime also treats explicit
null on optional fields as omitted. Matching replay bodies have a hard
10 MiB plugin-local ceiling and active local/fan-out replay work shares
a 64 MiB process-wide retained-body budget. Synthetic and fan-out
headers reuse the canonical secondary-request sanitizer shared with
request_mirror (Connection-listed hop-by-hop, Trailer, framing, Ferrum
markers, proxy-owned X-Forwarded-*), preserving Host for routing. That
snapshot is taken from the original client headers, not from the
already-transformed map, so an earlier request_transformer chain is
applied exactly once to the synthetic cohort as well. Synthetic and
fan-out requests are sent over HTTP/1.1 so the preserved Host is the
request authority; over HTTP/2 the two would disagree and ingress
validation would correctly reject every replay. A trigger declaring a
Content-Length above the 10 MiB replay ceiling is not buffered: it is
forwarded under the ordinary request-body limits and no load test
starts. Known limitation: an undeclared-length (chunked, or H2/H3
without Content-Length) trigger body above 10 MiB is refused with 413,
since the ceiling also bounds collection. Fan-out peers acknowledge an admitted trigger with 204
plus X-Loadtesting-Ack echoing the controller's X-Loadtesting-Run-Id;
a request carrying X-Loadtesting-Fanout whose key fails is refused
with 403 before backend dispatch.

key.description: Secret value that the X-Loadtesting-Key header must match to trigger the load test. Must be a randomly generated secret of at least 32 printable ASCII HTTP field-value characters with no leading or trailing space. The gateway never echoes the value in validation errors and strips this reserved header on matching and non-matching paths before later deferred plugins or backend dispatch. Underscore spellings (X_Loadtesting_Key and similar), which CGI-style backends fold onto the same variable, are stripped and redacted too but never authenticate a trigger.

duration_seconds.description: How long the test runs in seconds

ramp.description: When true, clients start gradually over the duration instead of all at once

request_timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds (1–60000). Each attempt is also capped to the remaining absolute run deadline so workers cannot outlive duration_seconds.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Maximum response bytes the synthetic client consumes per request (1–18446744073709551615). The runtime parses this as an unsigned 64-bit integer, so the finite upper bound is part of the admitted contract; a larger value is rejected. The client stops reading at the cap, bounding its own work and memory without changing the backend response.

gateway_port.description: Local gateway port for synthetic requests (1–65535). Defaults to the effective FERRUM_PROXY_HTTP_PORT (or FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT when gateway_tls is enabled) resolved with the same environment > ferrum.conf/--settings precedence the listener itself uses, then 8000/8443. A resolved port of 0 (disabled listener) is rejected whichever configuration source supplied it. Serving nodes screen the 127.0.0.1 dial target with the backend egress policy, so a policy that denies loopback rejects the plugin unless 127.0.0.1 is allow-listed; control-plane admission checks the range only.

gateway_tls.description: Use HTTPS for local loopback synthetic requests

gateway_tls_no_verify.description: Skip TLS cert verification for loopback connections. Defaults to true when gateway_tls is enabled (gateway cert typically won't match 127.0.0.1)

items.description: An http(s) URL with a non-empty authority and no URL userinfo, query, or fragment. This pattern models only the intrinsic URL grammar the constructor admits; the environment-dependent checks below (loopback-alias equality against the selected local target, normalized duplicate origins, and backend egress screening) need runtime context and stay runtime-only.

gateway_addresses.description: Remote gateway URLs for one-hop fan-out from the originating controller (at most 32). Peers receive X-Loadtesting-Fanout and never re-fanout. Entries must be unique http(s) URLs without userinfo, query, or fragment. Local-loopback aliases of the selected local target (127/8, IPv4-mapped loopback, ::1, localhost, and names beneath .localhost with matching scheme and effective port) are rejected. Fan-out sends the trigger key and the triggering request's headers (credentials included) and body, so an http:// entry is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] unless allow_plaintext is true. Each fan-out call is a single attempt bounded by duration_seconds and cancelled with the local run.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// gateway_addresses entry whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The trigger key and the triggering request's credentials then cross the network in clear.

LokiLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: loki_logging — Ships transaction logs to Grafana Loki via the push API in bounded, label-grouped streams. HTTP 204 is the canonical success response; other 2xx responses are accepted only when their body drains completely and is empty. Loki's blocked-ingestion status 260, non-empty/anomalous compatible-success responses, and every other non-retryable response are terminal; 408, 429, and 5xx responses use bounded exponential backoff with jitter. Explicit nulls and unknown top-level fields are rejected. `schema` and `schema_ref` are structurally exclusive. When `max_entry_bytes` is omitted, OpenAPI requires `buffer_max_bytes` to be at least the default per-entry ceiling (65536); a sibling comparison against an explicit `max_entry_bytes` is enforced only at construction. Named-schema existence is runtime-only.

endpoint_url.description: Loki push API URL (for example, http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push). Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored by runtime URL parsing. URL user information is rejected; use authorization_header or custom_headers instead. Ports must be 0–65535. Path and query components are redacted from operational and non-admin diagnostics.

authorization_header.description: Full Authorization header value (e.g. "Bearer <token>" or "Basic <b64>"). Leading and trailing whitespace is rejected.

custom_headers.description: Extra HTTP headers (for example, X-Scope-OrgID for multi-tenant Loki). Names use HTTP token syntax and are at most 65,535 ASCII bytes. Values may contain UTF-8 (HeaderValue obs-text); NUL, CR, and LF are rejected. All values are redacted from audit records and non-admin config reads.

labels.description: Static labels merged into every Loki stream. Keep cardinality low because labels are indexed. Names beginning with __ and the reserved ferrum_emitter label are rejected. Ferrum Edge adds a unique ferrum_emitter value per plugin instance so independently ordered emitters never share a Loki stream. Each replica and each rebuilt plugin generation therefore consumes a distinct active stream for every other label combination; size Loki max_streams_per_user limits and reload cadence accordingly.

include_proxy_id_label.description: Add the matched proxy_id as a Loki label

include_status_class_label.description: Add status_class (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx) as a Loki label

gzip.description: Gzip-compress the request body (Content-Encoding header set automatically)

batch_size.description: Number of entries to buffer before sending a batch

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing a partial batch

max_retries.description: Retries after the initial delivery attempt. Only transport failures, 408, 429, and 5xx retry. A received 204 is committed even when its best-effort body drain is anomalous, avoiding duplicates.

buffer_capacity.description: Channel capacity — new entries are dropped when full

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum retained bytes for one serialized JSON line plus its Loki labels. Configuration is rejected unless the configured serializer's minimum HTTP and stream lines plus static, reserved, and worst-case dynamic label values fit this budget. Request-shaped fields can still make an individual serialized line exceed the budget; those oversized entries are dropped before enqueue.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Per-plugin retained-content byte budget across queued, batched, and retrying entries. Must be at least max_entry_bytes; entries are dropped non-blockingly when the budget is exhausted. When max_entry_bytes is omitted, this field must be at least 65536 (the default per-entry ceiling). An arbitrary sibling comparison against an explicit max_entry_bytes is runtime-only.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Note: Loki labels (`build_http_labels` / `build_stream_labels`) read typed summary fields and are NOT affected by `rename:`. See docs/log_schema.md. Existence of the named schema is resolved at construction.

McpGatewayConfig.description: Plugin: mcp_gateway — HTTP MCP / Agent Tool Gateway for JSON-RPC MCP traffic. Supports transparent_proxy and aggregate_router modes, MCP session mediation, catalog aggregation, namespaced tool/resource/prompt routing, bounded JSON-RPC batch admission with per-item validation and ordered synthetic response assembly. Aggregate-router mode also supports OPT-IN MCP Streamable HTTP event streams (sessions.sse_multiplexing, default false). When enabled, GET with Accept text/event-stream attaches one generation-scoped server-message listener per live downstream session, and a POST carrying a JSON-RPC request whose result had to be fetched upstream is answered with its OWN text/event-stream response on that POST; a result the gateway already holds stays an application/json reply, 202 stays reserved for notification-only POSTs, and a freshly attached GET listener never carries a response to a request that arrived on a POST. Every aggregate JSON-RPC request with a representable id opens a bounded, type-sensitive request/stream identity preserving the exact numeric wire token before catalog refresh or upstream dispatch, so a concurrent notifications/cancelled marks a genuinely open request and its late result is suppressed (its POST stream closes carrying no message). A GET listener is not a precondition, and the client's Accept decides the representation. Delivered events enter the single retained-event ring already delivered, so they only occupy the Last-Event-ID replay window: an explicit resumption cursor replays them, a fresh listener never does, and a ring too small to keep one costs resumability rather than delivery. Notifications, batch members, and initialize never open a stream. Completing, cancelling, or refusing a stream returns its capacity exactly once through a request-owned lease, a late or duplicate response for a terminal identity is refused rather than misattributed; mismatched or ambiguous correlated responses are replaced by a bounded gateway -32603 error that carries the request's own JSON-RPC id token so the pending call still resolves, and are never framed as that request's event stream or returned as successful inline answers (the id comparison is byte-exact; mcp.sse.delivery records refused). Teardown is unconditional on client disconnect, session DELETE, idle eviction, and plugin reload/update/delete; a listener past its configured lifetime is superseded by a fresh GET so a stalled transport can never hold the slot. Duplicate listeners, invalid/unknown/stale identities, and invalid, oversized, unknown, or too-old Last-Event-ID cursors fail closed with fixed, value-redacted diagnostics. Aggregate upstream-routed members such as tools/call must be singleton requests so later plugin phases are preserved; batch request members return JSON-RPC -32009, while notification-only batches report the restriction once at batch level. MCP initialize must also be a singleton HTTP request: initialize batch members return JSON-RPC -32010 before any session mint or eviction, so no batch mints or evicts a session or returns a session header. A notification-only batch whose gateway dispatch otherwise fails reports JSON-RPC -32011. A batch member whose session is no longer live contributes a per-item JSON-RPC -32004 element because the singleton bare HTTP 404 cannot be expressed per item. Aggregate batches always answer HTTP 200 with a response array, so an unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version surfaces per item rather than as the singleton HTTP 400; transparent_proxy batches cannot be partially forwarded and are rejected whole with HTTP 400. The plugin also supports tool argument JSON Schema validation and mcp.* metadata emission. A servers entry may instead carry `openapi` (aggregate_router only): tools generated from OpenAPI operations that run as HTTP requests to this proxy's own configured backend through ordinary backend dispatch, answered with tools/call results (see McpGatewayOpenApiBridge); POST /api-specs generates such a gateway from the `x-ferrum-mcp` document extension. Aggregate tools/call rewrites stage a private gateway-authenticated public-to-upstream tool-name mapping so ai_tool_governor can keep policy keys on public namespaced identities. Aggregate admission is re-checked over the final backend-visible request body: a routed tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read, or passthrough message whose JSON-RPC message kind, method (or, for a client-sent response, answered id), selected upstream destination, mediated upstream session header, tool/prompt name, resource URI, or admitted arguments were changed by a later plugin (including a later mesh_route_dispatch destination rewrite) (for example a request_transformer body rule) is refused before egress with JSON-RPC -32014; the gateway's own public-to-upstream name rewrite is the only permitted difference, and the check holds on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3. The mediated upstream session header is also re-asserted over the final backend headers (every spelling removed, the recorded value re-inserted), including after a serverless_function pre_proxy header overlay, and a JSON-RPC envelope carrying both method and result or error is refused with -32600. A downstream aggregate session is bound to the principal that created it: a mapped Consumer by namespace and record id, or an unmapped external identity by its subject together with the verified authentication realm (mechanism and issuer / key source / directory), so equal subject strings from different accepted issuers, tenants of an issuer-less jwks_auth provider, identity claims, or auth plugins are different owners, and changing the verifying authority configuration ends existing external-identity sessions; a mismatch is refused with the ordinary 404 session-not-found response. Generic auth, rate limiting, WAF, retry, timeout, tracing, DLP, and semantic safety remain separate Ferrum plugins. Cannot be composed with request_deduplication on the same proxy; admission rejects the pair with 400 because a deduplicated replay is served before this plugin runs and cannot be proven to match the live catalog mapping. Two enabled mcp_gateway instances on one proxy may not have nesting endpoint.path scopes, and endpoint.path may not be "/", because the endpoint reserves its whole path subtree. A client JSON-RPC id token reflected into a gateway-authored singleton response is bounded at 4096 wire bytes; a larger id is refused with a fixed -32600 that does not echo it. The admitted singleton id is retained privately so a gateway-authored terminal decided in a response phase (result validation, an uninspectable or oversized upstream representation, an upstream transport failure) names the request it answers instead of returning id null. Every response phase is instance-scoped: an instance acts on a response only for a request it admitted itself, so instances with disjoint endpoint scopes on one proxy never apply each other's response policies. Unknown keys are rejected at the root and in every fixed-shape object here; the operator-defined servers.* and policy.tools.* key sets stay open. Rules this schema deliberately leaves to plugin load, because portable JSON Schema cannot compare sibling values or resolve external state: endpoint.path canonicalization beyond the shape checked here, the 512 distinct policy.tools grant groups cap, allowed_groups/denied_groups overlap, the 255-byte grant group bound, a group-conditioned policy.tools key naming a configured server namespace, HTTP header-name destinations that are protocol-managed, servers.*.headers reserved names / case-insensitive duplicates / session-header names / `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` resolution, policy.resources template deny keys decoding to valid URI templates, upstream_url host egress screening, namespace uniqueness, at-least-one-enabled-server (exactly one in transparent_proxy, at least one exposing a family in aggregate_router), max_batch_item_bytes <= max_batch_bytes, and the sse_* budget relationships.

enabled.description: An explicit null selects the default, exactly as omission does.

path.description: Canonical public MCP endpoint path, such as /mcp. Must not be "/" — the endpoint reserves its whole path subtree, so a root endpoint would refuse every other handler on the proxy and is rejected at admission. Only the exact configured spelling is served; /mcp and /mcp/ are distinct so authorization and MCP routing evaluate the same request target. Extra segments, repeated trailing slashes, case variants, encoded separators, and dot segments are different, rejected paths. Variants reaching the plugin return 404 with JSON-RPC -32600 / Unknown MCP endpoint; the HTTP frontend rejects encoded separators and dot segments earlier with 400. Two enabled mcp_gateway instances on one proxy may not have overlapping endpoint scopes, including case variants; admission rejects the pair. Queries do not change selection. Methods other than GET, POST, and DELETE return 405 when they reach this plugin.

protocol_versions.description: Supported MCP protocol versions, in preference order. The first entry is the gateway's preferred version, returned by aggregate-mode initialize when the client requests an unsupported version. Includes 2025-03-26 when JSON-RPC batches are desired; batches are admitted under validation.max_batch_* limits.

discovery.description: Catalog discovery requires aggregate_router. Explicit aggregate_tools, aggregate_resources, aggregate_prompts, namespace_separator, cache_ttl_seconds, on_new_tool, and on_schema_change fields are rejected in transparent_proxy, including explicit defaults, because every one of them is inert without a mediated catalog. An explicit null block, and an explicit null on any field below, selects the defaults exactly as omission does.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Also bounds recovery from a wholly unavailable catalog family — that outage is cached for this long before the family is retried.

sessions.description: An explicit null block, and an explicit null on any field below, selects the defaults exactly as omission does. The sse_* relationships (event bytes inside the retained-byte budget, replay inside retention, keepalive inside the listener lifetime) compare sibling values and are enforced at plugin load.

downstream_session_header.description: Must be a valid HTTP header name; rejected at config validation otherwise. This name is stamped onto the client response, so protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing destinations (`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`, case-insensitive) are also rejected. Names in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` request namespace (case-insensitive, `_` equivalent to `-`) are rejected because the gateway strips them from client requests.

upstream_session_header.description: Must be a valid HTTP header name; rejected at config validation otherwise. Names in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` request namespace (case-insensitive, `_` equivalent to `-`) are rejected because the gateway scrubs them before dispatch. Both configured session header names are registered as credential headers for the route (redacted from diagnostics and policy calls, withheld from request_mirror, bound into replay partitions).

session_ttl_seconds.description: Idle downstream MCP session lifetime before eviction.

max_sessions.description: Maximum downstream MCP sessions retained by this plugin instance. When full, only an expired session or one owned by the principal opening a replacement may be removed; otherwise initialization is refused.

max_sessions_per_principal.description: Maximum live downstream MCP sessions owned by one authenticated principal (or by unauthenticated requests as one shared principal). At this cap, the principal's own oldest session is evicted.

sse_multiplexing.description: Aggregate-router only. Enables the MCP Streamable HTTP event-stream surfaces: GET with Accept text/event-stream attaches one server-message listener for the downstream session, AND a POST carrying a JSON-RPC request whose result the gateway does not already hold is answered with its OWN text/event-stream response on that same POST. Response placement follows the advertised transport: a POST carrying a request is always answered on that POST (application/json when the result is ready, its own event stream when it had to be fetched), 202 stays reserved for a POST carrying only notifications and responses, and a freshly attached GET listener never carries a response to a request that arrived on a POST — only an explicit Last-Event-ID resumption replays one. The client's Accept decides the representation; a client offering only application/json is answered with JSON. OFF by default because the listener surface is optional: with it false, aggregate GET keeps a 405 rejection and every request is answered with application/json on its own POST, which is equally conforming. Transparent mode ignores this flag and continues to forward GET upstream.

sse_max_streams_per_session.description: Max concurrent OPEN request-stream identities per downstream SSE session. Completing or cancelling a stream returns its capacity; the same bound also caps the retained terminal records that refuse a late or duplicate response.

sse_max_retained_events.description: Capacity of the single retained-event ring, which serves both pre-listener staging and Last-Event-ID replay. An event still owed to a consumer is never evicted. A POST-attached response enters the ring already delivered, so a ring too small to keep it costs resumability rather than delivery and the eviction watermark advances so a stale cursor fails closed.

sse_max_retained_bytes.description: The one aggregate retained-byte budget for that ring (framed event bytes). Must leave room for SSE framing above sse_max_event_bytes.

sse_max_event_bytes.description: Max serialized JSON-RPC payload bytes admitted for one SSE event; a larger response is answered as application/json on the POST instead.

sse_max_replay_events.description: How many already-consumed events stay in the ring for Last-Event-ID resume; must not exceed sse_max_retained_events. 0 evicts a consumed event immediately, so POST-attached streams are delivered but never resumable: only the current delivery watermark can resume and any older cursor fails closed with HTTP 410.

sse_max_stream_id_bytes.description: Max UTF-8 bytes admitted for a JSON-RPC request id used as a stream identity.

sse_max_last_event_id_bytes.description: Max accepted Last-Event-ID header bytes; values are never logged.

sse_listener_max_lifetime_seconds.description: Bounded lifetime of one attached SSE listener; the client resumes with Last-Event-ID. The stream ends cleanly at this age whenever the transport is still polling its body, and native HTTP/3 enforces it as a hard bound around its send loop. On HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 a peer that stops reading can park the write and with it that timer, so the unconditional guarantee is supersession instead: past this age the session stops routing new responses to that listener and a fresh GET takes the single-listener slot rather than receiving 409.

sse_keepalive_seconds.description: Idle keepalive comment interval; must not exceed sse_listener_max_lifetime_seconds. Also how a vanished peer is discovered on a quiet session.

capabilities.description: An explicit null block, and an explicit null on any field below, selects the defaults exactly as omission does.

advertise_tools.description: Advertises the tools capability in the synthetic aggregate initialize result, with listChanged false because the gateway does not emit notifications/tools/list_changed.

advertise_resources.description: Advertises the resources capability in the synthetic aggregate initialize result, with listChanged false because the gateway does not emit notifications/resources/list_changed.

advertise_prompts.description: Advertises the prompts capability in the synthetic aggregate initialize result, with listChanged false because the gateway does not emit notifications/prompts/list_changed.

advertise_logging.description: In aggregate_router mode, requires passthrough_unknown_methods=true until logging methods are routed or implemented.

advertise_completions.description: In aggregate_router mode, requires passthrough_unknown_methods=true until explicit completion routing is implemented.

advertise_tasks.description: In aggregate_router mode, requires passthrough_unknown_methods=true until task methods are routed or implemented.

propertyNames.description: Server ids are embedded in public mcp:// resource URIs, so they must be URI-safe (ASCII alphanumerics, '.', '_', '-').

additionalProperties.description: A server is EITHER an HTTP MCP server (upstream_url) OR an OpenAPI bridge (openapi) whose tools are generated from OpenAPI operations and executed as HTTP requests to this proxy's own backend; exactly one of the two is required. Claude-Desktop-style stdio spawn fields (command, args, stdio) are rejected here: mcp_gateway is HTTP-only and never spawns a process. "At least one enabled server", "exactly one enabled server in transparent_proxy", "at least one enabled server exposing a family in aggregate_router", namespace uniqueness, "passthrough_unknown_methods requires an upstream_url server", and "no OpenAPI header parameter may be named after a session header" compare sibling entries and are enforced at plugin load.

upstream_url.description: HTTP or HTTPS upstream MCP endpoint URL. Credentials, query, and fragment are rejected. Literal-IP hosts are additionally screened against the backend egress policy at plugin load.

namespace.description: Public namespace prefix used for tool and prompt names. Must be non-blank and unique across servers.

headers.description: Upstream request headers (name to value, at most 32) sent on every gateway-originated request to this MCP server — initialize, notifications/initialized, every */list page, and the session DELETE — and installed on every routed call to it, replacing any client-supplied spelling (re-asserted over the final backend headers after later header rules). Use it for a service credential such as Authorization or an API-key header. A value that is exactly `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` is resolved from the process environment at plugin load (any other `${...}` reference is rejected before anything is read, and an unset or empty variable is a load error); the final value must be a valid HTTP header value. Names are case-insensitive and join the route's credential-header registry (redacted, withheld from secondary egress). Rejected at plugin load: duplicate names differing only in case, hop-by-hop and framing names, Host, Content-Type, Accept, MCP-Protocol-Version, Last-Event-ID, Forwarded / X-Forwarded-*, X-Ferrum-Hops, gateway x-consumer-* assertion names, and the configured session header names. Not accepted on an openapi server.

forward_client_credentials.description: aggregate_router only (rejected in transparent_proxy, which forwards the client request unchanged; not accepted on an openapi server). By default an aggregate-routed tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read, or passthrough request to this server does NOT carry the client's Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, or Cookie header, any header in the route's credential-header registry, or any query string (the backend query is committed empty, and the header boundary is re-asserted over the final backend headers after later header rules), because the client chose this upstream by naming an item (MCP token passthrough). Set true only for an upstream in the same trust domain that must receive end-user tokens; it restores the client credential headers and the ordinary query. Configured headers apply either way.

policy.description: Catalog policy requires aggregate_router. Explicit default_action, default_prompt_action, default_resource_action, tools, prompts, resources, and hide_denied_tools fields are rejected in transparent_proxy, including explicit defaults. An explicit null block, and an explicit null on any field below, selects the defaults exactly as omission does.

default_prompt_action.description: Action for a prompt with no policy.prompts entry. Defaults to policy.default_action.

default_resource_action.description: Action for a resource or resource template with no policy.resources entry. Defaults to policy.default_action.

prompts.description: Public namespaced prompt name to policy. A prompt whose action is not allow is omitted from prompts/list and prompts/get answers JSON-RPC -32001 before any upstream initialize or dispatch. The key set is operator-defined; each entry is a closed object.

resources.description: Public resource URI (mcp://{server_id}/...) or public resource-template URI (as resources/templates/list publishes it) to policy. A resource or template whose action is not allow is omitted from resources/list or resources/templates/list. resources/read is decided once the URI resolves to an upstream binding, before any upstream initialize or dispatch, and answers JSON-RPC -32001 when refused; an entry for the exact requested public URI wins, otherwise every catalog binding of the same upstream URI decides and any deny wins (each exact resource with that upstream URI and each matching template), so a denied resource cannot be read through an allowed template under another public spelling and a denied template covers the exact resources it matches (they are not listed either). Configured denies are decided from configuration against the resolved upstream URI (a deny key in mcp://{server_id}/... form is decoded at plugin load, and a template deny key must be a valid public resource-template URI or the configuration is rejected), so a deny holds even when that server's resources or templates have never listed; with a deny default, a template-routed read whose server's resources/list has never succeeded fails closed with -32006. The key set is operator-defined; each entry is a closed object.

tools.description: Public namespaced tool name to policy. The key set is operator-defined, so this map stays open; each entry is a closed object. An allow entry may carry a per-consumer grant through allowed_groups and denied_groups, matched against the request Consumer's acl_groups as read from the live configuration on every request. A tool is granted iff its action is allow, the request carries a gateway-mapped Consumer, that Consumer holds none of denied_groups (which takes precedence), and allowed_groups is absent or the Consumer holds at least one of its groups. A request with no mapped Consumer (an anonymous proxy, or an external identity with no Consumer mapping) is never granted a group-conditioned tool. An ungranted tool is omitted from tools/list whatever hide_denied_tools says, and tools/call answers it with JSON-RPC -32001; once any entry carries a group condition, a tools/call naming an unknown tool answers the same -32001 instead of -32003 so hidden tool names cannot be probed. The grant is re-decided in the final request-body hook after the admission re-check. Grants cover tools/list and tools/call only; prompts and resources are gated by policy.prompts / policy.resources actions (not per-consumer), and passthrough methods (including tasks/*) are not grant-checked. A group-conditioned key must be a configured server's namespace (enabled or not, exposing tools or not) followed by discovery.namespace_separator and a tool name. At most 512 distinct group names may be referenced across the whole map, and one entry may not name the same group in both lists. Those rules compare values across the configuration and are enforced at plugin load; pair grants with default_action deny and discovery.on_new_tool hide_until_configured.

allowed_groups.description: Requires action allow. The Consumer must hold at least one of these acl_groups. Omitting it (or null) drops only the allowed-group requirement; a mapped Consumer is still required whenever denied_groups is present. An empty list is rejected. Entries are matched byte-for-byte, must not contain control characters other than tab, LF, and CR, and are at most 255 bytes (the schema bounds code points; the byte bound is enforced at plugin load, as for Consumer acl_groups).

denied_groups.description: Requires action allow. A Consumer holding any of these acl_groups is not granted the tool, even when it also holds an allowed group; with no allowed_groups it grants every mapped Consumer except these, and never a request without a mapped Consumer. An empty list is rejected. Entries follow the allowed_groups entry rules.

validation.description: An explicit null block, and an explicit null on any field below, selects the defaults exactly as omission does. max_batch_item_bytes must not exceed max_batch_bytes; that comparison is between sibling values and is enforced at plugin load.

validate_tool_arguments.description: Validates tools/call arguments against the discovered inputSchema. It does NOT gate observability.log_argument_hash or observability.log_raw_arguments, which are evaluated independently.

validate_tool_results.description: Aggregate-router only. When true, compile each discovered tool outputSchema at catalog construction, pin the exact validator selected for each dispatched call, and validate bounded tools/call results against it before releasing the caller-visible response or publishing audit metadata. structuredContent is preferred; a single JSON text content block is accepted when structuredContent is absent; mixed disagreeing variants and exact response bytes with duplicate object members fail closed. Well-formed tool execution errors (result.isError true with array content) and upstream JSON-RPC errors are preserved; non-boolean or bare isError values, event-stream, and non-JSON tool results fail closed. Invalid or unrepresentable outputSchema values are refused at catalog admission with field-specific diagnostics. Default false.

max_upstream_response_bytes.description: Maximum bytes read from a single non-SSE upstream application/json response before the read is aborted (DoS backstop). Must be greater than 0.

max_catalog_items_per_list.description: Maximum items accumulated across paginated catalog list pages (tools/resources/prompts) before the aggregation is rejected. Must be greater than 0.

max_catalog_bytes_per_list.description: Maximum total serialized bytes accumulated across paginated catalog list pages before the aggregation is rejected. Must be greater than 0.

max_batch_items.description: Maximum JSON-RPC batch array members admitted before session, catalog, or upstream work. Empty batches are rejected separately as Invalid Request. Must be greater than 0.

max_batch_bytes.description: Maximum aggregate request-body bytes admitted for a JSON-RPC batch. Enforced on the raw request body before any JSON parsing, using the first non-whitespace byte to detect array-shaped input. Must be greater than 0 and at least max_batch_item_bytes.

max_batch_item_bytes.description: Maximum raw wire bytes admitted for one JSON-RPC batch member. Measured on the member's exact raw JSON slice as received (internal whitespace and escape sequences included, array separators and surrounding inter-member whitespace excluded), before the member is deserialized, so a member cannot shrink under the cap by normalizing. Oversized members yield a bounded per-item Invalid Request with id null (their id is never materialized or reflected) while siblings continue. Must be greater than 0 and must not exceed max_batch_bytes.

max_batch_response_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes admitted for an assembled JSON-RPC batch response array (including array framing). Oversized aggregates fail closed without returning a partial body. Must be greater than 0.

observability.description: There are no result-side observation settings. `log_raw_results` and `log_result_hash` had no producer anywhere in the plugin, so they are rejected as unknown keys rather than accepted and ignored.

log_raw_arguments.description: Copies raw MCP tool arguments into request metadata (mcp.arguments), capped at 4096 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary; a longer value is cut and mcp.arguments_truncated is set to "true". Arguments can contain secrets or PII; prefer log_argument_hash unless the logging path is explicitly protected. Evaluated independently of validation.validate_tool_arguments.

log_argument_hash.description: Emits mcp.arguments_hash. Evaluated independently of validation.validate_tool_arguments.

McpGatewayOpenApiBridge.description: mcp_gateway OpenAPI bridge server (aggregate_router only). Each operation is published as one MCP tool named `namespace` + discovery.namespace_separator + `name`, entering the same per-session catalog, policy (allow / deny / hide_from_discovery), discovery gates, per-consumer grants, validation.validate_tool_arguments, and mcp.* metadata as a tool listed by an upstream MCP server. A tools/call runs as an HTTP request to THIS proxy's own configured backend through ordinary backend dispatch (upstreams, retries, circuit breaker, TLS, observability): only the backend method, path, query, headers, and body change, never the destination host, scheme, or port, and no URL from an OpenAPI document is ever dialed. The proxy's allowed_methods applies to the bridged method too: a tool whose method the route does not allow is omitted from tools/list, and a call to it is refused with JSON-RPC -32003 (Unknown MCP tool) when no grants are configured, or -32001 when grants are configured. The method check follows tool policy and the per-consumer grant and precedes argument validation. Method- or path-conditioned plugin triggers, WAF path and method rules, and authorization keyed on the request path see the client's POST to the MCP endpoint, never the bridged method and path; restrict a bridged operation through mcp_gateway policy (deny, hide_from_discovery, per-consumer grants). Client request headers are an allowlist: only user-agent, accept-language, traceparent, tracestate, the gateway's correlation header, and forward_request_headers reach the backend. The response becomes a tools/call result: a 2xx is isError false with the body as text content plus structuredContent when it is a JSON object within max_structured_content_bytes, and a 2xx body the bridge cannot return (past a bound, coded, streamed, partial, ambiguous JSON) is omitted with a note, still isError false. Anything else is isError true with the status line and at most max_error_excerpt_bytes of the body; a gateway or dispatch failure carries its gateway-error class, derived from the dispatch outcome, in the status line. The JSON-RPC answer always rides HTTP 200 (status-code metrics and the wire X-Gateway-Error header reflect that 200); the backend status and failure class are always recorded as mcp.bridge.upstream_status and mcp.bridge.gateway_error. Generated by `x-ferrum-mcp` on POST /api-specs, or written by hand.

max_request_body_bytes.description: Largest JSON request body a tools/call may send; a larger `body` argument is refused with JSON-RPC -32602.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Largest 2xx backend body returned as a tool result. A larger declared or received body is omitted (the result stays isError false and says why) and is never copied into the response.

max_error_excerpt_bytes.description: Bytes of a non-2xx backend body quoted in the isError result (cut at a UTF-8 boundary, with a truncation note).

max_structured_content_bytes.description: Largest JSON object returned as structuredContent. A larger JSON body is checked before parsing and returned as text content only, with a note (isError false), never truncated.

forward_request_headers.description: Client request headers forwarded to the backend on top of the fixed user-agent, accept-language, traceparent, and tracestate set (plus the gateway's own correlation header). Every other client header is dropped. A reserved name (hop-by-hop, Host, Authorization, Cookie, Range, If-Range, method or URL override families, trace baggage, client-address attribution, MCP transport, the MCP session headers, FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER, or a Ferrum-internal field) is refused. Add backend credentials with request_transformer, which runs after mcp_gateway.

McpGatewayOpenApiOperation.description: One bridged operation. The generated tool's inputSchema is a closed object: one property per parameter (keyed by its name) plus `body` for a JSON request body. Serialized tool definitions are bounded at 256 KiB and their schemas by the same depth, node, and local-reference budgets as a discovered outputSchema.

name.description: Upstream tool name (unique within the server); the public name is namespaced.

method.description: Backend HTTP method. HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, and CONNECT are not bridged.

path.description: The operation's PUBLIC request path on this proxy (listen path included), with `{name}` path parameters each occupying a whole segment. It is mapped onto the backend exactly as a direct request to that path would be (strip_listen_path, backend_path). It must sit under the matched proxy's listen path on a segment boundary whether or not strip_listen_path is set; a call whose path does not is refused with JSON-RPC -32603 and nothing is dispatched. On an exact (`=`) or regex (`~`) route every bridged call is refused the same way. It must not be able to fall inside endpoint.path's reserved subtree (ASCII case-insensitive, like the runtime claim; a `{name}` segment matches any endpoint segment, and repeats of one name must match the same text); load rejects it, and a substituted path inside the scope is refused with JSON-RPC -32602 before dispatch. Path arguments are percent-encoded per segment and the result must be a canonical policy path, so an argument can never add `/`, a dot segment, `?`, or `#`.

request_body.description: A JSON request body, carried by the tools/call argument `body`.

output_schema.description: Published as the tool's outputSchema; must describe an object, because structuredContent is a JSON object.

annotations.description: Overrides the method-derived hints (readOnlyHint for GET, destructiveHint for DELETE, idempotentHint for PUT).

McpGatewayOpenApiParameter.description: A path, query, or header parameter. Query arrays are sent exploded and form-encoded; header arrays comma-joined. Object-typed parameters, cookie parameters, and array path parameters are rejected. A header parameter may never name a hop-by-hop field, Host, Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-*, X-Forwarded-*, Forwarded, an MCP transport field (Mcp-*, Last-Event-ID, the configured session headers), or a Ferrum-internal field (X-Ferrum-*, Ferrum-*, X-Gateway-*, X-Consumer-*), compared case-insensitively with `_` treated as `-`; the plugin refuses such a configuration at load and again when a call is built.

schema.description: JSON Schema of the argument; omitted means a string.

MeshAuthzAction.description:
Istio `spec.action`, required on every rule. There is deliberately NO
default: a rule whose action failed to deserialize used to fall back to
`allow`, turning an operator's DENY into a grant with no diagnostic.

`custom` delegates to a `meshConfig.extensionProviders` entry carried on
the mesh slice. A provider name that does not bind — and every `custom`
rule in a flat `mesh_policies` config, which has no provider source at
all — refuses with a fixed `403` that no provider's `failOpen` admits.

MeshAuthzConditionMatch.description:
One Istio `when[]` condition. At least one of `values` / `not_values`
must be non-empty; a condition with neither never matches and is
rejected at admission. Keys outside the documented Istio set are
rejected with a field-specific diagnostic so a DENY condition on an
unmodelled attribute cannot silently fail open. See `docs/mesh.md` →
"Condition keys" for the key set and the per-key value grammars.

MeshAuthzConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_authz — Layer 2 mesh authorization evaluator. Applies
Istio-style `MeshPolicy` (ALLOW / DENY / AUDIT) rules to the SPIFFE
identity extracted by `spiffe_identity` or the HBONE baggage on
ambient mTLS streams. DENY rules are evaluated first (first match
wins); the presence of any ALLOW rule with no match triggers an
implicit deny.
`to.hosts` / `notHosts` match normalized literal request authorities,
without service-alias expansion. Explicit decimal ports use one
canonical spelling on both request and pattern sides; wildcard ports
remain supported. Signed request ports are rejected at admission.

Source matching enforces both the positive identity matchers
(`principals` in Istio `<trust-domain>/ns/.../sa/...` form,
`serviceAccounts`, `namespaces`, `trustDomains`,
`requestPrincipals`) and the conjunctive negative and IP-block
matchers (`notPrincipals`/`notServiceAccounts`/`notNamespaces`/
`notTrustDomains`/`notRequestPrincipals`/`ipBlocks`/`notIpBlocks`/
`remoteIpBlocks`/`notRemoteIpBlocks`). `when:` conditions cover the
complete documented Istio condition-key set: `source.principal`,
`source.namespace`, `source.serviceAccount`, `source.trustDomain`,
`source.ip`, `remote.ip`, `destination.ip`,
`destination.port`, `connection.sni`, `request.auth.principal`,
`request.auth.presenter`, `request.auth.audiences`,
`request.auth.claims[...]` string or string-list values including
nested claim leaf paths, `request.headers[...]`, and
`experimental.envoy.filters.<filter>[<key>]`.
Dynamic header/claim keys follow Istio's loose map-key framing: the
first `[` and final `]` delimit a non-empty interior without a separate
HTTP-header-name parse. Known HTTP pseudo-headers (`:authority`,
`:method`, `:path`, `:scheme`) are sourced from typed request facts;
unusual admitted interiors that cannot materialize remain absent.
Values follow Istio's string-matcher grammar (`*` presence,
`<prefix>*`, `*<suffix>`, otherwise exact — a mid-string `*` is literal
text) for every key EXCEPT the ones Istio compiles differently:
`source.ip`/`remote.ip`/`destination.ip` are CIDR blocks;
`source.serviceAccount` is an exact match over
`<namespace>/<service-account>` where a bare `<service-account>` is
resolved against the declaring policy's namespace and a `*` is rejected;
and `source.namespace` treats every `*` as an arbitrary substring at any
position, including mid-string and repeated stars. Keys outside the
documented prefixes — and empty/oversized/control-character keys or
malformed values, non-numeric
`destination.port` values, malformed IP CIDRs, a `source.serviceAccount`
with a `*` or more than one `/`, a `source.trustDomain` with a `/` or a
repeated/mid-string `*`, a non-ASCII `connection.sni` value that
cannot be converted to its A-label, and collections over 64 `when[]`
entries per
rule or 256 values per list (16 values of at most 320 bytes for
`source.serviceAccount`) — are rejected during translation/config
validation with a field-specific diagnostic, on both `values` and
`notValues`, so DENY conditions cannot silently fail open.
`connection.sni` values are normalized at load to the spelling of the
received ClientHello SNI: one trailing dot is stripped, ASCII is
lowercased, and a non-ASCII (U-label) name is converted to its A-label
with IDNA. Other ASCII characters that DNS hostnames do not allow are
not rejected; such a value never matches.
An attribute the path CAN source but that this request lacks follows
ordinary Istio semantics (a `values` check fails; a `notValues`-only
check passes). An attribute the path can NEVER source — an HTTP-only key
on a TCP/UDP/DTLS connection, a source/remote/destination IP or
destination port with no typed transport evidence, or any
`experimental.envoy.filters.*` key — is fail-closed in
both directions, matching Istio's non-HTTP-port behavior: a DENY rule
ignores the field and still matches, while an ALLOW or AUDIT rule can
never match. `destination.ip` is sourced only from the captured pre-NAT
original destination or the connection's local address, never from a
client-settable header. That mesh-authz connection fact is separate
from VirtualService L4 `destinationSubnets`, which accepts only trusted
PROXY/capture original-destination evidence and never an ordinary
listener's bind/local address.
Negative identity matchers reject only when the source/JWT identity
is present and matches an excluded pattern; absent identities satisfy
the negative matcher so DENY policies such as `notPrincipals: ["*"]`
and `notRequestPrincipals: ["*"]` catch anonymous traffic. IP-block
matchers fail closed when the IP they test is absent, and malformed
CIDRs reject translated resources or direct plugin config. See
`docs/mesh.md`.

Auto-injected by mesh mode on every applicable topology; reserved
plugin id `__mesh_authz`. PolicyScope filtering (`MeshWide` /
`Namespace` / `WorkloadSelector` / `TargetRefs`) is applied at
construction time from the slice-embedded workload identity, except in
node-waypoint topology where the filter runs per-request against the
pod-scoped cache attached to `RequestContext`. `TargetRefs`
(AuthorizationPolicy `spec.targetRef` / `spec.targetRefs`) is
waypoint-only and is additionally re-checked per request against the
exact destination Service and waypoint Gateway/GatewayClass identity — construction-time
retention is OR over the attachment list and never widens a targeted
policy onto another destination. See `docs/mesh.md`.

Root-shape admission: an object, or `null` (how an omitted `config:`
block deserializes for every plugin, meaning "no configuration
supplied"). A scalar or array root is REJECTED at construction rather
than degraded into a default instance — a policy-free `mesh_authz`
never raises the implicit-deny floor and therefore allows every
request. Unknown root keys are rejected for the same reason.

mesh_slice.description:
Embedded mesh slice — supplied by mesh-mode auto-injection.
Carries the filtered policy set plus the workload's
`namespace`/`labels` used for slice-level scope filtering, the
admitted `ext_authz_providers` set, and the destination inventory.
Not intended for direct operator configuration; operator-managed
instances pass `mesh_policies` instead.

Deliberately left unmodelled here. The slice is a machine-authored
document produced by the same Ferrum build that consumes it, its
shape tracks every mesh resource family, and a partial schema for
it would drift into rejecting valid injected configuration. It is
admitted by the runtime deserializer instead, which fails the whole
plugin generation on a malformed slice so the previous valid
generation keeps serving. Its root members are closed (an
unrecognized top-level slice member is rejected), and its
`mesh_policies` member follows the same closed policy grammar
modelled below, including the never-match matcher refusals.

Its `ext_authz_providers` entries are closed (with their
`include_additional_headers_in_check` and
`include_request_body_in_check` objects) and may declare
`headers_to_upstream_on_allow` (provider response headers that
replace the backend request's same-named headers on an allowed
CUSTOM check, applied in this plugin's `before_proxy`; client copies
are always removed) and `headers_to_downstream_on_allow` (added to
the allowed response in `after_proxy`, `Set-Cookie` appended).
Gateway identity assertions (`x-consumer-*`, `x-path-param-*`, …),
`content-*`, and (upstream) `set-cookie` are refused there. Every
check carries `x-ferrum-source-principal`,
`x-ferrum-source-namespace`, `x-ferrum-source-service-account`, and
`x-ferrum-request-principal`.

mesh_policies.description:
Standalone-mode policy list. Used by direct configuration when no
slice is available. Rules with `action: custom` in this form always
DENY: a flat list carries no `extensionProviders` source, and a
delegation that cannot be executed is never allowed to fall through
to the ALLOW/DENY tiers.

The grammar is CLOSED at every level and `action` is REQUIRED on
every rule: each misspelling here removes a restriction the
operator wrote, so an unrecognized member fails admission rather
than silently widening the effective policy.

namespace.description:
Proxy workload namespace, used by the slice-level PolicyScope
filter to discard policies that do not apply to this workload.
Overrides any namespace embedded in `mesh_slice`.

labels.description:
Proxy workload labels, used by the slice-level scope filter for
`WorkloadSelector`-scoped policies. Overrides any labels embedded
in `mesh_slice`.

trust_domain_aliases.description:
Additional SPIFFE trust domains accepted as equivalent to the
peer cert's trust domain when authorising HBONE baggage
`source.principal`. Empty (default) means strict same-trust-domain
match. `null` is accepted and treated as absent. Each entry must be
a valid SPIFFE trust domain (SPIFFE-ID section 2.1): lowercase, at
most 255 bytes, and composed only of `[a-z0-9._-]`, including at
the first and last byte.

per_pod_policy_scoping.description:
When `true`, the construction-time slice-level scope filter is
skipped and policies are filtered per-connection using the
`PolicyScopeCache` attached to `RequestContext.node_waypoint_policy_scope`
(HTTP/HBONE) or `StreamConnectionContext.node_waypoint_policy_scope`
(raw TCP streams). A connection whose source pod has no resolved
per-pod scope records `mesh_authz.scope_missing`; when any
namespace/selector-scoped policy is configured it then **fails closed**
(`403`, `mesh_authz.deny_policy=scope_missing`) on the HTTP/HBONE
request path and raw TCP streams (at accept) — a missing scope
means the source workload left the live slice generation, not an
enrollment race, so a long-lived connection from a removed workload
stops being served under scoped authz. NodeWaypoint UDP/DTLS has no
trustworthy per-datagram/session pod scope, so slice preparation
disables UDP/DTLS service/proxy paths when enforcing
namespace/selector-scoped policies are present; mesh-wide UDP/DTLS
policy remains evaluable, and audit-only scoped policy does not
force suppression. Auto-set by mesh injection on `NodeWaypoint`
topology where one listener serves many pods.

ambient_udp_source_scoping.description: Enables node-waypoint Ambient UDP source-policy scoping. Injected by mesh runtime configuration rather than operator-managed plugin config.

cluster_domain.description: Primary Kubernetes cluster domain injected by mesh mode.

cluster_domains.description: Deduplicated cluster-domain aliases used for node-waypoint service host matching; injected by mesh mode.

node_waypoint_route_upstreams.description: Mesh-generated route upstream metadata used to precompute destination policy scopes for node-waypoint dispatch. Each entry and each target is closed: an unrecognized member is rejected.

node_waypoint_route_branches.description: Mesh-generated candidate destinations of each NodeWaypoint VirtualService route whose `mesh_route_dispatch` rules can select a destination other than the route's own: the route's own destination first, then each rule destination. Each candidate's destination policy is evaluated before dispatch, and the destination a request finally reaches is admitted only on its own verdict. Every entry and destination is closed; a destination names exactly one of `upstream_id` or `backend_host` + `backend_port`. A weighted split the route dispatches leg by leg (`mesh_route_dispatch` `weighted_splits`, issue #7387) is listed through its legs, never as a candidate of its own.

weighted_split.description:
The route reaches some candidates only through
weighted-split leg selection, so verdicts are recorded even
when no AuthorizationPolicy is loaded and a split no leg was
selected for is refused.

own_is_weighted_split.description:
The route's own destination (the first entry) is a weighted
split: it is never judged or admitted, and each selected
leg's own verdict decides.

trusted_hbone_assertors.description:
Allow-list of identity-asserting infrastructure components whose
HBONE baggage `source.principal` may rewrite the authz principal.
Bare service-account names match any peer whose SPIFFE path ends
with `/sa/<name>`; full SPIFFE IDs match exactly. Default is
`["ztunnel", "waypoint"]`. Explicit empty array disables all
baggage rewriting.

Matching a peer is necessary but NOT sufficient (issue #4274):
every entry also carries a grant that decides WHICH identities that
peer may assert. String entries and objects without `asserts` /
`scope` grant `same_namespace` only, so a peer in
`ns/attacker/sa/waypoint` can no longer assert
`ns/prod/sa/payments`. Baggage refused by the grant is dropped, the
peer-cert identity is used instead, and the request is stamped
`mesh_authz.ignored_baggage.assertion_out_of_scope=true`.

MeshAuthzPolicy.description:
One `MeshPolicy` document, as accepted by the `mesh_authz` plugin's
`mesh_policies` list and by the native/file mesh document. Mirrors
Istio `AuthorizationPolicy`.

The grammar is CLOSED at every level below: an unrecognized member is
rejected at admission rather than dropped, because every misspelling in
an authorization grammar removes a restriction. See `docs/mesh.md` →
"MeshPolicy" and "Rule Matching".

Matchers that could never match are rejected at plugin construction
too — for the flat `mesh_policies` form and an embedded `mesh_slice`
alike, with the same diagnostics as the native mesh validator: an
empty `name` / `namespace`, an empty `from[{}]` or `to[{}]` entry, a
`to.headers` pseudo-header, an invalid `hosts` / `not_hosts` pattern,
and an inadmissible `port_patterns` / `not_port_patterns` entry.

name.description: Policy name, used in deny diagnostics and metadata.

namespace.description:
The namespace that declared this policy. Load-bearing beyond
identification: a bare `source.serviceAccount` value in a `when`
condition is resolved against it.

rules.description:
Rules are additive. DENY rules are evaluated first and the first
match wins; if any ALLOW rule is loaded and none matches, the
implicit-deny floor refuses the request. An explicitly empty list
is a valid scaffold that matches nothing.

MeshAuthzPolicyScope.description:
Which workloads this policy applies to, discriminated by `kind`.
Resolved by the shared `policy_scope_applies_to_workload` predicate at
plugin construction — except in node-waypoint topology, where one
listener serves many pods and the filter runs per request against the
pod-scoped cache.

Closed like the rest of the grammar: each `kind` admits only its own
members, so an unrecognized sibling key (including one beside
`kind: mesh_wide`) is rejected at admission. The nested `selector` and
every `attachments` entry are closed too.

namespace.description: Applies to workloads in exactly this namespace.

selector.description:
Label/namespace selector. An empty selector matches EVERY
workload, which is why unknown members are rejected here: a
misspelled `labels` key would widen a targeted policy onto the
whole mesh instead of failing admission.

attachments.description:
Istio `spec.targetRefs` attachments. A policy matches when ANY
attachment applies (OR), and retention alone proves nothing —
every runtime consumer re-checks the exact attachment against
its own authoritative evidence. Waypoint-only.

MeshAuthzPrincipalMatch.description:
One source identity matcher. Every populated field must match. A source
with no verified peer identity never matches.

spiffe_id_pattern.description:
Glob over the Istio source principal
(`<trust-domain>/ns/<ns>/sa/<sa>`); a full `spiffe://…` pattern is
also accepted in direct config.

namespace_pattern.description: Glob over the source workload namespace.

trust_domain_pattern.description: Glob over the source trust domain.

MeshAuthzRequestMatch.description:
One request matcher (Istio `to[].operation`). Positive and negative
fields in the SAME matcher are conjunctive — never split a negative
field into a separate rule.

ALLOW/AUDIT rules fail closed when the attribute is absent. DENY and
`custom` rules treat an UNSOURCEABLE attribute as a match (Istio's
non-HTTP-port model), but an HTTP-family request whose header map was
parsed and simply lacks the named header is ABSENT, not unsourceable,
and fails a positive `headers` predicate for every action.

paths.description: Glob patterns, matched against the canonical policy path.

hosts.description:
Glob patterns over the normalized literal request authority. These
do NOT expand service aliases.

port_patterns.description: Istio string-match ports such as `"*"` or `"8*"`.

headers.description:
Header name (case-insensitive, lowercased at config load) to glob
value pattern. The pseudo-header names `:path`, `:method`,
`:authority`, and `:scheme` are rejected (they are not in the
request header map; use `paths` / `methods` / `hosts`, or a
`when: request.headers[:path]` condition). A header sent as several
field lines is matched as ONE value — every line joined with `, `
(`; ` for `cookie`) — the same reading `when: request.headers[...]`
conditions and CUSTOM forwarded headers use.

MeshAuthzRule.description:
One authorization rule. Every populated dimension must match (a
conjunction); within a dimension the entries are ORed.

request_principals.description:
Glob patterns over the JWT-derived `{issuer}/{subject}` request
principal. HTTP-only: on a Layer-4 session a DENY/`custom` rule
ignores it and an ALLOW/AUDIT rule can never match on it.

not_request_principals.description:
Conjunctive negative match over the request principal. An absent
principal SATISFIES it, which is how `["*"]` catches anonymous
HTTP traffic.

never_matches.description:
Synthetic marker for a rule that must affect policy accounting but
never match traffic — Istio's ALLOW-without-rules "allow nothing".
Set by translation; hand-authoring it is not useful.

MeshAuthzSourceNegation.description:
Conjunctive negative-identity and IP-block matchers for one Istio
`from[].source`. These AND with the ORed positive `from` list; placing
them in `from` would let traffic through whenever a single negative-only
entry matched.

Negative identity matchers succeed when the identity is ABSENT, which is
how `not_spiffe_id_patterns: ["*"]` catches anonymous traffic. IP-block
matchers fail CLOSED when the IP they test is absent.

ip_blocks.description: CIDR or bare IP (host route); matched against `source.ip`.

remote_ip_blocks.description: CIDR or bare IP; matched against XFF-derived `remote.ip`.

MeshBpfMetricsConfig.description:
Plugin: __mesh_bpf_metrics - reserved internal mesh NodeWaypoint
plugin that exposes BPF SOCK_OPS counters and fixed-bucket TCP
latency histograms (SRTT / SYN-to-ACK / accept-to-first-byte)
on the Prometheus scrape surface. Mesh mode auto-injects a
global instance on NodeWaypoint; operator-managed plugin configs
should not create names prefixed with `__`. Enabled instances
must use `scope: global` (at most one enabled instance per
process). Registration is OptionalFailOpen: Admin create/update
still returns HTTP 400 for an invalid enabled config, while
file-mode load/`ferrum-edge validate` and plugin-cache rebuild
warn and omit the instance.

Object configs are closed: the only admitted key is `prefix`.
A string `prefix` is trimmed before the identifier check.
Non-object configs (null, string, array, number, boolean) keep
the default prefix `ferrum_mesh_bpf`.

prefix.description:
Prometheus metric name prefix for every emitted BPF family
(`{prefix}_tcp_events_total`, `{prefix}_drops_total`,
`{prefix}_srtt_microseconds`, `{prefix}_syn_to_ack_microseconds`,
`{prefix}_accept_to_first_byte_microseconds`, and the ringbuf
families). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before the
identifier check; the trimmed value must match
`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and must not be empty. There is no
declared length limit beyond that grammar. Omit the key to
keep `ferrum_mesh_bpf`.

MeshOutboundRegistryConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_outbound_registry — Implements Istio
`outboundTrafficPolicy.mode: REGISTRY_ONLY`. Rejects HTTP
requests whose `Host` header is not in the configured destination
registry. Auto-injected by mesh mode when the EFFECTIVE outbound policy
resolves to `RegistryOnly` — workload-scoped
`Sidecar.outboundTrafficPolicy`, else mesh-wide
`MeshConfig.outboundTrafficPolicy`, else
`FERRUM_MESH_OUTBOUND_TRAFFIC_POLICY`; not registered when the effective
policy is `AllowAny` (default).
Operator-managed instances on non-mesh gateways behave as a generic
HTTP `Host` allowlist.

Matches against four kinds of entries: bare hostnames (no Host port),
explicit `host:port` pairs, `host:*` (any explicit Host port), and
wildcard hosts (`*.example.com`, `*.example.com:443`,
`*.example.com:*`). Empty registry fails closed. Request `Host`
ports use the registry grammar (decimal 1–65535); `:0`, signed, or
non-numeric ports are denied. Mesh-derived registries drop slice
hosts outside this grammar with a warning (they stay denied) instead
of failing the whole config; operator-authored entries stay strict.
