Denials log a rate-limited warning naming the denied host.

registry.description:
Known destinations. Bare hostnames match requests with no
explicit `Host` port. `host:port` entries match only that port.
`host:*` entries match any explicit port. Wildcard entries
(`*.example.com[:port|:*]`) match per `wildcard_match` (one
DNS label below the suffix by default). Hostname labels use ASCII letters, digits, and interior
hyphens; supply internationalized names in punycode. IPv4 names
and IPv6 literals are supported; bracket IPv6 when specifying a
numeric port. Bare IPv6 and IPv6:* are also accepted.
Numeric destination ports are decimal 1–65535 (leading zeros
allowed). Surrounding whitespace, hostname case, trailing
hostname dots, and IPv6 spelling are normalized. Empty or
whitespace-only entries are ignored; an empty effective registry
rejects all destinations wherever enforcement applies.
URLs, paths, userinfo, internal whitespace, malformed brackets,
misplaced wildcards, and invalid ports fail construction with
the zero-based registry entry index.

reject_status.description:
Status code returned for unknown destinations. Operators may
override to 404 to mask unknown destinations.

outbound_listen_ports.description:
Optional frontend listener ports where the registry is enforced.
Every instance skips the listener-stamped Inbound mesh direction
before any registry decision, even on a matching port. Empty means
enforce on every other HTTP-family request, including non-mesh
listeners (operator-managed default). Mesh auto-injection names
the outbound capture listener ports. Ports must be 1–65535; use
`[]` for intentional global scope.

namespace.description:
Value of the mesh_namespace label on
ferrum_mesh_outbound_registry_decisions_total. Mesh injection
explicitly supplies the runtime namespace. Direct instances use
this config value (default ferrum), independently of the enclosing
PluginConfig resource namespace.

wildcard_match.description:
How `*.suffix` registry entries match request hosts.
`one_label` (default) matches exactly one DNS label below the
suffix (`api.example.com`, not `a.b.example.com`); this is the
Ferrum mesh wildcard contract shared with Sidecar egress scoping,
the mesh DNS proxy, and the stream-family REGISTRY_ONLY lane, so
mesh auto-injection always uses it. `dns_suffix` matches any DNS
name below the suffix (`a.b.example.com` too), like Envoy
virtual-host domains and Istio's host matcher. The base domain
never matches either mode. In `dns_suffix` mode an authority
over 253 bytes or with an empty label never matches a wildcard,
and probing stops at the deepest configured suffix's label
count.

MeshRouteBackendTlsConfig.description:
Strict route-local backend TLS override for mesh_route_dispatch.
Unknown keys (for example `client_certpath` or
`verify_server_certificate`) fail admission instead of silently
disabling intended mTLS materials or verification.

`client_cert_path` and `client_key_path` must be supplied together.
A `system://` `server_ca_cert_path` cannot be combined with
`verify_server_cert: false` (the same contradiction Proxy and Upstream
admission reject); that pairing is a runtime check because the schema
cannot condition on a value prefix and a sibling boolean at once.

Admin writes of a `mesh_route_dispatch` plugin config apply the
Proxy/Upstream backend TLS reference admission to `client_cert_path`,
`client_key_path`, and `server_ca_cert_path` in every
`rules[].destination.backend_tls`: when admin namespace-claim
enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with
enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`,
or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace, and any other
reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is
loaded. A value already stored at the same rule index and field is
exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

MeshRouteBackoffStrategy.description:
Strict route-local retry delay strategy for mesh_route_dispatch. Each
delay is bounded to `[0, 300000]` ms by the shared gateway
`RetryConfig` field validation the route policy runs; `base_ms` must
additionally not exceed `max_ms`, which JSON Schema cannot express
across two sibling properties and is therefore a runtime-only check.

MeshRouteDispatchConfig.description:
Plugin: mesh_route_dispatch — Per-request route override driven by
method / header / query-param predicates. Closes the Istio
`VirtualService.http[].match` header/method gap without extending
the `Proxy` schema. Runs after authentication, authorization, and
rate limiting — admission decisions still use the public listener
identity; only downstream `before_proxy` plugins and backend
dispatch see the effective override destination.

At least one rule is required unless `weighted_splits` is set. When multiple plugin instances run on
one proxy, each matching instance replaces the override destination
set by earlier instances. Per-rule `backend_tls` is direct-backend
only (`upstream_id` destinations inherit TLS from the referenced
Upstream).

Unknown keys are rejected at every owned nesting level, including
route-local `retry` / backoff and destination `backend_tls`
(`additionalProperties: false` / serde `deny_unknown_fields`). Shared
gateway `RetryConfig` and `BackendTlsConfig` schemas remain open for
other consumers; mesh routes use `MeshRouteRetryConfig` and
`MeshRouteBackendTlsConfig`.

`rules` may be empty only when `weighted_splits` lists at least one
split (an instance that only resolves weighted splits).

items.description:
One ordered route rule. `destination` is required — and must
carry at least one override field — unless the rule carries a
`redirect` (which answers the request itself and needs no
backend). First match wins.

name.description:
Optional operator label for the rule: 1-128 printable ASCII
characters without whitespace. A match publishes
`mesh_route_dispatch.rule_index` (the rule's zero-based
position) and, when set, `mesh_route_dispatch.rule_name`
transaction-log metadata; both are withdrawn when a
NodeWaypoint authorization veto refuses the matched
destination.

match.description:
Match criteria — all configured fields must match for the
rule to fire. At least one of `methods`/`headers`/
`without_headers`/`query_params`/`authority`/
`source_namespace`/`uri`/`port` must be
configured, UNLESS the rule carries a route action
(`request_transform`, `response_transform`, `fault`,
`rewrite`, `redirect`, `timeout_ms`,
`timeout_disabled: true`, `request_timeout_ms`,
`attempt_timeout_ms`, `retry`, or
`retry_disabled: true`), which makes an empty match the
translator's deliberate action-only catch-all. An empty
match with no route action is rejected at load time because
it would silently shadow every later rule. `ignore_uri_case`
is not a predicate: it decorates `uri` and is rejected
without one.

oneOf.description:
Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.
Must be a non-empty RFC 9110 method token: the hot
path compares it with `==` against the request
method, so an operand carrying a space or another
non-token character can never match and is
rejected at config load.

Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of
`exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. The runtime is an
externally tagged enum, so both `{}` and
`{"exact": "GET", "prefix": "G"}` are rejected.
Prefix patterns are uppercased at compile time
(methods are uppercase ASCII per RFC 9110 §9.1);
regex patterns are interpreted verbatim inside
full-input anchors. `exact` / `prefix` operands
must be non-empty method tokens (case and
extension methods such as `PROPFIND` are
preserved); `regex` is a pattern rather than a
token and is only checked for regex validity.

methods.description: HTTP methods (any-of). Empty = no method restriction.

propertyNames.description:
Header names are RFC 9110 tokens, normalized to ASCII
lowercase at config load. A name outside the token
grammar (empty, `x bad`, `x:bad`) can never appear in
a parsed request header map, so it is rejected at
config load rather than admitted as a rule that
silently never fires.

oneOf.description: Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.

Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of
`exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. The runtime is an
externally tagged enum, so both `{}` and
`{"exact": "a", "prefix": "b"}` are rejected.
An empty `exact` is a legitimate "header present
and empty" predicate; empty `prefix` / `regex`
operands are rejected at config load.

headers.description: Header matches (all-of). Header names are case-insensitive.

without_headers.description:
Negated header matches (Istio `withoutHeaders`), keyed
and normalized exactly like `headers`. The rule fails
when ANY listed header is present and its value
satisfies the matcher; an absent header never vetoes
the rule, so `{"x-legacy": {"regex": ".*"}}` requires
the header to be absent.

port.description:
Destination port the client addressed (Istio
`HTTPMatchRequest.port`), read from trusted provenance
only: the original destination when capture rewrote the
accept socket, otherwise the frontend listener port —
never `Host` or forwarding headers. A request with
neither does not match.

oneOf.description:
Istio StringMatch shape — EXACTLY one of `exact` /
`prefix` / `regex`. `regex` must match the full
decoded value; empty `prefix` / `regex` operands
are rejected at config load.

query_params.description: Query parameter matches (all-of), compared after percent-decoding the backend-bound query representation available at the dispatch hook, including authentication-owned credential strips and any priority-overridden request_transformer that already ran. A deliberately later route/request transform remains a separate ordered operation. A request whose query cannot be decoded to one value is rejected with 400 before any rule is evaluated: a repeated or percent-encoded duplicate name, a literal '+' (RFC 3986 plus vs form-urlencoded space), an unencoded ';' (a pair separator for backends that also split on ';'; '%3B' is unambiguous), malformed percent-encoding, or a non-UTF-8 decoding.

uri.description:
Optional URI predicate (Istio `StringMatch` shape).
Exactly one of `exact` / `prefix` / `regex`. This is
normally omitted because the parent proxy `listen_path`
gates URI selection; the VirtualService translator emits
it for widened `ignoreUriCase` routes and collapsed
route-order fallbacks that need dispatch-layer URI
precision. Regex patterns must match the full URI path.

ignore_uri_case.description:
When true, folds ASCII case for `match.uri.exact` and
`match.uri.prefix` comparisons only. Regex URI matches
keep their operator-supplied regex unchanged; operators
who want case-insensitive regex should write `(?i)` in
the pattern. Requires `match.uri`.

source_namespace.description:
Source workload Kubernetes namespace (exact match).
Mirrors Istio `VirtualService.http[].match.sourceNamespace`:
the CRD models this as an exact-only string (no
`prefix`/`regex` arms). Resolved from the peer's SPIFFE
ID via the Istio convention
`spiffe://<trust-domain>/ns/<namespace>/sa/<service-account>`.
Matches are case-sensitive (Kubernetes namespace names
are RFC 1123 lowercase). The predicate fails closed
(returns no-match) when the request carries no resolved
peer SPIFFE identity, so non-mesh requests and clients
that present non-SPIFFE certificates do not match.
Empty / whitespace-only values are rejected at load time.

authority.description:
`:authority` / `Host` match (Istio `HTTPMatchRequest.authority`).
Exactly one of `exact` / `prefix` / `regex` per rule.
Exact and prefix patterns compare against the raw request
`Host`/`:authority` case-sensitively, including an
explicit request port when present. Regex patterns are
compiled verbatim and must match the full authority
string; operators who want case-insensitive regex should
write `(?i)` in the pattern. Distinct from
VirtualService-level `hosts`, which gates proxy
admission — this is a per-rule predicate evaluated AFTER
routing has picked the proxy.

oneOf.description: Bare-string back-compat form, interpreted as Exact.

destination.description:
Override applied on match. At least one field must be set
(enforced at rule level, where a `redirect` rule is allowed
to omit `destination` entirely). `upstream_id` is mutually
exclusive with the direct-backend fields
(`backend_host`/`backend_port`/`backend_tls`);
`backend_host` and `backend_port` must be set together, and
`backend_tls` requires both.

backend_host.description:
Direct-backend host. This is a BARE host — a DNS name,
an IPv4 literal, or an IPv6 literal in either `::1` or
`[::1]` form — with the port carried by `backend_port`.
The dispatch path hands the value straight to DNS
resolution, so an embedded authority port, scheme, path,
query, fragment, or userinfo resolves to nothing and is
rejected at config load rather than answering 502 on
every matching request. Leading / trailing whitespace is
trimmed and the value is ASCII-lowercased at load, so
the length bound applies to the TRIMMED value at
runtime while `maxLength` here counts the raw string.
The pattern is likewise a conservative approximation:
the runtime additionally parses the IPv6 forms, so a
colon-bearing value that is not a valid IPv6 literal
(`1:2:3`) passes this schema and is still refused at
admission.

backend_tls.description: Optional per-rule backend TLS override (direct backends only).

requires_node_waypoint_authz.description:
Trusted mesh-translator marker. When scoped NodeWaypoint
authorization is active, a matching destination carrying
this marker requires an authorized destination stamp.

timeout_ms.description:
Optional route-local backend response/read timeout in
milliseconds. Mutually exclusive with
`timeout_disabled: true`. `0` means "no timeout" and is the
value `timeout_disabled: true` resolves to.

timeout_disabled.description:
Explicitly clear the selected proxy's inherited backend
response/read timeout. Cannot be true when `timeout_ms` is set.

request_timeout_ms.description:
Optional TOTAL request deadline for this rule, in
milliseconds from request receipt (Gateway API
`HTTPRoute.rules[].timeouts.request`). Unlike `timeout_ms`,
which bounds one backend attempt's wait for response headers
and the idle gap between response frames, it spans every
attempt, retry backoff, and the streaming response body, and
is never re-armed by a retry. Request-scoped: it never changes
the selected proxy or upstream. Expiry before a non-gRPC
response head answers `504` (with `X-Gateway-Error:
request_timeout` when no backend held the request, otherwise
`backend_timeout`); expiry mid-body resets the HTTP/2
stream, closes the HTTP/1.1 connection, or resets the
HTTP/3 stream with `H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED`; a gRPC request
folds it into its RPC deadline and ends with
`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and native HTTP/3
enforce it alike. Expiry is charged to a backend's health
only when that backend held the cancelled attempt; expiry
before the attempt was handed to a backend, in retry backoff,
or after the response head is health-neutral. Upgraded
WebSocket / CONNECT-UDP tunnels are not bounded by it. `0` is
rejected; omit the field for no route deadline.

attempt_timeout_ms.description:
Optional TOTAL bound on each backend attempt for this rule, in
milliseconds (Gateway API
`HTTPRoute.rules[].timeouts.backendRequest`, which the
translator also projects as `timeout_ms`). The budget starts
when the attempt is handed to the backend and covers its
response head and its whole response body; every retry
attempt gets a fresh budget, and `request_timeout_ms`, when
set, still bounds the whole transaction. It is independent of
`timeout_ms` / `timeout_disabled`, which keep bounding the
header wait and the idle gap between frames. Expiry before a
non-gRPC response head answers the ordinary backend-timeout
`504` (retried when the rule's `retry` lists `504`); expiry
after the head has been sent is never retried and cuts the
body exactly like `request_timeout_ms` does (HTTP/2 stream
reset, HTTP/1.1 connection close, HTTP/3
`H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED` stream reset, health-neutral). A gRPC
request folds it into its RPC deadline, anchored when the rule
is selected and re-armed for each retry attempt, and ends with
`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and native HTTP/3
enforce it alike. Request-scoped: it never changes the
selected proxy or upstream. `0` is rejected; omit the field
for no per-attempt total bound.

retry.description:
Optional route-local retry policy. Mutually exclusive with
`retry_disabled: true`. Request-scoped: it replaces the
selected proxy's retry policy only for requests this rule
matches. Istio `VirtualService.http[].retries` and Gateway
API `HTTPRoute.rules[].retry` are projected here; the Gateway
API translator emits `max_retries` = `attempts` (retries
after the initial attempt), `retryable_status_codes` =
`codes`, a `fixed` backoff of `backoff`, the default
replay-safe `retryable_methods`, and
`retry_on_connect_failure: true`. Backoff and every attempt
stay inside the rule's `request_timeout_ms` budget.

retry_disabled.description:
Explicitly clear the selected proxy's inherited retry
policy. Cannot be true when `retry` is set.

request_transform.description:
Per-rule request header transforms (Istio VirtualService
`http[].headers.request.{set,add,remove}`). Published onto
`RequestContext.route_override_request_transform` when this
rule matches. Every enabled `request_transformer` on the
proxy applies only its static header rules first; proxy core
then applies this list exactly once after the last eligible
(enabled) instance so route-level header writes win under
multiple same-type instances and priority overrides. A
disabled RTDS transformer is not eligible and does not
consume the list. `apply_route_overrides: true` lets an
auto-emitted empty-rules instance act as that eligible
consumer. Validated at config load — CRLF in values,
unknown operations, and `add`/`update` destinations in the
gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace or
the router's `x-path-param-*` route-capture namespace
(case-insensitive, `_` or `-`) are rejected. The request list
is applied after the LATER of the last eligible consumer and
the last dispatch instance, so a consumer a priority override
moves ahead of the dispatcher still applies it. An effective
chain whose rules carry `request_transform` but that has no
configured `request_transformer` is refused at plugin-cache
construction and admin admission (the list would otherwise be
silently dropped); an RTDS-disabled transformer still counts
as configured.

value.description: Required and non-null for add/update; omitted or null for remove.

response_transform.description:
Per-rule response header transforms (Istio VirtualService
`http[].headers.response.{set,add,remove}`). Same shape as
`request_transform` but applied on the response path: every
enabled `response_transformer` applies static header rules
first, then proxy core applies this list exactly once after
the last eligible instance (ordinary H1/H2/H3, synthetic/
rejection, header simulation, and deadline provenance paths).

Because this publishes onto the `response_transformer`
write surface, it shares that plugin's closed destination
set: add/update of a protocol-managed hop-by-hop or
framing name (`connection`, `content-length`,
`keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`,
`te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`,
case-insensitive) is rejected at construction. Remove of
those names remains allowed. `request_transform` keeps its
existing contract. An effective chain whose rules carry
`response_transform` but that has no configured
`response_transformer` is refused at plugin-cache
construction and admin admission.

value.description: Required and non-null for add/update; omitted or null for remove.

fault.description:
Optional per-rule fault action; `null` is accepted and means
"no fault", exactly as omitting the key does. Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].fault` onto the matched dispatch
rule (replacing the historical proxy-scoped
`fault_injection` plugin that could not be collapsed
with sibling routes). At least one of `delay` / `abort`
must be present.

RTDS scope: the percentages baked into a per-rule fault
are NOT runtime-tunable via the GAP-3E RTDS keys
`ferrum.fault_injection.<scope>.{abort,delay}_percent` —
those keys apply only to `fault_injection` plugin
instances configured with `runtime_overlay_scope`.
Operators who need RTDS-driven fault percentages
should use a global / proxy-scoped `fault_injection`
plugin instead.

duration_ms.description:
Sleep duration in milliseconds before dispatch
when the percentile roll hits. Bounded to
`[1, 60_000]` (1 ms to 1 minute).

percentage.description:
Percent of matching requests that trigger the
delay. `0.0` is rejected at config load time
(omit the action to disable it instead). Positive
values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up
to that first bucket so every accepted value can
trigger.

Percent of matching requests that abort. Positive
values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to
that first bucket so every accepted value can trigger.

grpc_status.description:
Optional gRPC status code emitted only when the
immutable pre-plugin request flavor is native
gRPC. Plain HTTP, WebSocket, and gRPC-Web requests
never receive a stray `grpc-status` header even if
an earlier hook rewrites `content-type`.

body.description: Optional response body; empty when omitted.

rewrite.description:
Optional per-rule URI / authority rewrite; `null` is
accepted and means "no rewrite". Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].rewrite` onto the matched dispatch
rule so a rewriting route can be collapsed with sibling
routes onto one Ferrum proxy without rewriting the siblings'
traffic. At least one of `uri` / `authority` must be set.
Applied when the rule matches and no `redirect` fires.

uri.description:
Replacement request path forwarded to the backend. When
`match_prefix` is set (the source `match.uri` was a
prefix) only that prefix is replaced; otherwise the whole
path is replaced. Must be a canonical absolute path
without a query or fragment. Percent escapes, dot
segments, backslashes, and CRLF are rejected at load
time (the schema only checks the leading `/`; full
canonical-path admission is a runtime check). The
composed path is checked again before policy and
dispatch; ambiguous paths are refused, not resolved.

authority.description:
Replacement `Host` / `:authority` forwarded to the
backend. Must be exactly `host` or `host:port`: a DNS
name or IPv4 literal (letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`) or a
bracketed IPv6 literal, optionally followed by a decimal
port 1-65535. A path, query, fragment, userinfo,
whitespace, or bare IPv6 literal is rejected at load. The
runtime additionally parses the IPv6 literal and the port
range, which the pattern only approximates.

match_prefix.description:
Literal path prefix the source `match.uri.prefix`
matched. The plugin replaces exactly this prefix with
`uri` and appends the unmatched suffix VERBATIM (Istio
`HTTPRewrite` / Envoy `prefix_rewrite`), so a prefix
ending inside a path segment keeps that segment: with
`match_prefix: /prefix/old` and `uri: /new`,
`/prefix/oldtail` forwards as `/newtail`. A separator is
never synthesized; a doubled one is collapsed when both
sides carry a `/`. An empty string strips nothing and
prepends `uri` (the Gateway API root `PathPrefix: /`
case); omit the field for whole-path replacement. A
`match_prefix` with no `uri` is inert and dropped.
Normally set by the VirtualService or Gateway API
translator, not hand-authored.

redirect.description:
Optional per-rule HTTP redirect; `null` is accepted and
means "no redirect" (a rule that is `null` here still needs
a `destination`). Projects Istio
`VirtualService.http[].redirect`. When the rule matches the
request is answered with a 3xx + `Location` and never reaches
a backend; takes precedence over `rewrite` and the route
override destination. A status-only redirect is valid and
preserves the original URL. A rule carrying a `redirect`
does not require a `destination`. `port` and `derive_port`
are mutually exclusive (Istio oneof); scheme-default ports
are omitted from Location.

uri.description:
Replacement path for the Location header; request path
preserved when unset. Must be an absolute path (leading
`/`) of printable ASCII only — no fragment, whitespace,
raw control byte, or unencoded non-ASCII, query included
— whose path
component is already canonical (dot segments,
backslashes, and escapes that decode differently are
rejected at load — a runtime check the pattern does not
express). It may carry its own `?query` unless
`match_prefix` is set, because the unmatched request
suffix is appended after `uri`.

match_prefix.description:
Literal matched path prefix replaced by `uri`; the
unmatched suffix is appended verbatim, exactly as for
`rewrite.match_prefix` (no separator is synthesized at a
boundary that had none). An empty string strips nothing
and prepends `uri`; omit the field for whole-path
replacement. Normally emitted by the VirtualService or
Gateway API translator.

authority.description:
Replacement authority (`host` or `host:port`) for the
Location header; request authority preserved when unset.
Same grammar as `rewrite.authority`.

port.description:
Replacement authority port (Istio `redirect.port`); request
host is preserved when authority is unset. Mutually
exclusive with `derive_port`. Scheme-default ports
(`80`/`http`, `443`/`https`) are omitted from Location.

derive_port.description:
Dynamically derive the Location authority port (Istio
`redirect.derivePort`). `FROM_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT` uses 80 for
http and 443 for https (including when `scheme` is set on
the same redirect). `FROM_REQUEST_PORT` uses the trusted
request port: original-destination port when capture
rewrote the accept socket, otherwise the frontend listener
port — never spoofable `X-Forwarded-Port` / `Forwarded`
headers. Mutually exclusive with `port`.

scheme.description:
Replacement scheme for the Location header; request
scheme preserved when unset. The constructor
ASCII-lowercases the value before checking it, so
`HTTPS` and `Https` are accepted and stored as `https`.

redirect_code.description: HTTP redirect status code (Istio `redirectCode`). Defaults to 301.

reject_unmatched.description:
When `true`, requests that match no rule are rejected with 404
instead of falling through to the proxy's default backend. The
Istio VirtualService translator sets this so a route gated by a
method/header/query-param `match` does not serve traffic that
misses those predicates. Across multiple attached instances, the
decision is finalized only after all instances run and only when
no instance matched and no earlier route override exists.

weighted_splits.description:
Weighted splits dispatched leg by leg (issue #7387). When the
destination the whole dispatch group selects is one of these
`upstream_id`s (a matched rule's `destination.upstream_id`, or the
route's own `upstream_id` when no rule overrides it), the dispatch
finalizer the plugin cache installs after the last instance picks
one leg by weight (an exact, interleaved weighted cycle) and sends
the request through that leg's own upstream, so the leg's own
DestinationRule projection and authorization apply to exactly the
requests it receives. A split no leg was selected for is never
dispatched. NodeWaypoint mesh slice preparation writes this for a
VirtualService split that names a DestinationRule-governed Service
or external host and refuses a carried route that already carries
it.

upstream_id.description: The split destination this entry resolves; unique per instance.

The upstream this leg dispatches through. Distinct
within the split and never itself a weighted split.

weight.description: The leg's share, relative to the other legs.

originate_tls.description:
Dial this leg over TLS (backend scheme `https`) with
its upstream's backend TLS settings. The selected leg
decides the request's backend scheme; a leg without
it keeps the route's own scheme. NodeWaypoint slice
preparation sets it on an external host's leg whose
DestinationRule `tls.mode` originates TLS (`SIMPLE`,
`MUTUAL`, `ISTIO_MUTUAL`) on that port, never on a
Service leg, which keeps the mesh transport.

MeshRouteRetryConfig.description:
Strict route-local retry policy for mesh_route_dispatch. Unknown keys
(for example `max_retry` or `retry_on_connect_failur`) fail admission
instead of silently falling back to defaults. The numeric bounds below
mirror the shared gateway `RetryConfig` field validation the route
policy runs after deserialization.

items.description:
One of GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD / OPTIONS /
TRACE / CONNECT. The validator ASCII-uppercases before
comparing, so `get` and `Get` are accepted.

MeshTrustedHboneAssertors.description:
Trusted HBONE assertor allow-list shared by `mesh_authz`,
`workload_metrics`, and the injected
`_effective_mesh_authz_baggage_gates`. Both plugins admit it through one
parser, so this one schema is the contract for every copy. `null` (or
omission) selects the default `["ztunnel", "waypoint"]`; `[]` disables
baggage-derived identity entirely.

Whitespace is trimmed with Rust `str::trim` (Unicode `White_Space`)
before any comparison; the patterns spell that class out explicitly so
every JSON Schema regex dialect reads it the same way. A value that is
empty after trimming is refused.

asserts.description:
Exact SPIFFE IDs this assertor may assert and nothing
else — the inventory of workloads it actually fronts. An
empty array authorizes nothing. `null` is treated as
absent. Mutually exclusive with `scope`.

scope.description:
Explicit grant contract. `same_namespace` (the default
for every entry) permits only identities in the
assertor's own Kubernetes namespace; `mesh_wide` requires
`assertor` to be a full, exactly matched `spiffe://` ID,
permits any identity that clears the trust-domain gate,
and logs a warning at construction. Mutually exclusive
with `asserts`. `null` is treated as absent. Surrounding
whitespace is trimmed before the value is compared,
matching the `assertor` field's normalization; the
pattern rather than an `enum` is what expresses that.

assertor.description:
Bare service-account name (matches any peer whose SPIFFE path ends
with `/sa/<name>`) or full `spiffe://` SPIFFE ID (matches exactly)
identifying the peer this entry admits. Surrounding whitespace is
trimmed before matching.

MtlsAuthConfig.description: Plugin: mtls_auth — Authenticates client certificates on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC, WebSocket, terminated TCP+TLS, and UDP+DTLS. Null or an empty object uses defaults (`cert_field: subject_cn`). Stream proxies require frontend_tls=true and passthrough=false.

cert_field.description: Certificate field to use as identity. For subject_cn, subject_ou, subject_o, san_dns, and san_email Ferrum uses only the first matching value in certificate order. DNS SAN matching is ASCII case-insensitive; every other field uses exact matching.

cn.description: Issuer CN filter. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the trimmed value must contain a non-whitespace character.

o.description: Issuer O filter. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the trimmed value must contain a non-whitespace character.

ou.description: Issuer OU filter. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the trimmed value must contain a non-whitespace character.

ca_certificate_pem.description: Required for every allowed_issuers entry. Must contain exactly one currently valid PEM-encoded CA certificate with basicConstraints CA:TRUE and keyUsage keyCertSign. Ferrum verifies the leaf signature path through any presented intermediates to this pinned key; DN labels alone never authorize an issuer. The pin may be an intermediate or a higher-level root. A root issuer pin can succeed when the client omits that certificate from the presented chain. UDP+DTLS uses the same leaf-first verified presented chain as terminated TCP+TLS. The earliest notAfter on the path that satisfied the constraint is composed into the request and stream authorization deadline, so an issuer expiring before the leaf ends the authorization at its own expiry; across alternative verified paths the longest-lived matching path wins.

allowed_issuers.description: Per-proxy issuer pins. DN fields are descriptive filters (AND within an entry, OR across entries) and must match the pinned CA subject; the certificate signature path must also reach ca_certificate_pem. DN strings are trimmed; whitespace-only cn/o/ou values are rejected.

allowed_ca_fingerprints_sha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprints of allowed verified, client-presented intermediate/CA certificates. Matching uses the leaf-first presented chain on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC, WebSocket, terminated TCP+TLS, and UDP+DTLS. The leaf is never a CA fingerprint candidate; the corresponding CA certificate must be presented. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before hex decoding; uppercase and lowercase hex are accepted.

Oauth2IntrospectionConfig.description: Plugin: oauth2_introspection — RFC 7662 bearer token introspection with bounded, explicit multi-provider routing. Both ends of a returned validity window are enforced independently of the active member, as defense in depth against a contradictory provider response: exp, active_until, and expires_in close it, and nbf (RFC 7662 section 2.2) opens it. An active:true response whose nbf is still in the future is rejected with a bearer 401 and is not cached in either direction; a present non-integer nbf is a dependency-response error and returns 503, like malformed expiry data. An omitted nbf, exp, active_until, or expires_in remains supported, including a JSON null, which is treated as absent. Both bounds are absolute instants resolved once at the provider-response boundary and re-checked on every cache hit. Both are compared against the gateway clock with no leeway: this plugin deliberately has no clock-skew knob, matching its long-standing exp behaviour, so an authorization server whose clock runs ahead of the gateway can have a freshly issued token rejected for the first second(s) of its life, and each such request costs a provider round trip because that rejection is never cached. Keep the authorization server and the gateway clocks synchronized (NTP).

introspection_endpoint.description: Direct token introspection endpoint URL. Exactly one of introspection_endpoint or discovery_url must be configured. Must use https when client_auth.method is credentialed (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, or private_key_jwt) and the host is not a loopback IP literal; http is only permitted for a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or ::1), never for the name localhost. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. A path or query is accepted, but operational diagnostics record only the endpoint origin (scheme, host, port).

discovery_url.description: OIDC discovery URL used to resolve introspection_endpoint. Exactly one of introspection_endpoint or discovery_url must be configured. Must use https when client_auth.method is credentialed and the host is not a loopback IP literal; http is only permitted for a loopback IP literal, never for the name localhost. The discovered endpoint must preserve the discovery URL's scheme, normalized host, and effective port.

issuer.description: Expected iss claim in active introspection responses. Trimmed; a blank value is rejected. Independent of the private_key_jwt assertion audience (see client_auth.client_assertion_audience). When omitted, each active response's string iss joins the external identity realm, so equal subjects asserted for different issuers are different principals.

audiences.description: Accepted aud claims; OR matched. Entries are trimmed and must not be blank.

method.description: Client authentication method against the introspection endpoint. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before matching. Credentialed methods (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt) require an https endpoint for non-loopback hosts; http is only accepted for a loopback IP-literal host. The 'none' method is loopback-IP-literal-only regardless of scheme; the name localhost qualifies for neither. client_secret_basic and client_secret_post require client_id and client_secret; private_key_jwt requires client_id and private_key_pem.

client_secret.description: Literal client secret. Plugin config is never environment-expanded; a value containing a `${NAME}` placeholder is refused at admission.

private_key_pem.description: PEM private key for private_key_jwt. The key must be usable with private_key_jwt_alg: an EC key's curve must match the selected ES algorithm (P-256 for ES256, P-384 for ES384) and an RSA key must meet the signing backend's minimum modulus size. A mismatch is rejected at config load, not at request time.

client_assertion_audience.description: aud of private_key_jwt client assertions. Trimmed; a blank value is rejected. Defaults to the resolved introspection endpoint URL (the configured introspection_endpoint, or the endpoint discovery resolved). Independent of issuer: set it when the authorization server requires another audience, such as its issuer identifier.

name.description: Header carrying the token. Trimmed and lowercased; must be a valid HTTP header name.

prefix.description: Scheme prefix stripped from the header value. Null and the empty string both mean "no prefix".

positive_cache_ttl_secs.description: Active-token cache TTL cap, in seconds. 0 disables positive caching.

negative_cache_ttl_secs.description: Inactive-token cache TTL, in seconds. 0 disables negative caching.

max_concurrent_introspections.description: Uncached introspection calls this provider may have in flight. Non-queuing: a lookup that finds the limit exhausted fails fast with 503. Also bounded by the plugin-level max_concurrent_introspections and a fixed process-wide ceiling of 1024.

discovery_refresh_interval_secs.description: Seconds between discovery document re-fetches after a successful resolution. A failed refresh keeps serving the last known endpoint and retries with capped exponential backoff. Only valid with discovery_url.

accept_mtls_bound_tokens.description: Admit RFC 8705 certificate-bound tokens whose cnf is exactly one non-empty x5t#S256 member, only when the request's frontend client certificate has that base64url SHA-256 thumbprint; a missing or different certificate is a bearer 401. Re-verified on every request, including cache hits. Any other cnf (DPoP jkt, jwk, extra members) and any non-Bearer token_type still fail closed. A null cnf or token_type is treated as absent.

max_cache_entries.description: Per-provider hard entry ceiling. Active and negative entries receive independent 75/25 count partitions, so one result class cannot evict the other class.

max_cache_entry_bytes.description: Maximum normalized active authorization-result bytes retained for one token. A larger valid result is used for the current request but is not cached.

max_cache_total_bytes.description: Per-provider hard retained-byte ceiling covering fixed eviction indexes, token digests, entry state, and normalized authorization data. Must be at least the constructor-reported minimum footprint for max_cache_entries plus one max_cache_entry_bytes result.

token_hint_param.description: Value sent as RFC 7662 `token_type_hint` on every introspection request (for example `access_token`). Null and an omitted key both send no hint; a blank string is rejected.

scope_claim.description: Per-provider override of the global scope claim path.

role_claim.description: Per-provider override of the global role claim path.

consumer_identity_claim.description: Per-provider override of the global consumer-lookup claim path.

consumer_header_claim.description: Per-provider X-Authenticated-Identity display claim path. The display claim is resolved in this order: this provider's consumer_header_claim, then the plugin-level consumer_header_claim, then this provider's effective consumer_identity_claim (its own consumer_identity_claim, else the plugin-level consumer_identity_claim). When the selected display claim is absent or not a string, the header carries the authenticated identity value instead.

claim_headers.description: Claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

max_concurrent_introspections.description: Uncached introspection calls this plugin instance may have in flight across all of its providers. Non-queuing: a lookup that finds the limit exhausted fails fast with 503. A fixed process-wide ceiling of 1024 applies across every instance.

allow_provider_fanout.description: Allow one Authorization bearer token to be submitted sequentially to multiple providers. Enable only when every provider shares one credential trust boundary. By default, multi-provider configs must use distinct from_headers/from_params routing hints or have exactly one provider that uses the Authorization location.

consumer_header_claim.description: Claim used for X-Authenticated-Identity when no Consumer maps. Defaults to the effective consumer_identity_claim.

OidcRelyingPartyConfig.description: Plugin: oidc_relying_party — Browser OIDC relying party with authorization code + PKCE and encrypted sessions. ID token verification requires a JWT header kid that selects exactly one current trusted JWKS key; missing, empty, and unknown kid values are rejected with no all-keys fallback. Optional string fields accept null as "unset", matching constructor admission. Sessions too large for one browser cookie are split across bounded `<cookie_name>.N` chunk cookies.

issuer.description: Expected ID token issuer, compared as an exact case-sensitive string. Per RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 a present iss must be a single string; an array, object, number, boolean, or null iss is rejected. A discovery document is used only when its own `issuer` member is exactly this value (OpenID Connect Discovery section 4.3).

discovery_url.description: OIDC discovery URL. Mutually exclusive with authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and jwks_uri. The document must carry an `issuer` exactly equal to `issuer`. Its endpoints must use HTTPS and may live on other origins (Google and Microsoft Entra ID publish cross-origin endpoints); plain HTTP is accepted only for a loopback development discovery_url and only on its own origin. Every gateway-dialed URL (discovery_url, token_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint, jwks_uri, and discovered endpoints) admits plain HTTP only for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]), never for the name localhost, because DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects; configured browser-followed URLs (authorization_endpoint, end_session_endpoint, redirect_uri, post_logout_redirect_uri) and the issuer identifier keep the localhost development case, while a discovered plaintext endpoint must share the loopback IP-literal discovery origin. With client_auth.method none, a discovered token_endpoint must also be a loopback IP literal, and a discovered revocation_endpoint that is not one is ignored (logout skips revocation).

userinfo_endpoint.description: Optional UserInfo endpoint. When set alongside discovery_url, the explicit value overrides the UserInfo endpoint advertised by the discovery document, including one that omits it, and the discarded advertisement is not validated.

jwks_source.description: Admin-managed JWKS record used to verify ID tokens instead of fetching jwks_uri: `managed://jwks/<id>#jwks` (also accepted: `managed://jwks/<id>`, `managed://<id>#jwks`), stored through `/admin/tls/jwks`. Only with explicit authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint; mutually exclusive with jwks_uri and discovery_url. The fragment and collection must select JWKS material and `?` options are refused. The record is read from this node's managed TLS store (`FERRUM_TLS_MANAGED_STORE_PATH`): fresh while it is present, every key withdrawn (ID tokens refused) once it is deleted or holds no usable signing key, re-read every 900 seconds, on an unknown kid, and immediately after a local `/admin/tls/jwks` write. Admin writes refuse a reference to a record that does not exist; file mode refuses to start without it. Namespace-bounded operator tokens may not introduce one.

end_session_endpoint.description: Optional end-session endpoint used for RP-initiated logout. When set alongside discovery_url, the explicit value overrides the end-session endpoint advertised by the discovery document, including one that omits it, and the discarded advertisement is not validated.

post_logout_redirect_uri.description: Absolute HTTPS redirect URI sent to the provider after RP-initiated logout; HTTP is allowed only for localhost or literal loopback development endpoints.

method.description: Null or absent selects client_secret_basic. A non-string value is rejected. "none" is admitted only for a token endpoint whose host is a loopback IP literal (the name localhost does not qualify), including a token endpoint learned from discovery.

client_secret.description: Literal client secret. Plugin config is never environment-expanded; a value containing a `${NAME}` placeholder is refused at admission.

private_key_pem.description: Must support private_key_jwt_alg; admission signs a throwaway assertion, so a key on the wrong curve or of the wrong family is rejected at config load.

private_key_jwt_alg.description: Null or absent selects RS256. A non-string value is rejected for every method.

private_key_jwt_kid.description: Null or absent sends no kid header. A non-string value is rejected for every method.

redirect_uri.description: Absolute callback URI registered with the provider, with no fragment (RFC 6749 §3.1.2). Before issuing a browser challenge, Ferrum requires its host to match the validated request Host/:authority; DNS comparison is case-insensitive, IP literals compare by address, and ports are ignored. Trailing-dot DNS callback hosts and missing, malformed, or cross-host request authorities fail closed before state or cookies are issued.

callback_path.description: Callback path handled by Ferrum; must equal the path in redirect_uri. Also the correlation cookie's Path attribute, so it carries cookie-path syntax rules. Must already be a canonical request path (no percent-escapes, empty segments, dot segments, or backslashes), because it is compared with the frontend's canonical request path; dot segments are refused by the constructor.

logout_path.description: Must not resolve to the same path as callback_path; the callback branch is evaluated first. Must be a canonical request path, like callback_path. Logout is state-changing, so GET/HEAD requests must carry `Sec-Fetch-Site` same-origin or none, a POST is refused only when the browser reports cross-site or same-site, and other methods answer 405; a refused request clears nothing and contacts no provider.

claim_headers.description: Session claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

id_token_clock_skew_secs.description: Leeway added to the ID token exp when deciding whether the session's claims are still live. The ID token exp is an RFC 7519 section 2 NumericDate (a JSON number that may carry a fractional part) and is the session's authoritative claim lifetime, truncated toward the past; it does not fall back to session.ttl_secs or the access-token lifetime. The session is still additionally capped by session.ttl_secs and session.idle_ttl_secs.

authorization_params.description: Static extra authorization-request parameters, such as `prompt`, `acr_values`, `login_hint`, or `ui_locales`, appended after the parameters the plugin owns. Names the plugin sets (response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, max_age, response_mode, request, request_uri) are rejected case-insensitively; values must not contain control characters.

max_age_secs.description: OpenID Connect `max_age`. When set it is sent on the authorization request, the callback requires an ID token `auth_time` no older than this (plus id_token_clock_skew_secs), and a session whose login is older re-challenges instead of refreshing.

forward_access_token.description: Relay the session's current (refreshed) access token to the backend as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. When enabled the backend Authorization header is gateway-owned on this route: every client-supplied copy is removed first, so a request whose accepted principal is not this session forwards none.

encryption_secret.description: AEAD key material for durable session cookies and sealed pending authorization-code correlation cookies; must be at least 32 bytes and must not be a known published or placeholder value (including the documented `${OIDC_SESSION_SECRET_32_BYTES_MIN}` placeholder, the key Ferrum Foundry's OIDC template published, Ferrum's own sequential example/test secrets, and obvious placeholders such as changeme, change-me, replace-me, placeholder, or your-secret). Screening covers both the supplied value and the effective key material (standard Base64 decoded only when it yields at least 32 bytes, otherwise raw bytes before HKDF), including Base64 spellings of denied values and unresolved `${...}` templates anywhere in either textual value. A rejected value returns 400 naming this field without revealing the secret.

encryption_secret_previous.description: Previous encryption secret accepted while rotating session and pending-flow cookies within the same versioned OIDC context; subject to the same raw and effective-key screening as encryption_secret, including Base64 spellings of denied values and unresolved `${...}` templates anywhere in either textual value. A rejected value returns 400 naming this field without revealing the secret.

cookie_name.description: Explicit cookie name opts out of automatic naming and must be an RFC 6265 cookie-name token. An explicit __Host- name additionally requires secure with no domain and a root path, and an explicit __Secure- name requires secure. When omitted, the context-derived name is prefixed __Host- when secure with no domain and a root path, __Secure- when secure otherwise, and left unprefixed when secure is false because browsers reject a prefixed cookie without Secure.

ttl_secs.description: Absolute session lifetime. Bounded so it can take part in Unix-timestamp arithmetic on every authenticated request.

max_cookie_bytes.description: Maximum encoded size of the sealed session value and of sealed pending-flow correlation cookies. The minimum is what a sealed pending authorization flow needs before any original-URL bytes. A session whose complete Set-Cookie line would exceed 4000 bytes is split across `<cookie_name>.0`…`<cookie_name>.N` chunk cookies (at most 9) that each fit a browser cookie; a session above this cap is refused at the callback with a named error instead of being emitted. Every session cookie carries Max-Age equal to the remaining absolute session lifetime. Not part of the session context, and it bounds only what is issued: existing sessions and in-flight logins up to the 8000-byte admission maximum stay readable after it is lowered.

secure.description: When false, generated session and correlation cookie names carry no __Host-/__Secure- prefix, because a prefixed cookie without Secure is rejected by browsers. Secure correlation cookies always use __Host- with Path=/ and no Domain.

same_site.description: Case-insensitive; normalized to lower case. "none" requires secure=true.

domain.description: Optional bare DNS Domain attribute (leading dot allowed) for the durable session cookie. The short-lived sealed pending-flow correlation cookie never inherits this value; secure correlation cookies use __Host- with Path=/, while insecure loopback-development cookies are scoped to callback_path.

hide_session_cookie.description: Remove this plugin's own session and pending-flow correlation cookies from the Cookie header forwarded to the selected backend, leaving unrelated application cookies intact. The sealed session cookie is a complete replayable gateway credential and the upstream already receives the verified identity and claim headers, so passthrough must be an explicit opt-in.

state_cache_max_entries.description: Per-instance size of the pending-login replay cache (DoS admission). When it is full, further logins are still started as sealed-only flows (no local replay entry), each charged to its source under state_cache_max_entries_per_source, up to one more state_cache_max_entries; beyond that new login starts answer 503. Cross-replica callbacks use the sealed correlation cookie and do not require a shared state cache.

state_cache_max_entries_per_source.description: Per-instance maximum pending browser authorization flows started per resolved client IP, enforced whether or not the replay cache is full; must not exceed state_cache_max_entries.

trusted_redirect_hosts.description: Origins a post-login redirect may target, as `host` (the redirect_uri scheme's default port only) or `host:port`; an explicit default port (`host:443` for https) names the same origin as `host`. Hosts compare case-insensitively; an entry that is not a bare authority (path, query, fragment, or userinfo) is rejected. A target must also use redirect_uri's scheme and carry no userinfo, and a target containing an ASCII control character or a backslash is refused. An accepted target is emitted in its normalized URL form (for example lowercased host, default port omitted). The redirect_uri's own origin is always trusted; anything else lands on post_login_default_path.

refresh_skew_secs.description: Refresh lead time before token expiry; must not exceed session.ttl_secs / 2, which the constructor enforces across the two objects.

rp_initiated_logout.description: With an authentic session cookie, send id_token_hint on provider logout and attempt discovered refresh-token revocation within five seconds. Cookie copies remain valid within session and claims lifetime limits. Without a valid cookie, return the local logout page.

post_login_default_path.description: Redirect target when no trusted original URL exists. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed and a whitespace-only value is rejected. Emitted verbatim as Location, so it must not contain ASCII control characters or a backslash.

OpaPluginConfig.description:
Plugin: opa — Delegates HTTP request authorization to Open Policy
Agent's Data API in the `authorize` phase. The gateway POSTs
`{ "input": ... }` to `{opa_host}/v1/data/{policy_path}` and allows
only `true` decisions or objects with `allow: true` at
`decision_pointer`. Fails closed by default; `fail_open: true` is the
opt-in availability mode. Unknown configuration keys are rejected.
Request headers and query-located credentials are redacted before
being sent to OPA. The decision binds the request as of the authorize
phase; later request transforms are outside it. Each decision records
opa.decision and opa.reason transaction metadata.

opa_host.description: Base OPA URL using http:// or https://. URL credentials are not allowed; use `headers` for OPA authentication. A query string or fragment is rejected; a base path is accepted and is prepended to /v1/data/{policy_path}. Operational diagnostics record only the endpoint origin (scheme, host, port), never the configured path. An http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] unless allow_plaintext is true, because the decision and any `headers` credential travel on this call.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// opa_host whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The authorization input, the decision, and any `headers` credential then cross the network in clear.

policy_path.description: OPA data path appended under /v1/data/. Must be non-empty, must not start with '/', must not contain percent-encoding, a query, a fragment, a backslash, a space, or an ASCII control character, and must not contain empty, '.', or '..' segments. The normalized decision URL must still address the path under {opa_host}/v1/data/; a value the URL parser would rewrite out of that prefix is rejected at config load.

headers.description: Static HTTP headers sent to OPA on every decision request. Names use HTTP token syntax. Values must be valid HTTP field values: visible ASCII, space, horizontal tab, and UTF-8 (HeaderValue obs-text) are accepted; NUL, CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are rejected. The `content-type` header is managed by the plugin and cannot be configured here, case-insensitively. Neither can the gateway-owned `X-Ferrum-Hops` proxy hop count (any case, `_` or `-`), which the decision request carries itself.

timeout_ms.description: Requested per-decision timeout in milliseconds. Every positive value is accepted; the effective runtime timeout is capped at 30000 milliseconds.

max_response_bytes.description: Maximum decoded OPA response size. Oversized declared or streamed responses use the configured fail-open/fail-closed posture. An explicit null selects the default, exactly like omitting the key.

fail_open.description: Continue when OPA is unavailable, times out, returns non-2xx, returns malformed JSON, or exceeds max_response_bytes.

fail_closed.description: Inverse of `fail_open`. Configuring both fields is rejected at config load, even when the two values agree.

deny_status.description: HTTP status returned when OPA returns a policy denial.

deny_body.description: Response body returned on policy denial.

deny_headers.description: Headers added to the policy-denial response. Names and values are validated at config load: names use HTTP token syntax and values accept visible ASCII, space, horizontal tab, and UTF-8 (HeaderValue obs-text) while NUL, CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are rejected. Protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing destinations (`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`, case-insensitive) are rejected: the gateway derives Content-Length from the reject body and strips connection/framing fields at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary.

fail_closed_status.description: HTTP status returned when fail-closed handles OPA unavailability, timeouts, non-2xx responses, malformed JSON, or oversized responses.

fail_closed_body.description: Response body returned on fail-closed OPA errors.

fail_closed_headers.description: Headers added to fail-closed OPA error responses. Same name/value validation and protocol-managed hop-by-hop / framing destination rejection as deny_headers.

decision_pointer.description: JSON object-key path to the decision value in OPA's response.

include_query.description: Include the backend-bound request query as input.query (a flat decoded map, emitted only when unambiguous), input.query_pairs (an ordered, occurrence-complete pair list), and input.query_ambiguity (fixed-cardinality ambiguity classifications). Present query parameters configured as authentication credential locations are omitted by default.

include_query_credentials.description: Unsafe opt-in to include built-in, classifier-recognized, and authentication-plugin-marked query credentials in input.query and input.query_pairs. Keys listed in redact_query_keys remain redacted from both views.

include_headers.description: Include request headers as input.headers (one folded value per lowercase name), input.header_pairs (every field line the backend may receive, as {name, value}, grouped by name in sorted order with repeated lines in wire order), and input.header_ambiguity. Built-in and redact_headers names, active authentication credential headers, and names the shared sensitive-name classifier recognizes as credentials are omitted from all three.

include_body.description: After authentication succeeds, buffer and forward the request body. UTF-8 bodies use `body`; non-UTF-8 raw bytes use `body_base64`. A transport-proven empty body is `body: ""` on every frontend protocol; `body: null` means no body representation was collected (for example a WebSocket handshake). The body is read only from the gateway-owned buffered bytes, never from plugin metadata.

max_body_bytes.description: Plugin-local request body ceiling when include_body is enabled. The strictest of this value and the positive global request body limit is enforced; this value remains active when the global limit is unlimited (0). An explicit null selects the default, exactly like omitting the key.

include_consumer.description: Include input.consumer: the mapped Consumer (id, username, acl_groups, custom_id) or, for an external identity, identity, auth_method, and realm. realm is {mechanism, authority}, where authority is the opaque, stable lowercase-hex digest of the verifying authority (null for a single-authority mechanism), and realm itself is null when the identity was not committed by the authentication boundary. Equal identity strings from different realms are different principals.

query_ambiguity_policy.description: When include_query is enabled, controls what happens to a request whose query cannot be decoded to one value OPA and the backend are guaranteed to read identically: a duplicate decoded parameter name (including a percent-encoded alias such as a=1&%61=2 or a bare/valued pair such as flag&flag=1), a literal '+' (RFC 3986 plus vs form-urlencoded space), an unencoded ';' (a pair separator for backends that also split on ';'; reported as semicolon_separator, while '%3B' is unambiguous), malformed percent-encoding, or a non-UTF-8 decoding. 'reject' denies the request with the configured deny_status and deny_body before calling OPA. 'delegate' calls OPA anyway and lets the policy decide from the ordered, occurrence-complete input.query_pairs array and the input.query_ambiguity classifications; non-UTF-8 components are replacement-decoded and explicitly classified. input.query is omitted in that case so no rule can read from the flat map a value the backend does not execute. Omission is not itself a denial: an undefined input.query makes a deny-style Rego rule undefined rather than true, so a 'delegate' policy must deny on any input.query_ambiguity classification it does not handle.

header_ambiguity_policy.description: When include_headers is enabled, controls what happens to a request that repeats a header whose grammar is not a list (for example two X-Role field lines, or two map keys differing only in case): the backend may read the first line, the last, or the fold, while the folded input.headers value matches none of them. 'reject' denies with the configured deny_status and deny_body before calling OPA. 'delegate' calls OPA with input.header_ambiguity set to ["duplicate_field_lines"], every line in input.header_pairs, and the ambiguous names omitted from input.headers; the policy must then deny on any classification it does not handle. List-valued fields (Accept*, Cache-Control, Cookie, Forwarded, Via, X-Forwarded-*, and the other RFC 9110 lists) are never ambiguous.

max_concurrent_decisions.description: Optional per-instance bound on in-flight OPA decision calls. A request over the bound is not queued: it takes the configured failure posture immediately (fail_closed_status by default, continue under fail_open) and records opa.reason opa_concurrency_limit. Omit for no bound.

decision_request_headers.description: Opt-in allow obligations. Upstream request headers an allow decision object ({"allow": true, "headers": {...}} at decision_pointer) may set. Every listed name becomes gateway-owned for requests this instance lets through: client copies (any ASCII case, `_` or `-`) are removed, and only a policy-supplied value is forwarded. A decision whose headers name an unlisted header, repeat a name, or carry a non-string, invalid, or over-8192-byte value is refused as a policy denial. Names must be distinct (ASCII case and `_`/`-` folded). The constructor also refuses gateway-owned (x-consumer-*, x-ferrum-*, x-forwarded-*, x-geo-country, path-param assertions), hop-by-hop, framing, representation (content-type, content-encoding, content-range), and credential-bearing names (the built-in redact_headers list and the shared sensitive-name classifier). Effective-chain admission also refuses a destination any plugin on the same chain and an overlapping protocol publishes as a credential location (ASCII case and `_`/`-` folded), including WAF exemption, OpenAPI bypass, and MCP session headers. A request whose route's active credential headers include a destination is refused fail closed before the decision call, even under fail_open. Empty disables allow obligations.

decision_deny_response.description: Opt-in deny obligations. A deny decision object at decision_pointer may set `status` (400-599), `body` (string, at most 65536 bytes), and `headers` (at most 16 string values, merged over deny_headers; protocol-managed and gateway-owned diagnostic names refused). Absent members fall back to deny_status, deny_body, and deny_headers. A malformed obligation still denies, with the static response.

redact_headers.description: Additional request headers to redact from `input.headers` and `input.header_pairs`. Built-in sensitive headers, active authentication credential headers, and names the shared sensitive-name classifier recognizes as credentials are always omitted.

redact_query_keys.description: Additional query parameter names to omit from input.query and input.query_pairs, matched case-insensitively. Built-in credential names, names the shared sensitive-name classifier recognizes as credentials (for example refresh_token, client_secret, password, X-Amz-Signature), and query locations marked by authentication plugins are already omitted unless include_query_credentials is explicitly enabled.

OpenapiValidatorConcreteMediaType.description: Concrete RFC 9110 type/subtype and valid HTTP field value. Wildcard type/subtype, braces in tokens, leading whitespace, malformed parameters, and control bytes other than horizontal tab are rejected. Parameter names require token or quoted-string values.

OpenapiValidatorConfig.description:
Plugin: openapi_validator — validates request parameters (path, query,
header, cookie) and request and response bodies against operation
schemas generated from an attached OpenAPI/Swagger document. Supports
JSON, XML, form-urlencoded, multipart, text, and binary media types.
JSON Schema `format` is asserted under every `schema_draft` (unknown
formats such as OpenAPI's int32/int64/byte/password stay annotations).
Must be proxy-scoped; every config load rejects global and
proxy_group scope. Multipart Content-Disposition accepts ordinary
`filename` or a single bounded RFC 5987/8187 `filename*` (UTF-8 only;
unquoted ext-value) and rejects continuations, quoted `filename*`,
bare/non-token parameter segments, conflicts, and hostile extended
values.
XML conversion honors OpenAPI XML Object fields
`name`, `namespace`, `prefix`, `attribute`, and `wrapped` (namespace
matching uses the URI; `prefix` is serialization metadata only;
members that collide with a modeled name but not its XML construct or
namespace are rejected fail-closed rather than dropped or rebound).
Scalar elements contain text without structural members; namespace
declarations remain valid. A present empty wrapped array becomes [];
array containers reject unmodeled attributes, text, and wrapper children.
UTF-8 binary bodies receive full string-schema validation. Non-UTF-8
binary bodies support boolean schemas, optional string-compatible type,
byte-count minLength/maxLength, format: binary, and the annotations
listed in docs/openapi_validator.md. Other assertions require a text
representation and fail validation for non-UTF-8 bodies.
Usually generated by `x-ferrum-validate` on
`POST /api-specs` or `PUT /api-specs/{id}`; direct creation requires a
proxy-scoped plugin attached to a proxy with `api_spec_id` set.
Strict parameter import is selected with the import-only
`x-ferrum-validate.reject_unsupported_parameters` boolean (default false),
not a field of this runtime config. When true, optional unsupported
parameters refuse spec admission with `400 MalformedExtension` naming
the first affected operation, parameter, and reason; otherwise they are
warned about and dropped. Unsupported required parameters always refuse
import.
Every fixed-field object in this schema is closed: an unknown key at the
root or in `bypass`, `error_response`, an `operations[]` entry, or
`request_body` is rejected at construction so a misspelled enforcement
control cannot silently fall back to a weaker default. An explicit
`null` for a non-null field is likewise rejected instead of selecting
its omission default. Free-form maps
(media types, response status keys, `bypass.header_present`, encoding
property names) stay open but their keys are shape-validated.
Response schema failures emit only a fixed generic message plus the
allowlisted JSON Schema keyword; raw schema locations, backend instance values and
JSON property names never appear in client problem bodies or
`openapi_validator.response_error` metadata.
The REQUEST contract is decided in the dedicated
`validate_client_request_body_contract` lifecycle phase over the original
client representation, before any `before_proxy` hook or request-body
transformer can add, remove, rename, coerce, or replace fields
(`GHSA-896v-jx23-9g6p`). Buffering for that phase is selected from the
matched operation alone, never from a `Content-Type` a client can omit
or mismatch; in `block` mode a missing required body and a nonempty body
with no applicable declared media type both fail closed
(`GHSA-6p78-6x8c-9g9x`).

enforcement_mode.description: Blocking rejects mismatches, log_only records metadata and continues, disabled skips validation.

validate_request.description: Validate request bodies when an operation has a request schema, and request parameters when an operation declares `parameters`.

validate_response.description: Validate response bodies when an operation has a response schema.

request_content_types.description: Request media types in scope. JSON includes `+json`, XML includes `+xml`, text/plain covers `text/*`, and application/octet-stream covers common binary application, image, audio, and video types. An explicitly empty list is rejected; omit the field for the default scope.

response_content_types.description: Response media types in scope. JSON includes `+json`, XML includes `+xml`, text/plain covers `text/*`, and application/octet-stream covers common binary application, image, audio, and video types. An explicitly empty list is rejected; omit the field for the default scope.

fail_on_unknown_operation.description: Reject requests that do not match any generated operation. In block mode the client-visible problem title is "Unknown OpenAPI operation" with detail "No OpenAPI operation matched this request"; the method and path are not interpolated into either string.

fail_on_missing_response_schema.description: Reject a response whose selected response object yields no schema. Applied after status selection to a missing `Content-Type`, a content type outside `response_content_types`, an unmatched declared media type, a body returned for a status with no declared content, and a status covered by no response object. An empty body for an explicitly empty response declaration remains valid. Statuses with no body semantics (HEAD, 1xx, 204, 205, 304) are always skipped. Strict mode still schedules the response hook when every declared response has an empty content map.

max_body_bytes.description: Maximum raw or decompressed body size to validate, 1 to 67108864 (64 MiB). It is also the per-layer decoded ceiling while undoing Content-Encoding, so a larger value is rejected at admission.

schema_draft.description: Sole authoritative JSON Schema draft selector used when compiling every operation's request and response schemas. Per-operation draft fields are not part of the published contract; the importer emits this field only at the top-level config.

operations.description: Generated operation schema table. Required in file mode and other direct plugin configuration; POST /api-specs and PUT /api-specs/{id} generate it from the attached document when x-ferrum-validate is enabled. The importer replaces this from the spec on every spec PUT. Two operations with the same method and the same path_regex are rejected. Within a method, overlapping operations are ordered by literal-segment count, then by the leftmost differing segment (literal before `{template}`), then by document order; `operation_label` never affects selection.

consumers.description: Mapped Consumer usernames that skip validation. An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username.

header_present.description: Header name to shared secret. A request skips validation only when that header carries exactly the configured secret (compared in constant time). Presence alone never skips validation, because clients can send any header, so null is rejected. The secret must be 16 to 4096 visible ASCII characters (0x21-0x7E: no spaces, controls or non-ASCII), so characters and bytes coincide. Bypass header names are redacted from diagnostics and policy calls. Inject it from a trusted hop or gateway plugin and keep it out of client hands. Keys are matched case-insensitively at runtime; case-equivalent duplicate keys are rejected at construction.

unsupported_media_type_status_code.description: Status for a nonempty request body that no media entry declared for the matched operation covers (including a body sent with no `Content-Type` at all). Kept distinct from `request_status_code` so remapping schema failures does not also remap media-type refusals. `log_only` records the same decision and continues.

error_truncate_chars.description: Size bound on the validation diagnostic written to openapi_validator.request_error / openapi_validator.response_error metadata and to the problem body. Only ever narrows: the effective cap is min(error_truncate_chars, 256). This is not a confidentiality control. Admission also enforces the target's usize range. Diagnostics are payload-free by construction and never contain the rejected instance value, an expected enum/const constant, a raw schema path or schema-library / XML-parser rendering, a configured XML name or namespace, a hostile Content-Encoding coding token, a backend Content-Type, the request target, or a payload-chosen JSON/XML/form/multipart member name.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingHeader.description: Multipart Encoding Object header entry. A bare JSON Schema preserves Ferrum's historical required-header form. A Header Object is selected by exactly one of `schema` or `content` and is closed so misspelled presence controls cannot weaken validation. Schema form accepts the OAS schema-form fields (`style`/`explode`/`example`/`examples`). Simple serialization decodes comma-separated arrays and object key/value pairs; explode=true objects use comma-separated name=value members. Content form accepts only the common fields plus `content`. Header-location `allowEmptyValue` and `allowReserved` are rejected. The `content` form requires exactly one concrete media type whose Media Type Object carries `schema`.

content.description: OpenAPI Header Object content map. Exactly one concrete media type is required (no `type/*` or `*/*`). The full key, including any parameters, must be a valid RFC 9110 media type and HTTP header value. The header value is decoded as that media type under multipart header-size limits before schema validation. multipart/form-data is not supported as header content.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingHeaderContentMed.description: Media Type Object inside an Encoding Header Object `content` map. Encoding Objects are not valid on part headers; only schema (plus mutually-exclusive optional example metadata) is accepted.

OpenapiValidatorEncodingMap.description: OpenAPI Encoding Object map keyed by schema property name. Supported for application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data. Unsupported style/explode combinations are rejected at admission. The constructor also checks that every key names a declared schema property, deepObject selects an object, and spaceDelimited/pipeDelimited select an array or object. Exploded object child keys must not overlap root siblings or another exploded object; a free-form exploded object cannot coexist with another exploded object. These schema-dependent checks cannot be expressed by this map component alone.

style.description: Serialization style. `form` (default), `spaceDelimited`, `pipeDelimited`, and `deepObject` are supported. Path/header styles such as `matrix`, `label`, and `simple` are rejected.

explode.description: Defaults to true for `form`, false otherwise. `spaceDelimited` and `pipeDelimited` require explode=false; `deepObject` requires explode=true.

allowReserved.description: OpenAPI allowReserved flag. When false, literal RFC 3986 reserved bytes in form values are rejected and must be percent-encoded (serialization delimiters such as the form explode=false comma remain valid).
