contentType.description: Expected multipart part Content-Type (comma-separated list allowed). Only valid for multipart/form-data. Trimmed before use; must be nonempty and at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes after trimming (the byte limit is checked by the constructor).

headers.description: Additional multipart part Header Objects. Present values are validated against their schemas (or against the single media type declared in a Header Object `content` map after decoding under header-size limits); an absent header fails only when its Header Object sets required=true (the OpenAPI default is false). Only valid for multipart/form-data. Must not redefine Content-Type, Content-Disposition, or Content-Transfer-Encoding. Case-equivalent duplicate header names are rejected at construction and during API-spec extraction.

OpenapiValidatorFormEncodingMap.description: Form-urlencoded encodings cannot declare multipart headers or contentType.

OpenapiValidatorJsonSchema.description: JSON Schema value embedded in an openapi_validator operation. Accepts ordinary object schemas and OpenAPI 3.1 boolean schemas (`true` / `false`). Dialect selection is controlled by the top-level OpenapiValidatorConfig.schema_draft field, not per operation.

OpenapiValidatorMediaType.description: Media selector or map key. The base type uses MIME tokens (including braces), permits type/* and */*, trims surrounding Unicode whitespace, and is ASCII case-insensitive. Control characters are rejected anywhere; parameters after the first semicolon are ignored for selection. Lists and maps must be unique after trimming, ASCII lowercasing, and removing parameters. This normalized uniqueness is checked by the constructor; JSON Schema uniqueItems detects only literal duplicates.

OpenapiValidatorMediaTypeContent.description: Request-body content entry. A bare JSON Schema is canonical when no Encoding Object is present. An entry with `encoding` must use the strict Media Type Object shape, preventing ambiguous schema/wrapper parsing.

method.description: Nonempty method, normalized to uppercase by the constructor.

path_template.description: Effective OpenAPI path template used for metadata and path specificity ordering. When generated from a spec, this is the Paths key joined to the effective Server Object pathname (OpenAPI 3.x) or Swagger `basePath`, with the literal proxy listen_path prefix prepended (trailing prefix slashes trimmed). Root, host-only, exact, and regex listen routes add no prefix. One entry is emitted per distinct server pathname when multiple servers apply. strip_listen_path affects backend forwarding only.

path_regex.description: Regex used to match the full inbound request path, compiled at plugin load. Auto-generated specs derive it from the effective path template (including literal listen prefix and server/`basePath` prefix); operator-supplied full-path patterns are not prefixed or stripped and are automatically anchored as `^(?:...)$` (full-path match) so a loose pattern cannot substring-match an unintended superstring path.

operation_label.description: Optional metadata label. Defaults to "`METHOD path_template`".

request_required.description: Reject empty request bodies when the OpenAPI requestBody is required.

content.description: Media type to schema map. Each entry is either a bare JSON Schema (object or boolean) or, when encoding metadata is present, a Media Type Object with required `schema` and `encoding` fields. Keys must be a media type or media range (`type/subtype`, `type/*`, `*/*`). Exactly one of `content` or the `content_type` + `schema` form is allowed; the object is never treated as its own media map.

schema.description: Alternate single-schema form (object or boolean schema).

encoding.description: Alternate single-schema form encoding map. Only valid with application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data.

request_body.description: Request body schemas by media type.

parameters.description: Declared OpenAPI parameters, validated in `before_proxy` when `validate_request` is true. Generated from the operation's and its Path Item's `parameters` (operation entries override Path Item entries with the same `name` and `in`). `in` + `name` must be unique (header names case-insensitively).

responses.description: Status code to media type to JSON Schema map (object or boolean schemas). Response selection is status-first: an exact status code wins, then the narrowest matching OpenAPI wildcard range such as `4XX`, then `default`. A selected response object is final — a media-type miss inside it never falls through to a range or `default` object, because those cover status codes that are not otherwise declared. Media keys must be a media type or media range (`type/subtype`, `type/*`, `*/*`) and are matched most-specific-first. A declared status with an empty media map means the status is declared to carry no content; the importer emits those entries so the precedence rule holds. A status entry may alternatively use the OpenAPI Response Object shape `{description?, content: {mediaType: schema}}`; that form is closed and rejects any other key.

OpenapiValidatorParameter.description: One OpenAPI Parameter Object in the validator's supported subset: each location's default serialization (`simple` for path and header, `form` for query and cookie) over scalar, array-of-scalar, and object-of-scalar schemas. Anything else — another `style`, an array of arrays/objects, or a `form` + `explode: true` object — is rejected at construction (the importer omits such a parameter when it is optional and refuses the import when it is required). Path values come from the canonical request path, query values from the client's raw query string (at most 1024 pairs), header values from the pristine wire request headers (never a header map an earlier `before_proxy` hook mutated), and cookie values from the wire `Cookie` header, percent-decoded per the `form` serialization (at most 1024 pairs); a value that repeats for a non-array schema, a missing required parameter, a value that cannot be converted, or a schema failure is a request violation with `error_response.request_status_code` and the problem title "Request parameter validation failed". Diagnostics name the declared parameter and never contain its value.

name.description: Parameter name, at most 256 bytes without control characters. Path parameters must match a `{name}` expression of `path_template`; header names must be valid HTTP field names other than Accept, Content-Type, or Authorization (which OpenAPI ignores).

required.description: Defaults to true for path parameters (which must be required) and false otherwise.

style.description: Only the location's default style is accepted (`simple` for path/header, `form` for query/cookie).

explode.description: Defaults to true for query/cookie (`form`) and false for path/header (`simple`).

OpenapiValidatorResponse.description: One response status entry, either the generated media-map form or the closed OpenAPI Response Object form.

OpenapiValidatorResponseSchema.description: Response media schemas cannot carry an Encoding Object.

OtelTracingConfig.description: Plugin: otel_tracing — W3C Trace Context propagation and OTLP/HTTP JSON span export. This plugin has no exporter selector and always exports OTLP; Zipkin, Datadog, and Lightstep span export is configured through mesh Telemetry providers on workload_metrics. Trace-context trust defaults to untrusted (fail-closed). Parent sampling is honored; root sampling defaults to always_on. Server span names use low-cardinality proxy/route identifiers. Every configured property is non-null; omit optional properties instead of sending null. Configured strings are trimmed before use, so a whitespace-only value is rejected, and the enum-valued properties are accepted case-insensitively.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP collector endpoint. Omit for propagation-only mode. Must be an http or https URL with a non-empty host. URL userinfo is rejected; path/query credentials are redacted in diagnostics. An http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] unless allow_plaintext is true.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// endpoint whose host is not a loopback IP literal. Spans and any `authorization` / `headers` credential then cross the network in clear.

service_name.description: Service name in spans and resource attributes. Trimmed before use and rejected when blank. Retained as configured, not bounded by max_attribute_bytes.

deployment_environment.description: deployment.environment resource attribute. Trimmed before use and rejected when blank. Retained as configured, not bounded by max_attribute_bytes.

generate_trace_id.description: Generate trace IDs for requests without a usable incoming traceparent

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers sent with OTLP exports (values treated as secrets). Field names must be HTTP tokens and values must be legal HTTP header values; both are rejected at construction otherwise. Names are case-insensitive: two keys differing only in case are rejected, as are the exporter-managed Content-Type, Content-Length, Content-Encoding, Transfer-Encoding, and Host, and Authorization when `authorization` is set.

authorization.description: Authorization header value for OTLP exports (secret). Trimmed before use, rejected when blank, and rejected when it is not a legal HTTP header value — including in propagation-only mode. Diagnostics for a rejected value name the field and the expected type only, never the value.

flush_interval_ms.description: Max delay before flushing a partial batch

buffer_capacity.description: Capacity of the exporter's span queue; new spans are dropped when that queue is full. The flush worker holds its in-flight batch outside this queue, so total pending spans can reach buffer_capacity + batch_size. Aggregate retention is bounded by buffer_max_bytes and the process observability byte ceiling.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate queued span byte budget before new spans are dropped

max_attribute_bytes.description: Max retained bytes per request-derived string span attribute (consumer, user agent, route, namespace, addresses, url.path, mesh attributes). Configured identity — service_name and deployment_environment, in both the span and resource attribute sets — is retained as configured.

retry_delay_ms.description: Base delay before the first retry. Subsequent retries double it with +/-25% jitter, capped at 60000 ms. A collector Retry-After header on a retryable response (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) overrides this delay for that attempt, also capped at 60000 ms. Only 429, 502, 503, and 504 are retried; every other non-success status discards the batch.

trace_context_trust.description: Whether inbound W3C parents are adopted. Canonical values are untrusted and trusted; the value is trimmed and matched case-insensitively. untrusted (default) creates a fresh root and never parents under caller-chosen IDs. trusted adopts a valid lowercase W3C parent for internal/mesh propagation.

root_sampling.description: Sampling policy for locally created root traces. Canonical values are always_on, always_off, and ratio; the value is trimmed and matched case-insensitively.

root_sampling_ratio.description: Required when root_sampling=ratio; fraction of roots sampled. Rejected when set with any other root_sampling mode.

include_url_path.description: Include bounded url.path attribute (never used as span name)

compression.description: Export body compression. Canonical values are none and gzip; the value is trimmed and matched case-insensitively. gzip sends each OTLP/HTTP JSON batch with Content-Encoding gzip; when the compressed copy cannot be reserved under the process observability byte ceiling the batch is sent uncompressed.

PluginConfigBase.description: Shared plugin-config property bag and enabled-gated plugin-specific construction constraints. `POST /plugins/config` and `POST /batch` use `PluginConfigCreate` (`enabled` optional, default true). `PUT /plugins/config/{id}` uses `PluginConfigReplace` (`enabled` required). GET/list/backup responses use `PluginConfig` (`enabled` always present).

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID auto-generated if omitted or empty on create). Custom IDs must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric characters, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 254 chars).

namespace.description: Namespace this plugin config belongs to. Read-only on the wire — set from the `X-Ferrum-Namespace` request header (or the `ferrum` default) on every create/update; any value in the request body is ignored.

plugin_name.description: Plugin type name. Must be one of the available built-in plugins (e.g., key_auth, rate_limiting, cors, stdout_logging). Use `GET /plugins` to discover available plugin names.

config.description: Plugin-specific JSON configuration. When admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may introduce gateway TLS material in a plugin field only as inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace. It may not introduce a field that names a gateway filesystem path or native library setting at all, and it may not create or change a non-built-in plugin's config. Such writes are refused with `400`. Values already stored at the same field path are exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted. May be JSON `null` when the selected plugin's schema permits it (for example `stdout_logging`); object-only plugins still reject null while enabled. Resource-level size and depth constraints are always validated. Plugin-specific construction schemas in this document apply only when `enabled` is true or omitted (`POST` defaults `enabled` to true), matching admin admission: construction itself runs on create/update and config reload only when `enabled` is true. For plugins registered FailClosed or KeepLastKnownGood, unknown plugin names or invalid enabled plugin-specific config are validation-fatal when the plugin cache is built: they block gateway startup in file mode, and on DB/CP polling the new config snapshot is rejected as a whole (the gateway keeps serving the prior good config). Admin API create/update always performs strict construction for an enabled config and returns HTTP 400 before storage when that config is invalid, regardless of serving-mode failure policy. During file-mode load, pre-existing DB/CP snapshot application, or cache rebuild, plugins registered OptionalFailOpen (metrics, tracing, and alerting instrumentation such as `prometheus_metrics`, `otel_tracing`, and `proxy_alerts`) instead emit a validation/construction warning and omit that plugin instance from the published cache while admitting the surrounding snapshot. Log sinks (`stdout_logging`, `http_logging`, `tcp_logging`, `udp_logging`, `kafka_logging`, `loki_logging`, `statsd_logging`, `ws_logging`, `ws_frame_logging`) are KeepLastKnownGood: an invalid enabled log sink rejects the candidate and the prior generation keeps serving. Disabled plugin configs are stored without construction, allowing secret-dependent plugins such as `basic_auth` to be staged before their runtime secret is provisioned. Enabling performs full validation. See `PluginConfigs` section for per-plugin schema definitions. Viewer/operator responses use the audit-safe projection while admin responses remain raw. For loki_logging, that projection preserves only endpoint scheme/host/port and redacts the path, query, authorization, and every custom-header value.

proxy_id.description: Required when scope is `proxy` — must reference an existing proxy ID. Must be null (or omitted) when scope is `global` or `proxy_group`. The referenced proxy must exist. When a proxy is deleted, its proxy-scoped plugin configs are automatically deleted (cascade). Proxy-group-scoped plugins survive proxy deletion — only the association is removed.

enabled.description: Whether the plugin is active. Disabled configs are stored but not constructed; enabling them performs full plugin-specific validation. The `default: true` applies to `POST /plugins/config` only. `PUT /plugins/config/{id}` is a full replace, so an omitted `enabled` would silently re-enable a deliberately disabled config; the server rejects such a body with `400` and requires the field explicitly.

priority_override.description: Optional execution priority override. When set, replaces the plugin's built-in priority constant. Lower values execute first. Useful when multiple instances of the same plugin type are attached to a proxy (e.g., two http_logging instances shipping to Splunk and Datadog). When null (default), the plugin uses its built-in priority.

trigger.description: Optional declarative execution trigger for this one plugin instance. When omitted (the default) the instance executes exactly as it does today, governed only by scope, protocol filtering, and priority. When present, the compiled predicate tree decides once per request/connection whether this instance's hooks run at all. Patterns are compiled and bounded at write time and at plugin-cache publication; invalid shapes, unbounded regexes, malformed CIDRs, and unsupported plugin/phase combinations are rejected with HTTP 400. See `docs/plugin_execution_order.md` for the phase model and the fail-closed composition rules. Non-admin reads, audit diffs, and the configuration export withhold every `header`, `query`, and `cookie` `value` operand (`exact` / `prefix` entries and `regex`) anywhere in the tree; field names, match kinds, flags, and the tree structure stay visible, and a shape the trigger schema does not define is withheld wholesale.

api_spec_id.description:
ID of the `ApiSpec` that created this plugin via the spec-import admin
API (`POST /api-specs`). `null` for plugins created via direct admin
endpoints (`POST /plugins/config`). When set, `PUT /api-specs/{id}`
replaces this plugin as part of the bundle.

PluginConfigCreate.description: Request body for `POST /plugins/config` and `plugin_configs` items in `POST /batch`. `enabled` defaults to true when omitted. `id`, `priority_override`, and `proxy_id` may be omitted; the server generates `id` when empty. Plugin-specific construction constraints apply when `enabled` is true or omitted, matching admin admission. `PUT /plugins/config/{id}` uses `PluginConfigReplace` instead — an `allOf` onto `PluginConfig` cannot relax that schema's required `enabled`.

PluginScope.description:
`global` — plugin applies to all proxies; `proxy_id` must be null.
`proxy` — plugin applies only to the proxy referenced by `proxy_id`;
`proxy_id` is required.
`proxy_group` — plugin applies to a subset of proxies that reference it
in their `plugins` association list; `proxy_id` must be null. A single
shared plugin instance is used across all associated proxies, so stateful
plugins (e.g., rate_limiting) share counters across the group.

PluginTrigger.description:
Declarative per-instance plugin execution trigger. The instance runs
when `when` evaluates to true for the request or stream connection.

Bounds enforced at validation time: predicate-tree depth 8, 128 total
nodes, 64 entries per list, 1024 bytes per literal value, 256 bytes per
field name, 512 bytes of regex source, and a 64 KiB compiled-program /
256 KiB lazy-DFA ceiling per regex.

A trigger is evaluated at most once per request per instance and the
outcome is memoized, so every phase of that instance agrees even after a
later plugin rewrites the path, headers, or query.

Plugins that publish fixed core body ceilings or contextless initial-
header/response-trailer policy are rejected rather than half-gated. A
trigger on a response-presentation transform also makes finalized cache
or dedup replay provenance unprovable, so replay consumers fail closed.

PluginTriggerFieldMatch.description: Header / query / cookie predicate with explicit presence and multi-occurrence semantics.

name.description: Field name. Must be printable ASCII with no whitespace; the value is never trimmed, so a padded name is rejected rather than silently normalized into another configured field. Header names must additionally be valid HTTP tokens and are matched case-insensitively; query and cookie names are matched exactly. A named field occurrence remains present even when its value is not valid UTF-8: it satisfies presence but cannot satisfy a textual `value` matcher. A percent-encoded query name that cannot be decoded cannot be attributed to this configured name and is skipped. Invalid bytes are never lossily transcoded, copied, reflected, or logged.

presence.description: `present` requires at least one occurrence; `absent` requires none and cannot be combined with `value`.

multi_value.description: How `value` applies when the field occurs more than once: `any` requires at least one matching occurrence, `all` requires every occurrence to match (and at least one to exist).

PluginTriggerIdentityMatch.description: Authenticated-identity predicate. An empty identity string is treated as absent.

PluginTriggerMatch.description: A leaf predicate. Exactly one field must be set; combine predicates with `all` / `any` / `not` so a leaf never needs an implicit combination rule. An input that does not exist for the current context never satisfies a positive predicate: HTTP-only predicates (method, path, host, header, query, cookie) are false on a TCP/UDP/DTLS stream connection.

method.description: HTTP methods, compared ASCII-case-insensitively. The list is an OR.

path.description: Canonical policy path (the same value every security decision uses), never the raw request target. Exact/prefix values must start with / and be canonical: no percent escapes, backslashes, or literal dot segments. Regex patterns reject percent escapes but retain regex syntax.

host.description: Request authority host, ASCII-lowercased with the trailing DNS dot and any port removed. Uppercase ASCII in exact/prefix values or regex patterns requires case_insensitive: true; otherwise admission rejects it.

sni.description: Frontend TLS/QUIC SNI hostname, when the client supplied one, ASCII-lowercased with one trailing DNS dot removed. Available on HTTP and stream connections alike. Exact entries are normalized at load (one trailing dot dropped, lowercased, U-labels converted to A-labels with IDNA); prefix entries are lowercased with whole labels converted; regex patterns are left as written. Non-ASCII text that cannot be converted is rejected.

header.description: Request header field, evaluated against the pristine inbound wire view. Field names are ASCII-case-insensitive. A non-UTF-8 value remains structurally present but matches no configured text; it is never lossily transcoded.

query.description: Query parameter of the client's original request target. Names and values are compared after percent-decoding, case-sensitively.

cookie.description: Cookie from the request `Cookie` header. Names are case-sensitive per RFC 6265; a quoted cookie-value is unquoted before comparison.

protocol.description: Authoritative wire-protocol identity. The list is an OR. Transport and flavor are independent, so an HTTP/2 native-gRPC request matches both `http2` and `grpc`.

source_cidr.description: Exact addresses or CIDRs matched against the gateway-resolved client IP. IPv4-mapped IPv6 rules and peers are normalized onto the IPv4 space so one rule matches both forms. The list is an OR.

namespace.description: Namespace of the matched proxy. The list is an OR.

proxy_id.description: ID of the matched proxy. The list is an OR.

listen_port.description: Frontend listener port that accepted the request or connection.

consumer.description: Username of the mapped gateway Consumer. Never matches an unmapped external identity, even one that spells the same string; use `external_identity` for those. Only authoritative after the authentication boundary — a trigger using it does not gate hooks at or before `authenticate`, never gates a stream connection at all (whose one gated phase, `on_stream_connect`, is also where stream authentication runs), and is rejected outright on an authentication plugin and on a stream-only plugin where it could gate nothing.

external_identity.description: Unmapped external identity (a `jwks_auth`, `oidc_relying_party`, `oauth2_introspection`, `ldap_auth`, or `soap_ws_security` principal), present only when no gateway Consumer is mapped. Combine it with `external_identity_authority` (or, for a single-authority mechanism, `auth_method`) under `all` to scope it to one verifying authority. Post-authentication only, with the same stream limitation and the same refusals as `consumer`.

external_identity_authority.description: Verifying authority of the unmapped external identity: the opaque 64-character hex realm digest committed with it at the authentication boundary (the value `opa` exposes as `input.consumer.realm.authority`). Two providers of one mechanism have different digests, so combining this with `external_identity` keeps an equal subject from another authority out of an exemption. The list is an OR, comparison is case-insensitive, and a principal without a committed authority never matches. Post-authentication only, with the same stream limitation and the same refusals as `consumer`.

auth_method.description: Successful authentication mechanism name (for example `jwt_auth`), compared ASCII-case-insensitively. Post-authentication only, with the same stream limitation and the same refusals as `consumer`.

spiffe_id.description: Peer SPIFFE ID established by mesh/mTLS identity. Post-authentication only, with the same stream limitation and the same refusals as `consumer`. A stream connection additionally carries no authoritative, non-forgeable peer SPIFFE fact, so the predicate is never evaluated there rather than silently answering "absent".

PluginTriggerNode.description: One node of the predicate tree. Exactly one of `all`, `any`, `not`, or `match` must be set; any other combination (including an empty `all` or `any` list) is rejected, because it would have no defined truth value.

all.description: Logical AND over the child nodes.

any.description: Logical OR over the child nodes.

not.description: Logical NOT of the child node.

PluginTriggerProtocol.description: Authoritative wire-protocol identity. `http1` / `http2` / `http3` are the accepted frontend transport; `grpc` is a native gRPC request, `grpc_web` a recognized gRPC-Web request, and `websocket` a WebSocket upgrade (HTTP/1.1 Upgrade or RFC 8441 Extended CONNECT). `tcp`, `udp`, and `dtls` are stream-proxy connections.

PluginTriggerStringMatch.description: String comparison. Exactly one of `exact`, `prefix`, or `regex` must be set. `exact` and `prefix` lists are an OR.

regex.description: Regular expression, implicitly anchored as `^(?:…)$` so it can never partially match a longer value. Compiled once at validation time under a 64 KiB program and 256 KiB lazy-DFA ceiling; there are no backreferences or lookaround, so matching is linear in input length.

PrometheusMetricsConfig.description: Plugin: prometheus_metrics — Exports gateway metrics in Prometheus format. Null or an empty object uses defaults. At most one enabled instance is permitted and it must use global scope because the registry and tunables are process-wide. Unknown keys are rejected. `schema` and `schema_ref` are not accepted properties.

render_cache_ttl_seconds.description: How long the cached /metrics response is served before rebuilding (seconds)

stale_entry_ttl_seconds.description: How long idle metric entries live before eviction (seconds). Prevents unbounded memory growth from deleted/recreated proxies

mesh_series_budget_per_family.description: Hard ceiling on live MeshRequestKey series retained per mesh metric family in the process-wide MetricsRegistry. Shared by ordinary mesh identity dimensions and CEL-derived dimensions: newly observed keys beyond the budget are dropped until stale_entry_ttl_seconds eviction frees capacity, and counted on ferrum_mesh_metric_series_overflow_total{family}. 0 is rejected — there is no unlimited mode.

cache_invalidation_min_age_ms.description: Minimum age (ms) of the render cache before record() will invalidate it. Under extreme load this prevents an allocation per request

request_duration_buckets_ms.description: Finite bucket upper bounds (milliseconds) for the request-scoped duration histograms ferrum_request_duration_ms, ferrum_backend_duration_ms, ferrum_edge_overhead_ms, and ferrum_mesh_request_duration_ms. Must be strictly increasing (enforced by the plugin constructor); the +Inf bucket is implicit. Changing the layout drops the affected histogram series, which restart under the new layout.

session_duration_buckets_ms.description: Finite bucket upper bounds (milliseconds) for the session-scoped duration histograms ferrum_stream_duration_ms (TCP/UDP) and ferrum_websocket_session_duration_ms. Same rules as request_duration_buckets_ms.

ProxyAlertsConfig.description:
Plugin: proxy_alerts — in-gateway anomaly notifications for proxy
traffic. Observes HTTP/gRPC transaction summaries, TCP/UDP stream
disconnect summaries, and WebSocket disconnect summaries, then sends
Trigger/Resolve notifications to Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord,
generic HTTP webhooks, or SMTP email. See docs/proxy_alerts.md.

Unknown top-level keys are rejected. Present values must match their
declared types (`enabled` boolean, `quiet_hours_utc` array,
`max_concurrent_dispatches` integer 1..=4294967295, `max_delivery_retries`
integer 0..=8, `delivery_retry_base_ms` / `delivery_retry_max_ms`
integers in [10, 60000]). The constructor additionally requires
`delivery_retry_max_ms >= delivery_retry_base_ms`; standard JSON Schema
cannot compare those sibling numbers, so this schema does not claim
complete admission equivalence for that pair. The `channels` map remains
open for arbitrary channel names; each channel/rule variant is closed
to its selected shape. Rules may also be `enabled: false` drafts.
Webhook `method` is case-insensitive (constructor normalizes to
POST / PUT / PATCH). Channel URL and `*_env` strings must be nonempty;
HTTP webhook URLs must be HTTP(S) with a host and no userinfo.

Email `subject_template` / `body_template` reject empty strings.
Schema `maxLength` on those fields is a character ceiling for tooling;
the constructor enforces UTF-8 byte bounds (1024 / 65536) and balanced
`${` template syntax. SMTP `username` / `username_env` must be paired
with `password` / `password_env` and vice versa. `from` / `to` use the
constructor's ASCII addr-spec grammar (not annotation-only `format: email`).

Registration is OptionalFailOpen. Admin create/update performs strict
construction and returns HTTP 400 for an invalid enabled config before
storing it. During file-mode load, `ferrum-edge validate`, pre-existing
DB/CP snapshot application, or cache rebuild, invalid enabled configs
produce a validation/construction warning and omit this instance from
the published plugin cache rather than rejecting the surrounding
snapshot. `ferrum-edge validate` can therefore exit 0 with optional
plugin warnings; inspect those warnings to confirm the alert instance
is active.

enabled.description: Master runtime switch for this plugin instance.

default_cooldown_seconds.description: Per-rule fallback cooldown. Cooldown is tracked per `(rule, proxy, channel)`.

default_min_request_count.description: Per-rule fallback for error-rate, latency-percentile, and grpc-status-rate rules.

default_resolved_window_seconds.description: Per-rule fallback recovery quiet period after a breach clears.

max_concurrent_dispatches.description: Maximum concurrent outbound notification requests. Excess alerts are dropped, not queued. Values above uint32 (`4294967295`) are rejected.

max_delivery_retries.description:
Number of re-attempts after the initial send for transient
transport/HTTP failures (408/429/5xx and connect/timeout errors).
Retries hold the dispatch semaphore permit and never enqueue extra
work. Permanent failures (other 4xx) are not retried.

delivery_retry_base_ms.description: Initial jittered backoff delay between transient delivery retries.

delivery_retry_max_ms.description:
Upper bound for exponential jittered backoff between transient
delivery retries. The constructor requires this to be
`>= delivery_retry_base_ms`. That sibling comparison is
constructor-only; this schema cannot assert it.

quiet_hours_utc.description: UTC time windows where Trigger alerts are suppressed. Resolve alerts still dispatch.

channels.description: Map of channel name to channel definition. Rule `channels` entries reference these names.

rules.description: Alert rules evaluated per matched proxy. At least one rule must be active.

ProxyAlertsDisabledDraftRule.description:
Explicitly disabled draft rule. Runtime skips these before validation,
so incomplete, unknown, or otherwise invalid fields are allowed when
`enabled` is the boolean `false`. Active complete rules must not use
this branch (`enabled: false` is excluded from active variants).

webhook_url.description: Discord-compatible webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Discord webhook URL.

ProxyAlertsEmailAddress.description:
ASCII addr-spec as enforced by the constructor (no quoted local parts,
comments, or address literals; local-part dots cannot start, end, or
repeat). `format: email` is an annotation; this pattern is the
enforceable grammar. Constructor also caps the local part at 64 bytes.

ProxyAlertsEmailChannel.description:
Native SMTP delivery. TLS is mandatory: `starttls` upgrades the session
and fails closed when the relay does not advertise STARTTLS, and
`implicit_tls` handshakes immediately (SMTPS). Plaintext SMTP is not
offered, `AUTH` is never sent before the handshake completes, and
certificate verification is always enforced (this channel does not honor
`FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY`; use `FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` for private CAs).
Username and password (inline or `*_env`) must be paired: either both
sides are set or neither is.

smtp_host.description: SMTP relay hostname or IP literal. No scheme, port, path, or credentials. Literal IPs must pass the resolved backend egress policy at admission (including allow/deny CIDRs and dangerous-range overrides). Construction does not resolve DNS; every send rechecks the resolved IP before connecting.

smtp_port.description: SMTP port. Defaults to 587 for `starttls` and 465 for `implicit_tls`.

tls_mode.description: TLS posture for the session. Both values complete a verified handshake before any credential or message data is written.

tls_server_name.description: Verified TLS identity override. Defaults to `smtp_host`.

username.description: SMTP AUTH username. Prefer `username_env`. Must be paired with `password` or `password_env`.

username_env.description: Environment variable containing the SMTP AUTH username.

password.description: SMTP AUTH password. Prefer `password_env`. Redacted from lower-privilege plugin projections and audit records; full-admin reads remain raw by repository policy. Must be paired with `username` or `username_env`.

password_env.description: Environment variable containing the SMTP AUTH password.

from.description: Envelope and header sender address (max 254 bytes, ASCII addr-spec).

subject_template.description:
Subject template. Schema `maxLength` is a character ceiling for
tooling. The constructor enforces a 1024-byte UTF-8 bound (a
600-character string of `é` is 1200 bytes and is rejected), rejects
empty strings, and rejects unbalanced `${` placeholders.

body_template.description:
Plain-text body template. Adds `${fields}`, the notification's
key/value rows rendered as `Name: value` lines. Schema `maxLength`
is a character ceiling; the constructor enforces a 65536-byte UTF-8
bound, rejects empty strings, and rejects unbalanced `${`
placeholders.

helo_name.description: EHLO identity. Defaults to the domain of `from`.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Applied independently to DNS resolution, TCP connect, and the TLS handshake, so a stalled connect can take up to three times this value before it fails.

command_timeout_ms.description: Bounds each SMTP command/reply exchange, including DATA.

ProxyAlertsEnvName.description:
Name of a `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable
(`<NAME>` uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) resolved at construction.
Any other process environment variable, including every other
`FERRUM_*` setting, is refused at admission with a 400. The named
variable must also be set and nonempty at construction; that
process-environment check is constructor-only.

classes.description: Error classes counted by this rule. HTTP rules also check `body_error_class`.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching errors occur in the window.

threshold_percent.description: Alert when the matching status-code percentage is at least this value.

min_request_count.description: Minimum total requests in the window before the percentage can alert.

threshold_count.description:
Alert when at least this many completed gRPC transactions carry a
matching terminal application status in the window. Evaluated from
the terminal `log()` summary after buffered, trailers-only, and
streamed bodies finish. HTTP transport status is not consulted.

ProxyAlertsGrpcStatusList.description:
Terminal gRPC application statuses to match. Integers are standard codes
`0..=16`. The string `OTHER` matches malformed (`u32::MAX`) and future
out-of-range codes, matching the bounded StatsD/Prometheus bucket.
Distinct from HTTP `status_codes`.

threshold_percent.description:
Alert when the matching gRPC-status percentage among gRPC
transactions is at least this value. Plain HTTP samples do not
enter the denominator.

min_request_count.description: Minimum gRPC transactions in the window before the percentage can alert.

ProxyAlertsHttpUrl.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no `user:pass@` userinfo. Empty
strings are rejected. `format: uri` is a Draft 2020-12 annotation;
this pattern is the enforceable constructor approximation
(constructor also parses the URL and rejects a missing host).

metric.description: Latency metric to observe. `stream_duration_ms` applies to TCP/UDP/DTLS/WebSocket sessions and is measured on a process-monotonic clock (not UTC wall time); connect/disconnect timestamps remain civil-clock values for rendering. The other metrics apply to HTTP-family summaries.

threshold_ms.description: Alert when the bucket upper-bound estimate for the percentile is strictly greater than this threshold.

min_request_count.description: Minimum observations in the window before the percentile can alert.

from.description: UTC start time in strict HH:MM form.

to.description: UTC end time in strict HH:MM form. Values earlier than `from` wrap past midnight.

weekdays.description: Days the window applies to (`0 = Sunday` ... `6 = Saturday`). Omit or use `[]` for every day.

resolved_window_seconds.description: How long the rule must stay below threshold before a Resolve notification is sent.

ProxyAlertsRule.description:
Active rules are discriminator-selected closed variants. An explicit
`enabled: false` draft object is also accepted and may contain
incomplete or unknown fields; runtime skips drafts before validation.
Active variants reject `enabled: false` so a complete disabled rule
cannot satisfy more than one `oneOf` branch.

ProxyAlertsRuleCommon.description: Shared rule fields. Closed-object enforcement lives on each selected rule variant via `unevaluatedProperties: false` so common and type-specific keys compose correctly.

name.description: Unique rule name within this plugin config.

enabled.description: Active rules are enabled when this field is omitted or `true`. Use `ProxyAlertsDisabledDraftRule` (`enabled: false`) for incomplete drafts.

channels.description: Channel names from the top-level `channels` map.

webhook_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Slack incoming webhook URL.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching responses occur in the window.

causes.description: Stream disconnect causes counted by this rule.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching disconnects occur in the window.

webhook_url.description: Microsoft Teams incoming webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Teams incoming webhook URL.

url.description: HTTP(S) endpoint URL. Prefer `url_env` for secrets.

url_env.description: Environment variable containing the HTTP(S) endpoint URL.

method.description:
HTTP method. Case-insensitive; the constructor normalizes to POST,
PUT, or PATCH. Spellings such as `post` and `pAtCh` are accepted.

headers.description: Headers sent with the webhook request. JSON content types JSON-escape template substitutions.

body_template.description:
Template body. Supports generic notification variables plus
proxy_alerts variables such as `${rule_name}`, `${proxy_name}`,
`${incident_key}` (stable per plugin config + namespace + proxy +
rule; use it as the receiver's correlation key, e.g. PagerDuty
`dedup_key`),
`${observed}`, `${threshold}`, `${sample_count}` (total samples in
the rule window), `${window_seconds}`, and `${reason}`. Empty
strings are allowed. Unbalanced `${`
placeholders are rejected at construction; JSON Schema cannot
express balanced-placeholder syntax.

RateLimitingConfig.description: Plugin: rate_limiting — Per-IP, per-consumer, per-SPIFFE-identity, or per-policy aggregate (`limit_by: service`) request rate limiting. Quota 429 responses carry a Retry-After header. On stream proxies, consumer mode uses the identified stream Consumer when available and otherwise falls back to client IP; `spiffe_identity` keys on the SPIFFE ID extracted by the `spiffe_identity` / `mtls_auth` mesh chain and falls back to client IP when no SPIFFE identity is present. Supports centralized Redis-backed mode for coordinating rate limits across multiple gateway instances. `limits` must contain exactly one `scope: default` rule for generic keys and fallback IPs, plus optional `scope: consumers` rules that apply the same rate rule to one or many consumer identities, each with an independent counter. Counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. Residual admission rules this schema cannot express, enforced by the plugin constructor alone: one consumer identity may not appear in two different `scope: consumers` rules (JSON Schema can only reject a duplicate inside one rule), and `redis_url` details noted on that field.

limit_by.description:
Rate limit key. Parsed case-insensitively; `null` is the same as omitting the field:
- `ip` (default) — client IP.
- `consumer` — identified consumer (HTTP) or stream consumer (TCP/UDP); falls back to client IP when no consumer is present.
- `spiffe_identity` — SPIFFE ID extracted from peer certificate (mesh authn). `spiffe` is accepted as an alias.
- `service` — one aggregate budget per policy shared by every caller (a total route/service rate), charged after authentication (authorize phase) on HTTP and once per connection/session on TCP/UDP. With `sync_mode: redis` the budget is shared by every gateway serving the policy. Compose it beside a per-caller instance to enforce both a per-caller and a total limit.

ipv6_prefix.description: IPv6 prefix length used to group source addresses for IP rate-limit keys. IPv4 addresses remain host-specific.

expose_headers.description: Inject x-ratelimit-* headers on requests and responses. Every admitted (counted) request's client-visible response carries the headers, including successful WebSocket handshake responses and gateway-generated responses such as cache hits, response mocks, serverless short-circuits, and rejections from plugins that run after rate limiting. The header names are one public set, so when several rate_limiting instances run on a route exactly one verdict is published: the limiter that refused the request, or — when all of them admitted — the tightest remaining budget. A refusing limiter with expose_headers=false, and any fail-closed 503, publish no rate-limit headers at all.

max_state_entries.description: Hard cap on distinct keys this policy keeps in local (and Redis-fallback) state. At the cap, keys already tracked keep their budgets and a previously unseen key is refused with 429 until idle keys are pruned. Read per admission and not part of the local-state compatibility fingerprint, so changing it never resets live budgets.

limits.description: Rate-limit rules. Must include exactly one `scope: default` rule. `scope: consumers` rules are only valid when `limit_by` is `consumer`.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Count MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests instead of HTTP requests (null or omitted counts requests). Only tools/call is charged: each tools/call member of a JSON-RPC batch is one charge, including notification-form tools/call members (a tools/call without an id is still charged); notifications/* methods, initialize, tools/list, and every other method pass uncounted. The charge runs in before_proxy over the buffered body, with the media types mcp_gateway admits (application/json, application/json-rpc, +json, or no Content-Type); a body with duplicate member names, or a batch past 32 members / 1 MiB / 256 KiB per member, is refused with JSON-RPC -32600. So is an in-scope request whose Content-Type declares a charset other than UTF-8, and a body strict UTF-8 JSON cannot read (UTF-16/32, a byte-order mark, NaN, comments, invalid UTF-8) that could still carry a tools/call for a lenient upstream parser. These recognizer bounds are fixed at 32 members / 1 MiB / 256 KiB per member; setting mcp_gateway validation.max_batch_* above these values makes the limiter refuse the larger request with -32600. An in-scope request with non-identity Content-Encoding is refused with JSON-RPC -32017 unless an earlier decompression hook has removed the encoding. An exhausted budget is answered on HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC error (code -32015, one per request-form batch member) plus x-ratelimit-* headers when expose_headers is set; a fail-closed Redis outage answers -32016. The mode is HTTP-only.

endpoint_path.description: Inspect and buffer only requests to exactly this path (normally mcp_gateway endpoint.path). No query, fragment, or control character.

tools.description: Count only calls naming one of these public tool names. The per-name bound is enforced by the constructor in UTF-8 bytes (maxLength counts characters).

per_tool.description: Keep one budget per listed tool instead of one shared by every counted call. Requires tools.

sync_mode.description: Rate limit state storage: 'local' (in-memory per instance) or 'redis' (centralized across instances), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works (Redis, Valkey, DragonflyDB, KeyDB, Garnet).

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection (upgrades redis:// to rediss://; the URL scheme is matched case-insensitively and stored lowercase). CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed explicitly refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback (the default) uses per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Effective Redis connection-attempt timeout in seconds. Applied to the redis-rs inner connection config for cached, dedicated, and health-check paths (TCP connect, TLS handshake when enabled, Redis protocol handshake). It is also the deadline for the proactive `INFO CLUSTER` topology screen (and the no-eviction memory screen) issued on every new connection, on the pooled and dedicated paths as well as the recovery probe — the redis-rs 500ms command cap does not preempt it. That per-command cap is installed on the connection once it is screened, so ordinary command execution stays bounded. Gateway DNS screening/resolution of the Redis hostname runs before this timeout starts.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Interval in seconds for health check pings when Redis is marked unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

RateLimitingRuleConfig.description: One rate_limiting rule. Every rule must set either one or more preset fields (`requests_per_second`/`requests_per_minute`/`requests_per_hour`) or the custom-window pair (`window_seconds` + `max_requests`), but not both styles in the same rule. Exactly one rule in the plugin config must use `scope: default`. `scope: consumers` is only valid with `limit_by: consumer`; each listed identity gets its own independent counter using this rule's windows.

scope.description: `default` applies to all keys without a more specific consumer rule and to IP fallback. `consumers` selects the identities listed in `consumers`; each identity has its own counter. Parsed case-insensitively.

consumers.description: Effective consumer identities for `scope: consumers` rules. Each listed identity gets an independent counter using this rule's windows. Matched against the mapped Consumer username only; an unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username, and is counted under its own realm-scoped key. A repeated identity is rejected here and across rules; JSON Schema can only express the within-rule half, so the cross-rule duplicate is refused by the plugin constructor alone.

requests_per_second.description: Max requests per second. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

requests_per_minute.description: Max requests per minute. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

requests_per_hour.description: Max requests per hour. Capped at 1000000 (see `max_requests`).

window_seconds.description: Custom rate-limit window length in seconds. Must be paired with `max_requests`. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and as a signed Redis TTL.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests permitted within `window_seconds`. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key, not by one timestamp per admitted request.

RateSpec.description: Closed rate limit specification used by grpc_method_router (method_rate_limits entries and default_rate_limit). Both fields are required and must be positive integers; unknown keys are rejected by the runtime and by this schema.

max_requests.description: Maximum requests allowed in the window. Capped at 1000000 as an operational budget ceiling. Local sliding-window memory is bounded independently by a fixed aggregate-bucket ring per key.

window_seconds.description: Time window in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.

RequestDeduplicationConfig.description: Plugin: request_deduplication — Idempotency-key based request deduplication. Gateway-authored dispatch errors are not completed responses: proven pre-wire failures release the matching owner token at finalization, while any possible execution retains the in-flight lease until inflight_ttl_seconds. Real backend error responses remain replayable; provenance is independent of HTTP status. Logical keys are scoped by stable plugin-config identity, matched proxy namespace and ID, peer SPIFFE identity when present, authenticated identity when configured, and idempotency header value, then stored as framed SHA-256 digests. Stable plugin identity partitions sibling Redis-backed instances even when they share an explicit/default prefix, and matched proxy namespaces remain isolated even when an explicit Redis prefix is shared, while the same configured instance shares keys across gateways. Per-request completion ownership (logical key, fingerprint, local owner token, and optional Redis lock token) is held in an instance-keyed private structure rather than shared public metadata, so multiple scoped instances with distinct headers mark and token-release independently on the same request. Cached responses replay only when the request fingerprint also matches method, authority/host, exact path, effective outbound query string, deterministic request headers that can affect routing/transforms, and request-body digest. Cached bytes are already-finalized representations and bypass ordinary presentation transforms on replay while remaining subject to response inspection and final-body validation; a current-policy redaction decision runs only its required transform and fails closed with 502 if rewriting cannot complete. Applicable methods with declared bodies are prebuffered so keys added by earlier header transforms can be fingerprinted. Reusing a logical idempotency key for a different fingerprint returns 409. A synthetic short-circuit whose own execution performed the protected external operation — a terminate-mode serverless_function invocation or an ai_federation provider call — declares that provenance and never releases its ownership. What is published once every response decision is final depends on whether that finalized response can be retained. A terminate-mode serverless_function response that fits the entry/total limits and carries an establishable presentation policy is published as an ordinary REPLAYABLE completion through the fenced transition: an identical retry receives the cached status and body with X-Idempotent-Replayed: true for ttl_seconds and the function is invoked exactly once. Every other outcome — a response too large to retain, an unprovable or straddled presentation policy, a streamed fallthrough, an interrupted delivery, and every ai_federation-marked provider call, whose synthetic body was never a backend response and is never stored — publishes a durable non-replayable 409 completion tombstone under the key instead, so an identical idempotency-key retry cannot repeat the billable operation when inflight_ttl_seconds elapses. That tombstone is retained for max(ttl_seconds, inflight_ttl_seconds): it replaces an in-flight marker that blocked duplicates for inflight_ttl_seconds, so a deployment with inflight_ttl_seconds greater than ttl_seconds never becomes re-executable sooner than a bare marker left it, while ordinary replayable completions keep ttl_seconds. Externally executed synthetic plugins that do not declare this provenance must define their own completion contract. Completed response retention is bounded by per-entry and exact local total byte limits; size-skipped responses return normally and are not retained. In local mode, ordinary skipped responses clear in-flight state immediately. Supports centralized Redis-backed mode for cross-instance deduplication. The Redis endpoint must be deployed with maxmemory-policy noeviction (or no maxmemory limit at all): a deduplication record is the control rather than a cache copy, so an evicting endpoint would silently drop a live in-flight or completed record mid-lease and let a retry execute the operation a second time while Redis stayed reachable. Every newly established connection — first dial, dedicated transaction connection, and background recovery probe — is screened with INFO MEMORY and used only when the server proves maxmemory:0 or maxmemory_policy:noeviction; a proven allkeys-*/volatile-* policy is terminal for that client generation and an unproven screen is a recoverable outage, after which on_redis_unavailable governs (fail-closed by default). Redis mode stores ownership and completion in ONE versioned operation record per logical key: acquisition is a token-owned SET NX before backend dispatch, and publication is a compare-and-set fenced on that still-current token, so publication and the ownership transition are atomic. An owner whose inflight_ttl_seconds lease expired can neither overwrite a successor's completed response nor publish while a successor owns the operation; its local completion is discarded instead. Current-version records with a missing or empty in-flight owner token, impossible state-dependent fields, or mismatched inner/outer replay fingerprints fail closed as unknown writer state. When a completed response cannot be represented within max_entry_size_bytes, a small non-replayable completion tombstone is published so peers receive a deterministic 409 for max(ttl_seconds, inflight_ttl_seconds) instead of becoming free to re-execute when the raw lease expires; a record published without a replay payload never expires sooner than the lease it replaced. Redis values include the fingerprint, obey the per-entry size limit for both retained response size and serialized payload size, and v7 logical keys plus the versioned record format are not backward-compatible with earlier versions. The matched route's response-header policy (a mesh_route_dispatch response_transform) is bound into the request fingerprint rather than the logical key: it changes how a result is presented, not which operation an identical retry executes, so a response-header-only route reload returns 409 for a same-key retry instead of addressing a fresh key and executing the operation again. A request whose idempotency header, authority, or framing/coding header is present under case-variant spellings with different values is refused with 400 rather than resolved by map iteration order. When Redis cannot be consulted, on_redis_unavailable decides between a fail-closed 503 (default) and an explicitly opted-in process-local fallback. Unknown top-level keys are rejected, and Redis-only keys are rejected outside sync_mode='redis'. If an owned terminal response fits locally but its serialized Redis value exceeds the cap, Redis admission settles before ordinary local eviction; the matching local gateway preserves one replay while active entries occupy the cap, and later pressure converts an unretainable protected replay to a fixed-size execution barrier that inherits the completion's original insertion time and retention while peers remain blocked. Persistent per-key execution barriers are hard-capped at max_entries; overflow extends one fixed process-global deadline and returns 503 for applicable idempotency-key requests rather than allocating unbounded key state or failing open. If a completion is skipped only by the local total cap and Redis publication fails, local and distributed in-flight locks are left to expire under inflight_ttl_seconds to avoid immediate duplicate execution without a replay value. When sync_mode is redis, redis_url is required. Every retained response, local or Redis, is stamped with the response-side presentation policy it was produced under: a content digest of the published response_transformer RTDS gate map plus a content digest of the effective static presentation rules of the proxy (response_transformer, sse, and a2a_gateway in its configured-public-base mode), folded in configured execution order. A stored response replays only while both digests still match the live policy; a stamp that no longer matches, a record written without provenance, and a record with malformed provenance all return 409 rather than replaying under a superseded policy or re-executing a possibly completed side effect. A response whose request straddled a gate publication, or whose effective presentation policy could not be established, is retained for replay neither in Redis nor locally, while in-flight ownership is kept until its TTL. The non-replayable external-operation completion tombstone is the one exception: its bytes are a fixed 409 refusal that asserts no presentation policy, so it is published even under an unprovable or straddled policy rather than leaving an already-performed operation executable again when inflight_ttl_seconds elapses. Only fixed-size digests are stored, never rule text or header values. The built-in priority 3010 runs after route dispatch and request_transformer header/query rules but before terminate-mode serverless execution. Admission rejects every same-protocol request header/query mutator at or after deduplication (including priority overrides), and rejects any deferred request-body transformer whose final bytes were not already established by pre-before_proxy normalization. request_deduplication cannot be composed with mcp_gateway on the same proxy: admission rejects the pair with 400 (fatal in file mode, rejected update in DP) because an MCP public-URI rewrite is derived from live upstream discovery state that no persisted digest can witness. It also cannot be composed with an a2a_gateway instance that derives its public base from the request - discovery.public_base_url unset while discovery.trust_forwarded_headers is true - because the rewritten Agent Card origin then depends on per-request forwarded headers and the connection's transport security, neither of which the fingerprint binds; that refusal is per instance, so a configured-public-base a2a_gateway composes normally.

header_name.description: Request header name containing the deduplication key. Must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP field-name token. Names in the gateway-owned x-consumer-* request namespace (case-insensitive, `_` equivalent to `-`) are rejected at config load, because the gateway strips them from every client request and no request could carry the key.

ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live in seconds for cached completed responses. Must be greater than zero and representable as an unsigned 64-bit integer.

inflight_ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live in seconds for in-flight request entries used to coalesce duplicate requests while the first is still being processed. Defaults to `ttl_seconds` when omitted. Must be greater than zero and representable as an unsigned 64-bit integer.

max_entries.description: Maximum number of tracked local deduplication entries and hard maximum number of persistent per-key execution barriers. Active in-flight work is never evicted while live and may temporarily exceed the entry target, up to the separate hard max_inflight_entries ceiling. If completed external operations fill the per-key barrier budget, additional barriers collapse into one fixed process-global deadline and applicable idempotency-key requests receive 503 until it expires.

max_inflight_entries.description: Hard ceiling on live local in-flight markers per policy identity, counted exactly and reserved by a single atomic compare-and-swap — requests currently executing plus interrupted or ambiguous requests (for example a client that reset a streamed response) whose markers are retained until inflight_ttl_seconds. Defaults to max_entries when omitted. A request with a new idempotency key that cannot reserve a slot is refused with 503 and any Redis ownership it acquired is released; requests for keys that are already tracked still replay or conflict, and live ownership is never evicted to admit new work. Execution barriers are bounded separately by max_entries. Must be greater than zero and representable as an unsigned 64-bit integer.

max_entry_size_bytes.description: Maximum retained size of one completed response entry. Oversized responses return the original response to the client without retaining a replayable entry. In local mode, ordinary oversized responses clear in-flight state without retaining it, so a later retry can re-execute. A completed external operation instead atomically replaces its exact owner with a fixed-size execution barrier retained for max(ttl_seconds, inflight_ttl_seconds), without retaining response bytes. In Redis mode, when a replayable response does not fit, a small non-replayable completion tombstone is atomically published so peers refuse identical retries for the same barrier window.

max_total_size_bytes.description: Exact maximum retained size across local completed response entries. Responses that would exceed this cap are returned normally and are not retained. In local mode, ordinary skipped responses clear in-flight state immediately, while a completed external operation uses a fixed-size execution barrier with its authoritative retention and no response-byte charge. In Redis mode, an ordinary local-total-cap skip keeps local and distributed in-flight locks until inflight_ttl_seconds only if Redis publication fails.

applicable_methods.description: HTTP methods that require deduplication. Must contain at least one entry, and every entry must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP method token. The runtime parser trims surrounding whitespace and uppercases the token before matching (`" post "` is accepted and matches `POST`), which is why the pattern tolerates padding.

scope_by_consumer.description: Additionally include the authenticated consumer's display identity in the deduplication key. Caller isolation no longer depends on this flag — every logical key binds a mandatory caller-authorization partition (authentication mechanism, resolved identity/consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, and SHA-256 digests of every credential header presented, unless caller_partition is authenticated_identity) plus the effective destination, so two credentials resolving to one display subject with different scopes can never claim or replay one another's operation under the default caller_partition.

anonymous_caller_scope.description: How anonymous callers (no gateway identity, no credential header, no peer SPIFFE identity) are partitioned. caller_address (default) binds the gateway-resolved canonical peer address, which the origin observes through Ferrum's regenerated X-Forwarded-For; a request whose canonical address cannot be parsed is refused rather than keyed incompletely. shared is an explicit operator attestation that the origin does not vary its result by caller address on this route — only set it when that is known-safe, because it re-opens cross-caller replay for address-sensitive origins. It applies to anonymous callers only: an authenticated caller always binds its canonical peer address, because the backend receives Ferrum's regenerated forwarding identity for that caller too and may vary policy or content by it. Explicit null is rejected (`'anonymous_caller_scope' must be a string`); omit the field to select the default. The runtime parser trims surrounding whitespace and is case-insensitive, and `_`/`-` are interchangeable (`" SHARED "`, `"caller-address"` are accepted); the enum lists only canonical and alias forms because JSON Schema cannot express case-insensitivity, so strict schema validators may reject mixed-case or padded inputs the gateway itself accepts.

caller_partition.description: How the caller dimension of the logical key is bound. `credential` (default) binds the full caller-authorization partition: mechanism, resolved identity and consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, SHA-256 digests of every presented credential header (pristine and live views), and the canonical peer address — so a refreshed token, a per-request signature (hmac_auth, SigV4), or a new client address is a different caller and a retry executes again. `authenticated_identity` is an operator opt-in for clients whose credentials or addresses change between retries: when the gateway verified a principal (a resolved Consumer, a peer SPIFFE identity, or an external identity committed with its verified realm through the authentication boundary) the key binds that principal only — no credential digests and no peer address — and the request fingerprint binds the presence but not the values of credential headers, of credential query parameters an authentication plugin captured from its configured query location, and of the signature-context headers `date`, `x-amz-date`, `x-amz-content-sha256`, `amz-sdk-invocation-id`, `amz-sdk-request`, `digest`, and `content-digest` (exactly this list) that an hmac_auth or SigV4 re-signature or an AWS SDK retry attempt regenerates. A credential header or query parameter renamed by an earlier request_transformer keeps that classification under its current name; every other header and query pair stays value-bound. Two credentials of one principal with different scopes then share an operation, so scope-level distinction rests on the authorization plugins that ran before deduplication. Requests without a verified principal fall back to `credential`. The mode is framed into the key, so changing it never reuses retained state. Matched exactly (no case or whitespace normalization).

enforce_required.description: Reject requests missing the deduplication header with 400

sync_mode.description: Dedup cache storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized completed responses plus distributed in-flight locks). Any RESP-compatible server works, and the endpoint must not evict (see the component description). The runtime parser is case-insensitive (`"REDIS"` selects centralized mode and requires redis_url); the enum lists only the canonical spellings because JSON Schema cannot express case-insensitivity, so strict schema validators may reject mixed-case inputs the gateway itself accepts.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Must be non-empty when supplied. When omitted, the runtime derives `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:dedup` (for example `ferrum:dedup` when the namespace is `ferrum`). No static OpenAPI default is advertised because the value depends on the gateway namespace. Sibling request_deduplication instances remain isolated under a shared default or explicit prefix because logical keys include the stable plugin-config id. Matched proxy namespaces also remain isolated when an explicit prefix is shared across namespaces; corresponding copies of one config still share locks and completed values across gateways.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

on_redis_unavailable.description: Behavior when `sync_mode: redis` is configured but Redis cannot be consulted. `fail_closed` (default) refuses the request with 503 rather than making an ownership decision only one process can see: during an outage a local-only decision lets the same idempotency key execute once per gateway process. `local_only` explicitly opts into process-local deduplication for availability. Only valid when `sync_mode` is `redis`.

RequestMirrorConfig.description:
Plugin: request_mirror — Duplicates live proxy traffic to a secondary
destination for shadow testing, validation, or migration checks
without affecting client responses. The shadow request is dispatched in
the finalized-request-egress phase, after request-body transforms and
after every final request-policy hook has accepted the backend-visible
representation, so the mirror receives the byte-identical finalized body
plus the finalized pre-egress header baseline. A preceding function may
add a later backend-only header overlay. Final request-body policy never
rejects only after mirror dispatch; backend admission or transport still
can. Only the properties below are
admitted; unknown top-level keys are rejected so misspelled sampling,
body, protocol, or endpoint controls cannot silently fall back to
security-sensitive defaults (cleartext http, 100% mirroring, body
mirroring enabled). Mirrored requests are
fire-and-forget: spawned via `tokio::spawn`, the gateway never waits
for the mirror response and mirror failures never propagate to the
client. Mirror response metadata (status, size, latency) is captured
via a `tokio::sync::watch` channel and surfaced through transaction
logs. Outbound mirror headers use Ferrum's canonical secondary-request
sanitizer (Connection-listed hop-by-hop, Trailer, framing, Ferrum
request-only markers, and proxy-owned X-Forwarded-* identity); these
forwarding fields are stripped rather than regenerated, so mirrors do
not receive Ferrum-authored X-Forwarded-* identity. Host is derived from
the mirror URL (mesh shadow Host uses a protocol-valid DNS `-shadow`
suffix; IPv4/IPv6 literals are left unchanged). Cross-origin credential
forwarding is deny-by-default: any header whose lowercased name is a
built-in credential (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization,
Proxy-Authenticate, WWW-Authenticate, X-Api-Key, …), contains a built-in
credential substring
(so vendor variants like x-openai-api-key / x-amz-security-token are also
caught), is credential-shaped (any separator-delimited segment is a
credential-class word such as auth, jwt, session, sid, key, pass, pwd,
ticket, otp, or contains a credential stem such as session, sessid,
token, secret, auth, pwd, otp, verifier, or contains key or pass other
than ordinary words such as keyword or passenger; the whole name code
is denied too; continuation cursors like
x-continuation-token, authorship/authority names, and Idempotency-Key
are not), or matches a configured
sensitive_header_patterns entry is stripped before the distinct mirror
origin. Native gRPC metadata travels
as HTTP/2 headers, so the same predicate covers gRPC credential metadata.
Forwarding any denied header requires the fail-closed pair
forward_sensitive_headers=true plus a non-empty exact-name
forward_sensitive_header_allowlist. Native gRPC mirrors re-synthesise te: trailers and dial
via the shared PluginHttpClient HTTP/2 companion (h2c prior knowledge for
cleartext http targets; ALPN h2 for https). Ordinary HTTP mirrors keep
the default all-version client so HTTP/1.1 destinations continue to work.
Mirror response bodies are always drained under max_response_body_bytes
so Content-Length responses do not strand keep-alive pools; the short
post-header drain cap is clamped to whatever remains of the absolute
mirror deadline, and a deadline that expires after response headers but
before the body completes is counted as a drain TIMEOUT rather than a
transport failure. Each selected instance copies the finalized request
body once into an owned Bytes retained by its detached task (the primary
buffer is untouched and never shared with the mirror), and that copy is
admitted under max_in_flight plus that instance's
max_retained_request_body_bytes budget. Sampling and that
admission run in the authorize phase, BEFORE the request body is
collected: a percentage-zero, sampled-out, or saturated request keeps
streaming and never allocates a mirror body, and
max_mirrored_request_body_bytes bounds a single mirrored body even when
the global request-body limit is unlimited. The mirror request
always has a finite deadline (mirror_timeout_ms, else positive proxy
backend_read_timeout_ms, else 60000ms, capped at 300000ms), and that
deadline is ABSOLUTE for the whole detached mirror: every shared-client
attempt, every FERRUM_PLUGIN_HTTP_RETRY_DELAY_MS delay between retried
attempts, and the response drain spend the same budget, so enabling
FERRUM_PLUGIN_HTTP_MAX_RETRIES cannot extend it or hold the max_in_flight
permit past it.
Several runtime admission rules cannot be expressed portably in JSON
Schema and are enforced only at construction: allowlist entries must
name a header/query parameter the deny-by-default policy actually strips;
pattern and allowlist lengths are measured in UTF-8 BYTES after trimming
(JSON Schema maxLength counts characters); an explicit
max_mirrored_request_body_bytes must not exceed the sibling
max_retained_request_body_bytes; byte-count fields require a JSON
integer LITERAL, so a whole-valued float such as 1.0 is rejected at
construction even though JSON Schema treats it as an integer; and a
cleartext mirror (mirror_protocol http, the default) to a mirror_host
that is not a loopback IP literal requires allow_plaintext true. Label-safe
process-wide ferrum_request_mirror_*_total lifecycle counters are exported
on authenticated /metrics (no URLs, header names, or plugin IDs). The mirror
request-target snapshots the same canonical backend-visible query primary
dispatch uses (after auth credential strips), then drops deny-by-default
sensitive query pairs from the mirror URL only. Query names are classified
with bounded staged percent-decode (every layer through a hard cap of 4;
residual valid %XX, malformed, or control-bearing names fail closed).
Built-in token/sig/signature matching is delimiter-bounded (oauth_token,
x-amz-signature, x-goog-signature denied; continuation_token and signal
retained). The same credential-shaped rule as headers applies to the
decoded name (session_id, jwt, access_key, private_key, key, sid, …
denied; continuation_token retained). Credentials keep provenance
through renames: a request_transformer rename whose source is a
credential name under this mirror's classifiers and patterns (across
chained instances) makes the destination a credential, and any header
or query value equal to a credential value seen on the request is
withheld under whatever name it now has.
Delimiter variants of api_key are denied, and raw semicolon-
bearing segments fail closed because backend query parsers disagree on
whether they contain additional pairs. Retained pairs keep raw encoding,
order, flags, empty values, +, percent escapes, and non-ASCII encoded
bytes. The primary backend
request-target is never rewritten. Forwarding a denied query name requires
forward_sensitive_query=true plus a non-empty exact decoded-name
forward_sensitive_query_allowlist.

mirror_host.description: Hostname or IP of the mirror target. Normalized to ASCII-lowercase at config load.
