A bare host only: surrounding whitespace is trimmed, but a blank value, a scheme (https://example.test), an embedded path/query/fragment, userinfo, or a host:port authority (example.test:80) is rejected at construction. An IP literal is validated exactly as the runtime IP parser does: an IPv6 literal may be written bracketed ([2001:db8::10]) or bare (2001:db8::10) and is normalized to the bracketed URL authority; an IPv4 literal may be bare or bracketed ([127.0.0.1]) and is normalized to its bare form. Malformed IPv6 literals (:::1, 1::2::3, 12345::1, or an embedded IPv4 tail with an out-of-range or zero-padded octet) and malformed bracketed IPv4 are rejected. No other value may contain brackets or a colon. null is rejected because mirror_host is required.

mirror_port.description: Port of the mirror target. Defaults to 80 (http) or 443 (https).

mirror_protocol.description: Transport scheme for the mirror URL. Matched case-insensitively: the value is ASCII-lowercased at construction, so HTTPS and https are the same setting. http (the default) is admitted without allow_plaintext only when mirror_host is a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or ::1); any other host needs https or an explicit allow_plaintext true. For native gRPC content-types, http uses cleartext HTTP/2 prior knowledge (h2c) and https negotiates ALPN h2 via the shared plugin HTTP/2 companion. Ordinary HTTP mirrors retain the default all-version client (HTTP/1.1 capable).

allow_plaintext.description: Explicit opt-in to mirror over cleartext http to a mirror_host that is not a loopback IP literal. The mirror request replays the backend-visible request (its body by default, plus any allowlisted credential headers or query names), so leave this false and use mirror_protocol https unless the path to the mirror is otherwise protected. Has no effect with https or a loopback IP literal host.

mirror_path.description: Override path used for the mirror request. Must start with `/` and cannot contain a query or fragment. Empty (and null) is treated as omitted. Path selection precedence is: (1) this explicit mirror_path, which always wins; (2) otherwise the matched mesh_route_dispatch route_override_path (the final selected/rebased URI), read without consuming the override primary dispatch still needs; (3) otherwise the backend-effective authorized path when route-sensitive backend-path policy such as grpc_method_router is active, so a rewritten unauthorized method is never replayed to the shadow destination; (4) otherwise the original request path.

percentage.description: Percentage of requests to mirror (0.0–100.0). Quantized to 0.1% steps as round(percentage × 10) in 0..=1000. Sampling is deterministic and evenly spaced (Bresenham phase accumulator over a 1,000-request cycle): 0% never selects, 100% always selects, and other thresholds mirror exactly that many requests per cycle with gaps of floor(1000/threshold) or ceil(1000/threshold). No RNG. Construction/reload resets the phase to 0 so the first selection is deferred (no mirrored prefix burst). The phase stays bounded in 0..1000 via lock-free atomic updates on the request hot path.

mirror_request_body.description: When true, the request body is forwarded to the mirror target. Binary-safe (preserves gRPC protobuf and other non-UTF-8 payloads). Body collection is gated by authorize-phase sampling and admission: only an admitted request is buffered, and one owned copy of the finalized body per selected instance — not a buffer shared with the primary request — is charged against that instance's max_retained_request_body_bytes for each in-flight task. When false, or when percentage quantizes to 0, this instance declares no request-body capability at all.

max_in_flight.description: Maximum mirror tasks allowed concurrently. Requests that arrive while every permit is in use are still served normally but are not mirrored. Capped at 1048576 (2^20): a larger value is rejected at construction rather than panicking Tokio's semaphore.

max_retained_request_body_bytes.description: Aggregate retained request-body budget for in-flight mirrors on this plugin instance. Charged at pre-buffer admission as the full max_mirrored_request_body_bytes ceiling for every admitted request (declared Content-Length is never trusted for the charge; it is used only to skip already-oversized bodies before sampling) and reconciled to the observed body length, returning any surplus exactly once. Size this against max_in_flight times max_mirrored_request_body_bytes when mirroring at high concurrency. Exhaustion drops the new mirror attempt without affecting the primary request. Default is 64 MiB.

max_mirrored_request_body_bytes.description: Positive plugin-local ceiling on one mirrored request body, applied even when the global FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES is set to 0 (unlimited). Combined with the global limit by the proxy; the strictest positive value wins, and it applies only to requests this instance admitted for mirroring. An explicit value above max_retained_request_body_bytes is rejected at construction; when the key is omitted the default clamps down to max_retained_request_body_bytes instead of failing. Default is 10 MiB, matching the global default.

mirror_timeout_ms.description: Finite, ABSOLUTE mirror deadline in milliseconds covering every shared-client attempt, every retry delay between attempts, and the response-body drain. When omitted, uses the matched proxy backend_read_timeout_ms when positive, otherwise 60000. Always capped at 300000. A zero primary timeout never disables this deadline.

forward_sensitive_headers.description: Dangerous opt-in. When true, selected origin-bound credential headers may cross to the distinct mirror origin, but only exact names listed in forward_sensitive_header_allowlist. Construction is fail-closed: both fields are required together and the allowlist must be non-empty.

forward_sensitive_header_allowlist.description: Lowercased exact allowlist of denied sensitive header names to forward when forward_sensitive_headers is true. Each entry must be a valid HTTP header name (at most 256 bytes) that the deny-by-default policy actually strips (a built-in credential or a sensitive_header_patterns match); non-sensitive names are rejected at construction. At most 64 entries. Default (with forward_sensitive_headers false) strips every sensitive header.

sensitive_header_patterns.description: Additional lowercased substrings matched against the header name (case-insensitive; each at most 128 bytes, at most 64 entries) that extend the built-in deny-by-default credential set. A header whose lowercased name contains any pattern is stripped before the mirror origin unless it is on the exact-name forward_sensitive_header_allowlist. Covers HTTP headers and native gRPC metadata (gRPC metadata is carried as HTTP/2 headers). Default empty.

forward_sensitive_query.description: Dangerous opt-in. When true, selected origin-bound credential query parameter names may cross to the distinct mirror origin, but only exact percent-decoded names listed in forward_sensitive_query_allowlist. Construction is fail-closed: both fields are required together and the allowlist must be non-empty. Does not change the primary backend request-target.

forward_sensitive_query_allowlist.description: Lowercased exact allowlist of denied sensitive query parameter names to forward when forward_sensitive_query is true. Entries are visible ASCII without whitespace; brackets such as filter[key] are allowed, while % + = & ? # / @ ; are refused because entries match the decoded name. Each entry is matched against the fully percent-decoded (bounded staged decode) ASCII-lowercased name (at most 256 bytes) that the deny-by-default policy actually strips (a built-in credential or a sensitive_query_patterns match); non-sensitive names are rejected at construction. At most 64 entries. Default (with forward_sensitive_query false) strips every sensitive query pair.

sensitive_query_patterns.description: Additional lowercased substrings matched against each staged percent-decoded query parameter name (case-insensitive; each at most 128 bytes, at most 64 entries) that extend the built-in deny-by-default query credential set. A name whose decoded lowercased form contains any pattern is stripped from the mirror request-target unless it is on the exact-name forward_sensitive_query_allowlist. Default empty.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Cap on bytes drained from every mirror response when deriving its size (with or without Content-Length). Streaming is aborted as soon as the limit is crossed and the mirror task records the truncated/observed count. Bytes are discarded after measurement so HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pools can reclaim the socket. Must be a JSON integer literal: a whole-valued float such as 1.0 is rejected at construction. Default is 1 MiB.

RequestSizeLimitingConfig.description:
Plugin: request_size_limiting — Per-proxy request body size limits.
Rejects oversized requests with HTTP 413 in three places: an early
Content-Length fast path (`on_request_received`), a buffered-body
check when another plugin already loaded the body (`before_proxy`),
and a final post-transform check before forwarding to the backend
(`on_final_request_body`).
`max_bytes` is additionally published to the proxy core as the effective
streaming/buffering ceiling, so unbuffered H1/H2, H3, and streaming-gRPC
uploads (chunked or unknown-length) are bounded at this route limit
before any byte is forwarded or retained. The effective bound is the
strictest active (nonzero) value of this limit and
FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES; a global limit of 0 means unlimited
and does not disable an active route limit, and multiple instances
compose to their minimum.
Repeated identical Content-Length values (RFC 9110 §8.6, which arrive
comma-folded in plugin-facing header maps) are parsed per member and
compared against the limit. A declared length that cannot be reduced to
one agreed value fails closed with HTTP 400 and
`{"error":"Request Content-Length is ambiguous"}`.
The ceiling applies to every method: an HTTP/2 GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS
request carrying DATA without Content-Length is forwarded through the
size-limited adapter, not replaced by an empty backend body (residual:
an HTTPS backend with HTTP/2 enabled whose target is not yet
capability-classified can negotiate HTTP/1.1 via ALPN and send an
unknown-length GET/HEAD bodyless until classified; pool warmup,
FERRUM_POOL_WARMUP_ENABLED, classifies targets up front).
Every 413 for this policy, from any plugin hook or from the proxy core's
streaming overrun, carries the one shared body
`{"error":"Request body exceeds maximum size"}` without the limit. A
Content-Length or buffered-body refusal by the plugin records
`request_size_limiting.reason`, `request_size_limiting.instance` (the
plugin-config id), `request_size_limiting.limit_bytes`, and (except for
an ambiguous Content-Length) `request_size_limiting.observed_bytes` in
request metadata. A final-body refusal records them only when its hook
receives a request context, on any protocol: always on the native
HTTP/3 preparation and HTTP/3 bridge paths, and elsewhere only when
another plugin on the route requests the final-body context. A
streaming overrun refused by the proxy core records none of them.

max_bytes.description: Maximum allowed request body size in bytes. Required and must be a positive JSON integer — the gateway rejects plugin creation when it is missing or null, 0, negative, fractional or in exponent form (for example 1048576.0), or not a number (for example "1048576"), with a diagnostic naming that fault class.

RequestTerminationConfig.description: Plugin: request_termination — Returns a canned response without proxying to the backend. The response body and `content-type` are rendered once at construction time so the request hot path is allocation-light. Useful for maintenance windows, mocking, or path/header-based short-circuiting. Runs after CORS so browser preflight responses are still emitted correctly. HTTP-family only. Configuration must be an object; unknown top-level and trigger keys are rejected. Null/scalar/array configs and explicit null property values are rejected; omit optional properties to select their defaults. Native gRPC (`application/grpc` on H2/H3) is terminated as a mapped trailers-only error: HTTP 200, `content-type: application/grpc`, a nonzero `grpc-status` from the gateway HTTP-to-gRPC map, and no DATA body. A configured HTTP 2xx does not mock a successful RPC (`200` maps to INTERNAL / 13). `grpc-message` is derived from the canned body text, not returned as RPC DATA. gRPC-Web uses browser framing rather than the configured body. WebSocket support applies to the handshake only. The plugin runs in `on_request_received` at priority 125, before authentication, authorization, IP restriction, rate limiting, and the WAF, so a termination (including a configured 2xx mock) is served without authenticating the caller or counting against rate limits; use `response_mock` (a `before_proxy` plugin that runs after authentication) for authenticated mocking.

status_code.description: Final HTTP status code returned for ordinary HTTP. Must be an integer from 200 to 599, including JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 503.0); informational statuses (including 101) and out-of-range values are rejected at construction rather than coerced. Statuses 204, 205, and 304 force an empty body. A configured 2xx status never establishes a CONNECT/Extended CONNECT tunnel — those requests fail closed with 403. Native gRPC ignores this as a wire HTTP status and maps it to `grpc-status` under HTTP 200; 503 maps to UNAVAILABLE (14) and unmapped codes including 200 map to INTERNAL (13).

content_type.description: `Content-Type` header value for ordinary HTTP. Every character must be visible ASCII, space, or HTAB (runtime construction refuses obs-text and control bytes exactly as this schema does); surrounding spaces and tabs are trimmed and the result must be nonempty. The default-body renderer classifies the media subtype exactly as `json`/`xml` or an RFC 6838 structured suffix (`+json`/`+xml`) after stripping parameters — not by arbitrary substring match (so `application/notjson` is plain text). JSON types pass a valid JSON `message` through as the body and fail safe to the `{message,status_code}` envelope when it is not; XML and other types keep their envelope or plain-text renderers. Native gRPC responses overwrite this with `application/grpc`.

body.description: Explicit response body. When the field is present — including an explicit empty string — it is returned verbatim and `message` is ignored. Omitting the field selects the default renderer built from `message`. Must be empty or omitted for statuses 204, 205, and 304. Native gRPC does not send these bytes as RPC DATA.

message.description: Used to build the default body when `body` is omitted. JSON media types (`json` or `+json` after parameter stripping) emit a complete, unambiguous JSON `message` as the response body — the parsed value, compactly serialized, not string-escaped inside an envelope. Objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null all pass through this way. Malformed JSON, duplicate object member names, and other parser-ambiguous documents fail safe into the legacy `{"message":...,"status_code":...}` envelope so the response stays valid JSON and construction never panics. XML media types wrap the message in `<message>` (XML 1.0 character validation/escaping); other types emit `message` as plain text. JSON escaping of envelope string slots is applied automatically; XML-invalid control characters in `message` are rejected when XML rendering is selected.

headers.description: Extra response headers for the canned response, for example `Retry-After` on a 503 maintenance page or `Cache-Control: no-store` so downstream caches do not keep serving it. At most 32 entries. Names must be HTTP field-name tokens and are case-insensitive (two spellings of one name are rejected at construction); they are emitted lowercase. Values are visible ASCII with interior spaces/tabs, no leading or trailing whitespace, at most 4096 bytes. Refused names: protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing fields (`Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`); `Content-Type` (use `content_type`); credential and challenge fields (`Set-Cookie`, `Set-Cookie2`, `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `WWW-Authenticate`, `Authentication-Info`, `Proxy-Authentication-Info`); and gateway-owned fields (`X-Gateway-Error`, `X-Gateway-Upstream-Status`, and the `X-Ferrum-*` and `grpc-*` families). The fail-closed `403` for a 2xx CONNECT/Extended CONNECT termination does not carry these headers. Native gRPC still answers trailers-only with `content-type: application/grpc`.

trigger.description: Optional trigger condition. Without a trigger every request on the proxy is terminated (maintenance-mode default). Set only one of `path_prefix` or `header`; configuring both is rejected. Unknown nested keys are rejected. When `trigger` is present it must contain exactly `path_prefix`, or `header` with optional `header_value`; an empty trigger and a detached `header_value` are invalid.

path_prefix.description: Only terminate when the canonical request path starts with this prefix. Must start with `/`, or be exactly `*` to match the asterisk-form target of a server-wide `OPTIONS *` request (which only reaches the plugin on a route that matches that target, such as a host-only or regex route; prefix listen paths never match `*`), and contain no control characters (C0, DEL, or C1), query delimiter (`?`), fragment delimiter (`#`), literal space, `<`, `>`, or backtick; any other value can never match a parsed `Uri::path()`. Literal `"`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `|`, and UTF-8 are reachable and admitted. The prefix must also already be a canonical policy path: request paths are canonicalized at the frontend boundary (percent-escapes of characters that are legal literally in a path are decoded, and every other escape — separators, double encodings, control characters, invalid escapes, and escapes of bytes outside that decode set such as `%20` or `%7B` — is rejected with `400`, as are dot segments and backslashes in either spelling). No percent escape, literal `\`, or literal `.`/`..` segment can appear in a canonical path, so a prefix such as `/%61dmin`, `/api%2Fadmin`, `/api%20name`, `/api/../admin`, `/a?b`, `/api name`, or `/api\admin` is rejected at admission rather than silently never matching. A `.` inside a segment is fine. See `docs/request_path_canonicalization.md`. Mutually exclusive with `header`.

header.description: Only terminate when this request header is present on any raw field line (including non-UTF-8 values). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the result must be a nonempty HTTP field name (RFC 7230 token). The comparison is case-insensitive on the header name. Mutually exclusive with `path_prefix`.

header_value.description: Optional exact value for `header`. Empty (default) matches presence of any field line. A non-empty value must be a legal HTTP field value (no control character other than HTAB) and not only whitespace; surrounding spaces/tabs are trimmed. It matches when any individual field line's RFC 9110 field value (the line with surrounding spaces/tabs stripped, so HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 compare identically) equals it exactly — never against a comma-folded multi-line serialization.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write, creating intermediate objects as needed.
remove: delete the field.
rename: move old → new, with rollback if the destination is unreachable.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Dot-notation body path. Supports nested objects
('user.address.city'), array indexing via numeric segments
('items.0.name'), and backslash-escaped literal dots
('meta.weird\\.key'). Empty segments (an empty path, or a
leading, trailing, or doubled unescaped `.`) are rejected.
`rename` additionally rejects unescaped numeric segments here
and in `new_key`.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Accepts any JSON value — strings, numbers, booleans, objects,
arrays, and explicit null.
Strings that parse as JSON (e.g., "42", "true", '{"a":1}')
are inserted as the parsed type at runtime; otherwise kept
as a JSON string.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Array indices and empty dot-segments are rejected in a rename
`key` / `new_key`.

RequestTransformerConfig.description:
Plugin: request_transformer — Modifies request headers, query params,
and JSON body. Configuration is fail-closed: unknown top-level keys
and unknown per-rule keys are rejected at plugin load time. Header
and query rules enforce operation-exact fields (only add/update
accept `value`; only rename accepts `new_key`; remove accepts
neither). Every configured header `value` must be a valid HTTP
`HeaderValue` (same complete syntax accepted at H1/H2/H3 emission),
including rejection of CR/LF and other forbidden control bytes.
Unknown operations / targets and missing required fields are also
rejected. Every rule must set an explicit `target` (`header`,
`query`, or `body`); there is no default.

When `apply_route_overrides: true`, the plugin accepts an empty `rules`
array so it can participate in the chain-level route-header final
phase for per-rule transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch` onto
`RequestContext.route_override_request_transform`. Every enabled
instance applies only its static `rules` first; proxy core then applies
the matched route list exactly once after the last eligible instance —
route-level header writes win under multiple same-type instances and
priority overrides. The Istio VirtualService translator auto-emits a
proxy-scoped instance with `rules: []` + `apply_route_overrides: true`
on routes that carry `headers.request.{set,add,remove}` and have no
operator-configured `request_transformer`. That exact translator-owned
consumer — generated id, proxy scope and ownership, empty `rules`, and
`apply_route_overrides: true` — is ADDITIVE: a same-name global
transformer keeps its operator-authored header / query / body rules, so
a VS-translated route does not silently lose them and no shadowing
warning is emitted for it. An ordinary operator-configured proxy-scoped
instance keeps the normal proxy-replaces-global contract.

At least one of a non-empty `rules` array or `apply_route_overrides:
true` is required: a config with no effect is rejected at plugin load
time. Per-operation required and forbidden properties are modelled in
the target-specific rule schemas below. Operation-incompatible extras
are rejected by PRESENCE, so an explicit `null` fails exactly as a
string would; explicit `null` on an optional top-level field is
accepted and treated as absent.

apply_route_overrides.description:
When `true`, this instance accepts an empty `rules` array and
participates in the chain-level request route-header finalization
phase for transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch`. The plugin
declares `modifies_request_headers() == true` so the dispatcher
allocates a separate cloned header map for route-level writes
(preserving the gateway invariant that `ctx.headers` carries the
original inbound headers during `before_proxy`). Auto-emitted by the
Istio VirtualService translator. Explicit `null` is accepted and
treated as `false`.

runtime_overlay_scope.description: Optional RTDS boolean key controlling whether the transformer runs. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed at runtime. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent.

default_enabled.description: Fallback when `runtime_overlay_scope` is configured but the accepted RTDS overlay has no boolean value for that key. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent (so the `true` default applies).

runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled.description: Reserved, mesh-managed. Mesh slice preparation writes the accepted RTDS overlay's value for `runtime_overlay_scope` here, so the gate is validated, built, and published in the same request generation as the rules it gates (GHSA-83rc-23c9-3g9x). The plugin resolves one immutable decision at construction and every request phase reads it, so the gate is never re-evaluated mid-request. Ignored without `runtime_overlay_scope`, and rewritten authoritatively on every mesh apply — operators should not set it by hand; an explicitly authored value simply acts as a static pin outside mesh mode.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite). Note: this is
the historical Ferrum semantics, not Istio's "append to
multi-value" semantics — use `update` to overwrite.
update: write the header value.
remove: delete the header.
rename: move old → new header name.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
HTTP header name; must be a complete HTTP field-name token (the
same grammar `HeaderName` accepts). Add/update destinations and
rename destinations
reject gateway-owned names (case-insensitive, with `_` treated as
`-`, so `X_Forwarded_For` and `content_length` are refused too):
host, content-length,
connection, transfer-encoding, keep-alive, proxy-authorization,
proxy-connection, te, trailer, upgrade, expect, x-forwarded-for,
x-forwarded-proto, x-forwarded-host,
x-ferrum-original-content-encoding, and x-grpc-web-mode. They also
reject every name in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer
assertion namespace (including x-consumer-username and
x-consumer-custom-id) and in the router's `x-path-param-*`
route-capture namespace (either spelling); the error names the
rule.
Removal and rename sources remain allowed, except for the
gateway-owned x-ferrum-hops proxy hop count (either spelling):
every rule that names it, as key or new_key, is rejected.
Use preserve_host_header for Host or trusted-proxy configuration
for forwarding identity.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must be a valid HTTP HeaderValue (HTAB, visible ASCII, and
obs-text are accepted; CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are
rejected).
May reference up to 8 request variables, compiled at load time:
`$(consumer.username)`, `$(client_ip)`, `$(request_id)`,
`$(header.<name>)` and `$(query.<name>)` (both read from the
ORIGINAL client request, so a rename cannot relabel a
credential). `$$(` writes a literal `$(`; an unknown variable, an
unterminated `$(`, or a credential-bearing source name (the
built-in credential headers in any `_` / `-` spelling, or any
name the shared sensitive-name classifier flags: `*token*`,
`*secret*`, `password`, `api_key`, …) is rejected. When a
variable is unavailable for a request — or names a credential
location an auth plugin marked — or the resolved text is not a
valid HeaderValue, the rule is skipped for that request and
`request_transformer.rule_skipped` transaction metadata records
`template_unresolved` / `template_invalid_header_value`.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must be a complete HTTP field-name token and must not be a
gateway-owned destination listed under key.

operation.description:
add: append if the decoded name is absent (does not overwrite;
existing duplicates are left untouched).
update: rewrite every matching decoded-name pair's value, or
append when absent.
remove: delete every matching decoded-name pair.
rename: rename every matching pair, preserving value encoding
and key-without-equals shape; existing destination names stay.
Mutations apply to an ordered, duplicate-aware representation of
the retained raw query after authentication-owned credential
pairs (`auth.strip_query_param.*`) are removed from that input,
and are published as the outbound query for every primary
backend URL builder and request_mirror. The proxy still applies
a final strip pass as defense in depth. A rename/update of a
marked credential name therefore cannot relocate the secret.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Query parameter name matched after percent-decoding. Must not
contain CR or LF.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must not contain CR or LF. Authored onto the outbound query with
RFC 3986 percent-encoding (`%20` for spaces, never `+`). Accepts
the same `$(...)` request variables as a header `value`; the
resolved text is percent-encoded like any authored value.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must not contain CR or LF.

ResourceLabels.description: Informational operator metadata. Keys must be nonblank; keys and values cannot contain control characters. Runtime length limits are UTF-8 bytes (128 per key, 512 per value). Independent of target tags, routing, access control and api_spec_id. Omitted labels on resource PUT preserve the current map; an explicit map replaces it and {} clears it. Labels are retained in GET/list, backup/restore, file configuration and CP/DP sync. The provisioned-by label identifies the application that provisioned a resource; it is caller-supplied information, not proof of ownership. Resource labels landed on main in pull request 5483 on 2026-09-12, and every published release through v0.9.4 rejects the `labels` field with unknown field `labels`. v0.9.5 is the first tagged release with resource labels; operators and clients should use v0.9.5 or later.

ResponseCachingConfig.description: Plugin: response_caching — In-memory HTTP response caching. Cache keys are opaque SHA-256 digests over typed, length-framed fields: the effective post-routing destination (proxy, listen path, upstream or direct host/port/scheme, authority, rewritten path), the matched proxy's backend_path, strip_listen_path, and preserve_host_header (so a proxy-only reload that changes the assembled origin path or outbound Host cannot keep replaying the previous route through a retained global instance), the effective frontend scheme from private connection provenance (the proxy regenerates X-Forwarded-Proto from it, so an HTTPS representation is never replayed to plaintext or vice versa), the original authority, method, path, backend-effective outbound query, a mandatory caller-authorization partition (authentication mechanism, resolved identity/consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, and digests of every credential header presented — taken over both the pristine inbound wire header view and the live backend-visible one, so an earlier ai_stream_router credential rewrite cannot erase the original caller distinction; every caller also binds its canonical peer address, and only an anonymous caller's binding is relaxable per anonymous_caller_scope), and a digest of the complete configured/origin-selected Vary tuple including every name, presence flag, and value. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie are mandatory dimensions on every retained response, including anonymous responses, and are emitted in Vary so downstream shared caches cannot cross Ferrum's private caller partition. That Vary list is published on the MISS response itself, and on an honored request Cache-Control: no-cache refresh (X-Cache-Status: BYPASS, which stores its replacement under the same partition), as well as on later hits, so every freshly fetched publicly cacheable response a downstream cache stores already carries the same selection; an origin Vary: * is left untouched. No raw delimiter concatenation is used anywhere in key construction, so an attacker-supplied header or query value cannot forge a field boundary and collide two distinct requests onto one key. Keys are never logged. GET/HEAD lookup requires a private transport-owned proof that the complete H1/H2/H3 upload is empty; non-empty or unproven bodies bypass, and admission rejects deferred request-body transforms that could synthesize bytes after lookup. Honors Cache-Control freshness, upstream Age/Date (a comma-folded repeated Age uses its first member rather than resetting to zero), current Age generation on hits, ETag/Last-Modified revalidation (304, tolerating a bounded number of empty entity-tag list members), Vary, and never caches responses with Set-Cookie (matched case-insensitively, as is Content-Range). Retained entries are sanitized: connection-scoped and proxy-authentication fields (Connection and everything it nominates, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Authenticate, Proxy-Authorization, Proxy-Connection, TE, Trailer, Transfer-Encoding, Upgrade), every field the origin qualified with private="…" or no-cache="…", and every field the shared replay-sanitation policy also applied by ai_semantic_cache and request_deduplication classifies as per-response state (Set-Cookie/Set-Cookie2, WWW-Authenticate, response credentials, per-request trace and correlation identifiers such as traceparent, b3, x-b3-*, X-Request-Id, X-Correlation-Id, Retry-After, and every RateLimit/X-RateLimit/X-AI-RateLimit/Anthropic-RateLimit field) are dropped before storage, so no replay can emit them; the response that produced the miss is delivered untouched. Responses to requests carrying Authorization in either the pristine inbound or live backend-visible view are stored only with an explicit origin shared-cache opt-in (public, must-revalidate, or s-maxage). Partial (206) and validator-only (304) responses, and any response carrying Content-Range, are never stored as reusable representations. Gateway-generated transport failures are refused from typed backend-dispatch provenance on every HTTP version, so listing 502/504 in cacheable_status_codes retains genuine origin error pages without pinning a local connect/read failure over a recovered origin. Includes a bounded FIFO cacheability predictor (amortized O(1) admission, no full-map sort at capacity) that suppresses repeat cache lookups for variants known to be uncacheable. Unsafe-method invalidation is deferred until a non-error origin response (private provenance recorded before after_proxy hooks), is classified independently of cacheable_methods storage eligibility, skips served cache HITs that never contacted the origin, is confined to the same normalized/transformed Host/authority partition as lookup, and treats a slash-terminated mutated path (including the root) as its own descendant boundary so its children are invalidated too. Store-side staging (header delta, reduced snapshot, timing, lookup path, keys) is written only once a request is known to reach the origin (MISS or no-cache refresh), never on a HIT, REVALIDATED, PREDICTED-BYPASS, or request no-store. Lookup outcomes are exported as the bounded ferrum_response_cache_lookups_total{status} counter (hit, miss, bypass, revalidated, predicted_bypass; never a key, path, host, or caller label). Multiple instances on one proxy namespace request staging metadata under response_caching.<instance_id>.* so differing query/consumer/Vary/method/SSE/status policies remain independent across priority order and reload generations. Unknown top-level keys are rejected with path-qualified diagnostics and spelling suggestions so misspelled Vary, consumer, query, Cache-Control, status/method, capacity, or invalidation fields cannot silently weaken isolation or retention. HTTP only.

ttl_seconds.description: Fallback freshness lifetime in seconds when the backend response has no s-maxage, max-age, or Expires, or when respect_cache_control is explicitly false. Must be an unsigned 64-bit integer: a negative value or one above 18446744073709551615 is rejected at admission. With the default true policy, precedence is s-maxage > max-age > Expires minus Date > ttl_seconds; missing Date uses response receipt time. Invalid or repeated Expires, or invalid/repeated Date for Expires-based freshness, means already expired. Upstream Age, Date, response delay, and cache residency still reduce remaining freshness.

max_entries.description: Maximum number of cached entries, 1 to 10000000. Overflow is evicted oldest-first from an insertion-ordered queue in amortized O(1) per admitted entry — no full-map clone or sort is performed while the accounting mutex is held. A value above the ceiling is rejected at admission.

max_entry_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of a single cached response body (1 MiB by default). Larger responses are not cached. Must be greater than zero.

max_total_size_bytes.description: Maximum accounted retained in-memory response-entry footprint across all entries (100 MiB by default). Concurrent stores and replacements are admitted atomically. When the byte cap is the limiting dimension, every expired entry is reclaimed in expiration order through an ordered index; fresh entries are never evicted to admit a new representation, and the store is refused if it still does not fit. Reclamation cost is bounded by entries actually retired rather than by cache size. An entry larger than the cap alone is never cached. Must be greater than zero.

cacheable_methods.description: HTTP methods eligible for caching (uppercased before use, so any letter casing of the two accepted tokens is admitted). Must contain at least one entry, and every entry must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP method token that is also a bodyless retrieval method — only GET and HEAD are accepted; every other method token, including POST and OPTIONS, is rejected at admission. A body-bearing method is rejected at admission because cache lookup runs in before_proxy, ahead of on_final_request_body, so the exact backend-visible request body cannot be bound into the key. At runtime the transport must observe the complete H1/H2/H3 upload and privately prove it is empty before lookup; a non-empty or unproven body, any Transfer-Encoding, or a non-zero/unparsable Content-Length bypasses lookup and storage.

cacheable_status_codes.description: Response status codes eligible for caching. Must contain at least one entry, and every entry must be a final status between 200 and 599 whose caching semantics the plugin implements. 1xx (interim), 206 (partial content — requires Range/Content-Range, strong-validator, completeness, and request-applicability tracking), 304 (validator metadata that freshens an existing stored representation rather than a representation of its own), and 401/407 (only valid with an authentication challenge that a shared cache cannot retain: WWW-Authenticate is per-response state under the shared replay-sanitation policy and Proxy-Authenticate is hop-scoped, so a stored copy would replay a challenge-less 401/407) are rejected at admission and refused again at store time, so a caller cannot poison the shared cache with a truncated, validator-only, or challenge-less entry. A 2xx response carrying Content-Range is likewise never stored.

respect_cache_control.description: Honor backend Cache-Control directives (no-store, private, no-cache, max-age, s-maxage, must-revalidate, public) and explicit Expires freshness. Setting false ignores the origin's Cache-Control entirely, not only its lifetimes: freshness comes from ttl_seconds instead of Cache-Control and Expires (age accounting still applies), and the origin's storage prohibitions are ignored too — a response marked no-store, private, or no-cache is stored, and fields it qualified with private="…" or no-cache="…" are retained (still only within the mandatory caller partition). Conversely, because public, must-revalidate, and s-maxage are also ignored, a response to an Authorization-bearing request can never satisfy the shared-cache opt-in and is never stored. Parsing is grammar-aware: the qualified field-name forms private="x-account" and no-cache="x-secret" are understood, and the named fields are removed from the retained entry so they are never replayed from the shared cache. A qualified argument that is not a well-formed quoted field-name list (unquoted, unterminated, empty, or not a valid field name) fails closed to the bare directive and the whole response is refused. Duplicate max-age/s-maxage keep the most restrictive value; malformed lifetime directives contribute zero.

respect_no_cache.description: Honor client request Cache-Control. no-cache bypasses lookup and refreshes the entry (the replacement is stored under the same partition and carries the downstream Vary contract); no-store bypasses lookup and stores nothing. A request max-age is enforced against the stored entry's current age, and a request min-fresh against its remaining freshness (RFC 9111 §5.2.1), so an entry the client would not accept is refetched rather than served — a request max-age=0 always refetches. When false, the whole request Cache-Control value is a bound key dimension and none of these directives is acted on.

vary_by_headers.description: Additional request header names (lowercased) to include in the cache key even when the backend does not send Vary. Merged with any backend Vary response header, with the dimensions already published for the base key, and with the mandatory authorization/cookie/proxy-authorization names; the merged list is emitted on the MISS response as well as on later hits. Every entry must be a valid RFC 9110 HTTP field-name token.

ignore_request_headers.description: Operator attestation that these request headers never select the origin's response (for example a per-request X-Request-Id stamped by an upstream CDN or load balancer), so they must not fragment the cache. Each named header is removed from the request in before_proxy, before the cache key is derived, and is therefore never sent to the origin either — the key still binds every header the origin actually receives, so this relaxes hit rate without opening an unbound dimension. Matching is case-insensitive and applies to every request this instance handles. Names are rejected at admission when they are not valid RFC 9110 field-name tokens, when they are also listed in vary_by_headers, when they name a credential or session header (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, the built-in credential headers, or anything the log-redaction rules classify as sensitive), a gateway-owned header the proxy re-asserts on the backend request after lookup (X-Ferrum-Hops and the rest of the X-Ferrum-* namespace, X-Consumer-*, X-Authenticated-Identity, X-Geo-Country, X-Path-Param-*), Host or a hop-by-hop field, Cache-Control, Pragma, Range, Max-Forwards, any If-* precondition, any Content-* field, Expect, Accept, Accept-Encoding, or proxy-owned forwarding identity (any X-Forwarded-* field, Forwarded, X-Real-IP, Via). Family refusals are prefix matches, and these admission refusals are ASCII case-insensitive with _ treated as - (for example, keep_alive, proxy_connection, and transfer_encoding are refused). Stripping a named header and the vary_by_headers overlap check use exact field-name matching (ASCII case-insensitive only), so x_cdn_hop does not remove X-Cdn-Hop. A non-empty list makes this instance a request-header mutator at its priority, so it cannot share a proxy with request_deduplication, which refuses any later header mutator. The operator must also ensure no later plugin derives the response from an ignored header.

anonymous_caller_scope.description: How anonymous callers (no gateway identity, no credential header, no peer SPIFFE identity) are partitioned. The value is trimmed and ASCII-lowercased before it is matched, and caller-address is an accepted alias of caller_address, so caller_address, caller-address, and shared are admitted in any letter casing and with surrounding whitespace. caller_address (default) binds the gateway-resolved canonical peer address, which the origin observes through Ferrum's regenerated X-Forwarded-For; a request whose canonical address cannot be parsed bypasses the cache entirely rather than being keyed incompletely. shared is an explicit operator attestation that the origin does not vary its response by caller address on this route and lets anonymous callers share one retained representation — only set it when that is known-safe, because it re-opens cross-caller replay for address-sensitive origins. It applies to anonymous callers only: an authenticated caller always binds its canonical peer address, because the backend receives Ferrum's regenerated forwarding identity for that caller too and may vary policy or content by it.

add_cache_status_header.description: Add X-Cache-Status (MISS, HIT, BYPASS, REVALIDATED, PREDICTED-BYPASS) to downstream responses. Cache hits also emit a current Age header. Publication of the downstream Vary contract on a MISS or no-cache refresh is independent of this flag.

invalidate_on_unsafe_methods.description: After a non-error origin response (status < 400) to an unsafe method (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and extension/custom methods, which fail closed as unsafe), invalidate cached entries for the matched path (and descendants under the same path prefix) within the same matched-proxy and normalized/transformed Host/authority partition used by cache lookup. The descendant boundary is the mutated path plus exactly one / separator, so a path that already ends in / — including the root / — is its own boundary and its children are invalidated as well. Invalidation is an indexed exact lookup plus one ordered range over the mutated path's descendants, so its cost is bounded by the entries it removes rather than by cache size. Method safety is independent of cacheable_methods: an unsafe method listed there still invalidates after an origin MISS and non-error response; a served cache HIT that never contacted the origin does not. Safe methods outside cacheable_methods (OPTIONS, or HEAD under a GET-only set) bypass without invalidating. Error responses, transport failures, and gateway-only synthetics do not invalidate. Invalidation uses private origin-status provenance recorded before after_proxy hooks, so an earlier response hook that replaces the client-visible response cannot suppress eviction after a successful mutation.

ResponseMockConfig.description: Plugin: response_mock — Returns mock responses for API testing before backends are ready. Rule paths are relative to a prefix listen_path with trailing slashes trimmed before stripping; exact (`=`), regex (`~`), root (`/`), and host-only scopes match the full request path. Rules are evaluated in order (first match wins); an optional per-rule `match` adds exact request header / query parameter conditions. Supports HTTP and WebSocket upgrade handshakes only: a match short-circuits only the HTTP handshake response and does not establish or mock an upgraded WebSocket frame stream, so a 2xx rule that matches a WebSocket handshake fails closed with 500 on every frontend (H1/H2/H3). Native gRPC (`application/grpc` on H2/H3) is unsupported — the plugin is not selected for that protocol because Reject results normalize to trailers-only gRPC errors that discard configured bodies. Unknown top-level and per-rule keys are rejected. The free-form headers map accepts string-valued response headers but rejects protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing names (`Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Content-Length`, including case variants); the gateway derives Content-Length from the mock body/status/method and strips connection/framing fields at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary. Status codes must be final (200–599); informational statuses, including 101, are rejected. `delay_ms` runs under the shared fault-delay bounds (one-minute ceiling, FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_FAULT_DELAYS budget, shutdown and HTTP/3 peer cancellation). HEAD omits content bytes while keeping representation Content-Length; 204/205/304 omit body and Content-Length on every frontend (H1/H2/H3). Runtime construction and request-flavor enforcement are the authoritative final boundaries. Size limits apply independently per rule and field; there is no aggregate instance memory budget. For example, 1024 rules can retain 256 MiB of body payload alone, plus headers, conditions, regexes, and other overhead. Runtime string limits count UTF-8 bytes; maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard.

rules.description: Mock rules evaluated in order (first match wins)

method.description: HTTP method token to match (omit or null to match all methods). When supplied it must be a non-empty HTTP method token (runtime validates via http::Method). Registered standard methods are matched case-insensitively (get matches GET); extension methods are case-sensitive per RFC 9110 section 9.1 and match the configured spelling exactly.

path.description: Non-empty rule path. Relative to a prefix listen_path (e.g., /users for listen_path /api/v1). For exact (`=`), regex (`~`), root (`/`), and host-only proxies, use the full request path. Regex rule paths use a ~ prefix (auto-anchored). Full Rust regex compilation remains a runtime-only check.

match.description: Optional extra request conditions; every listed condition must hold. A rule whose conditions do not hold is skipped and evaluation continues with the next rule. Omitted or null adds no conditions.

additionalProperties.description: At most 8192 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

headers.description: 1–16 header name → exact value pairs. Matches when every named header is present on the client-sent request with a field line byte-for-byte equal to the value (names case-insensitive and unique ignoring case, values case-sensitive). Gateway-asserted names (`x-consumer-*`, the private GeoIP header, path-param headers) are rejected. Values must be valid HTTP header values of at most 8192 bytes and are redacted in non-admin config projections. Reads pristine client field lines, so earlier header additions, rewrites, and removals do not affect matching.

propertyNames.description: 1–256 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

additionalProperties.description: At most 8192 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative.

query_params.description: 1–16 query parameter name → exact value pairs, compared against the current percent-decoded query map (last occurrence wins; a bare `?flag` has the value ""). Unlike match.headers, earlier query additions, rewrites, and removals affect matching. At default priorities, request_transformer (3000) runs before response_mock (3030); priority overrides can change which rewrites have run at evaluation. Names are 1–256 UTF-8 bytes, values at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Values are redacted in non-admin config projections.

status_code.description: HTTP status code to return (default 200). Must be a final status 200–599. Informational statuses (100–199, including 101) and values outside 100–599 are rejected at construction rather than coerced: a mock never upgrades the connection, and HTTP/2 / HTTP/3 cannot carry 101. A 2xx rule that matches a WebSocket handshake fails closed with status 500 on every frontend instead of claiming an established WebSocket. Omitted or null selects 200.

headers.description: Response headers (default content-type application/json), at most 64 entries with values of at most 8192 bytes. Omitted or null selects that default. Names must be HTTP field-name tokens. Protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing names (`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`) are rejected at construction, including case variants. Values must be valid HTTP header values (HTAB and printable ASCII).

body.description: Response body string (default empty), at most 262144 UTF-8 bytes at runtime. maxLength counts Unicode characters and is only a coarse schema guard; runtime byte validation is authoritative, so a multibyte body can be refused below maxLength. Omitted or null selects empty. On the wire, HEAD responses omit content bytes while keeping representation Content-Length. Statuses 204, 205, and 304 omit both the body and Content-Length even when this field is non-empty. Shared synthetic-response finalization keeps H1, H2, and H3 aligned.

delay_ms.description: Simulated latency in milliseconds (default 0). Omitted or null selects 0. Must be an unsigned integer 0–60000 (1 minute, the shared fault-delay ceiling); negative values and values above the cap are rejected at config validation. The delay counts against the process-wide FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_FAULT_DELAYS budget (shared with fault_injection): an exhausted budget or gateway shutdown serves the mock immediately, and a client that is gone (HTTP/3 connection close) ends the delay with 499. A non-completing delay records `fault_delay_outcome`.

passthrough_on_no_match.description: If true, unmatched requests (including WebSocket upgrades) continue to the backend. If false (default), returns 404. Omitted or null selects false.

ResponseSizeLimitingConfig.description:
Plugin: response_size_limiting — Per-proxy response body size limits.
Rejects oversized responses with HTTP 502 either via Content-Length
fast path (`after_proxy`) or after final buffering when
`require_buffered_check: true` is set (`on_final_response_body`).
`max_bytes` is additionally published to the proxy core as the effective
collection/streaming ceiling across H1/H2, H3, gRPC, retries,
coalescing, mesh mTLS, and HBONE: buffered collection aborts at this
route ceiling rather than retaining up to the larger global allowance,
and unknown-length streaming paths engage the frame-by-frame
`SizeLimitedStreamingResponse` adapter at this ceiling (known-length
paths reject an over-limit declaration before forwarding). Already-buffered
synthetic responses (mock, serverless, cache, federation, dedup replay)
are checked against the ceiling even when no plugin activated the
response body-hook gate, after any body transform. The effective bound
is the strictest active (nonzero) value of this limit and
FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES; a global limit of 0 means unlimited
and does not disable an active route limit, and multiple instances
compose to their minimum. It also bounds the buffered-representation
decode gate and compression admission.
Response-transformer output above this ceiling is a deterministic
gateway policy refusal: HTTP 502 with the Response body too large JSON error and limit,
X-Gateway-Error: overload, and error_class: dispatch_policy_rejected.
It emits one bounded warning. Oversized backend bodies retain backend
attribution; actual aggregate-buffer exhaustion remains HTTP 503.
Repeated identical Content-Length values are parsed per comma-folded
member and compared against the limit; a declared length that cannot be
reduced to one agreed value fails closed with HTTP 502. Bodyless
semantics (HEAD, 1xx, 204/205/304) are exempt from both checks.
Streaming rewrites are charged on the client-visible bytes: response
stream inspectors (every Forward, Terminate payload, and end-of-stream
flush), incremental gRPC-Web translation (base64 text expansion and the
generated trailer frame), and the gateway-generated mcp_gateway
aggregate SSE listener (greeting, events, keepalives) cannot deliver
more than the effective ceiling; the crossing frame is withheld and the
committed stream ends with a ResponseBodyTooLarge abort/reset.
Unknown keys and non-object configs are rejected. Explicit null
members are rejected; omitted keys keep defaults.

max_bytes.description: Maximum allowed response body size in bytes. Required and must be greater than zero — the gateway rejects plugin creation when missing or 0.

require_buffered_check.description: Force route-bounded whole-body buffering so the complete final post-transform size is proven before response headers are committed. Unknown-length streams are already bounded frame by frame when this is false. Enabling it adds memory overhead and rejects indefinite SSE streams whose complete size cannot be proven, including the gateway-generated mcp_gateway aggregate SSE listener (HTTP 502 before commit). An event stream whose backend declared one exact Content-Length within max_bytes (agreeing repeated members count as one), matching the pristine backend response, has proven its size and is admitted when no streaming response inspector on the route (for example an sse retry_ms prefix or an ai_* stream inspector) can rewrite its bytes.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write, creating intermediate objects as needed.
remove: delete the field.
rename: move old → new, with rollback if the destination is unreachable.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Dot-notation body path. Supports nested objects, array indexing
('items.0'), and backslash-escaped literal dots. Empty segments
(an empty path, or a leading, trailing, or doubled unescaped `.`)
are rejected. `rename` additionally rejects unescaped numeric
segments here and in `new_key`.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Accepts any JSON value — strings, numbers, booleans, objects,
arrays, and explicit null. Strings that parse as JSON
(e.g., "42", "true", '{"a":1}') are inserted as the parsed
type at runtime; otherwise kept as a JSON string.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Array indices and empty dot-segments are rejected in a rename
`key` / `new_key`.

ResponseTransformerConfig.description:
Plugin: response_transformer — Modifies response headers and JSON
body. Configuration is fail-closed: unknown top-level keys and
unknown per-rule keys are rejected at plugin load time. Header
rules enforce operation-exact fields (only add/update accept
`value`; only rename accepts `new_key`; remove accepts neither).
Protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing destinations are rejected
for add/update and as rename destinations (`Connection`,
`Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`,
`Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Content-Length`,
case-insensitive); remove of those names remains allowed. The
gateway derives Content-Length and strips connection/framing
fields at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary after every
mutable hook. Every configured header `value` must be a valid
HTTP `HeaderValue` (same complete syntax accepted at emission),
including rejection of non-CR/LF forbidden control bytes. Unknown
operations / targets and missing required fields are also
rejected. Every rule must set an explicit `target` (`header` or
`body`); there is no default. Valid targets are `header` and
`body` only — unlike request_transformer, there is no `query`
target.

Body-rule output above the effective response ceiling is refused with
HTTP 502 and the Response body too large JSON error with numeric limit, X-Gateway-Error:
overload, and error_class: dispatch_policy_rejected. One warning names
proxy id, plugin, ceiling, and the produced-size lower bound at the first
refused serializer write; no payload is logged. Exactly-at-ceiling
output passes. Aggregate retained-buffer exhaustion remains HTTP 503.

When `apply_route_overrides: true`, the plugin accepts an empty `rules`
array so it can participate in the chain-level response route-header
final phase for transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch` onto
`RequestContext.route_override_response_transform`. Every enabled
instance applies only its static rules first; proxy core then applies
the matched route list exactly once after the last eligible instance.
The same composition contract as `request_transformer` applies on the
response side: the exact translator-owned empty-rule consumer is
ADDITIVE to a same-name global transformer (no shadowing, no warning),
while an ordinary operator-configured proxy-scoped instance replaces the
global.

At least one of a non-empty `rules` array or `apply_route_overrides:
true` is required: a config with no effect is rejected at plugin load
time. Per-operation required and forbidden properties are modelled in
the target-specific rule schemas below, by PRESENCE — an explicit `null`
fails exactly as a string would. Explicit `null` on an optional
top-level field is accepted and treated as absent.

apply_route_overrides.description:
Counterpart to `request_transformer.apply_route_overrides` for
response headers: accept empty `rules` and remain eligible for the
chain-level route-header finalization phase. Auto-emitted by the
Istio VirtualService translator on routes carrying
`headers.response.{set,add,remove}` that have no operator-configured
`response_transformer`, and by the Gateway API translator on rules
carrying `ResponseHeaderModifier`. With no
static `rules`, the instance's fail-closed response-trailer policy
applies only to requests whose matched `mesh_route_dispatch` rule
published a `response_transform`, so other requests on the same
proxy keep their backend trailers; any static rule makes that policy
apply to every response. Such a rules-free instance cannot carry a
per-instance `trigger`. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as
`false`.

runtime_overlay_scope.description: Optional RTDS boolean key controlling whether the transformer runs. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed at runtime. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent.

default_enabled.description: Fallback when `runtime_overlay_scope` is configured but the accepted RTDS overlay has no boolean value for that key. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent (so the `true` default applies).

runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled.description: Reserved, mesh-managed. Counterpart to `RequestTransformerConfig.runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled`. Binding the gate to the generation is what keeps this plugin's buffering preflight and its later header/body hooks in agreement: a gate that moved between those phases could otherwise stream a response that had already been header-marked as transformed (GHSA-83rc-23c9-3g9x).

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write the header value.
remove: delete the header.
rename: move old → new header name. Set-Cookie is rejected as
either source or destination (case-insensitive), regardless of
cookie count, because its multi-value representation is name-bound.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
HTTP header name; must be a complete HTTP field-name token (the same
grammar `HeaderName` accepts). For add/update, must not be a
protocol-managed
hop-by-hop or framing destination (`connection`, `content-length`,
`keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`,
`trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`). Remove may target
those names. `rename` additionally rejects `set-cookie` as source.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must be a valid HTTP HeaderValue (HTAB, visible ASCII, and
obs-text are accepted; CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are
rejected).

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must be a complete HTTP field-name token, must not be `set-cookie`,
and must not be a protocol-managed hop-by-hop or framing destination
(`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`,
`proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`,
`transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`).

SecurityHeadersConfig.description: Plugin: security_headers — Injects validated response security headers (secure defaults) and strips fingerprinting headers at the client-visible initial-header boundary, including buffered gRPC/gRPC-Web and WebSocket handshakes. Unknown configuration keys are rejected, `config` must be an object, and `set` and `remove` reject gateway-owned destinations: protocol-managed hop-by-hop / framing fields and representation metadata (`content-type`, `content-encoding`, `content-range`). `set` holds at most 64 entries, `remove` at most 64 names, and every configured value at most 8192 bytes. With `override_existing: false`, a backend copy of a built-in security header that browsers ignore entirely (empty or ineffective) is replaced rather than preserved; values browsers act on are kept. An effective policy that sets and removes nothing is rejected.

content_type_options.description: X-Content-Type-Options. true = nosniff (default); a string must be `nosniff` (ASCII case-insensitive, optional surrounding spaces/tabs); false/null/"" disables.

frame_options.description: X-Frame-Options. Default SAMEORIGIN; a string must be `DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN` (ASCII case-insensitive, optional surrounding spaces/tabs), because browsers ignore any other value; false/null/"" disables.

referrer_policy.description: Referrer-Policy. Default strict-origin-when-cross-origin; a string must be a comma-separated list of Referrer-Policy tokens (no-referrer, no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin, origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin, strict-origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, unsafe-url; ASCII case-insensitive); false/null/"" disables.

hsts.description: Strict-Transport-Security (opt-in). true = max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; a string is used verbatim and must use the admitted subset of RFC 6797: exactly one `max-age=<delta-seconds>` directive (optionally quoted), at most one valueless `includeSubDomains`, and `;`-separated token directives with an optional token or quoted value (configured quoted values may not contain `"`, `\`, or `;`); directive names are ASCII case-insensitive; false/null/"" disables; an object {max_age, include_subdomains, preload} builds the value. Object members accept JSON null as the documented default: max_age 31536000 (unsigned 64-bit integer), include_subdomains true, preload false.

set.description: Arbitrary response headers to set (name -> value), at most 64 entries. An entry for X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security (case-insensitive name) must carry a value the matching built-in option accepts (`nosniff`; `DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN`; a comma-separated list of Referrer-Policy tokens; an HSTS value with exactly one `max-age`), since browsers ignore any other value; an empty value is rejected. Names accept the complete HTTP field-name token grammar, are limited to 65,535 ASCII bytes, and are canonicalized to lowercase, EXCEPT protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing destinations (`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`, case-insensitive) and representation metadata (`content-type`, `content-encoding`, `content-range`), which are rejected at construction — the gateway owns framing at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary, where it derives Content-Length from the final body, preserves a valid representation length only for HEAD, and removes it on ordinary streamed responses; content-type-selective body inspection, compression, and range handling decide from the backend representation before this plugin runs. Values must satisfy the HTTP HeaderValue builder rules (only HTAB and printable ASCII) and are at most 8192 bytes.

remove.description: Valid HTTP field names (maximum 65,535 ASCII bytes, at most 64 names) to strip case-insensitively. Names are canonicalized to lowercase. Protocol-managed hop-by-hop / framing destinations and representation metadata (`content-type`, `content-encoding`, `content-range`) are rejected, the same closed set `set` refuses. Defaults to Server and X-Powered-By; set [] to strip nothing.

override_existing.description: When false, only add a header the backend did not already set. A backend copy of a built-in security header (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, Permissions-Policy) that browsers ignore entirely — empty, or ineffective under browser processing (a lone ALLOW-FROM/ALLOWALL, no known Referrer-Policy token, first X-Content-Type-Options value not nosniff, HSTS without exactly one valid max-age) — counts as missing and every case variant is replaced; any value a browser acts on (for example DENY, SAMEORIGIN or no-referrer, future-policy) is kept even when it differs from the configured default. STS/nosniff case variants collapse to one effective backend copy under the lowercase name; if several are effective, the bytewise first header-name spelling wins because the map has no wire order. X-Frame-Options is classified across all spellings together, preserving jointly effective sets such as ALLOWALL plus an unknown value. Other built-in headers keep all spellings when any copy is effective. Backend HSTS classification splits only at unquoted semicolons and respects escaped characters in quoted extensions; extension text cannot supply or duplicate max-age. Arbitrary `set` headers keep pure presence semantics. Null selects true.

ServerlessFunctionConfig.description:
Plugin: serverless_function — Invokes AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, or
Google Cloud Functions as middleware in the proxy pipeline. The function
is invoked in the finalized-request-egress phase, after request-body
transforms and after every final request-policy hook (WAF body rules,
OpenAPI request schema, body validation, the post-transform request-size
ceiling) has accepted the exact backend-visible body, so those policies
never reject only after the function was contacted. Backend admission,
circuit-breaker, or transport checks can still fail later. In
`pre_proxy` mode the function response can inject request headers and
metadata before the backend call. In `terminate` mode the function
response is returned directly to the client. Native gRPC terminate
requires a JSON contract with `grpc_status` plus optional
`message_base64` (raw protobuf bytes), `grpc_message`,
`status_details_base64`, and custom `trailers`; the gateway frames an
uncompressed unary DATA message and owns reserved terminal metadata.
The request is classified as native gRPC by the HTTP flavor the
frontend stamps at intake, not by a mutable effective content-type.
Every terminal trailer value is bounded by an 8 KiB wire-value
ceiling, measured after sanitization and after base64 or
percent-encoding, and the complete terminal metadata block —
`grpc-status`, `grpc-message`, `grpc-status-details-bin`, every
custom trailer, and `content-type` — is bounded by a separate 16 KiB
aggregate budget charged as name + value + 32 bytes per field, the
way HTTP/2 charges `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE` and HTTP/3 charges
`SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE`. Custom trailers are additionally
capped at 32 entries. `grpc_message` is authored as human-readable text
and emitted in the canonical percent-encoded `grpc-message` wire form
(uppercase hex for `%` and every byte outside the grammar's
unescaped range). Custom trailers use the gRPC Custom-Metadata name
alphabet and printable-ASCII value grammar; `-bin` values must be
standard base64 with or without padding. Names are case-insensitive,
so two `trailers` members differing only in case are rejected rather
than one silently overwriting the other. The raw function output is
also screened for duplicate JSON object member names before parsing —
byte-identical, escaped-equivalent, or nested inside `trailers` — so a
document whose terminal outcome depends on which parser reads it is
refused instead of resolved.
gRPC-Web terminate is rejected with 500. Streaming and compression
contract shapes fail closed. Malformed or oversized function output
fails closed without reflecting untrusted bodies. The validated
framed response enters the shared response-body policy lifecycle, so
configured gRPC response validators and limits still apply; if a body
policy or transform invalidates that authorized representation, the
response fails closed to a nonzero gRPC error rather than degrading to
an empty successful trailers-only reply. An over-limit raw function
response on a native gRPC terminate request is likewise a mandatory
rejection rather than a fall-through, even with `on_error: continue`.
The same representation is produced on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3:
the HTTP/3 finalized-request-egress rejection is written through the
context-aware writer, so the authored frame, the terminal metadata, and
an original gRPC-Web client's browser framing all survive that
boundary. The status-only shape carries
the same provenance: unchanged, it stays trailers-only and restores its
complete terminal metadata (grpc-status, optional grpc-message,
grpc-status-details-bin, and validated custom trailers) from the
validated contract rather than the reject header map, with an omitted
grpc-message emitted as omission rather than a synthesized reason; a
changed status or an unauthored body fails closed the same way and
discards every authored terminal key with it, and it can never
authorize DATA. Cloud credential
fields fall
back to well-known environment variables. Every recognized provider
field is validated whenever it is SUPPLIED, independently of which
provider the row selects: JSON type, the Lambda Invoke identifier
grammars, the HTTP field-value grammar for credential headers, and the
lexical URL contract. A well-typed, well-formed field belonging to an
inactive provider stays accepted, so changing `provider` later cannot
turn an already-admitted row into a constructor error. Terminate mode forwards
applicable end-to-end response headers, preserving repeated Set-Cookie
and list-valued Link while requiring Location, Content-Location, and
Refresh to remain singleton,
while stripping hop-by-hop, Connection-listed, transport-managed,
provider-control, and credential-bearing fields. URL-valued Location,
Content-Location, Refresh (url= and bare URI forms after semicolon,
comma, or ASCII-whitespace delay separators), and every Link target are removed
when a relative, absolute, encoded, or nested target exposes the
configured signed function path/query. Duplicate singleton URL-valued
fields fail closed instead of being comma-folded; repeated Link lines
are revalidated as the exact combined list returned downstream.
Complete signed paths match at
slash-delimited segment boundaries even with added prefix or descendant
segments, not inside arbitrary substrings. The complete slash-trimmed
signed path is also protected when copied exactly into either side of a
decoded query pair; longer scalar lookalikes remain observable. Both
non-empty components of every configured query pair are protected
credential scalars: a key
remains protected whether it is key-only (`?SIGNED_TOKEN=`) or paired
with a value (`?SIGNED_TOKEN=1`), and a non-empty value is protected
independently. Exact ASCII-case-insensitive URI scheme copies are also
governed. Leading and trailing slashes remain part of each scalar;
a slash-only scalar remains protected and makes ambiguous URL-path
surfaces fail closed. Each scalar remains protected if copied into
either side of another query pair or into decoded paths at URI-component
boundaries (including path-parameter/query delimiters), and decoded fragments are checked
directly at URI-component boundaries even when they are scalar rather
than URI-shaped. Query comparison
percent-decodes generic URI components but preserves literal `+` characters
instead of applying form-data space conversion. Inspection checks
explicit numeric authority ports before normalization can erase default
ports, and is bounded to 16 KiB per field, 32 Link targets, 32 embedded
path URI references, eight percent-decoding transforms, and two nested
URI-reference hops. URI userinfo, residual
encoding, malformed target syntax, malformed percent triplets,
percent-decoded non-UTF-8 bytes, budget overflow, or another structural
URI reference at the nesting boundary fails closed even for root
function destinations, while unrelated URL targets, non-URL
Refresh directives, quoted Link parameters, and scalar labels without
signed components remain observable.
Later body rewrites invalidate ranges, validators, integrity metadata,
and content-bound signatures while unmodified responses retain them;
206 Partial Content and 226 IM Used responses skip rewriting to preserve
range and delta semantics; transform-dependent header hooks also decline
them rather than relabelling untouched bytes. Inspection still runs,
and enforcing
redaction-dependent plugins reject governed content when those bytes
cannot be safely rewritten.
Proven pre-invocation payload-validation, unsupported-gRPC-Web,
DNS-policy,
and literal-IP-policy rejections release every acquired deduplication
owner after commit. Real remote 502 responses remain application
responses; uncertain post-invocation failures retain their protection.
Deduplicated terminal replays preserve the final status/body but use
sanitized headers: session/authentication fields, Retry-After,
trace/correlation fields, and rate-limit counters are not replayed. The
stored body is already finalized and bypasses ordinary presentation
transforms on replay while remaining subject to response inspection and
final-body validation. A current-policy redaction decision runs only its
required transform and fails closed with 502 if rewriting cannot
complete.
If request_deduplication is attached, every same-protocol instance must
have a strictly lower effective priority than terminate mode; candidate
admission rejects equal or reversed ordering before persistence. This
candidate check derives static serverless capabilities without resolving
CP-local cloud credentials; runtime construction still validates the
node-local credentials and environment fail closed. CP and admin
admission of the plugin config itself is shape-only for the same
reason: every supplied field is validated, while AWS/Azure/GCP
credentials that intentionally exist only on data planes are resolved
and enforced when the serving node builds its plugin cache. `validate`
therefore checks the shape of the row rather than whether the
validating node holds the credentials the row needs at serve time.
HEAD/204/205/304 bodies are empty. Automatic redirects are disabled;
pre_proxy accepts only 2xx as approval, while terminate may
intentionally return only final 2xx-5xx statuses (200-599).
Informational and out-of-range three-digit function statuses follow the
configured error path. For aws_lambda, every non-2xx Lambda Invoke API
status (throttling, access denied, a missing function, an oversized
payload, a service fault) is authored by the Lambda service rather than
by the function, so it is an invocation failure
(`lambda_service_error`) under `on_error` / `error_status_code` in
every mode, and the AWS error body is never returned.

provider.description: Cloud provider for the serverless function.

mode.description:
pre_proxy: invoke and inject headers/metadata, then continue.
terminate: invoke and return response to client (HTTP body
passthrough, or native-gRPC JSON unary contract).

function_url.description: HTTP(S) trigger URL without URL userinfo or a fragment.
