Required for azure_functions and gcp_cloud_functions; ignored for aws_lambda invocation (the URL is derived from region + function name), but still validated when supplied, whichever provider is selected. The lexical contract matches runtime admission: a non-empty host (a registered name, an IPv4 literal, or a bracketed IPv6 literal), an optional port of 0-65535, no URL userinfo, no fragment, and no raw ASCII whitespace or control character anywhere in the value. Path/query credentials are structurally redacted from diagnostics and non-admin/audit projections.

aws_region.description: AWS region (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, then AWS_REGION env vars. The default endpoint is partition-aware: cn-* regions derive lambda.<region>.amazonaws.com.cn and every other region derives lambda.<region>.amazonaws.com. The air-gapped ISO partitions and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud are not derived and require an explicit aws_endpoint_url. When the key id or secret resolves from the process environment, the region must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials).

aws_access_key_id.description: IAM access key (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID env var. The key id is interpolated into the SigV4 Authorization header, so the effective config or environment value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab); validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_secret_access_key.description: IAM secret key (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env var. A process-environment credential may only be signed for an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_function_name.description: Lambda function name, partial ARN, or full ARN (aws_lambda only), matching the Lambda Invoke API FunctionName grammar. Falls back to AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME env var; the environment value is held to the same grammar. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. Existence and invoke permission are not checked at admission.

aws_session_token.description: STS session token (aws_lambda only). Falls back to AWS_SESSION_TOKEN env var only when aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key also resolve from the environment; the environment token is never paired with a config key pair. Sent verbatim as x-amz-security-token, so the effective value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab). A process-environment token may only be sent to an official AWS Lambda endpoint (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). Not allowed with aws_credentials: default_chain.

aws_qualifier.description: Optional version/alias qualifier (e.g., $LATEST, prod), matching the Lambda Invoke API Qualifier grammar. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

aws_endpoint_url.description: Optional HTTP(S) Lambda endpoint override for LocalStack or a VPC-internal endpoint. Must be an origin without userinfo, path, query, or fragment, using the same lexical URL contract as `function_url` (non-empty host, port 0-65535, no raw whitespace or control characters). Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected. Falls back to `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL`. A non-default port is part of the signed SigV4 canonical `Host`, so a verifying endpoint accepts the invocation. When the AWS key id or secret resolves from the process environment, a configured override must be an official AWS Lambda endpoint unless `allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials` is true (see that field); an `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL` fallback is set by the same environment owner and is trusted like the environment credentials.

aws_credentials.description: aws_lambda only. `static` (default) signs with a literal key pair from the config or from the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) environment variables, resolved once when the plugin is built. `default_chain` signs with the gateway process's own AWS identity from the AWS SDK default credential chain — environment variables, shared config/credentials profiles, web identity (EKS IRSA), ECS container credentials, and EC2 instance metadata (IMDSv2) — cached and refreshed in the background before expiry, so temporary workload credentials keep working without a reload. A request waits (bounded) only when no usable credential is cached; expired credentials are never used, and an unavailable chain is an invocation failure (`aws_credentials_unavailable`) under `on_error`. `default_chain` may not be combined with aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key, or aws_session_token, and is subject to the same ambient endpoint scope as process-environment credentials (see allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_credentials). It requires a build with the `secrets-aws` (or `cloud-secrets`) Cargo feature: CP/admin shape-only admission accepts the row, and a serving node built without the feature refuses to construct it.

allow_custom_endpoint_with_ambient_crede.description: aws_lambda only. When `aws_access_key_id` or `aws_secret_access_key` is omitted from the config and resolves from the gateway process environment (`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` is then used too; it never completes a config key pair), or when `aws_credentials` is `default_chain`, `aws_region` must be a lowercase commercial, GovCloud, or China region, and the config-chosen Lambda endpoint (the host derived from `aws_region`, or the `aws_endpoint_url` override) must be an official AWS Lambda endpoint for that region over HTTPS on the default port: lambda[-fips].<region>.amazonaws.com, lambda[-fips].<region>.api.aws, or an interface VPC endpoint vpce-<id>[-<az>].lambda[-fips].<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com, where <region> is a commercial or GovCloud region; a cn-* region uses amazonaws.com.cn and the dual-stack api.amazonwebservices.com.cn instead. An `AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL` set in the environment (used only when the config sets no `aws_endpoint_url`) is trusted like the environment credentials. Anything else is refused at configuration admission (CP/admin shape-only admission screens a configured `aws_region` and `aws_endpoint_url` whenever the config omits the key pair), and every invocation re-checks the endpoint and fails closed with 500 (`ambient_credential_endpoint_refused`) regardless of `on_error`. Credentials written into the config are not scoped. Set true only to deliberately sign invocations for a private endpoint (for example LocalStack), an air-gapped ISO partition, or the AWS European Sovereign Cloud with the process credentials; anyone who can write this plugin config can then direct those credentials to that endpoint.

azure_function_key.description: Function key for x-functions-key auth (azure_functions only). Falls back to the FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_AZURE_FUNCTIONS_KEY env var (never the ambient AZURE_FUNCTIONS_KEY, because the key is sent to the config-chosen function_url). The value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab); the effective config or environment value is parsed at admission so an unusable credential never reaches the serving cache. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

gcp_bearer_token.description: Bearer token for Authorization header (gcp_cloud_functions only). Falls back to the FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_GCP_CLOUD_FUNCTIONS_BEARER_TOKEN env var (never the ambient GCP_CLOUD_FUNCTIONS_BEARER_TOKEN). The assembled `Bearer <token>` value must be representable as an HTTP field value (no NUL, CR, LF, or other control byte except horizontal tab) and is parsed at admission. Validated whenever supplied, whichever provider is selected.

payload_format.description: `ferrum` (default) sends the Ferrum invocation payload and uses the Ferrum response contracts. `aws_api_gateway_v2` (aws_lambda with mode terminate only) sends an API Gateway HTTP API proxy event, payload format 2.0 (`version`, `routeKey`, `rawPath`, `rawQueryString`, `cookies`, `headers`, `queryStringParameters`, `requestContext`, `body`, `isBase64Encoded`), built from the same finalized request view and the same fail-closed forward_headers / forward_query_params / forward_body selection, and maps the function result like an API Gateway proxy integration: a JSON object with `statusCode` (integer 200-599) is a structured response with optional `headers`, `multiValueHeaders`, `cookies` (one Set-Cookie each), `body`, and `isBase64Encoded`, with an identical name/value pair in `headers` and `multiValueHeaders` merged into one field line and at most 128 header field lines / 32 KiB of header names and values; a JSON string result is returned as the decoded string and any other JSON value as its JSON text, both with status 200 and content-type application/json. Mapped headers are sanitized like provider response headers. A duplicate-member or malformed result fails with `invalid_api_gateway_response` under `on_error`. Native gRPC terminate requests are refused before invocation with `unsupported_grpc_payload_format`.

forward_body.description: Include one authoritative lossless finalized request-body representation in the function payload for every HTTP method. Ferrum never parses JSON into a structured value: exact UTF-8 bytes are carried as a string with body_encoding=utf8, arbitrary bytes are base64 with body_encoding=base64, and the active hook Content-Type is carried separately as body_content_type. The plugin buffers before invocation and fails closed if bytes are unavailable or either the original or active request headers use a non-identity Content-Encoding. Because invocation occurs after request-body transforms and final request-policy acceptance, this plugin may share a protocol chain with a request-body transformer and observes the exact backend-visible bytes. Candidate admission and runtime cache construction retain the fail-closed composition refusal only for registered custom plugins that declare pre-finalization request-body egress.

forward_headers.description: Each entry must be a non-empty RFC 9110 HTTP field-name token (no empty string, spaces, or other separators), matching runtime admission. Header names to forward into the function payload (lowercased at config load). Values come from the finalized backend-visible header view (the function is invoked in the finalized-request-egress phase, after request-body transforms and every final request-policy hook), so a header an earlier plugin removed - authorization under strip_authorization_on_success, or a gateway-owned claim_headers destination with no verified claim - is omitted rather than re-read from the client's original request.

forward_query_params.description: Include decoded query parameters from the shared canonical backend-bound query view in the function payload, after omitting credentials that an earlier auth plugin marked for backend stripping. Behavior is identical on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 and includes any earlier ordered query transform. Duplicate decoded names (including percent-encoded aliases and bare/valued pairs), literal '+', an unencoded ';' ('%3B' is unambiguous), malformed percent-encoding, non-UTF-8 decodings, and parameters lacking their original encoded representation are rejected before invocation even when on_error=continue.

timeout_ms.description: Function invocation timeout in milliseconds, 1-900000 (15 minutes, the AWS Lambda synchronous invocation maximum). A larger value is rejected at admission.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Max function response body size (10 MiB default), 1-67108864 (64 MiB). The response is buffered whole, so this is the per-invocation retained-memory ceiling; a larger value is rejected at admission.

on_error.description: reject: return error to client. continue: skip and proxy normally.

error_status_code.description: Final HTTP error status when rejecting an invocation or pre_proxy non-2xx response. Must be in range 400-599.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// function_url or aws_endpoint_url whose host is not a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1]. The invocation payload and the provider credential (function key, bearer token, or SigV4 signature) then cross the network in clear. The AWS_LAMBDA_ENDPOINT_URL environment fallback is operator-controlled and is not screened. Omit for false; an explicit null is rejected like every other optional field.

SoapWsSecurityConfig.description: Plugin: soap_ws_security — Validates WS-Security headers in SOAP envelopes. Malformed XML returns HTTP 400 with a fixed parser category; document names, positions, and raw parser details are never returned or logged. A document type (or any other markup) declaration in the prolog is refused with 400; the same characters inside CDATA, comments, or character data are ordinary text, and a declaration after the prolog is malformed XML. Supports UsernameToken (PasswordText/PasswordDigest), X.509 signature verification, SAML 2.0 assertion validation, timestamp freshness, and nonce/assertion replay protection. Media types are parsed STRUCTURALLY (type/subtype plus parameters) and matched by exact essence, never substring-matched; content_type.mode defaults to 'strict', under which every request on the proxy is governed and a missing/unsupported/malformed representation is rejected (415/415/400) before backend dispatch, while 'mixed_route' is the explicit pass-through opt-out. Recognized representations are text/xml, application/soap+xml, application/xml, application/xop+xml, and MTOM/XOP multipart/related (root part validated, attachments never decoded). MTOM package framing is strict and line-anchored: delimiter lines only at body start or immediately after CRLF with exact CRLF framing, exactly one close-delimiter with a boundary-free epilogue, strict US-ASCII unfolded part headers with unique Content-Type/Content-ID/Content-Transfer-Encoding, package-unique nonblank Content-IDs, exactly one part matching `start`, and root selection only after the whole package is framed — every other shape fails closed under bounded part/header/candidate ceilings. Because Ferrum implements no WS-Security attachment-signature transform, an enabled x509_signature refuses both MTOM multipart/related and bare application/xop+xml with 415 (and an explicit content_type.allow_mtom=true alongside it is refused at admission); username_token and saml keep accepting MTOM/XOP because they authenticate identity and never claimed attachment integrity. Buffers governed bodies as raw bytes and decodes UTF-8 / UTF-16LE / UTF-16BE from BOM and Content-Type charset before validation; charset/BOM/XML-declaration conflicts and malformed encodings fail closed (415/400) without logging bodies. Original wire bytes are preserved for the backend. A configuration that establishes a principal (username_token, x509_signature, or saml) is an AUTH PLUGIN: it buffers the body before the authenticate phase, validates there, and publishes the SOAP principal as an EXTERNAL authenticated_identity (backend header X-Authenticated-Identity). It never sets identified_consumer: a same-named Consumer is not bound (issue #6082), so Consumer ACL groups and Consumer-specific policy do not apply and access_control admits a SOAP principal only through allow_authenticated_identity; identity-keyed rate limiting, logging, retries, and chargeback observe the one SOAP identity. require_mechanisms (default 'all') selects whether every enabled identity mechanism must be presented and verify, or ('any', at least two enabled) whether they are alternatives of which at least one must be presented and every presented one must verify. A timestamp-only configuration establishes no principal and keeps validating in before_proxy; the two phases never both run. Composition admission requires an identity-establishing instance to be the proxy's sole authentication mechanism in either auth mode, rejects it alongside compression decompress_request, and rejects an explicit content_type.allow_mtom=true alongside an enabled x509_signature; for that identity-establishing form on_final_request_body refuses to dispatch a message whose bytes changed after validation (a timestamp-only policy authenticates nobody, claims no integrity over the Body, and therefore does not bind the representation). Because an identity-establishing instance is the proxy's sole authentication mechanism, a request the SOAP policy passes through — a non-SOAP media type under mixed_route, or a governed envelope with no wsse:Security header under reject_missing_security_header=false — reaches the authentication chain with no identity and is answered 401 rather than forwarded anonymously; pair those options with a timestamp-only instance or separate the proxies. At least one security feature must be enabled. Every evaluated xsd:dateTime (Timestamp Created/Expires, PasswordDigest Created, SAML Conditions and SubjectConfirmationData bounds) must carry a Z or ±hh:mm zone designator; a zoneless value is rejected rather than read as UTC. Both signature paths settle TRUST FIRST: certificate fingerprint match (plus the matched certificate's notBefore/notAfter window) and SignatureValue-over-SignedInfo verify before any attacker-selected Reference is resolved, canonicalized, or digested. Duplicate Reference URIs are rejected, the X.509 Reference ceiling is 8, one bounded id index is built per message, and every canonicalization is charged against an aggregate per-message byte budget plus a separate namespace-resolution allowance charged scanned entries x compared prefix bytes plus the length of every compared namespace URI (32 x decoded body length, floor 4194304) so inherited namespace declarations, long prefixes, long inherited URIs, and canonical attribute ordering cannot multiply pre-verification CPU. Fixed raw-markup ceilings are enforced before parsing: a start tag with more than 64 attributes (namespace declarations included), an attribute name over 128 bytes, a namespace declaration name over 70 bytes, a namespace URI over 2048 bytes, more than 256 namespace declarations in scope at one element (scope tracked with nesting, so sibling redeclarations do not accumulate), more than 256 distinct (prefix, URI) bindings per envelope, or accumulated parser comparison work (duplicate-attribute, prefix-resolution, and inherited-scope merge) beyond 32 x envelope length (floor 1048576) is refused with 400. Structural selection is namespace-qualified and positional: one SOAP Envelope, at most one Header and exactly one Body as its direct children in the same envelope namespace, and one wsse:Security header targeting this receiver as a direct child of that Header; duplicates or misplaced elements fail closed. X.509 success additionally requires a Reference resolving uniquely to the backend-visible Body; References may resolve inside any block of the namespace-correct SOAP Header (the Security header or, e.g., WS-Addressing blocks) or the Body, never the Header element itself or anything outside them; and require_signed_timestamp rejects a missing Timestamp (pairing it with timestamp.require=false is refused at admission). SAML requires a mandatory bounded Conditions window, the configured service audience on every AudienceRestriction, no Conditions child other than AudienceRestriction and at most one each of OneTimeUse and ProxyRestriction, each in its standard shape (an xsi:type must resolve to that element's own standard SAML type, and no extension attribute or non-Audience child is admitted; an unsupported, derived, or extended condition makes the assertion indeterminate and is rejected, SAML Core 2.0 sections 2.5.1.1 and 7.1), exactly one qualifying SubjectConfirmation (a confirmation that does not name the configured recipient with its own bounded NotOnOrAfter and no InResponseTo is skipped, not fatal), exactly one namespace-correct nonblank Subject NameID resolved BEFORE the single-use claim (so an assertion that authenticates nobody fails closed with 401 without consuming replay state), and a single-use claim on the assertion id — so nonce.replay_scope is required when saml is enabled. Both signature paths apply Exclusive XML Canonicalization (xml-exc-c14n#) to SignedInfo and referenced elements, including InclusiveNamespaces PrefixList. Reference transform chains may contain the enveloped-signature transform followed by exclusive c14n; unsupported canonicalization or transform algorithms fail closed (inclusive c14n, comments, XPath, XSLT, and other XMLDSIG transforms are not supported). On a governed representation, malformed XML, unsupported/ambiguous envelope structure, and XML parsing-budget failures reject with 400 regardless of reject_missing_security_header, which governs an absent header only. Configuration admission is strict and fail-closed: the root object and every nested fixed-shape object reject unknown keys and wrong-typed values (including explicit JSON null — omit a field to use its default) before defaults apply, malformed credential / cert / issuer / algorithm entries are rejected rather than silently dropped, and every duration and cache control must fall inside its documented inclusive range. Invalid password_type and algorithm-enum diagnostics name only the field and accepted choices, never the rejected value. Fixed-shape properties are non-nullable in this schema. There is no nonce_replay_protection alias — nonce.* is the only canonical shape. Nonce replay entry/byte caps are exact under concurrent PasswordDigest claims. PasswordDigest additionally validates the UsernameToken's own wsu:Created against a bounded freshness window and binds it to the independently validated outer wsu:Timestamp, and requires an explicit nonce.replay_scope ('process' for a declared single-replica deployment, or 'shared' with sync_mode=redis for cross-replica atomic claims). A shared-backend outage fails closed, and every shared-replay connection must prove a non-evicting Redis memory policy (maxmemory 0 or maxmemory_policy noeviction) before it carries a claim. Every element value the gateway acts on is read once and returned UNCHANGED: only xsd:dateTime instants and xsd:base64Binary payloads are whitespace-collapsed, so a NameID, Issuer, Audience, Username, or PasswordText value with significant leading/trailing spaces is matched byte for byte against the bytes the signature covered and against configuration. Canonicalization charges the per-message work budget BEFORE each emitted run, so a refused canonical form is never fully allocated. username_token.remove_credential (default false) deletes the verified UsernameToken — or the whole wsse:Security header when it holds only the credential — from the backend-visible message; it is admitted only for an enabled PasswordText policy with no enabled x509_signature or saml and no explicit content_type.allow_mtom=true, its final-body proof binds the sanitized representation, and a signed envelope (400) or an unspliceable UTF-16/MTOM representation (415) is refused rather than forwarded with the credential intact. The schema's conditionals mirror those admission rules, so a configuration this component accepts is one the constructor accepts.

require_mechanisms.description:
How the enabled identity mechanisms (username_token,
x509_signature, saml) combine. 'all' (default): every enabled
mechanism must be presented and must verify. 'any':
WS-SecurityPolicy-style alternatives — a mechanism runs only when
its token is presented (a wsse:UsernameToken or message ds:Signature
as a direct child of the selected Security header, or a SAML
Assertion anywhere in the message); at least one enabled mechanism
must be presented (otherwise 401), and EVERY presented token must
verify, so a failing token rejects the message even beside a valid
one. 'any' requires at least two enabled identity mechanisms and is
refused at admission otherwise. The published principal is the first
verified mechanism in the order UsernameToken, X.509, SAML.

reject_missing_security_header.description:
Reject SOAP requests that lack a WS-Security header. This governs an
ABSENT HEADER ONLY. On a governed representation, malformed XML,
unsupported or ambiguous SOAP envelope structure (duplicate or
misplaced Envelope/Header/Body/Security), and XML parsing-budget
failures always reject with 400 regardless of this setting: a
gateway/backend parser disagreement must never become a
pass-through.

content_type.description:
Which requests this proxy governs. Media types are parsed
structurally (type/subtype plus RFC 9110 parameters) and matched by
exact essence; they are never substring-matched, so a
`multipart/form-data; boundary=application/xml` request is not SOAP
and a SOAP envelope labelled `application/octet-stream` is not
exempt. Recognized representations: text/xml (SOAP 1.1),
application/soap+xml (SOAP 1.2), application/xml,
application/xop+xml, and MTOM/XOP multipart/related whose `type`
parameter names a SOAP/XOP root essence.

mode.description:
'strict' (default) governs every request on this proxy: a
missing Content-Type returns 415, an unsupported media type
returns 415, and a malformed one returns 400 — all before
backend dispatch. 'mixed_route' is the explicit opt-out that
passes non-SOAP media types through the SOAP policy; a
malformed media-type label still fails closed in that mode
because an unparsable
label cannot be proven non-SOAP. With an identity-establishing
configuration the pass-through still reaches the authentication
chain, where the absence of a SOAP principal is answered 401,
so mixed anonymous traffic belongs on a timestamp-only instance
or a separate proxy.

allow_mtom.description:
Accept MTOM/XOP multipart/related packaging. The root part is
the first part (when the `start` parameter is supplied it must
name that part); the gateway validates that part's envelope and
never reads or decodes attachment payloads. Set false to declare
that this route does not accept MTOM at all; a SOAP-bearing
multipart then returns 415. Package framing is STRICT because
the parser decides which bytes are the envelope: delimiter LINES
are recognized only at the body start or immediately after a
CRLF with exact CRLF framing and no transport padding, and the
`--boundary` token may appear nowhere else (a padded, LF-ended,
or `--boundaryX` line, a token opened by a bare LF or CR, or a
token mid-line in the preamble, a part, or the epilogue refuses
the package); exactly one close-delimiter is required; the
package Content-Type must not carry an RFC 2231 extended or
continuation form (`boundary*`, `type*0`, `start*`, ...) of
boundary/type/start; part headers must be US-ASCII with no
obsolete folding, must be well-formed `token: value` pairs, and
may carry at most one Content-Type / Content-ID /
Content-Transfer-Encoding each; Content-ID values must be
package-unique (ignoring ASCII case and a leading `cid:`) and
nonblank, while a Content-ID or `start` carrying `%`, `+`, or
embedded whitespace is refused (a percent-decoding backend
would resolve it to a different part); and the root part must
declare a SOAP/XOP essence and must not declare a re-encoding
Content-Transfer-Encoding (anything other than 7bit/8bit/binary).
The whole package is
framed and every part parsed before a root is selected, so no
later ambiguity is missed by an early return. Bounds are
fail-closed (at most 64 parts; at most 8 KiB and 32 header lines
per part). MUST NOT be explicitly
true when x509_signature.enabled is true — that pairing is
refused at admission, and XOP representations (multipart/related
and bare application/xop+xml) return 415 under an enabled
x509_signature regardless, because Ferrum implements no
WS-Security attachment-signature transform and an X.509
signature therefore cannot cover attachment octets.

sync_mode.description: PasswordDigest replay-claim storage. 'redis' is required by (and only valid with) nonce.replay_scope = 'shared'; it is what makes replay protection cross-replica. Any RESP-compatible server works.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL with a redis:// or rediss:// scheme and a non-empty authority/hostname. Must not carry a URL fragment; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. Required when sync_mode is 'redis'.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for shared replay claims. Must be non-empty when supplied. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:soap_ws_security:{plugin-config-id}`, which isolates independent PasswordDigest policies inside a namespace while keeping every replica of one policy claiming against the same keyspace. An explicit prefix is the opt-in for deliberately sharing a keyspace across policies.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be greater than zero.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be greater than zero.

require.description: Require a wsu:Timestamp element in the Security header. This controls whether the element may be ABSENT; a Timestamp that IS present is always validated against max_age_seconds / clock_skew_seconds / Expires, so an out-of-policy Timestamp is never ignored and the PasswordDigest binding always compares against a validated instant.

max_age_seconds.description: Maximum age (seconds) of the Created timestamp before rejection. Zero is rejected because it would accept no timestamp at all.

require_expires.description: Require an Expires element inside the Timestamp

clock_skew_seconds.description: Clock skew tolerance (seconds) for timestamp validation. Zero is permitted (strictest). The maximum keeps every admitted value inside representable duration arithmetic.

username_token.description:
WS-Security UsernameToken authentication. Unknown usernames, wrong
PasswordText values, and wrong PasswordDigest values share one
generic HTTP 401 body (`{"error":"WS-Security: invalid credentials"}`)
and must not disclose whether the principal exists. Lookup misses
still perform PasswordText/PasswordDigest verification against
process-local dummy material. Structural token or policy failures
remain distinct.

password_type.description: Password format. PasswordDigest hashes password with nonce+timestamp; PasswordText sends the password directly (TLS only).

credentials.description: Allowed username/password pairs for UsernameToken authentication. Every entry must be an object with a username and password that each contain at least one non-whitespace character; a malformed entry is rejected rather than dropped, and duplicate usernames are rejected because credential selection is first-wins. Values are matched EXACTLY, including any leading or trailing spaces — the gateway compares the credential the client sent byte for byte and never trims it. A `password` of exactly `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` is resolved once at admission from that process environment variable (populated directly or through the _FILE/_VAULT/_AWS/_AZURE/_GCP secret suffixes); a `${...}` reference to any other variable, or an unset, empty, or whitespace-only value, is refused at admission without echoing the name or value, and the variable must be set on every node that constructs the plugin. Required and non-empty when `enabled` is true.

created_max_age_seconds.description: Freshness window (seconds) for the UsernameToken's own wsu:Created — the instant hashed into the PasswordDigest, distinct from the outer Timestamp Created. Without it a captured token stays digest-valid forever and only the replay TTL limits resubmission. Zero is rejected. The value validated is byte-for-byte the value fed to the digest.

created_clock_skew_seconds.description: Clock skew tolerance (seconds) for the UsernameToken Created freshness window and for the Timestamp Expires comparison. Zero is permitted (strictest).

created_max_timestamp_divergence_seconds.description: Maximum permitted absolute difference between the UsernameToken Created and the outer wsu:Timestamp Created. This binding is what prevents a captured UsernameToken from being paired with a freshly minted outer Timestamp — moving the outer instant no longer moves the inner one, and moving the inner one invalidates the captured digest. Zero is permitted (the two instants must be identical). The UsernameToken Created must also not fall past an outer Expires.

require_timestamp_binding.description: Require an outer wsu:Timestamp carrying a valid Created for PasswordDigest requests, so the Timestamp binding cannot be dropped by omitting the element. The outer Timestamp is validated on every request in which it appears — including when timestamp.require is false — so the instant bound against is always an independently validated one.

remove_credential.description:
Delete the verified `wsse:UsernameToken` — or the whole
`wsse:Security` header, when the credential is all it carries —
from the message the BACKEND receives, so a reusable PasswordText
secret is not handed to every system behind the gateway. The
authenticated identity is still published normally
(`authenticated_identity`,
`ctx.metadata["soap_ws_username"]`).

Off by default, because a backend may legitimately read the
token. Admission requires `enabled: true` and an explicit
`password_type: PasswordText`, and refuses the option alongside
an enabled `x509_signature` or `saml` or an explicit
`content_type.allow_mtom: true` — rewriting an envelope whose
content a signature covers, or re-framing an MTOM package, is
refused rather than done silently.

At request time a governed envelope that carries an XMLDSIG
`Signature` is rejected with 400, and a representation whose
bytes cannot be spliced (a UTF-16 body, an MTOM package) is
rejected with 415. Neither is forwarded with the credential
intact. The final-body integrity proof binds the SANITIZED
representation, so this plugin's own removal is admitted while
every other post-validation body mutation still fails closed
with 500. Gateway-internal views (access logs, mirrors) may
still observe the original buffered body; the option governs the
backend-visible request.

trusted_certs.description: PEM file paths of trusted signing certificates (matched by SHA-256 fingerprint). A matched certificate is trusted only inside its own notBefore/notAfter window, checked on every request; an expired or not-yet-valid pin is admitted with a warning but its signatures are rejected with 401. Non-string or blank entries are rejected rather than dropped. Required and non-empty when `enabled` is true.

allowed_algorithms.description: Allowed XMLDSig signature algorithms. Unsupported values are rejected rather than dropped.

allowed_digest_algorithms.description:
Allowed XMLDSig `<Reference>` digest algorithms. Tracked
independently of `allowed_algorithms` so signature method
and reference digest can be gated separately — e.g. accept
rsa-sha256 signatures over sha1 digests (rare but valid)
without also accepting rsa-sha1 signatures. Defaults to
sha256 only; add `sha1` to allow legacy reference digests.

require_signed_timestamp.description:
Require a wsu:Timestamp to be PRESENT and covered by the
signature. A message with no Timestamp is rejected rather than
passing vacuously, and pairing this with timestamp.require=false
is refused at admission as a contradiction.

saml.description:
SAML 2.0 assertion validation. The plugin cryptographically verifies
the assertion's `<Signature>` element (XMLDSIG) before resolving
signature references or trusting assertion claims. Verification
steps, in order:
  1. Locate `<Signature>` inside the assertion (rejected if absent).
     More than one `<Assertion>` inside the WS-Security block is
     rejected outright.
  2. Resolve the signing algorithm and confirm it is in `allowed_signature_algorithms`.
  3. Match the signing certificate from `KeyInfo/X509Data/X509Certificate`
     against `trusted_signing_certs` by SHA-256 fingerprint of the full DER
     (leaf-cert trust — no CA chain validation; operators supply the IdP's
     actual signing certificate(s) as published in IdP metadata).
  4. Verify `<SignatureValue>` over exclusive-canonicalized `<SignedInfo>`
     (`xml-exc-c14n#`, including `InclusiveNamespaces PrefixList`) using the
     matched cert's RSA public key.
  5. ONLY THEN verify the single `<Reference>` digest after the supported
     transform chain (XMLDSIG enveloped-signature followed by Exclusive XML
     Canonicalization `xml-exc-c14n#`, including `InclusiveNamespaces
     PrefixList`). The digest algorithm must be in
     `allowed_digest_algorithms` and the Reference must target the enclosing
     Assertion ID. Exactly one Reference is supported, so a duplicate cannot
     re-canonicalize the assertion.
  6. Validate Issuer (must match `trusted_issuers`), the MANDATORY bounded
     Conditions window (both NotBefore and NotOnOrAfter required, span capped
     by `max_assertion_lifetime_seconds`, `clock_skew_seconds` tolerance), the
     service `audience` on every AudienceRestriction, and every other
     Conditions child: at most one OneTimeUse and at most one
     ProxyRestriction are accepted, each standard condition only in its
     standard shape (an `xsi:type` must resolve to its own standard SAML
     type; no extension attributes or non-Audience children), and any
     other condition (a `saml:Condition` extension, a derived or extended
     standard condition, or a foreign element) makes the assertion
     indeterminate and is rejected (SAML Core 2.0 section 2.5.1.1) before
     its id is claimed. Exactly one SubjectConfirmation must qualify by
     naming `recipient`; a non-qualifying confirmation is skipped, and
     none or more than one qualifying is rejected.
  7. Resolve exactly one namespace-correct, nonblank Subject NameID.
     This happens before replay state is consumed, so an otherwise
     valid assertion that authenticates nobody fails with 401
     without burning its assertion id.
  8. Claim the assertion id for single use in the declared
     nonce.replay_scope, which is REQUIRED when SAML is enabled. Every
     accepted assertion is claimed exactly once, so OneTimeUse needs no
     special case; a replay-backend outage fails closed. Claims are retained
     for the fixed 93601s horizon, which dominates
     max_assertion_lifetime_seconds + 2 x clock_skew_seconds. 'process' scope
     is a single-replica declaration and makes NO cross-replica claim;
     multi-replica SAML deployments must use 'shared'.
  9. Publish the Subject NameID as the request principal
     (an external authenticated_identity, never mapped to a Consumer) and
     mirror it into `ctx.metadata["soap_ws_saml_subject"]`.
On any failure the request is rejected with HTTP 401. Rejections never echo
the issuer, audience, recipient, subject, or assertion id. Unsupported
canonicalization or transform algorithms fail closed; inclusive c14n,
comments, XPath, XSLT, and other XMLDSIG transforms are not supported.

trusted_issuers.description:
SAML Issuer URIs that are accepted as the source of an assertion.
Required and non-empty when `enabled` is true. The Issuer string
inside the signed assertion must match one of these values
exactly, including any surrounding whitespace — the gateway acts
on the character data the signature covered and never trims it.

trusted_signing_certs.description:
PEM file paths of IdP X.509 signing certificates. The cert
presented inside the assertion's `KeyInfo` must match one of
these by SHA-256 fingerprint of the full DER, and is trusted only
inside its own notBefore/notAfter window (checked on every
request; an out-of-window pin is admitted with a warning but its
assertions are rejected with 401). Required and non-empty when
`enabled` is true.

Rotating an IdP signing cert does NOT require a gateway restart:
the trust list is read when the plugin generation is
constructed, so changing this list and applying a configuration
reload (file-mode SIGHUP, a database/CP change, a DP push)
installs the new trust material in place — the retired signer is
refused from the first request served by the new generation, and
the process, its listeners, and its connections are untouched.
What is NOT detected is replacing a PEM's CONTENTS at an
unchanged path: nothing watches the file, so the reload must
change the configuration (typically the path list) for the new
material to be read.

allowed_signature_algorithms.description:
XMLDSig signature algorithms accepted on SAML assertions.
Defaults to RSA-SHA256 only. Adding `rsa-sha1` accepts legacy
IdPs that still emit SHA-1 signatures. Tracked independently
of `allowed_digest_algorithms`.

allowed_digest_algorithms.description:
XMLDSig `<Reference>` digest algorithms accepted inside the
assertion's SignedInfo. Defaults to SHA-256 only. Add `sha1`
only to interoperate with IdPs that still emit SHA-1 digests.
Independent of `allowed_signature_algorithms` so an operator
can choose any combination.

audience.description:
Required when `enabled` is true. Every
`Conditions/AudienceRestriction` in the assertion must name this
exact value (each restriction is a conjunct). Without it, an
assertion minted by the same trusted issuer for another relying
party is accepted here.

recipient.description:
Required when `enabled` is true. Matched against
`Subject/SubjectConfirmation/SubjectConfirmationData/@Recipient`
so a captured assertion cannot be presented to a different
endpoint.

max_assertion_lifetime_seconds.description:
Maximum permitted `Conditions/@NotOnOrAfter - @NotBefore` span.
Both instants are mandatory and the window must be non-empty,
so an assertion with absent or unbounded Conditions is refused
rather than becoming an indefinite bearer credential.

allowed_subject_confirmation_methods.description:
Accepted SubjectConfirmation @Method URIs. Only
'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer' is implemented;
'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:holder-of-key' is rejected at
admission because the confirmation key is not bound to the
message signature. Exactly one acceptable SubjectConfirmation
must be present, its SubjectConfirmationData must name
`recipient`, carry its own NotOnOrAfter, honour NotBefore when
present, and omit InResponseTo.

clock_skew_seconds.description: Clock skew tolerance (seconds) for SAML NotBefore / NotOnOrAfter. Zero is permitted (strictest); the maximum keeps every admitted value inside representable duration arithmetic.

nonce.description:
Replay protection cache. A nonce is retained only after its
PasswordDigest verifies, and the cache is
bounded on three independent axes: per-nonce encoded length,
retained entries, and retained key UTF-8 payload bytes counted once
per shared immutable key allocation. An exact ordered age index
provides O(log n) expiry operations without a lookup-map scan or
stale queue. Capacity maintenance reclaims only entries already
past the fixed retention horizon and at most 64 of them per
request; a nonce inside it is never evicted. If that bounded
reclamation cannot make room the request fails closed (HTTP 401)
rather than accepting a nonce whose replay window cannot be recorded
or unprotecting one that was already claimed. This is the only
canonical shape; there is no `nonce_replay_protection` alias.

Accepted SAML assertion-id claims share this same bounded state for
the same fixed horizon, under a separate internal claim-kind
namespace so an attacker-chosen nonce can never burn an assertion
claim or the reverse. They count against max_cache_size and
max_total_cache_bytes (a fixed 64-byte SHA-256 hex claim key each),
so a SAML-enabled process scope must be sized for peak accepted
assertion rate as well as peak PasswordDigest rate.

replay_scope declares where those claims live and is REQUIRED when
username_token is enabled with password_type PasswordDigest, and
whenever saml is enabled. It has no default because a gateway
cannot observe its own replica count.
The entry/byte caps and bounded expiry maintenance described above
apply to replay_scope=process; under replay_scope=shared the bounds
that apply are Redis's own memory policy plus the fixed expiry on
each claim key, and max_cache_size / max_total_cache_bytes are
inert. The encoded-length ceiling applies on both paths.

Claim retention is FIXED at 93601 seconds (~26 h) on both paths and
is not configurable: it is
max created_max_age_seconds (86400) + 2 × max
created_clock_skew_seconds (3600) + 1, the widest span over which
any configuration this schema admits can accept an unchanged
UsernameToken. Retention derived from the *configured* window is not
sufficient, because replay state outlives the generation that wrote
it: a later reload may widen created_max_age_seconds /
created_clock_skew_seconds after the shorter retention has already
elapsed, and the claim cannot then be resurrected in either scope
(a process entry may already have been reclaimed or refreshed, and
Redis SET NX cannot extend a key it finds present). Retaining every
claim for the schema-wide maximum makes any later admitted widening
safe with no rollout ordering, drain window, or operator procedure.
There is no cache_ttl_seconds field; it was removed rather than
redefined, and supplying it fails admission as an unknown key.

replay_scope.description: Where PasswordDigest nonce and SAML assertion-id replay claims live. REQUIRED when username_token.enabled is true and password_type is PasswordDigest, and whenever saml.enabled is true; there is no default. "process" registers state under a stable {namespace}|{plugin-config-id} scope so a reload generation inherits the previous generation's claims instead of starting from an empty cache — it is explicitly NOT cross-replica protection, and selecting it asserts a single-replica deployment. Process-scope claims are lost on process restart, crash, or reschedule; a captured PasswordDigest token still inside its Created window can then be accepted again. Reload survival is not restart survival. "shared" claims each nonce with one atomic Redis SET NX EX so exactly one request across all replicas wins a nonce inside its TTL; it requires sync_mode=redis and a redis_url, and the key is SHA-256(nonce) in hex so the nonce never reaches a Redis keyspace, MONITOR, SLOWLOG, or client error log. A shared-backend outage fails closed with HTTP 401 (failure class nonce_shared_backend_unavailable); there is no degrade-to-local option because a per-replica fallback would reinstate the cross-replica bypass. Recovery is automatic: any error that marks the shared client unavailable — connect, DNS, a hostname that currently resolves to an egress-denied address, or a transient command error — also arms the background recovery checker, which restores enforcement within redis_health_check_interval_seconds without a reload (a literal-IP egress-policy denial is the exception and is a configuration fix; hostname denials re-screen because DNS answers can change). Because SET NX cannot tell an evicted claim from an unused nonce or assertion, every shared-replay connection (first dial and recovery probe) runs INFO MEMORY and must prove maxmemory 0 or maxmemory_policy noeviction before it carries a claim: a proven evicting policy is terminal for the plugin generation, an unprovable answer is a recoverable outage, and both fail closed like any other shared-backend outage. Durability across failover is Redis's own: run the replay keyspace with consistent failover, since a lost claim key makes its nonce claimable again. Admission enforces the pairing in both directions: shared without sync_mode=redis is rejected, and sync_mode=redis without shared is rejected.

max_cache_size.description: Maximum retained replay entries — PasswordDigest nonces plus accepted SAML assertion-id claims (replay_scope=process only). Zero is rejected because it would make replay detection inert. Capacity maintenance uses an ordered age index and reclaims at most 64 entries per request, and only entries already past the fixed 93601-second retention horizon. A nonce inside that horizon is never evicted, so a claim that cannot be recorded is rejected with 401 instead of admitting an unprotected nonce. Size this (and max_total_cache_bytes) for peak authenticated PasswordDigest rate — plus peak accepted SAML assertion rate when saml is enabled — × 93601 s, roughly 1 claim/second sustained at the default and about 10/second at the 1000000 ceiling. Higher sustained rates need replay_scope=shared, where retention is Redis's cost rather than the gateway's.

max_encoded_length.description: Maximum length of the encoded wsse:Nonce value, enforced before Base64 decoding and before any cache insertion so an oversized nonce is never decoded or retained.

max_total_cache_bytes.description: Maximum total retained nonce-key UTF-8 payload bytes, counted once per logical nonce's immutable allocation shared by the lookup map and age index. Hash/tree node and reference-count control-block overhead is excluded and remains bounded by max_cache_size. Must be at least max_encoded_length. Like max_cache_size this is a fail-closed cap: exhausting it rejects the claim with 401 rather than evicting a nonce that is still inside its retention window.

SpecExposeConfig.description: Plugin: spec_expose — Exposes API specification documents (OpenAPI, WSDL, WADL) for GET and HEAD on the canonical /specz sub-path. HEAD retains the GET representation through response-body policy, then returns the final status and representation headers without a wire body. Unauthenticated. Only works with prefix-based listen_path proxies (HTTP only). Successful upstream fetches are capped by max_response_body_bytes, decoded from origin Content-Encoding (gzip, x-gzip, br, identity) to identity bytes before cache and /specz, and cached in-process for cache_ttl_seconds (default 300s). Unsupported or malformed origin coding is HTTP 502. Failed fetches are coalesced and negatively cached with bounded exponential backoff; excess cache-miss waiters receive HTTP 503 with Retry-After.

spec_url.description: Full URL (http or https only) to fetch the API specification document (e.g., https://internal-service/docs/openapi.yaml). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. The authority must be nonempty and must not contain userinfo ('@'). Paths and queries may be used for origin routing or signed access, but are omitted from gateway diagnostics. Remaining URL parse details (IPv6 literals, IDNA, percent-encoding) are runtime-only.

content_type.description: Trusted response Content-Type override; it is not restricted by the upstream allow-list. When set it must be nonempty after trim and a valid HTTP header value (HTAB and printable ASCII). When omitted or null, only supported spec media types are preserved from upstream (case-insensitive media-type comparison, with original parameters retained); every other or missing value falls back to application/octet-stream.

tls_no_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when fetching the spec. Omitted or null defaults to the gateway's FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY setting. When verification is enabled and a gateway CA bundle is configured, load or parse failure rejects plugin construction instead of widening trust.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live for the in-process spec body cache (seconds). Omitted or null defaults to 300. The first /specz request fetches the spec from spec_url and stores the identity document; subsequent requests within the TTL window return the cached copy without re-fetching. Set to 0 to disable durable positive caching; callers admitted before an in-flight fetch completes still share that fetch regardless of scheduling delay, while later requests immediately re-fetch. Failed fetches use bounded negative-cache backoff regardless of this value.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Maximum upstream spec response body size to buffer, decode, and cache. Omitted or null defaults to 26214400. Must be greater than zero. The coded origin body is streamed with this cap, then decoded to identity under the same bound, so oversized or explosively compressed responses are rejected with HTTP 502 before unbounded memory growth.

SpiffeIdentityConfig.description:
Plugin: spiffe_identity — Extracts the SPIFFE ID from the peer
certificate's URI SAN and populates `ctx.peer_spiffe_id` /
`StreamConnectionContext` metadata for downstream auth and rate-limit
plugins (notably `mesh_authz` and `rate_limiting` with
`limit_by: spiffe_identity`).

Auto-injected by mesh mode on every applicable topology; reserved
plugin id `__mesh_spiffe_identity`. Standalone usage is supported on
non-mesh gateways that still terminate mTLS and want to surface the
SPIFFE identity to other plugins.

The trust domain is admitted exactly as SPIFFE-ID section 2.1 defines
it: non-empty, at most 255 bytes, lowercase, and composed only of
`[a-z0-9.-_]` — including at the first and last byte. Userinfo, ports,
percent-encoding, and the SPIFFE ID's own 2048-byte total bound are
still enforced.

A certificate-derived peer identity is admitted as an authenticated
principal carrying the leaf certificate's `notAfter` as its
authorization deadline, so SPIFFE-only policy chains (this plugin plus
`mesh_authz`, with no `mtls_auth`) are bounded by SVID expiry on the
request, WebSocket, streaming-body, TCP+TLS, and UDP+DTLS paths. Every
request re-checks the leaf validity window, and an expired or
not-yet-valid SVID is refused with the same fixed `403`
`{"error":"invalid SPIFFE identity certificate"}` body as a malformed
one. A pre-stamped kernel-attested or HBONE-asserted `peer_spiffe_id`
carries no validity window and is not treated as certificate-bounded.

`null` and `{}` select the default extraction-only behavior: no
identity is required, every trust domain the listener's verifier
accepted is admitted, and nothing is forwarded to the backend. Every
field below is an opt-in tightening of that default.

Rejections never echo the peer certificate: a malformed SPIFFE URI SAN
is the fixed `403` `{"error":"invalid SPIFFE identity certificate"}`,
and its debug diagnostic names only a fixed reason, never the URI or
any credential its userinfo or query carried.

A proxy- or proxy-group-scoped instance on a stream proxy is refused at
admission unless that proxy sets `frontend_tls: true` and
`passthrough: false`, exactly as for `mtls_auth`. Global instances are
exempt and remain no-ops on plaintext listeners.

require_identity.description:
When true, a request or stream that reaches this plugin without a
usable SPIFFE identity (no client certificate, a certificate with
no SPIFFE URI SAN, or certificate DER that does not parse) is
refused with a fixed `403` `{"error":"SPIFFE identity required"}`.
A pre-stamped kernel-attested or HBONE-asserted identity counts as
present.

allowed_trust_domains.description:
When set, only identities whose trust domain is listed are
admitted; any other identity — certificate-derived or pre-stamped —
is refused with a fixed `403`
`{"error":"SPIFFE trust domain not allowed"}`. Entries are bare
SPIFFE trust domains (SPIFFE-ID section 2.1 grammar, no
`spiffe://` scheme), matched exactly. Omit the field to admit every
trust domain; an explicit empty list is rejected.

forward_identity.description:
When true, the admitted SPIFFE ID is forwarded to the backend in
the fixed gateway-owned request header `x-ferrum-peer-spiffe-id`
(HTTP family only). Every client-supplied copy — compared ASCII
case-insensitively with `_` read as `-` — is removed from the
initial header block before the gateway's value is set, including
on requests that carry no identity; client request-trailer copies
are dropped by the gateway's request-trailer boundary, which owns
the whole `x-ferrum-*` namespace.

SseConfig.description: Plugin: sse — Server-Sent Events stream handler. Validates SSE client criteria, shapes requests, and ensures proper streaming response headers. Unknown keys and non-object configs are rejected. Explicit null members are rejected; omitted keys keep defaults. wrap_non_sse_responses implies client-visible text/event-stream for wrapped responses.

require_get_method.description: Reject non-GET requests with 405 (SSE is read-only). While this or require_accept_header is enabled, the checks are route admission policy: a native gRPC or WebSocket request to the route, which runs only plain-HTTP plugins, is refused with 403 (rejection phase route_protocol_admission) instead of skipping them.

require_accept_header.description: Require an affirmative Accept: text/event-stream entry (406 otherwise; q=0, malformed, or duplicate quality is not affirmative). While this or require_get_method is enabled, native gRPC and WebSocket requests to the route are refused with 403 (rejection phase route_protocol_admission).

strip_accept_encoding.description: Strip Accept-Encoding to prevent compressed responses breaking SSE framing

add_no_buffering_header.description: Add X-Accel-Buffering: no to disable nginx/ALB response buffering

strip_content_length.description: Remove Content-Length from SSE responses (streams are indefinite)

retry_ms.description: EventSource reconnection hint in milliseconds, prepended as a retry: field when wrapping, and written once ahead of the first bytes of a streamed genuine backend text/event-stream 2xx response (as its own line, so it dispatches no event; a later backend retry: field overrides it). Never written into a stream under a non-identity Content-Encoding, a Cache-Control: no-transform stream, or a 206/226 response. Admitted over the JSON numeric VALUE, so an exact integer-valued number (2500.0) is accepted exactly as 2500 is; fractional values and magnitudes outside the unsigned 64-bit range above are rejected.

force_sse_content_type.description: Force Content-Type: text/event-stream even if backend returns something else. Not applied to a response carrying Cache-Control: no-transform (RFC 9110 section 7.7 forbids an intermediary changing Content-Type on one), to 206/226 responses, or to bodies under a non-identity Content-Encoding, whether or not wrap_non_sse_responses is enabled.

wrap_non_sse_responses.description: Wrap non-SSE response bodies in data: ...\n\n SSE event framing (enables response buffering). Implies client-visible text/event-stream for wrapped responses and composes with force_sse_content_type. Wrapping and its relabel are declined together — the origin representation is forwarded unchanged — for 206/226 responses, responses carrying Cache-Control: no-transform (RFC 9110 section 7.7, which also blocks force_sse_content_type), and bodies under a non-identity Content-Encoding. A framed event that exceeds the effective response-body ceiling returns the gateway capacity refusal instead of the unframed body. Only responses this plugin's after_proxy relabelled are framed, so synthetic responses (response_mock, terminate-mode serverless_function, cache hits) keep their own body and media type.

StatsdLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: statsd_logging — Sends transaction metrics to a StatsD-compatible server over UDP. Unknown top-level keys are rejected at construction / Admin validation. Nested `global_tags` remains an intentionally open string map, but keys must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* (max 64 bytes) and cannot override reserved or schema-renamed runtime tags (namespace, method, status, status_class, grpc_status, proxy, protocol, error, cause, direction, body_outcome, body_error, result, io_side, error_class). The authoritative namespace tag is always appended and preserves the full validated Ferrum namespace (up to 254 bytes). Metric prefixes are sanitized and capped at 256 UTF-8 bytes after trim; encoded global_tags (+ namespace) are capped at 400 bytes. `schema` and `schema_ref` are structurally exclusive. When `max_entry_bytes` is omitted, OpenAPI requires `buffer_max_bytes` to be at least 131074 (`2 * (65536 + 1)`); a sibling comparison against an explicit `max_entry_bytes` is enforced only at construction. Named-schema existence is runtime-only. Construction also rejects a prefix/tag/schema combination whose smallest ordinary record (HTTP, gRPC, stream, or WebSocket) cannot fit `max_entry_bytes`. UDP datagrams never exceed a 1452-byte conservative IPv4/IPv6 payload ceiling; indivisible oversized lines are dropped rather than fragmented. Hot-path admission reserves a queue slot and a provisional max_entry_bytes lease before rendering StatsD line protocol, then shrinks the lease to the exact retained size under buffer_max_bytes. Delivery retains admitted payloads plus at most one MTU-bounded datagram buffer. Mirror summaries are excluded from request.* families. Timers require finite non-negative samples (the -1.0 no-backend TTFB sentinel is omitted). gRPC transactions add a bounded grpc_status tag and request.grpc_status.{code} counter (0-16 or OTHER) while keeping HTTP status/status_class distinct. WebSocket session completion emits websocket.* families via on_ws_disconnect. Registration policy is KeepLastKnownGood (an invalid enabled config fails file-mode load and `ferrum-edge validate`, and a reload keeps the prior generation). See docs/plugins.md.

host.description: StatsD server hostname or IP address. Must be a bare hostname or IP without scheme, path, query, fragment, credentials, or port (bracketed and unbracketed IPv6 literals are allowed).

prefix.description: Metric name prefix (e.g., ferrum.request.count). Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before sanitization; empty after trim is rejected. Runtime admission enforces at most 256 UTF-8 bytes after sanitization, so a longer raw string may still be refused. Construction also requires max_entry_bytes to fit the smallest ordinary record under this prefix.

propertyNames.description: Tag keys are restricted to the ASCII grammar `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`, so OpenAPI `maxLength: 64` matches the runtime 64-byte key ceiling. Reserved runtime tag names are excluded case-insensitively.

global_tags.description: Extra DogStatsD tags appended to every metric. Keys must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` (max 64 ASCII bytes) and cannot override reserved runtime tags or effective schema-renamed runtime keys (enforced at construction). Encoded global_tags (+ authoritative namespace) are capped at 400 bytes.

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing buffered metrics

buffer_capacity.description: Channel capacity — new entries are dropped when full

max_batch_lines.description: Max transaction records to batch before flushing. The threshold counts admitted transaction payloads (each rendering several newline-separated metric lines), not individual metric lines.

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum rendered StatsD line-protocol bytes for one admitted transaction. Configuration is rejected unless the smallest ordinary record (HTTP, gRPC, stream, or WebSocket) with the resolved prefix, global tags, and schema fits this budget. Request-shaped fields can still make an individual render exceed the budget; those oversized entries are dropped before enqueue.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained rendered-content budget across queued entries, one MTU-bounded datagram buffer, and retries. Admission reserves two copies plus framing before rendering and shrinks that lease to the exact retained size. Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1). When max_entry_bytes is omitted, this field must be at least 131074 (the default-dependent bound). An arbitrary sibling comparison against an explicit max_entry_bytes is runtime-only.

max_retries.description: Retry attempts after the initial UDP send fails. Defaults to 0 (no retries). Consumed by the shared batching logger.

retry_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts. Defaults to 0. Consumed by the shared batching logger when `max_retries` > 0.

schema.description: Only `rename` and `omit` apply to statsd output — they operate on tag keys that map 1:1 to a native summary field: HTTP: `method`↔`http_method`, `status`↔`response_status_code`, `proxy`↔`proxy_id`. Stream: `protocol`↔`protocol`, `proxy`↔`proxy_id`, `cause`↔`disconnect_cause`, `direction`↔`disconnect_direction`. Rename targets must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* and must not collide with reserved runtime tags. `static_fields`, `derived_fields`, `metadata`, `order`, and `timestamp_format` are no-ops for statsd (line protocol, not JSON). See docs/log_schema.md.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Same statsd caveats as above. Existence of the named schema is resolved at construction.

StdoutLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: stdout_logging — Writes one JSON transaction/stream summary per line to the bounded non-blocking stdout writer. Independent of FERRUM_LOG_LEVEL. Accepted keys are filter, sampling, schema, and schema_ref; null or an empty object uses defaults. The optional filter runs before sampling and schema application. `schema` and `schema_ref` are mutually exclusive. `filter.expression` is mutually exclusive with the flat filter keys (status_code_min, status_code_max, min_latency_ms, errors_only) by key presence, including `errors_only: false`. Registered KeepLastKnownGood: an invalid enabled config fails file-mode startup and is refused on reload (the previous generation keeps serving) rather than being omitted. A global instance without an execution trigger also logs route-miss 404s (no proxy; metadata.rejection_phase = route_not_found).

filter.description: Optional predicate that suppresses log entries before they are serialized. All present fields must match for an entry to be logged. The expression form is mutually exclusive with the flat predicates. When omitted, every transaction is logged.

status_code_min.description: HTTP responses with status < this value are skipped. Stream summaries (no HTTP status) are always skipped when any status_code_* bound is set.

status_code_max.description: HTTP responses with status > this value are skipped. Must be greater than or equal to status_code_min when both are set, otherwise plugin validation rejects the config.

min_latency_ms.description: Skip summaries whose total latency / stream duration is below this many milliseconds.

errors_only.description: HTTP-family summaries require an authoritative terminal failure: dispatch/error_class, body failure, incomplete body, client disconnect, gateway rejection, or nonzero final grpc_status. Stream summaries require error_class or connection_error. Status and latency predicates remain independent and must also match.

sampling.description: Keep a deterministic, evenly spaced fraction of the records the filter admits: exactly `rate` x 1,000,000 of every 1,000,000 candidate records per instance, counted across HTTP, stream, and WebSocket session-end records. Skipped records are never serialized. `null` disables sampling.

rate.description: Fraction of records to keep, resolved to whole records per million; values that round to zero (below 0.0000005) are rejected. `1` keeps every record.

always_log_errors.description: When true, terminal failures (the `errors_only` predicate for HTTP-family records; `error_class` or `connection_error` for streams) are always logged and do not consume a sample.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. See docs/log_schema.md.

SummaryLogSchema.description: Customizable output schema for transaction-log JSON / line protocol. Rename keys, drop fields, reorder, inject static stamping, emit derived fields, flatten metadata. Metadata redaction always applies on every code path — sensitive substrings (`authorization`, `cookie`, `password`, `token`, …) cannot be introduced via `static_fields` or `derived_fields` (rejected at construction). This object, each `derived_fields` entry, and `metadata` are strict fixed shapes: unknown keys are rejected with a nested path. HTTP summaries include the normalized terminal `grpc_status` field (separate from `response_status_code`) when the request is gRPC. It can be renamed, omitted, or ordered like every other native field. `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reuse this same shape against their own record families; whatever a family cannot express (`summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, or a derived kind with no source field) is rejected at construction with a plugin- and field-specific diagnostic. Constraints this document cannot express are still enforced at construction and are NOT relaxations of the runtime contract: `omit` / `rename` / `order` names must resolve against the record family's field inventory for the selected `summary_type`; a field may not be both omitted and renamed; the combined native, static, and derived output keys must be unique; `order` must list every non-extension output key unless it contains `"*"`; and `rename` targets, `static_fields` keys (including nested keys) and `derived_fields` names may not match a sensitive-data substring or a credential-class name (for example `session_id`, `client_assertion`, `gpg_passphrase`, `private_rsa_key`; see docs/log_schema.md), while a `static_fields` string value that looks like a literal HTTP auth credential is refused. Under `metadata.mode: flatten`, `omit` may not list `metadata` and `rename` may not rename it; under `metadata.mode: omit`, `rename` may not rename it (those directives would otherwise be silently ignored). The whole `static_fields` object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values, quotes, separators, braces) must be at most 16384 bytes and a static value may nest at most 8 objects/arrays deep. `transforms` keys must be fields of the selected `summary_type`, may not also be omitted, `ip_prefix` applies only to `client_ip` / `backend_resolved_ip`, and a `hash` `secret_ref` must resolve to a set `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` value of at least 32 bytes. See docs/log_schema.md.

summary_type.description: Which summary type(s) this schema applies to. Summaries of the other type fall back to native serialization (the schema only customizes types it claims to handle).

omit.description: Native field names to drop from output.

rename.description: Map of native field name -> output key (at most 128 bytes).

order.description: Explicit output order, by output key. May contain `"*"` once as a wildcard for "every unlisted entry in natural order." Without `"*"`, every field must be listed. Entries are unique — a repeated output key (or a second `"*"`) is rejected.

static_fields.description: Literal JSON values injected at top level. Keys / nested keys matching sensitive substrings or credential-class names (for example `session_id`) are rejected at compile time. A `null` value is rejected — use `omit` to drop a field. At most 64 entries; keys are at most 128 bytes; the whole object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values included) is at most 16384 bytes; a value nests at most 8 objects/arrays deep. Static fields are stamped into every record, so these bounds are a per-record cost cap.

derived_fields.description: Computed values; emitted alongside native fields.

name.description: Output key for the derived value.

kind.description: `status_class`: `"1xx"`–`"5xx"` from `response_status_code` (stream: `"none"`). `backend_host`: hostname from `backend_target` (port stripped, IPv6 brackets honored). `summary_kind`: `"http"`, `"stream"`, or `"websocket_disconnect"` (the last only for `ws_logging` WebSocket disconnect entries). `outcome`: `"ok"` / `"error"`.

prefix.description: Prepended to each metadata key when promoted to top-level (e.g. `"meta_"`); only `flatten` reads it. Control characters are rejected. The type and the control-character restriction are validated in every mode, so a `nested` or `omit` schema cannot carry a value that would only start failing once the mode is switched to `flatten`.

on_collision.description: Behavior when a metadata key collides with an already-emitted field; only `flatten` reads it. `skip` keeps the existing value; `overwrite` replaces the colliding field's value in place with the (redacted) metadata value, so every key appears exactly once in the record. Validated in every mode, like `prefix`.

timestamp_format.description: Conversion applied to timestamp string fields (`timestamp_received`, `timestamp_connected`, `timestamp_disconnected`). Parse failures fall back to the raw RFC3339 string.

transforms.description: Per-field value transforms, keyed by native source field name (before `rename`), applied when the field is emitted: `truncate` keeps at most `max_bytes` bytes (cut on a UTF-8 boundary); `ip_prefix` keeps the network prefix of an IP address (`ipv4_bits` default 24, `ipv6_bits` default 48; IPv4-mapped IPv6 is masked as IPv4; a value that is not an address is emitted as `null`); `hash` replaces the value with the lowercase-hex keyed HMAC-SHA-256 under the secret named by `secret_ref`, which must be a `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference resolved at construction (literal secrets are refused; the value must be at least 32 bytes). Only the transaction-summary loggers support `transforms`; `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reject the key, and statsd ignores it. Kafka partition keys and Loki labels read typed fields and are not transformed.

TcpConnectionThrottleConfig.description: Plugin: tcp_connection_throttle — Caps active TCP/TCP+TLS connections per Consumer when a stream auth plugin identified one, else per canonical client IP. Explicit proxy/proxy-group attachment to any other protocol is rejected during configuration admission and plugin-cache validation. A global policy with a nonempty effective target set must cover at least one TCP/TCP+TLS proxy; mixed global scope is filtered from unsupported listeners. UDP/DTLS is not protected; use udp_rate_limiting for datagram/session admission. Enforcement is process-local, so each replica independently permits up to the configured limit and the deployment-wide allowance can be the limit multiplied by the number of replicas receiving the same identity. A counter entry is removed inline by the permit release that takes it to zero, so there is no background sweep. IP keys use the canonical client IP: IPv4 (including IPv4-mapped IPv6) is keyed per address, while native IPv6 sources are grouped to ipv6_prefix (default /64), so hosts in one /64 share a budget unless it is raised to 128. For IP keys the gateway-wide accept-time bound FERRUM_TCP_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP (default 256, counted across every TCP stream listener and grouped by FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX) applies first and closes over-cap connections before this plugin runs, so a max_connections_per_key above that bound can never bind; this plugin can only tighten it. Refusals are counted per proxy in the Prometheus counter ferrum_tcp_connection_throttle_rejections_total.

max_connections_per_key.description: Maximum active TCP connections allowed for one Consumer/IP key in this ferrum-edge process. Each replica enforces this limit independently. For IP keys the effective limit is also bounded by FERRUM_TCP_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP (default 256), which is enforced at accept time before this plugin runs.

ipv6_prefix.description: Prefix length used to group native IPv6 client addresses into one IP key. The default 64 makes every host in one /64 share a budget; 128 keys each IPv6 address separately. IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 clients are always keyed per address, and Consumer keys are unaffected. Independent of FERRUM_PER_IP_IPV6_PREFIX, which only groups the gateway-wide FERRUM_*_PER_IP caps.

TcpLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: tcp_logging — Sends transaction logs as NDJSON over a persistent TCP or TCP+TLS connection. Only the properties below are admitted; unknown keys (for example a misspelled `tlls`) are rejected so transport security cannot silently default to plaintext. `connect_timeout_ms` bounds DNS, TCP connect, and TLS handshake when enabled. `write_timeout_ms` bounds each batch write/flush; timeouts discard the writer and use the shared retry/reconnect path. Delivery is at-least-once after partial-write failure. Registration policy is KeepLastKnownGood: an invalid enabled candidate rejects startup or reload publication instead of silently removing or downgrading the previously accepted logger.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the TCP log receiver. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Must be a bare hostname or IP without scheme, path, query, fragment, credentials, or port (bracketed and unbracketed IPv6 literals are allowed).

port.description: Port of the TCP log receiver

tls.description: Enable TLS encryption for the connection

tls_server_name.description: DNS or IP identity for TLS SNI/certificate verification (defaults to `host`). Allowed only when `tls` is true. Accepts rustls DNS/IP identities, including absolute names (trailing dot) and underscore labels. The schema rejects URL schemes, paths, queries, fragments, credentials, whitespace, and host:port values; full rustls DNS/IP identity validation is enforced during plugin admission.

batch_size.description: Number of entries to buffer before sending a batch

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing a partial batch

max_retries.description: Retry attempts on failed batch delivery

retry_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts

buffer_capacity.description: Channel capacity — new entries are dropped when full

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes for one admitted NDJSON record. Oversized records are dropped before enqueue.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained serialized-content budget across queued, assembled, and retrying records. Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1) and at most 268435456 (256 MiB). When `max_entry_bytes` is omitted, the default entry size requires at least 131074.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Connection establishment timeout in milliseconds. Covers DNS resolution, TCP connect, and the TLS handshake when `tls` is true.

write_timeout_ms.description: Per-batch socket write_all + flush timeout in milliseconds. On timeout the persistent writer is discarded and retries reconnect.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. See docs/log_schema.md.

TransactionDebuggerConfig.description: Plugin: transaction_debugger — Emits verbose request/response and terminal diagnostics via tracing::debug on the transaction_debug target. Requires FERRUM_LOG_LEVEL=debug to see output. Unsupported keys are rejected. Body capture is opt-in and default off.
