It never forces an ineligible message to buffer: a body is sampled only when the message declares an identity Content-Encoding, a Content-Length that fits inside the configured cap (or, with the explicit capture_body_prefix opt-in, a text/plain or form Content-Length up to 1048576 bytes), and a capturable textual Content-Type (application/json, +json, text/json, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, text/plain). gRPC (application/grpc*), SSE (text/event-stream), WebSocket upgrades (including H2/H3 Extended CONNECT, excluded by typed request provenance rather than headers), XML, GraphQL, multipart, text/html, binary media types, chunked/unknown-length, and encoded messages keep streaming and are reported as omitted with a stable reason. XML and GraphQL are excluded because Ferrum has no bounded structure-aware redactor for them. Request samples are taken after all request transforms (backend-visible bytes) and response samples after all response transforms (client-visible bytes). Content-Length is only an admission screen: both final body hooks re-check the actual body length against the configured cap before any scan and fail closed with a content-free over_capture_limit omission, and an actually empty body (a HEAD or 304 response declares a length it never sends) is reported with the fixed empty_body reason rather than as a malformed structured body. Samples are redacted before rendering (JSON/form per field, text/plain per line as a coarse operator opt-in, plus credential-shaped values anywhere). In text/plain bodies every `name=value` / `name: value` line is dropped unless each field name parses cleanly and is declared in safe_text_fields (fail closed), a malformed JSON body renders as a fixed content-free marker instead of a partial rendering, control and bidi characters are escaped, non-UTF-8 bodies (including an incomplete multibyte tail) render as a fixed marker, and every capture reports whether it was captured, truncated, binary, or omitted. When the transaction_debug DEBUG target is disabled no body is buffered for capture. Captured bytes go only to the transaction_debug tracing target and are never written into transaction-log metadata. Values are also screened by shape regardless of field or header name: compact JWS/JWE tokens (recognized from the base64url-decoded JSON protected header, so whitespace inside the header does not evade it), well-known provider API keys, AWS access key ids, and PEM private-key blocks are redacted in captured bodies and in header dumps. Exactly one capture record is emitted per enabled direction even when a transform flips the decision between the header phase and the final body hook. Capture can be targeted with capture_request_header (plus an optional exact capture_request_header_value), capture_sample_rate, and capture_expires_at; a request outside the target never buffers and is reported as omitted with reason not_selected or capture_expired. capture_body_prefix opts text/plain and form bodies whose declared Content-Length exceeds the cap (up to 1048576 bytes) into buffering and renders a redacted prefix of complete lines or pairs marked truncated; JSON, chunked/unknown-length, and larger bodies are unchanged.

capture_body_prefix.description: Admit text/plain and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies whose declared Content-Length exceeds the capture cap (up to 1048576 bytes) and render a redacted prefix of the complete lines / pairs that fit inside the cap, marked truncated. JSON bodies, which need the whole document for field redaction, and chunked/unknown-length bodies are unchanged. True requires log_request_body or log_response_body true. Null is rejected.

capture_sample_rate.description: Fraction of requests whose bodies are captured, chosen deterministically per request so both directions agree. Requests that are not sampled never buffer and report reason not_selected. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

capture_request_header.description: Capture only requests that carry this request header (an HTTP header token, compared case-insensitively). Other requests never buffer and report reason not_selected. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

capture_request_header_value.description: Exact value capture_request_header must carry (compared after trimming the received value). 1-256 visible ASCII characters without surrounding spaces. When set, the selector header is redacted from header dumps. Requires capture_request_header.

capture_expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant after which capture stops: requests received at or after it never buffer and report reason capture_expired. A past instant is accepted. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

redacted_headers.description: Additional header names to redact beyond the built-in sensitive list. Each entry must be a nonempty HTTP header token (RFC 9110 tchar). Empty strings and names with spaces are rejected.

log_request_body.description: Enable bounded, redacted capture of the backend-visible request body. Null is rejected.

log_response_body.description: Enable bounded, redacted capture of the client-visible response body. Null is rejected.

max_request_body_bytes.description: Per-request capture budget in bytes. Requires log_request_body true; out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Per-response capture budget in bytes. Requires log_response_body true; out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped.

redacted_body_fields.description: Additional body field names (compared case-insensitively) to redact beyond the built-in credential markers. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before the 128-character maximum is applied. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true when the array is nonempty. An empty array is valid without a capture switch. Independently of this list, everything under an Azure "On Your Data" `parameters` object inside a `data_sources` / `dataSources` / `data-sources` container is replaced wholesale. Recognizing that container name never short-circuits the ordinary visitor: a captured body is arbitrary JSON, so a value under that name which is not the provider's conventional array (an object, string, number, boolean, or null) is still traversed with the same member-name and credential-shaped-string rules as the rest of the body.

safe_text_fields.description: Field names (compared case-insensitively) whose `name=value` / `name: value` lines may be rendered in captured text/plain bodies. A line containing `=` or `:` is kept only when every delimiter follows a declared name; a line with a missing, empty, quoted, undeclared, or non-ASCII-identifier name is dropped. Entries that the credential classifier or the sensitive body-field rules match are rejected: a credential-shaped name cannot be declared safe. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true when the array is nonempty.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Projects the terminal diagnostic records (HTTP, stream, WebSocket disconnect) emitted on the `transaction_debug` target; the diagnostic field inventory is the plugin's own (`outcome`, `method`, `path`, `status`, `rejection_phase`, `latency_plugin_ms`, …), not the transaction summary's. A portable named schema can only reference names shared with the summary registry, so use an inline `schema:` for diagnostic-only fields. See docs/log_schema.md.

TransactionLogSchemaConfig.description: Plugin: transaction_log_schema — Config-only plugin that registers named `SummaryLogSchema` definitions into a process-global registry for other logging plugins to consume via `schema_ref:`. Required scope is `global`; constructed by the loader BEFORE any plugin that uses `schema_ref:` so resolution always succeeds. The registry is atomically replaced on every config reload — renamed or removed schemas do not leak. Config-only instances are discarded after staging and never retained in runtime hook or protocol cache lists. Admin create/update/delete, batch, and restore validate the complete prospective namespace graph without consulting or modifying the live registry. Unknown outer and nested fixed-shape keys are rejected. See docs/log_schema.md.

schemas.description: Map of schema name → schema definition. Names are non-empty and referenced by other plugins as `schema_ref: <name>`. Duplicate names across multiple enabled `transaction_log_schema` plugins in the same namespace are rejected before persistence or load.

TransformerBodyRenamePath.description:
A dot-notation body path usable as a `rename` source or destination.
Array indices are rejected at plugin load time: rename over an array is
ambiguous (move? swap? overwrite?) and `Vec::remove`'s leftward shift
would silently drop a trailing element. Use `remove` + `add` to relocate
an array element. An ESCAPED numeric segment (`counts\.0` — a literal
key named `counts.0`) remains valid, so the exclusion applies only to an
unescaped path whose dot-delimited segments contain a plain integer.

TransformerOperationFieldExactness.description:
The operation-exact field contract both transformers enforce at plugin
load time, shared by every header / query / body rule schema: `add` and
`update` require `value` and forbid `new_key`; `rename` requires
`new_key` and forbids `value`; `remove` forbids both. Forbidden
properties are rejected by PRESENCE, so an explicit `null` fails exactly
as a string would. A body `value` may itself be `null` on `add` /
`update` — that sets the target field to JSON null.

UdpLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: udp_logging — Sends transaction logs to a UDP/DTLS endpoint in batches. Unknown top-level keys are rejected at construction / Admin validation so transport typos (for example `dtsl`) cannot silently fall back to plaintext. DTLS-only fields require `dtls: true` (omitted or false rejects them) so Admin/spec admission cannot accept plaintext configs that runtime would ignore. WebSocket session ends are sent as the shared session-end transaction record via on_ws_disconnect. Registration policy is KeepLastKnownGood (an invalid enabled instance rejects the candidate; a reload keeps the prior generation).

host.description: UDP endpoint hostname or IP address. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Must be a bare hostname or IP without scheme, path, query, fragment, credentials, or port (bracketed and unbracketed IPv6 literals are allowed).

dtls.description: Enable DTLS encryption for log datagrams. Shared Admin / CP validation checks configuration shape without opening node-local sources. On the consuming node, certificate/key/CA sources are materialized and cached for the plugin generation. When false or omitted, DTLS-only fields are rejected.

dtls_cert_path.description: PEM client certificate for DTLS mutual TLS. Materialized during the consuming node's dependency/construction phase when dtls is true; must be paired with dtls_key_path. Rejected unless dtls is true. Whitespace-only values are rejected. Where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

dtls_key_path.description: PEM private key for DTLS mutual TLS (ECDSA P-256 or P-384). Must be paired with dtls_cert_path. Rejected unless dtls is true. Whitespace-only values are rejected. Where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

dtls_ca_cert_path.description: PEM CA certificate for verifying the DTLS server. Materialized on the consuming node whenever set with dtls true, including when dtls_no_verify is true (the source must still be valid even though verification is disabled). Rejected unless dtls is true. Whitespace-only values are rejected. Where admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

dtls_no_verify.description: Skip DTLS server certificate verification (testing only). Rejected unless dtls is true.

batch_size.description: Number of entries to buffer before sending a batch

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing a partial batch

max_retries.description: Retry attempts on failed batch delivery

retry_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts

buffer_capacity.description: Channel capacity — new entries are dropped when full

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized bytes for one admitted JSON record. Oversized records are dropped before enqueue.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained serialized-content budget across queued, assembled, and retrying records. Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1) and at most 268435456 (256 MiB). When `max_entry_bytes` is omitted, the default entry size requires at least 131074.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. See docs/log_schema.md.

UdpRateLimitingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `udp_rate_limiting` plugin. Rate limits UDP
datagrams per resolved client IP using a fixed-window algorithm with
atomic counters. Excess datagrams are silently dropped (standard UDP
flood mitigation). By default (`direction: both`) client→backend and
backend→client datagrams share the same window per client IP; IPv6
clients are grouped by `ipv6_prefix`. A proxy- or proxy-group-scoped
attachment must reach only UDP/DTLS proxies (a TCP or HTTP-family
target is refused at admission). `datagrams_per_second`
and `bytes_per_second` are per-second rates; the effective per-window
cap is `rate × window_seconds`. `sync_mode` is parsed case-insensitively
(`LOCAL`, `Redis`); `redis` requires `redis_url`. Unknown top-level keys
are rejected by the runtime and by this schema. Counter storage supports
only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally
unsupported. Residual admission rules this schema cannot express,
enforced by the constructor alone: the checked product of a configured
rate and `window_seconds` must fit in an unsigned 64-bit integer.

datagrams_per_second.description: Sustained datagram rate per second per client IP. The effective per-window cap is `datagrams_per_second × window_seconds`. With the default `direction: both`, client→backend and backend→client datagrams count against the same cap. At least one of `datagrams_per_second` or `bytes_per_second` is required.

bytes_per_second.description: Sustained payload-byte rate per second per client IP (sum of datagram payload sizes). The effective per-window cap is `bytes_per_second × window_seconds`. With the default `direction: both`, both directions count against the same cap. At least one of `datagrams_per_second` or `bytes_per_second` is required.

window_seconds.description: Window length in seconds. Defaults to 1 second. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the derived Redis TTL (`window_seconds + 1`) and activity-retention horizon (`window_seconds × 2`) cannot wrap. The effective per-window cap is `datagrams_per_second × window_seconds` (and similarly for bytes).

ipv6_prefix.description: IPv6 prefix length used to group client addresses into one budget (for example 56 or 48 to stop rotation across a delegated prefix). IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 clients remain host-specific.

direction.description: Which datagrams are counted and limited. `both` (default) charges client→backend and backend→client datagrams to one combined budget; `client_to_backend` or `backend_to_client` limits only that direction and neither counts nor drops the other.

sync_mode.description: Datagram/byte counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Must be non-empty when set; setting it explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed drops the datagram; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

paths.description: Paths that short-circuit the entire WAF. Each entry matches from the start of the path: a plain string is an exact full-path match, `prefix*` is a prefix match, and `~regex` is a start-anchored regex (implicit `^(?:...)` wrapper so every alternation branch is anchored). Use `~.*pattern` for a floating substring match. Keep entries tight — an over-broad pattern silently disables the WAF on unintended routes. Exact and `prefix*` entries are matched against the canonical request path, so one that is not itself canonical (a percent escape, a backslash, a dot segment, or `//`) is rejected at construction; `~regex` entries are not checked this way.

consumers.description: Mapped Consumer usernames. An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username.

match.description: How paths, methods, ips, and consumers combine. all (default) short-circuits the WAF only when every configured criterion matches, so adding a criterion narrows the exemption; any short-circuits on the first matching criterion. An exemption with no criterion configured exempts nothing.

header_present.description: Header name to shared-secret value. When a request carries one of these headers with exactly the configured value (compared in constant time), every rule is suppressed for that request, and so are the fail_closed and block dispositions of on_body_too_large, on_unlisted_content_type, on_unlisted_response_content_type, and on_scan_timeout. Clients choose their own headers, so presence-only (null) entries are not admitted and each value must be a secret of at least 16 characters that only a trusted hop in front of the gateway injects. Header names are matched case-insensitively; case-equivalent duplicates are rejected.

WafPluginConfig.description: Plugin: waf — OWASP-style content-pattern threat detection for HTTP-family requests and optional responses. Fixed-shape objects reject unknown keys; intentionally open maps are rule_modes / rule_overrides (rule-id keys), category_modes (built-in category keys, validated against the rule pack), conditions.headers, and global_exemptions.header_present. On an upgraded WebSocket session the same body rule sets govern complete application messages: client-to-backend messages use the request body rules (request_inspection + request_body_inspection), backend-to-client messages use the response body rules (response_inspection + response_body_inspection). Text and Binary messages are both inspected — the HTTP media-type selectors (body_methods, body_content_types, inspect_multipart, inspect_binary_body) do not apply because a WebSocket message carries no Content-Type — control frames are never scanned, and max_scan_bytes / on_body_too_large / on_scan_timeout close the connection with RFC 6455 code 1008 on the same terms as the HTTP body path, which for their fail_closed dispositions means only when that direction carries an enforcing body policy.

mode.description: Global WAF mode. enforce is rejected at construction when no reachable enforcement path remains after default_rule_action, rule_modes, rule_overrides, disabled rules, paranoia filtering, and inspection-surface toggles. Built-in rules are monitor-only unless opted in. Anomaly scoring, stream.tcp_require_tls, enforce-action stream.signatures that some runtime hook can apply (inspect_tcp or inspect_udp), on_body_too_large: block (when a body inspection hook can run), and on_unlisted_content_type: block (when some HTTP request body can be unlisted; see that property) each satisfy admission without per-rule action: enforce. monitor with zero enforcing rules remains valid. Every optional property of this schema also accepts an explicit null, which the runtime treats exactly as an omitted key and replaces with the documented default.

default_rule_action.description: Bulk action applied to built-in rules that inherit it. Unset leaves the pack monitor-only; per-rule rule_modes entries still take precedence. Encoding-evasion heuristics (FE-ENCODING-001 and FE-ENCODING-002) stay monitor under bulk enforce until an explicit rule_modes or rule_overrides.action entry promotes them. Combine with paranoia_level to enforce only the low-false-positive core of the rule pack. block/reject are accepted aliases of enforce, log/warn of monitor, and disable/off of disabled.

detection_paranoia_level.description: Detection-only paranoia band. Defaults to paranoia_level (no band) and must be at least paranoia_level. Rules whose paranoia_min is above paranoia_level but within this level are compiled and scanned as detection-only: always monitor whatever default_rule_action or category_modes say, zero anomaly-score contribution, never an enforcing body policy, and never an admission enforcement path. Only an explicit rule_modes enforce entry promotes a band rule to a normal enforcing rule, exactly as it force-compiles a rule above this level; rule_overrides.<id>.action: enforce does not. A band body rule still turns on inspection of its body direction, so the configuration-level on_body_too_large: block and on_unlisted_content_type: block dispositions then apply to that direction (deliberately fail-closed). Their hits are reported in waf.detection_rule_hits and waf.detection_paranoia instead of waf.rule_hits, and a request with only detection hits keeps waf.action=clean.

category_modes.description: Per-category action for built-in rules, keyed by rule-pack category (for example sqli, xss, encoding_evasion). Precedence, lowest first: default_rule_action, category_modes, rule_overrides.action, rule_modes. Naming an opt-in category such as encoding_evasion promotes its rules. Custom rules keep their own action. A category no built-in rule carries is rejected. Values accept the same aliases as default_rule_action.

log_to_metadata.description: Write waf.* decision metadata into transaction logs, including waf.matched_fields: the query:, header:, cookie:, and response_header: field NAMES matched hits came from (percent-encoded, at most 16 per scan, each cut at 128 bytes) — never a matched value. Detection-only (paranoia band) hits list theirs in waf.detection_matched_fields.

log_to_stdout.description: Emit structured WAF hit diagnostics. Warnings are sampled once per source site per 10 seconds across instances, with suppressed-event counts. Every hit remains available at debug level; transaction metadata is controlled separately by log_to_metadata.

scan_budget_ms.description: Post-hoc scan deadline in milliseconds; 0 disables the timeout wrapper. Parsed as an unsigned 64-bit integer, so a negative or above-u64 value is rejected at construction. The deadline is post-hoc only on every surface, including bodies and WebSocket messages: the scan always runs and its hits always decide first, so an enforcing rule that matched still rejects even when the scan finished over budget. on_scan_timeout governs only a scan that completed clean but late. The budget bounds the scan itself: the clock starts after the body path's fairness yield, so scheduler re-poll delay is never counted. Size it against active_rules x max_scan_bytes, the only term that is under the operator's control.

max_scan_bytes.description: Maximum bytes scanned from each governed body. Must be greater than zero — construction rejects 0.

on_scan_timeout.description: Outcome for a scan that completed CLEAN but over scan_budget_ms. Because the scan always runs and its hits always decide first, this names a body the WAF inspected end to end and found nothing in, so it is a latency control rather than a coverage control. log_and_allow (default) forwards with a sampled warning and waf.scan_timed_out metadata; allow forwards silently. fail_closed is the opt-in strict-latency posture: it rejects when the governed body direction carries an enforcing body policy, resolved through request_body_policy_enforces / response_body_policy_enforces, which ask the same question as on_body_too_large: fail_closed and additionally count an on_body_too_large: block size cap while globally enforcing; monitor mode and monitor-only rule sets without that cap never start blocking. block rejects every over-budget scan on every surface, independently of global mode. Request metadata, header, query, and path scans are not disposition-aware under fail_closed: they are bounded by the frontend header limits rather than by max_scan_bytes, so only block applies the strict deadline to them. A rejection sets waf.action=blocked with waf.block_reason=scan_timeout; the timeout block itself contributes no waf.rule_hits, though an earlier monitor-only phase may already have recorded some. On a WebSocket session the same table decides the message, with the RFC 6455 code 1008 Close taking the place of the HTTP rejection, and a missed deadline is recorded with a sampled warning independently of log_to_stdout because messages carry no waf.* metadata.

on_body_too_large.description: Behavior when a governed body exceeds max_scan_bytes. fail_closed (default) rejects when that direction has an applicable enforcing body rule or anomaly scoring with an applicable body rule, and otherwise scans the prefix and records truncation, so monitor-only or conditionally out-of-scope policy never starts blocking. scan_truncated is the explicit compatibility opt-out that always scans only the prefix and forwards the complete body — prefix-only inspection lets a padded suffix carry blocked content past an enforcing rule. skip scans nothing. block rejects every oversize governed body while mode is enforce, otherwise scans the prefix. Under mode: enforce, block is itself a reachable admission enforcement path when a body inspection hook can run (HTTP bodies and WebSocket application messages share this setting), and it is a blocking disposition for the buffered-representation claim on BOTH directions, so an origin-encoded body is decoded before the cap is measured. fail_closed, scan_truncated, and skip do not satisfy that admission gate.

on_unlisted_content_type.description: Disposition for a non-empty request body whose Content-Type is outside the scan scope (not in body_content_types including the +json/+xml suffix mapping, multipart while inspect_multipart is off, or missing/unknown while inspect_binary_body is off). The declared type is attacker-controlled and many backends parse a body without consulting it. allow forwards it uninspected; fail_closed (default) rejects it when an enforcing request-body policy applies to the request, and records it otherwise; block rejects every such body while mode is enforce. Scope: HTTP request bodies only (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, native gRPC, and gRPC-Web), on every method once the request declares a body (see body_methods), on requests no global exemption short-circuits, and when this instance's request-body hook runs (request_inspection and request_body_inspection on, with an active request-body rule or FE-ENCODING-001/002). Response bodies and WebSocket messages are never governed by it. gRPC and gRPC-Web bodies are unlisted by default, except the +json codecs (application/grpc+json, application/grpc-web+json), which the suffix mapping scans as JSON, one length-prefixed message at a time; a grpc-encoding-compressed message is refused when an enforcing request-body policy applies (waf.block_reason=grpc_message_uninspectable) and recorded as waf.body_uninspected=grpc_compressed otherwise. A refusing configuration buffers the body and decides over the finalized headers and actual bytes, so an empty body always passes and the rejection (reject_status_code) arrives at end of stream. Rejections set waf.block_reason=content_type and waf.body_uninspected=content_type; recorded-but-allowed bodies set waf.body_uninspected=content_type. Under mode enforce, block is a reachable admission enforcement path when the request-body hook can run (as above) and at least one content type is left unscanned (not both inspect_multipart and inspect_binary_body); fail_closed is not.

on_unlisted_response_content_type.description: Response-side counterpart of on_unlisted_content_type, for a non-empty response body whose Content-Type is outside the same scan scope while this instance inspects response bodies. allow forwards it uninspected and records waf.body_uninspected=content_type with waf.body_uninspected_target=response_body when the body was buffered; fail_closed (default) rejects it when an enforcing response-body policy applies to the request, so monitor-only response policy never blocks; block rejects every such body while mode is enforce. Refusing values buffer the unlisted body and decide over the exact bytes, so an empty body passes. text/event-stream responses, bodiless responses (HEAD, 1xx, 204, 304), and exempt requests are never governed. Routes that serve opaque media under enforcing response-body rules list or exempt it, enable inspect_binary_body, or set allow. Neither value satisfies mode enforce admission on its own.

rule_modes.description: Per-rule action overrides keyed by rule id. Values accept the same aliases as default_rule_action. Highest action precedence. An enforce entry force-compiles the rule even above paranoia_level, and promotes a detection-band rule to a normal enforcing rule.

rule_overrides.description: Per-rule tuning by rule id (built-in or custom): attach fp_filters, scope via conditions, raise/lower paranoia_min, change severity, or set action without forking the rule pack. Unknown rule ids and unsupported fields are rejected. action sits below rule_modes and above category_modes. rule_overrides.<id>.action sets the action of a rule that is already enforced by level; only rule_modes: enforce promotes a rule above paranoia_level (including a detection-band rule), so an override's enforce leaves a band rule monitor-only and a rule above detection_paranoia_level compiled out.

exclude.description: Field exclusions: stop this one rule inspecting the named fields while it keeps inspecting every other field, and every other rule keeps inspecting these. query_params names are compared after one percent-decode (case-sensitive) and apply to query_keys, query_values, and full_url rules; a full_url match is re-verified against the URL rebuilt without the excluded pairs, and FE-HPP-001 drops them before comparing duplicates. headers are case-insensitive and apply to header_names, header_values, and response_headers rules. cookies are cookie names and apply to cookies rules. An exclusion that does not fit the rule's target, or one that names no field (an empty object, or only null or empty lists), is rejected. Query pairs are split on & only and cookies on ; only, so a backend that also splits on ; (query) or , (cookie) can read an excluded pair's value as a further field the excluding rule does not inspect.

paths.description: Exact paths by default. A trailing `*` means prefix match, and a leading `~` means an operator-authored regex matched with regex `is_match`; regex conditions may match anywhere in the path unless the pattern itself is anchored.

consumers.description: Mapped Consumer usernames. An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username.

scoring.description: Anomaly scoring. When enabled, every matched rule contributes its severity weight (or per-rule score) to this WAF instance's cumulative score; the request is rejected when that instance's score reaches its block_threshold and mode is enforce, even when no individual rule is set to enforce. Sibling WAF instances on the same proxy accumulate and threshold independently. Per-instance totals are exposed as waf.instances.<plugin-config-id>.score; waf.score is emitted only when a single scoring instance contributed, otherwise waf.instance_scores carries a deterministic sorted id=score list. enabled: false short-circuits parsing, so the remaining members are not validated in that case — block_threshold must be at least 1 only when scoring is actually enabled.

weights.description: Per-severity weights; defaults info=0 low=2 medium=3 high=5 critical=10.

body_methods.description: HTTP methods whose request bodies are always buffered and scanned. Body governance is not a method allowlist: a request on any other method (except CONNECT) is buffered, scanned, and governed by on_unlisted_content_type whenever a body may follow its head — it carries a Content-Type, declares HTTP/1.1 framing (Content-Length greater than zero or Transfer-Encoding), is an HTTP/2 request whose HEADERS frame lacked END_STREAM, or is any HTTP/3 request — and any non-empty finalized body is decided whatever the method. DELETE is included by default because it may carry content that backends parse. WebSocket messages ignore it. An empty list therefore does not turn off request-body scanning for requests that may carry a body.

body_content_types.description: Base media types whose request/response bodies are eligible for inspection. Matching is on the lowercased base type with parameters stripped. RFC 6839 structured-syntax suffixes map onto their base family and re-check this list: a type ending in `+json` (for example `application/vnd.api+json` or `application/ld+json`) is inspected when `application/json` is listed, and one ending in `+xml` (for example `application/atom+xml`) when either `application/xml` or `text/xml` is listed. The suffix rule reuses this allowlist rather than adding hidden types, so removing `application/json` also excludes `+json` types. `multipart/*` is governed by `inspect_multipart`; anything else by `inspect_binary_body`.

WafRule.description: A custom WAF rule. `pattern` is required for every match_kind except `luhn`, and `luhn` is only supported on body targets (`body_text` / `request_body`, `body_json_path`, `response_body`); both conditions are modeled below and enforced at construction. Optional properties also accept an explicit null, treated as an omitted key.

target.description: Scan target. A string selects a target that needs no extra fields (`body_json_path` is object-only). Object form uses `type` plus target-specific fields: optional non-empty `names` only for `header_values`/`request_headers`, and required non-empty `path` only for `body_json_path`. Aliases `request_headers`, `request_query`, `request_path`, `request_url`, `request_method`, and `request_body` match runtime parsing.

names.description: Optional header-name filter for header_values/request_headers; must be non-empty when provided.

path.description: Required dotted JSON path for body_json_path targets.

pattern.description: Pattern text; a CIDR rule accepts an IP or CIDR range. Required and non-empty for every match_kind except `luhn`.

action.description: Per-rule action. Unset (or null) INHERITS the global mode's default: `enforce` under `mode: enforce`, `monitor` under `monitor` and `disabled`. block/reject alias enforce, log/warn alias monitor, and disable/off alias disabled.

score.description: Anomaly-score contribution when scoring is enabled; defaults to the per-severity weight.

paths.description: Exact paths by default. A trailing `*` means prefix match, and a leading `~` means an operator-authored regex matched with regex `is_match`; regex conditions may match anywhere in the path unless the pattern itself is anchored.

consumers.description: Mapped Consumer usernames. An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username.

WafStreamConfig.description: Optional raw TCP/UDP inspection. When present the WAF also attaches to stream proxies. L7 signature scanning runs over plaintext application bytes (plain TCP opening segment, decrypted TLS/DTLS payloads); encrypted passthrough traffic is never L7-scanned. Governed by the global `mode`. A block carrying neither signatures nor tcp_require_tls is treated as absent, and the plugin stays HTTP-family only. Every optional property also accepts an explicit null, treated as an omitted key.

tcp_require_tls.description: Reject a TCP connection whose opening bytes are not a TLS/DTLS ClientHello. Applies to plain/passthrough proxies; a no-op once TLS is terminated.

inspect_tcp.description: Run signatures over the opening bytes of TCP streams. TCP frontends only: a UDP or DTLS session carries no TCP first bytes and is never judged by this switch.

inspect_udp.description: Run signatures over UDP/DTLS datagram payloads.

inspect_response.description: Also scan backend→client datagrams (client→backend only by default). A direction switch INSIDE UDP inspection, read after inspect_udp has admitted the datagram hook — it is not an independent surface, so it inspects nothing while inspect_udp is false and does not by itself satisfy mode: enforce admission.

id.description: Stable identifier, surfaced in logs and `waf.rule_hits`. Must be unique within this stream block.

pattern.description: Byte regex matched against the stream/datagram payload.

action.description: Signature action; block/reject alias enforce, log/warn alias monitor, and disable/off alias disabled. A disabled signature is dropped from the active set entirely.

WorkloadMetricsConfig.description:
Plugin: workload_metrics — Adds Istio / GAMMA-style workload identity
labels and Telemetry CRD tag overrides into transaction metadata, and
owns trace-context propagation for the mesh. The existing logging,
metrics, and OTel sinks pick these up via `TransactionSummary.metadata`
and `StreamTransactionSummary.metadata` without plugin-trait changes.

Auto-injected by mesh mode on every applicable topology; reserved
plugin id `__mesh_workload_metrics`. Standalone use is supported on
non-mesh gateways that want Istio-style workload labels in logs.

Runtime admission permits at most 32 distinct custom tag names across
`custom_tags`, `custom_header_tags`, and `custom_env_tags` combined. The
individual `maxProperties: 32` bounds remain for generated clients, but
the cross-property combined total cannot be expressed mechanically.
The same 32-name union bound applies across every effective instance
on a proxy, including potentially triggered instances. Names compose;
later instances win for values they stamp. Invalid root/field types
are construction errors; OptionalFailOpen warns and omits the instance.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit a cleartext http:// tracing provider URL (Zipkin url, Datadog agent_url, Lightstep collector_url, OpenTelemetry endpoint) whose host is not a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1]. Without it, such a provider fails construction when its exporter is built. Mesh injection writes `true` whenever a translated Istio Telemetry / MeshConfig provider uses http://, so in-cluster collectors keep working and the cleartext posture stays visible in the injected config. This cross-field rule is enforced at construction only.

node_id.description: Mesh node identifier attached to workload metadata.

topology.description: Mesh topology name attached to workload metadata.

namespace.description: Mesh namespace attached to workload metadata and used when deriving the default `service_name`.

labels.description:
Workload label hints, not arbitrary metadata injection. Workload
selects the first nonblank canonical-name, app.kubernetes.io/name,
app, k8s-app, or workload label, then the SPIFFE service account.
App selects app.kubernetes.io/name, app, or k8s-app; service selects
service.istio.io/canonical-name, service, or app. Both fall back to
workload, whose final fallback is unknown.

trust_domain_aliases.description: Additional SPIFFE trust domains accepted as equivalent to the workload's trust domain.

trusted_hbone_assertors.description:
Allow-list of identity-asserting infrastructure components whose
HBONE baggage `source.principal` may be trusted for workload
metrics source attribution. Bare service-account names match any
peer whose SPIFFE path ends with `/sa/<name>`; full SPIFFE IDs
match exactly. Default is `["ztunnel", "waypoint"]`. Explicit
empty array disables baggage-derived source attribution. Null
selects the default, as does omission.

The same `MeshTrustedHboneAssertors` schema and the same semantics
as the `mesh_authz` field of the same name — the two plugins share
ONE parser and ONE relation, so telemetry
attribution can never grant what authorization refused (issue
#4274). Refused baggage is stamped
`mesh.ignored_baggage=assertion_out_of_scope`.

sampling_percentage.description:
Tracing sampling percentage 0.0–100.0. Populated from Istio
`Telemetry.tracing.randomSamplingPercentage` and, as a baseline,
from `MeshProxyConfig.tracing_sampling` (Telemetry wins when both
are present). `ProxyConfig.spec.tracing.sampling` has no
counterpart in Istio's `networking.istio.io/v1beta1` ProxyConfig
CRD schema, so the Kubernetes API server prunes it and the
baseline arrives over native/file/xDS mesh config rather than the
CRD watcher. Non-numeric or out-of-range ProxyConfig / Telemetry
sampling values fail closed at Kubernetes translation.
Direct standalone omission leaves new roots unsampled; a valid
upstream W3C or B3 sampling decision is still inherited.

custom_tags.description:
Custom tags injected into transaction metadata and exported spans.
Names are limited to 128 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, or `-`
and cannot collide with reserved, sensitive, `mesh.*`, trace,
authorization keys, a reviewed gateway-published metadata key (for
example `grpc_full_method`, `consumer_username`, `namespace`), or a
built-in plugin's metadata namespace (`<plugin>.<key>` or
`<plugin>_<key>`, for example `ai_transcript_audit.record_id`). This map, `custom_header_tags`, and
`custom_env_tags` may contain at most 32 distinct tag names combined.
For Istio environment tags, values here are `defaultValue`
fallbacks only — live data-plane resolution uses `custom_env_tags`.

custom_header_tags.description:
Custom tags populated from request headers (`tag_name ->
header_name`). Credential-bearing source headers (including a
`pat` segment such as `x-pat` and a terminal `auth` segment such
as `x-basic-auth`) and reserved or sensitive destination names
are rejected; runtime values over 1024
bytes are omitted. Fail closed: a source header not declared in
`safe_tag_sources` is copied as `[REDACTED]`, never verbatim. This
map, `custom_tags`, and `custom_env_tags` may contain at most
32 distinct tag names combined.

custom_env_tags.description:
Istio `customTags.<tag>.environment` lookups (`tag_name ->
env_var_name`) resolved from the local data-plane process
environment at plugin construction and reload. Controllers must
not resolve these against the controller-host environment. A
present UTF-8 value overrides any matching `custom_tags` default;
a missing variable keeps that default when present and otherwise
omits the tag. Credential-bearing environment variable names
(including secret/password/token/key/credential names, the
metadata redactor's credential classes such as session
identifiers, passphrases/passcodes, PINs and one-time codes, JWTs,
signatures, private/signing key material and bearer assertions,
database connection locations, client credential identifiers, a
`PAT` segment such as `GITHUB_PAT`, a terminal `AUTH` segment such
as `BASIC_AUTH`, and operator-configured sensitive metadata names)
are rejected.
Non-UTF-8 or >1024-byte values fail construction closed. Values of
variables declared in `safe_tag_sources` are emitted as custom
transaction and trace metadata; any other variable is emitted as
`[REDACTED]` (fail closed). Diagnostics never include resolved
values or rejected credential-bearing variable names. This map,
`custom_tags`, and `custom_header_tags` may contain at most
32 distinct tag names combined.

safe_tag_sources.description:
Header names (case-insensitive) and environment variable names
(case-sensitive) whose values `custom_header_tags` and
`custom_env_tags` may copy verbatim. Every undeclared source is
copied as `[REDACTED]`. An entry that the credential classifiers
match (for example `x-session-id`, `GPG_PASSPHRASE`, `x-key-private`)
is rejected: a credential-shaped source cannot be declared safe.
Diagnostics name the entry index only.

metrics.description:
Istio Telemetry-CRD-style metrics customization. Both fields are
optional and additive. The object, each `tag_overrides` entry, and
each `operation` are closed: unknown fields, and fields belonging
to a different operation `type`, are rejected at construction.

metric.description:
Metric family targeted by this override. Supported values
are `REQUEST_COUNT`, `REQUEST_DURATION`, `REQUEST_SIZE`,
`RESPONSE_SIZE`, `TCP_OPENED_CONNECTIONS`,
`TCP_CLOSED_CONNECTIONS`, `TCP_SENT_BYTES`,
`TCP_RECEIVED_BYTES`, `GRPC_REQUEST_MESSAGES`,
`GRPC_RESPONSE_MESSAGES`, their matching `ferrum_mesh_*`
metric names, and `ALL_METRICS`; omitted means all
metrics, as does null. Other names fail direct plugin
construction. Istio translation separately warns and
omits recognized families Ferrum does not emit.

name.description:
Tag name to override. Accepts Istio names such as
`source_workload` and `grpc_response_status`, and Ferrum
`mesh.*` label names. TCP families never render
`response_code` or `grpc_response_status`. A
`response_code` value that is a status's canonical
decimal spelling shares that status's series.

operation.description:
One of `{"type": "remove"}`,
`{"type": "rename", "new_name": "..."}`,
`{"type": "set", "value": "..."}` (literal), or
`{"type": "set_expr", "cel": "..."}` /
`{"type": "set_expr", "expression": {...}}` (compiled
Telemetry UPSERT CEL). Expressions are compiled at
construction/reload; the metric hot path evaluates the
precompiled plan only. Supported CEL attributes are the
finalized mesh metric-key peer labels plus
`request.method`, `request.host`, `response.code`, and
`destination.port`. With several effective
`workload_metrics` instances, inputs are stamped from the
union required by the final composed per-family plans;
replacing one family also replaces that family's input
requirements. Exact CEL label values and ordinary mesh
identity series share a finite per-family live-series
budget configured on the global `prometheus_metrics`
plugin as `mesh_series_budget_per_family` (default
10_000, range 1–1_000_000); further distinct keys are
dropped and counted on
`ferrum_mesh_metric_series_overflow_total{family}` with
fixed family labels only. Stale TTL eviction releases
capacity. HTTP-only attributes are rejected for TCP /
`ALL_METRICS` selectors. Diagnostics never echo
expression text.

value.description:
Replacement tag value when `type` is `set`. OpenAPI
`maxLength` counts Unicode characters; runtime
admission separately enforces at most 256 UTF-8 bytes,
so multibyte values may be rejected below 256
characters.

cel.description:
Bounded CEL source when `type` is `set_expr`. Set
exactly one of `cel` and `expression`. Limits:
512 UTF-8 bytes including surrounding whitespace, 32
tokens, nesting depth 8, 24 AST nodes. Supported
forms: attribute reads,
`string(<int attribute>)`, and
`has(<string attribute>) ? <then> : <else>`.
OpenAPI `maxLength` counts Unicode characters;
runtime admission separately enforces the 512-byte UTF-8 limit,
so a multibyte expression can be rejected
below 512 characters.

expression.description:
Precompiled CEL AST produced by Telemetry translation
/ materialization (`op`: `literal`, `attribute`,
`string_of_int`, `has_then_else`).

tag_overrides.description:
Ordered per-metric tag overrides translated from the Istio
Telemetry CRD. Runtime admission accepts at most 128 entries
and at most 16384 encoded bytes across the per-family plans
stamped into transaction metadata.

disabled_metrics.description:
Names of metrics suppressed by this workload. Supported values
are `REQUEST_COUNT`, `REQUEST_DURATION`, `REQUEST_SIZE`,
`RESPONSE_SIZE`, `TCP_OPENED_CONNECTIONS`,
`TCP_CLOSED_CONNECTIONS`, `TCP_SENT_BYTES`,
`TCP_RECEIVED_BYTES`, `GRPC_REQUEST_MESSAGES`,
`GRPC_RESPONSE_MESSAGES`, their matching `ferrum_mesh_*` metric
names, and `ALL_METRICS`. Other names fail direct construction;
Istio translation separately warns and omits recognized
families Ferrum does not emit.

tracing_providers.description:
Per-provider tracing exporters surfaced from the Istio Telemetry
CRD via the mesh slice. Also enables trace-context propagation
when span reporting is disabled. Present null or [] disables
exporters and overrides the singular fallback. A `zipkin`
provider also injects the active span as B3 (`x-b3-traceid`,
`x-b3-spanid`, `x-b3-parentspanid`, `x-b3-sampled`) beside W3C
`traceparent`; B3 is likewise refreshed from the active span
whenever the backend request still carries B3 headers, and the
single-header `b3` form is written when the request used it.
Spans an exporter refuses at enqueue or discards at delivery
(`reason="export_failed"`) are counted on
`ferrum_mesh_tracing_spans_dropped_total{provider,reason}` with
fixed labels only.

tracing_provider.description:
Singular tracing exporter fallback. Ignored when
`tracing_providers` is present. Omitted/null means no provider.

span_reporting_disabled.description:
When `true`, trace context is still propagated but no spans are
exported. Matches Istio Telemetry CRD `disableSpanReporting`.

service_name.description:
Service name attached to exported spans. Defaults to
ferrum-edge-mesh-<namespace> for a nonblank namespace, otherwise
ferrum-edge-mesh. Must be nonblank when exporters are active.

deployment_environment.description:
`deployment.environment` resource attribute stamped on exported
spans. Read by the shared OTel exporter options off this same
root config object.

batch_size.description:
Span export batch size. Read by the shared OTel exporter options
off this same root config object.

flush_interval_ms.description:
Span export flush interval in milliseconds. Read by the shared
OTel exporter options off this same root config object.

buffer_capacity.description:
Maximum buffered spans awaiting export. Read by the shared OTel
exporter options off this same root config object.

buffer_max_bytes.description:
Maximum retained bytes of buffered spans. Read by the shared OTel
exporter options off this same root config object.

max_retries.description:
Span export retry attempts. Read by the shared OTel exporter
options off this same root config object.

retry_delay_ms.description:
Delay between span export retries, in milliseconds. Read by the
shared OTel exporter options off this same root config object.

direction_emit.description:
Which traffic directions emit telemetry, translated from
`Telemetry.tracing[].match.mode`. Omitted/null defaults to
server-only. Unknown nested fields are rejected.

_effective_mesh_authz_baggage_gates.description:
Internal mesh-injection field: an exact copy of every enabled
global `mesh_authz` baggage gate, evaluated as a fail-closed
conjunction. Not operator-facing; direct instances configure
`trusted_hbone_assertors` / `trust_domain_aliases` instead.

customTagName.description:
Runtime additionally rejects reserved telemetry names and sensitive
names, including operator-configured classifiers. String/label
byte limits and cross-map/cross-instance unions are checked at
admission; JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode characters.

provider.description:
Direct provider envelope; name-only references belong to Istio
translation. The envelope and each `config` are closed: unknown
fields are rejected at construction. Active exporters
require an absolute HTTP(S) endpoint with a host and no embedded
credentials. Lightstep reads its bearer token from the named local
environment variable at construction; the name must be
`FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` (`<NAME>` uppercase
`[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`), and any other variable is refused at
admission even while span reporting is disabled. URL/header/token validation
and local environment availability are runtime checks. Exporter
ranges in the parent conditional apply only with at least one
selected provider and reporting enabled; inactive numeric options
still require unsigned integer types.

celExpression.description:
Compiled AST uses snake_case attribute names, unlike CEL source.
Runtime enforces depth <= 8, total nodes <= 24, literal values <=
256 UTF-8 bytes, and family-specific attribute availability.
Recursive shape is modeled here; aggregate node/depth and encoded
plan-byte budgets remain runtime admission checks.

WsFrameLoggingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `ws_frame_logging` plugin. Logs WebSocket message
metadata (direction, frame type, payload size, optional payload
fingerprint, Close code / reason length) under the `ws_frame_log`
tracing target after the shared H1/H2/H3 relay successfully delivers
the final post-plugin message (`outcome=delivered`), and records every
gateway-published policy Close separately (`outcome=policy_close`).
Granularity is one record per complete (reassembled) message, not per
wire frame: a Text/Binary message sent as several fragments produces
one record whose `size_bytes` is the reassembled payload length
(inflated length under `websocket_permessage_deflate: terminate`), and
the disconnect record's `frames_*` counters count delivered messages.
Logs Text and Binary messages by default; Ping/Pong are opt-in via
`log_ping_pong`. Peer Close frames are logged on the delivery path with
`close_code` / `close_reason_len` (raw reason text is never logged).
`size_bytes` for Close with a status code is `2 + reason.len()`. The
plugin never transforms or drops frames — it is purely observational.
Cancelled or failed destination writes produce no frame event; frame
and disconnect `frames_*` / `bytes_*` counters share that success-only
boundary. Disconnect records also emit `io_side` (`read`/`write`/`none`),
success-only `bytes_c2b` / `bytes_b2c`, and `termination_reason` (the
relay's bounded session-end classification, e.g. `normal_peer_close`,
`relay_error`, `idle_timeout`, `drain`, `max_lifetime`). On HTTP/3, a
client-side QUIC write/FIN failure after the relay accepted the final
Close is attributed on the disconnect record (`backend_to_client` /
`write`).

`policy_close` records are emitted once per relay-half decision after
the full decision is known, independent of this plugin's priority
(including under `priority_override`): a terminal Close from any
`on_ws_frame` plugin, a fragment-budget Close, and parser rejections of
an inbound message (plugin or global frame/message size ceilings,
incomplete-message bounds, terminated `permessage-deflate` faults).
Session-level stops and relay transport faults are reported on the
disconnect record instead. Every frame, policy-close, and disconnect
record carries `plugin_id` (the plugin-config resource id, `-` when
unattributed) so multiple effective instances stay distinguishable.

Volume controls (`sample_rate`, `direction`,
`max_records_per_connection`) select `delivered` records only;
`policy_close` and disconnect records are always emitted at the
configured level.

Default `log_level` is `info` so healthy frame traffic does not become
warning-level noise. Under the gateway's default
`FERRUM_LOG_LEVEL=warn` EnvFilter, constructing an enabled empty config
emits an actionable construction-time warning naming the filtered level
while normal frame records remain suppressed. Validation and cache
publication can construct an instance separately, so the diagnostic can
repeat. A filter stricter than `warn` (or `ws_frame_log=off`) also
suppresses that diagnostic; operators using such a filter must
deliberately admit the configured target level. Explicit `trace` or
`debug` likewise require a matching (or more verbose) runtime filter;
`warn` is available only when selected deliberately. Filtering skips
fingerprint computation and tracing event construction only — frame
parsing, plugin selection (`requires_ws_frame_hooks`), `on_ws_frame` /
`on_ws_policy_close` dispatch, delivery prepare/emit, and disconnect
dispatch still occur, so H1 raw-copy tunnel mode remains unavailable
while this plugin is attached.

Admission contract: only the keys below are allowed; unknown keys and
explicit `null` field values are rejected. `payload_preview_bytes`
values above 65536 are rejected (not clamped). The plugin is registered
KeepLastKnownGood, like every log sink. Admin create/update performs
strict construction and returns HTTP 400 for an invalid enabled config
before storing it. File-mode load and `ferrum-edge validate` fail, and
a DB/CP/DP reload whose invalid enabled config cannot be constructed is
rejected so the previously published plugin generation keeps
serving.

Raw frame contents are never logged: WebSocket payloads routinely carry
credentials (bearer tokens, cookies, API keys), so when
`include_payload_preview` is enabled the `preview` field contains only a
keyed, non-reversible fingerprint of the form
`hmac-sha256:<12 hex chars> len=<bytes>` (with a trailing `+` after the
digest when only a prefix of the payload was hashed). The key is
generated per plugin instance and is not exposed in logs, so log access
alone cannot confirm guessed payloads offline. Close reasons are treated
as application payload and are never logged in the clear.

log_level.description: Tracing level for frame log output. Case-sensitive; unknown values (e.g., `"error"`, `"INFO"`) and explicit `null` are rejected at config load time. Healthy records default to `info`; construction warns when the active filter suppresses the configured level.

include_payload_preview.description: Emit a keyed, non-reversible payload fingerprint (`hmac-sha256:<prefix> len=<n>`) in the `preview` field. Raw frame bytes are never logged. Explicit `null` is rejected.

payload_preview_bytes.description: Maximum number of leading payload bytes folded into the fingerprint digest. Values above 65536 are rejected (not clamped). Must be greater than zero when `include_payload_preview` is true; zero is accepted only when previews are disabled. Explicit `null` is rejected.

log_ping_pong.description: Whether to log ping/pong frames in addition to text/binary frames. Explicit `null` is rejected.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of WebSocket connections whose `delivered` records are emitted. Sampling is deterministic per connection (a session is either fully recorded or not), so a sampled session stays coherent; unsampled sessions skip fingerprinting entirely. `0` emits no `delivered` records while keeping `policy_close` and disconnect records. Values outside 0–1, non-numbers, and explicit `null` are rejected.

direction.description: Relay direction whose `delivered` records are emitted. Does not filter `policy_close` or disconnect records. Case-sensitive; unknown values and explicit `null` are rejected.

max_records_per_connection.description: Maximum `delivered` records emitted per WebSocket connection, shared by both directions. `0` (default) is unlimited. When a connection reaches the cap the plugin emits one `event=record_cap_reached` record and suppresses further `delivered` records for that connection; `policy_close` and disconnect records are not capped. Explicit `null` is rejected.

WsLoggingConfig.description: Plugin: ws_logging — Sends transaction logs to a WebSocket endpoint in batches with bounded establishment/write timeouts, per-entry and queued-byte admission budgets, and structurally redacted endpoint diagnostics. Unknown top-level keys are rejected. `schema` and `schema_ref` are mutually exclusive. `buffer_max_bytes` must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1) at runtime; this schema encodes the absolute floor (2050) but cannot express that sibling-field arithmetic.

endpoint_url.description: WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://) to send transaction logs to. Must include a hostname, an explicit port (if any) of 1-65535, and no URL user information or fragment. A query parameter whose decoded name marks a credential is refused at runtime: exactly `jwt`, `pass`, `pwd`, `sid`, `sig`, or `signature`; any name ending in `key`; or any name containing `access_key`, `accesskey`, `api-key`, `api_key`, `apikey`, `assertion`, `auth` (so also `authorization`, `x-auth`), `bearer`, `cookie`, `credential`, `passphrase`, `passwd`, `password`, `secret`, `session`, or `token` (case-insensitive; a name still percent-encoded after one decode is refused too). The screen is a name heuristic; send collector credentials in `custom_headers`. Operational diagnostics always use a structurally redacted form (`scheme://host[:port]/redacted`). Malformed or non-WebSocket schemes are rejected at config load time. The constructor canonicalizes the value (lowercase scheme, percent-encoded path) before the collector handshake so admitted representations match the tungstenite request URI.

custom_headers.description: Header name to string value pairs added to every WebSocket upgrade request; the supported channel for collector credentials. A value may embed one `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference. Admission checks only its shape and refuses any other variable, so a control plane needs no collector credential; the serving node reads the variable when it starts the plugin generation; an unset/empty value rejects that config reload or aborts gateway startup. Handshake-owned headers (`Host`, `Connection`, `Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Key`, `Sec-WebSocket-Version`, `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `Expect`), case-insensitive duplicates, and invalid names or values are refused. Values are never logged and are redacted in admin API projections.

inbound_message_policy.description: `invalidate` closes the connection on a collector Text/Binary frame and reconnects for the next batch. `ignore` discards such frames (bounded to 64 KiB per message) and keeps the connection, for collectors that send greetings or per-batch acknowledgements. Close frames and read errors invalidate the connection under either policy.

reconnect_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds before reconnecting after connection failure

connect_timeout_ms.description: Bound covering DNS, TCP, TLS, and WebSocket Upgrade establishment. On timeout the partial transport is dropped and retry/reconnect advances. When the endpoint resolves to several addresses, each but the last may spend at most an equal share of the remaining budget connecting.

write_timeout_ms.description: Bound covering batch write/flush progress on an established socket. On timeout the complete connection (writer and drain task) is invalidated before retry/reconnect. Delivery is at-least-once.

batch_size.description: Number of entries to buffer before sending a batch

flush_interval_ms.description: Max milliseconds before flushing a partial batch

max_retries.description: Retry attempts on failed batch delivery

retry_delay_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds between retry attempts

buffer_capacity.description: Channel slot capacity. Hot-path hooks reserve a slot before serialization; new entries are dropped when full.

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized size of one admitted log record

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate serialized-content budget across queued records, contiguous batch assembly, and retries. Admission conservatively reserves two copies plus JSON-array framing, so this value must be greater than or equal to 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1). Runtime validation enforces that sibling-field lower bound; this schema encodes only the absolute floor (2050) when max_entry_bytes is at its minimum.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. WebSocket disconnect entries are serialized through the schema as well (`rename`, `omit`, `order`, `static_fields`, `derived_fields`, and `metadata` all apply). Because `ws_logging` opts into the WebSocket-disconnect capability, the named schema is recompiled under that capability at resolve time, so the WebSocket-disconnect native fields (`event`, `frames_client_to_backend`, `frames_backend_to_client`, `bytes_client_to_backend`, `bytes_backend_to_client`, `timestamp_connected`, `timestamp_disconnected`, `direction`, `io_side`, `connection_id`, `handshake_status_code`, …) are available in addition to the shared HTTP fields (`http_method` and `request_path` carry the upgrade handshake on disconnect entries). See docs/log_schema.md.

WsMessageSizeLimitingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `ws_message_size_limiting` plugin. Enforces an
actual wire-frame payload ceiling before payload reservation and an
independent reassembled-message ceiling. Violations trigger a bounded
close frame (RFC 6455 close code 1009 — Message Too Big) sent to both
client and backend after shared relay cancellation is published, and
increment `ferrum_ws_message_size_limit_rejected_total{direction}`.
The top-level fields are the default for both directions;
`client_to_backend` and `backend_to_client` override any of them for
frames read from that peer. Under `websocket_permessage_deflate:
terminate`, a compressed or inflated frame/message over this plugin's
ceiling closes with the configured `close_reason`; a fault at an
independent global or decompression ceiling keeps the adapter's fixed
reason.

max_frame_bytes.description: Maximum frame payload size in bytes, the default for both directions. Required and must be greater than zero — the plugin rejects configs with `max_frame_bytes` of 0 at config load time. Applied to Text, Binary, Ping, and Pong frames in both directions; Close frames bypass the size check. Note that Ping/Pong are RFC 6455 control frames capped at 125 bytes by the protocol itself, so values below 125 will close the connection on heartbeat traffic.

max_message_bytes.description: Maximum reassembled Text/Binary message payload in bytes, the default for both directions. Defaults to four times `max_frame_bytes` and must be greater than or equal to `max_frame_bytes`. Continuation frames are still checked separately against `max_frame_bytes`; a cumulative message larger than the frame limit is valid until this independent bound is exceeded.

close_reason.description: Close frame reason text sent to both peers when either limit is exceeded, the default for both directions. Truncated to 123 UTF-8 bytes (the WebSocket protocol close-frame reason limit) on a UTF-8 char boundary.

client_to_backend.description: Override for frames the client sends (the client-side parser).

backend_to_client.description: Override for frames the backend sends (the backend-side parser).

WsMessageSizeLimitingDirectionConfig.description:
Per-direction override for `ws_message_size_limiting`. Omitted fields
inherit the top-level value, except that when `max_message_bytes` is
set at neither level it defaults to four times this direction's
effective `max_frame_bytes`. The resolved values must satisfy
`max_message_bytes >= max_frame_bytes`; an inherited explicit
top-level `max_message_bytes` below a raised override
`max_frame_bytes` is rejected. Ping/Pong count against this
direction's `max_frame_bytes`, so values below 125 close the
connection on heartbeat traffic.

max_frame_bytes.description: Maximum frame payload in bytes for this direction.

max_message_bytes.description: Maximum reassembled Text/Binary message payload in bytes for this direction.

close_reason.description: Close frame reason text for violations in this direction; truncated to 123 UTF-8 bytes on a UTF-8 char boundary.

WsRateLimitingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `ws_rate_limiting` plugin. Enforces WebSocket
frame rate limiting using a token-bucket algorithm, per connection by
default or as an aggregate budget shared by every session of one
consumer, client IP, or proxy (`limit_by`). When the bucket is
exhausted, the plugin sends a WebSocket close frame (RFC 6455 close code
1008 — Policy Violation) to both client and backend. Both directions
(client→backend and backend→client) consume from the same bucket. Both
values stay within 1–1000000. With `sync_mode: "redis"`,
`frames_per_second` and `burst_size` must also form an integer-multiple
refill window of at most 3600 seconds so Redis two-window enforcement
cannot over-admit or under-admit relative to the local token bucket,
including across Redis failure/recovery; a local-only policy accepts any
capacity/refill pair. Redis mode externalizes those per-connection
counters under a per-plugin/gateway-instance key namespace; it does not
coordinate a portable per-connection frame budget across gateway
instances, reconnects, or plugin rebuilds. Aggregate `limit_by` budgets
are keyed by their portable identity instead, so replicas of one policy
share them. `sync_mode` is parsed case-insensitively (`LOCAL`, `Redis`);
`redis` requires `redis_url`. Unknown top-level keys are rejected by the
runtime and by this schema. Counter storage supports only local memory
and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported.
Residual admission rules this schema cannot express, enforced by the
constructor alone: with `sync_mode: "redis"`, `burst_size` must be >=
`frames_per_second`, an integer multiple of it, and
`burst_size / frames_per_second` must be at most 3600 seconds.

frames_per_second.description: Token refill rate per second. Range 1–1000000. Must be greater than zero — configs with `frames_per_second: 0` are rejected at config load time. With `sync_mode: redis`, together with `burst_size`, must yield an integer-multiple refill window of at most 3600 seconds so Redis and local sustained rates match.

burst_size.description: Maximum burst capacity (tokens). Range 1–1000000. Defaults to the value of `frames_per_second` when not explicitly set. Must be greater than zero. With `sync_mode: redis` it must also be greater than or equal to `frames_per_second`, an integer multiple of `frames_per_second`, and yield a refill window (`burst_size / frames_per_second`) of at most 3600 seconds: configs that Redis cannot represent without over-admitting or under-admitting relative to the local token bucket are rejected at config load time. A local-only policy accepts any pair, including a burst smaller than the sustained rate.

close_reason.description: Close-frame reason text sent when the frame rate is exceeded. Truncated on a UTF-8 char boundary to 123 bytes (the RFC 6455 §5.5 control-frame payload limit) so the frame stays well-formed.

limit_by.description: Budget dimension. `connection` (default) gives every WebSocket session its own bucket. `consumer` shares one bucket across every session of the authenticated principal (a mapped Consumer, or an unmapped external identity keyed together with its verifying realm, so the two never share a bucket); anonymous sessions share their client IP's bucket. `ip` shares one bucket per resolved client IP. `service` shares one bucket per proxy. The identity is resolved once at upgrade admission. Aggregate budgets use the same 50,000-key local cap; with `sync_mode: redis` they are keyed by that identity (no per-instance UUID), so replicas of one policy share them.

sync_mode.description: Frame counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (externalized per-connection counters namespaced per plugin/gateway instance; not a portable cross-instance budget), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. With an aggregate `limit_by` (`consumer`, `ip`, `service`) the Redis counter is keyed by that identity and shared by every replica of the policy; a refused frame batch is handed back, so refusals never consume the shared budget. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share the surrounding key namespace. Must be non-empty when set. In the default `limit_by: connection` mode this plugin still prepends a per-instance UUID to every logical connection key, so an explicit shared prefix does not opt two plugin or gateway instances into a shared per-connection frame budget. Aggregate `limit_by` keys carry no instance UUID.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed closes the WebSocket with a policy Close frame; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.
